Security in the cloud, meaning the data, its encryption, its access and its configuration, stays with the customer.
The split follows control, and control follows who owns the layer.
questionsV2.recallLine: During contract review for moving a bank's backup archive to an infrastructure cloud provider, who is responsible for the data centers, host hardware and hypervisors?

optionsShort.A: Orrell Trust, the controller retaining security responsibility
optionsShort.B: The credit unions, whose customers the data describes
optionsShort.C: The provider, under the shared responsibility model
optionsShort.D: Whichever party the SLA names per incident

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: Confuses accountability with responsibility. Orrell Trust must rely on the provider for what it cannot physically do.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Assigns infrastructure duties by data origin. The credit unions sit further from the hypervisor than the bank.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Negotiates the split incident by incident. It is structural to the service model; an SLA documents it.

questionsV2.question: For the inventory to support security accountability, which pair of attributes MUST every asset record carry?

options.A: The purchase price and its current depreciated value
options.B: The warranty expiry and the vendor's support contact
options.C: A unique identifier and a named, accountable owner
options.D: The rack location and its scheduled maintenance window

questionsV2.explanation:
Security accountability needs two things: a way to refer to exactly one asset, and a person answerable for it (C). With both, 500 retired drives cannot vanish, because each carries a number and somebody has to sign for its disposition. Without that pair no other attribute can be enforced.
An inventory becomes a security control when every entry is uniquely identifiable and owned.
questionsV2.recallLine: The rebuilt inventory still needs its minimum record defined. For it to support security accountability, which pair of attributes MUST every entry carry?

optionsShort.A: Purchase price and current depreciated value
optionsShort.B: Warranty expiry and the vendor's support contact
optionsShort.C: A unique identifier and a named owner
optionsShort.D: Rack location and scheduled maintenance window

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Serves accounting and depreciation. A drive's book value would not flag that it left the building readable.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Drives maintenance decisions. Warranty and vendor data establish nobody who answers when an asset is mishandled.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Describes where and when. Location fields go stale precisely at disposal, the moment this incident occurred.

questionsV2.question: Wexmoor Diagnostics, a clinical laboratory, holds eleven years of patient results in a warehouse whose tables were tagged Internal when it was built in 2019. Since then the lab has loaded genetic marker panels into the same tables, merged the patient identifiers of two acquired laboratories, and accumulated roughly 40,000 duplicate subject records. The data owner has funding for one remediation project this year. Which data maintenance activity should she fund FIRST?

options.A: Deduplicate the merged patient identifiers so each subject resolves to a single record.
options.B: Re-run the classification review so the genetic panels carry the tags they now warrant.
options.C: Rebuild the warehouse indexes and refresh statistics to recover the degraded query times.
options.D: Archive results older than seven years to cold storage under the retention schedule.

questionsV2.explanation:
Classification is the input every other protection reads. Access rules, encryption strength, retention and disposal all derive from the label, so a label that no longer describes the contents miscalibrates every one of them at once. Genetic markers are a more sensitive class than the chemistry results the Internal tag was chosen for in 2019, and the tag has not moved. Re-running the classification review (B) goes first.
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 RA-2 requires the categorization to be reviewed when the information a system processes changes. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.12 says the same of classification, and A 5.13 of the labeling that follows it.
Correct the label before you correct the rows underneath it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A patient warehouse tagged Internal in 2019 now holds genetic panels and duplicate records. Which maintenance activity should the data owner fund FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Deduplicate the merged patient identifiers
optionsShort.B: Reclassify the tables for genetic data
optionsShort.C: Rebuild indexes to recover query times
optionsShort.D: Archive results past the retention period

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: Genuine maintenance, and the duplicates do real harm. It runs inside an envelope sized for chemistry panels.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: A performance task. Slow queries cost the lab money and nothing else.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Moves data under a schedule written before the genetic panels existed, carrying the stale tag into the archive.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | RA-2 Security Categorization
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.5.12 Classification of information; A.5.13 Labeling of information
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.4.4 Data maintenance

questionsV2.question: Trentmoor Water District operates 62 programmable logic controllers at eleven pumping stations. The manufacturer's support ended four months ago and no further firmware fixes will be issued. Replacement units are funded, but delivery and commissioning run 14 months out, and the operations director intends to keep the existing controllers in service throughout. The district's asset retention policy requires a documented decision whenever an asset is kept in service past end of support. Which action must the district complete BEFORE it commits to another 14 months of unsupported operation?

options.D: A risk acceptance signed by the system owner, with compensating controls and a review date.
options.A: Weekly authenticated vulnerability scanning of all 62 controllers, reported to the operations director.
options.B: A vendor quotation for custom extended support covering the entire 14-month replacement window.
options.C: An asset register update marking each controller unsupported and flagged for replacement funding.

questionsV2.explanation:
End of support is a governance event before it is a technical one. The manufacturer stops issuing fixes and the residual risk moves onto the operator's books, where somebody has to sign for it. A retention policy demanding a documented decision is demanding exactly that signature, with the mitigations named and a date on which the acceptance is re-examined (D).
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SA-22 governs unsupported system components and requires documented justification and mitigations where they are retained. PM-9 and RA-7 carry the risk-acceptance path, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.9 puts the accountability on the asset owner and not on the operator running the plant.
Unsupported operation should be a signed choice, not the default that arrives when a date passes.
questionsV2.recallLine: A water district will run 62 controllers for 14 months past the manufacturer's last firmware fix. What must it complete BEFORE that?

optionsShort.D: Signed risk acceptance with compensating controls
optionsShort.A: Weekly authenticated scanning of the controllers
optionsShort.B: Quotation for custom extended support
optionsShort.C: Register update marking them unsupported

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: Detective work. A scan faithfully reports flaws for which no patch exists, which informs the acceptance.

B.label: correct but not first
B.wouldAnswer: Worth doing, and it might change the outcome. A quotation is an input to the decision, not the decision.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Records a state. A register can read unsupported for a year with nobody having agreed to run that way.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SA-22 Unsupported System Components; RA-7 Risk Response
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.5.9 Inventory of information and other associated assets
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.5 Ensure appropriate asset retention (EOL, EOS)

questionsV2.question: Arden Polymer's asset register lists 210 servers. At the annual review the infrastructure manager finds 38 running an operating system whose extended-support contract expires in six weeks; 12 of those 38 hold the recipe database the company classifies Restricted, and 9 sit in a DMZ reachable from partner networks. Migration capacity and change windows exist for 20 servers before the contract lapses. The remaining 18 will run unsupported for at least a quarter. Which basis for choosing the 20 is BEST?

options.C: The classification of the data each server holds and its reachability from untrusted networks.
options.A: The date each server was commissioned, moving the oldest hardware out of service first.
options.B: The number of business applications each server hosts, moving the busiest workloads first.
options.D: The remaining book value of each server, moving the fully depreciated assets first.

questionsV2.explanation:
Choosing what to migrate is a risk ranking, and the two variables that set the risk are already on the page: what a server holds, and who can reach it. The nine DMZ machines and the twelve carrying Restricted recipe data are where an unpatchable flaw becomes a loss, so those come off the expiring contract first, and the eighteen left behind are the ones that get written mitigations (C).
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 RA-2 ties the protection a system gets to the categorization of the information in it, and SA-22 requires either supported components or documented mitigations for what remains.
Rank by consequence and reachability, then document what you knowingly leave behind.
questionsV2.recallLine: Only 20 of 38 servers can leave an expiring support contract in time. Which basis for choosing them is BEST?

optionsShort.C: Data classification and network exposure
optionsShort.A: Age of the hardware
optionsShort.B: Number of applications hosted
optionsShort.D: Remaining depreciation on the asset

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The basis for a hardware refresh, where age predicts failure. The oldest boxes may be the least reachable.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Ranks by business load, an availability argument. A busy print server beats no idle DMZ host holding recipes.

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: A finance basis driven by the depreciation schedule. Book value bears no relation to what an attacker can reach.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SA-22 Unsupported System Components; RA-2 Security Categorization
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.5 Ensure appropriate asset retention (EOL, EOS)

questionsV2.question: Tarrowgate Analytics discovers, during a quarterly reconciliation of its cloud accounts against the asset register, a virtual machine that has been running in the production subscription for eight months and appears in no register entry. It carries no tags, no backup policy and no patch group. Four project teams hold deployment rights to that subscription and none claims it; the machine is serving traffic on port 443. Which action should the infrastructure team take FIRST?

options.A: Trace the deployment credentials in the audit log and confirm ownership with that team's manager.
options.B: Shut the machine down and wait to see which team reports the resulting outage.
options.C: Add the machine to the weekly authenticated vulnerability scan and review what it finds.
options.D: Apply the standard hardened baseline and enroll the machine in the monthly patch group.

questionsV2.explanation:
An asset nobody owns cannot be classified, cannot be given a maintenance window anyone will approve, and cannot be retired without a fight. Ownership is the prerequisite, and the audit log holds it: the credential that created the machine belongs to a person, in a team, with a manager who can adopt the asset or disown it in writing. Tracing that credential (A) comes first.
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-8 requires the component inventory to carry an owner for each entry, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.9 makes that owner accountable for the protection the asset gets.
Establish who owns it, then protect it.
questionsV2.recallLine: An unclaimed production virtual machine has been serving traffic for eight months and sits in no asset register. What should happen FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Trace the deployment credentials to an owner
optionsShort.B: Shut it down and await complaints
optionsShort.C: Add it to the vulnerability scan
optionsShort.D: Apply the baseline and patch group

B.label: correct but not first
B.wouldAnswer: The scream test, real once the trail has gone cold. A machine answering on 443 may be serving paying customers.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Detective. A scan produces findings nobody is accountable for closing, which fills a register with exceptions.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Belongs at provisioning. A baseline applied blind can break an unknown workload, and nobody can approve a reboot.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-8 System Component Inventory
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.5.9 Inventory of information and other associated assets
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.3.3 Asset management

questionsV2.question: Penhale Fitness, a 40-club gym chain, is finishing a member app. The product team wants the app to report the member's precise position every two minutes so the chain can study travel patterns around its clubs. The only feature that needs location today is the club finder. The privacy officer must recommend one collection design to the steering group, which meets on Thursday. Which design MOST reduces the privacy exposure the app creates?

options.C: Coarse location, requested while the club-finder screen is open, with no background collection.
options.A: Precise location, collected continuously, encrypted at rest under per-member keys held offline.
options.B: Precise location, collected continuously, purged automatically thirty days after each point is captured.
options.D: Coarse location, collected continuously in the background, taken under explicit member opt-in.

questionsV2.explanation:
Data that was never gathered cannot leak, cannot be subpoenaed, cannot be sold with the business, and does not appear in the notification when the backend is breached. Coarse position, requested only while the club-finder screen is open (C), gathers the least. Every other design accepts a continuous positional track and then tries to hold it safely, which is a strictly larger problem.
GDPR Article 5(1)(c) states the minimization principle, and Article 25 requires it to be engineered in at design time. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 PM-25 and the PT control family carry the same rule for personally identifiable information.
Ask what the feature requires before asking how to guard what you took.
questionsV2.recallLine: A gym app needs location for a club finder, but product wants a continuous precise track. Which collection design MOST reduces exposure?

optionsShort.C: Coarse location while the club finder is open
optionsShort.A: Continuous precise track, encrypted at rest
optionsShort.B: Continuous precise track, purged after thirty days
optionsShort.D: Coarse location, collected continuously, with consent

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Defends the store against theft and insider browsing. Ciphertext at rest does not shrink what the chain holds.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: A retention control at the far end. Thirty days of two-minute fixes still shows where a member lives and sleeps.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Lowers granularity and makes the processing lawful. A background track still serves a purpose no feature asked for.

sources: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) | Article 5(1)(c) data minimization; Article 25 data protection by design
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PM-25 Minimization of PII Used in Testing, Training, and Research; PT-2 Authority to Process PII
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.4.2 Data collection

questionsV2.question: At Beltram Foods the head of merchandising asks for the store-loyalty dataset to be reclassified from Confidential to Internal, so it can be loaded into a low-cost analytics service that is not approved for Confidential data. The set holds names, email addresses and two years of purchase history for 1.8 million shoppers. He argues the data has no competitive value and that the current label is slowing the business. The information security manager objects. Which consideration should carry the GREATEST weight in the committee's decision?

options.B: The harm to the 1.8 million shoppers if the purchase history were disclosed.
options.A: The competitive value of the same purchase history to a rival grocery chain.
options.C: The cost difference between the approved platform and the proposed analytics service.
options.D: The absence of payment card numbers or government identifiers from the dataset.

questionsV2.explanation:
Classification measures the impact of a loss, and impact is counted for everyone who bears it. Names, addresses and two years of what 1.8 million households buy make a re-identifiable behavioral profile. A disclosure exposes pregnancies, medications, religious observance and income, and that harm lands on people who never chose to be in the file (B).
FIPS 199 sets categorization by the adverse effect a confidentiality loss would have on organizational operations, organizational assets and individuals, and it is the third of those that decides this case. NIST SP 800-122 treats identifiability and context of use as what makes personal information sensitive, more than the presence of any one field.
Label by consequence, then let the label choose the platform.
questionsV2.recallLine: A merchandiser wants a two-year loyalty dataset downgraded so cheaper analytics can use it. Which consideration carries GREATEST weight in classifying it?

optionsShort.B: Harm to the shoppers if disclosed
optionsShort.A: Competitive value to a rival chain
optionsShort.C: Cost difference between the two platforms
optionsShort.D: No card numbers in the dataset

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: The argument merchandising already made. A real dimension of impact, counting only harm the firm itself feels.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Belongs to procurement. The price of an approved platform is an argument for buying capacity.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Applies the cardholder test, right for PCI scope. No card number is needed to read a life off two years of receipts.

sources: FIPS 199 | Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information Systems
NIST SP 800-122 | Guide to Protecting the Confidentiality of PII, Section 3.2 PII Confidentiality Impact Levels
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.1.1 Data classification

questionsV2.question: Drumlin Mutual's data catalog records no owner for the agent-commission dataset. Marketing built the pipeline that assembles it nightly and pays for the warehouse capacity; Finance uses it to calculate commission payments and would have to restate them if the figures were wrong; IT operations runs the servers and holds the backups; internal audit reviews it quarterly. The catalog requires one accountable owner per dataset. Which unit is the MOST appropriate owner?

options.A: Marketing, which built the pipeline and funds the warehouse capacity it consumes.
options.D: Finance, which depends on the figures and bears the loss when they are wrong.
options.C: IT operations, which runs the servers and holds the backups of the dataset.
options.B: Internal audit, which reviews the dataset quarterly and reports on its accuracy.

questionsV2.explanation:
Ownership follows accountability for the business outcome. When the commission figures are wrong, Finance restates payments to agents, answers the regulator and absorbs the cost, and that exposure is exactly what an owner accepts when they set a classification, approve access and sign a retention decision (D).
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 CM-8 requires an owner recorded against each inventoried asset, and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.9 defines that owner as the party responsible for the asset across its lifecycle, deliberately separate from whoever operates it.
Ask who has to explain the error to the regulator.
questionsV2.recallLine: Four units touch an agent-commission dataset that needs one accountable owner in the catalog. Which unit is the MOST appropriate owner?

optionsShort.A: Marketing, which built the pipeline
optionsShort.D: Finance, which bears the loss
optionsShort.C: IT operations, which runs the servers
optionsShort.B: Internal audit, which reviews it quarterly

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Confuses building with owning. Marketing supplies the dataset and pays a bill; a cost center is not accountability.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: The custodian role stated plainly. Running servers and holding backups is done on an owner's instructions.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Would dissolve the independence audit exists to provide. No function can review what it is accountable for.

sources: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.5.9 Inventory of information and other associated assets
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-8 System Component Inventory
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.3.1 Information and asset ownership

questionsV2.question: Vasterly Retail's records schedule purges email older than three years, and a nightly job enforces it across all mailboxes. On Tuesday the general counsel issues a litigation hold naming 41 custodians, including two who left the company last year and whose mailboxes are now in an archive tier. The messaging administrator has ten hours before the purge job runs again. Which action should he take FIRST?

options.A: Place the 41 mailboxes, archives included, on hold so the purge job skips them.
options.B: Export the 41 mailboxes to a review platform and hand the files to counsel.
options.C: Disable the nightly purge job for every mailbox until the litigation is resolved.
options.D: Amend the records schedule to retain all email for seven years instead of three.

questionsV2.explanation:
Preservation suspends destruction for the named data, and the mechanism has to reach every copy the schedule reaches. That is why the two departed custodians in the archive tier matter more here than the thirty-nine live mailboxes. An in-place hold marks all 41 so the nightly job passes over them while the rest of the estate keeps aging out on schedule, and it fits inside the ten hours available (A).
Federal Rules of Civil Procedure Rule 37(e) turns a failure to preserve into sanctions. ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A 5.33 requires records to be protected against unauthorized deletion, and NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SI-12 covers retention and handling.
Preserve narrowly and at once, then collect.
questionsV2.recallLine: A nightly purge runs in ten hours and counsel has just issued a hold on 41 custodians. What should the administrator do FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Place the named mailboxes on hold
optionsShort.B: Export the mailboxes for counsel
optionsShort.C: Disable the purge job entirely
optionsShort.D: Extend the schedule to seven years

B.label: correct but not first
B.wouldAnswer: Collection, and it is coming. A copied file does not stop that mailbox being purged an hour later.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Halts deletion company-wide, turning a 41-custodian hold into estate-wide over-retention. That is discoverable too.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Rewrites the default for everyone to handle an exception for a few, which is what a hold exists to avoid.

sources: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure | Rule 37(e) Failure to Preserve Electronically Stored Information
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SI-12 Information Management and Retention
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.5.33 Protection of records
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.4.5 Data retention

questionsV2.question: Sablon Group, a French insurer, forbids any transfer of policyholder personal data outside the EEA without a lawful transfer mechanism. Its chosen analytics vendor runs production in Frankfurt, but the vendor's support desk in Manila holds standing read access to production records so it can work tickets, and the vendor will not staff a European desk. Signature is three weeks away and the business will not change vendors. Which measure BEST brings the arrangement inside that requirement?

options.A: Pin every storage bucket, database and backup target to the Frankfurt region.
options.C: Execute standard contractual clauses covering the Manila desk, with a transfer impact assessment.
options.B: Encrypt the production database at rest with keys Sablon holds in Frankfurt.
options.D: Log every Manila support session and review the access records each month.

questionsV2.explanation:
Access is transfer. When a support engineer in Manila reads a policyholder record held on a Frankfurt server, personal data has left the EEA as surely as a replicated backup would, and no storage setting reaches that path. Standard contractual clauses covering the Manila desk, with a transfer impact assessment (C), is the measure that fits.
GDPR Chapter V governs the case, and the Article 46(2)(c) standard contractual clauses are the mechanism available where neither an adequacy decision nor binding corporate rules apply. Schrems II and EDPB Recommendations 01/2020 add the transfer impact assessment and whatever supplementary measures it calls for.
When the access path cannot be removed, make the transfer lawful and bound it in the contract.
questionsV2.recallLine: An EEA insurer's vendor answers tickets from Manila with standing read access to production. Which measure BEST satisfies the transfer rule?

optionsShort.A: Pin all storage to the Frankfurt region
optionsShort.C: Standard contractual clauses and a transfer assessment
optionsShort.B: Encrypt the database at rest
optionsShort.D: Log and review the support sessions

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Answers a storage-residency question. Pinning regions leaves the Manila session exactly as it was.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Defends the database against stolen disks or a snapshot. The support desk is an authorized reader.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Produces a tidy record of transfers that were unlawful at the moment they happened. Useful to an investigation.

sources: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) | Chapter V, Article 46(2)(c) standard contractual clauses
EDPB | Recommendations 01/2020 on supplementary transfer tools
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.4.3 Data location

questionsV2.question: Halverson University and Brightpath Wellbeing run a student wellbeing program together. The university selected the participating cohorts and receives cohort-level reports; Brightpath designed the questionnaire, set the two-year retention period and reuses the responses to improve its own risk model. A student asks Brightpath to erase her responses; Brightpath tells her to contact the university, and the university says Brightpath decides how long the data is kept. Which instrument does the arrangement MOST clearly require?

options.A: An Article 28 processor contract binding Brightpath to the university's documented instructions.
options.B: An Article 26 arrangement dividing the two parties' obligations, its essence published to students.
options.C: A data sharing notice added to the university's published student privacy statement.
options.D: A data protection impact assessment covering the program's monitoring of enrolled students.

questionsV2.explanation:
Roles follow the facts of who decides. Brightpath designed the questionnaire, fixed the retention period and reuses the responses for its own risk model. The university chose the cohorts and takes the reports. Both are determining purposes and means, which makes them joint controllers under GDPR Article 26. That article requires a transparent arrangement (B) setting out which party discharges which obligation, with its essence made available to the data subjects, and the student free to exercise her rights against either party. That is precisely the ping-pong the stem describes.
Establish who determines the purpose, and the paperwork follows from it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A university and a wellbeing vendor each set part of the purpose and retention for student responses. Which instrument does that MOST clearly require?

optionsShort.A: Article 28 processor contract
optionsShort.B: Article 26 joint controller arrangement
optionsShort.C: A data sharing notice to students
optionsShort.D: A data protection impact assessment

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The instrument for a genuine processor. One that sets retention and reuses data is a controller under Article 28(10).

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Publishes what happens and allocates nothing. Students still would not know which party must erase a response.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Very likely required too, under the Article 35 threshold. An assessment documents risk and allocates no duty.

sources: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) | Article 26 joint controllers; Article 28(10); Article 35
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.4.1 Data roles (owners, controllers, custodians, processors, users/subjects)

questionsV2.question: Corrindale Bank's payment service holds cardholder numbers in memory while it authorizes a transaction. During an outage a support engineer captures a core dump of the crashed process and uploads it to the vendor's ticket portal for analysis; the dump is 6 GB and carries the whole process heap. Full-disk encryption is enabled on the server and TLS 1.3 protects the upload. Which control MOST directly prevents a recurrence?

options.D: Disable core dumps for the payment service and emit a redacted crash report instead.
options.B: Require the vendor portal to accept uploads over a mutually authenticated TLS connection.
options.C: Encrypt the dump file at rest on the server before the engineer uploads it.
options.A: Add a data loss prevention rule blocking uploads of files above one gigabyte.

questionsV2.explanation:
The card numbers were protected in every state the bank had planned for and exposed in the one it had not. A crash dump is process memory written to disk: data in use becomes data at rest in a file nobody classified, and then data in transit to a third party. Suppressing the dump, or replacing it with a report that carries stack frames and no heap (D), removes the copy.
PCI DSS v4.0 Requirement 3.5.1 requires the primary account number to be unreadable wherever it is stored, and NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 SI-11 covers error handling that does not reveal information to unauthorized parties.
Stop the copy being created.
questionsV2.recallLine: A support engineer sent a 6 GB core dump containing card numbers to a vendor portal. Which control MOST directly prevents a recurrence?

optionsShort.D: Disable core dumps, emit a redacted report
optionsShort.B: Require mutual TLS to the portal
optionsShort.C: Encrypt the dump file at rest
optionsShort.A: Block uploads above one gigabyte

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Hardens a channel TLS 1.3 already protects. A well-authenticated upload of cleartext card numbers is a disclosure.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Leaves the file readable inside the engineer's own session, where the copy was made, and the upload decrypts it.

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Keys on file size, a property of this incident and not of the risk. A 200 MB dump sails straight through.

sources: PCI DSS v4.0 | Requirement 3.5.1 PAN rendered unreadable wherever stored
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SI-11 Error Handling
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.6.1 Data states (in use, in transit, at rest)

questionsV2.question: Corbin and Hale, a valuation firm, emails 300-page appraisal reports to client contacts. Last month an analyst sent a report to the wrong recipient at a competitor; the firm wants any future misdirected report to become unreadable once the mistake is noticed, including copies already downloaded and forwarded. Email is the required delivery channel and clients will not install a portal. Which protection method BEST meets that requirement?

options.A: Digital rights management, issuing each report a license the firm can revoke centrally.
options.B: An outbound data loss prevention rule that quarantines reports addressed to external domains.
options.C: A cloud access security broker enforcing policy on the firm's sanctioned cloud storage.
options.D: S/MIME encryption of each report to the recipient's certificate before the mail leaves.

questionsV2.explanation:
The unusual part of this requirement is that the protection has to survive delivery and then be withdrawable. Enterprise rights management is the method built for it: the document is encrypted, every open is a license check against the firm's server, and revoking a license turns copies already sitting in a competitor's inbox back into ciphertext (A).
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-16 covers security attributes bound to information as it moves between systems, and the ISC2 outline files rights management beside DLP and the cloud access broker as a data protection method.
Ask whether the control has to reach past the moment of delivery.
questionsV2.recallLine: A valuation firm must be able to render a misdirected report unreadable after it has been delivered. Which protection method BEST meets that?

optionsShort.A: Digital rights management with revocable licenses
optionsShort.B: Outbound DLP quarantining external mail
optionsShort.C: A cloud access security broker
optionsShort.D: S/MIME encryption to the recipient

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Strong against misdirection before it happens, and it reaches nothing already delivered.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Governs how staff use cloud services and inspects that traffic. This report left by mail, which it never sees.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Right when interception is the worry. Once the wrong recipient decrypts the file, the firm holds no lever.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-16 Security and Privacy Attributes
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.6.4 Data protection methods (DRM, DLP, CASB)

questionsV2.question: Merrow Actuarial is exiting a multi-tenant SaaS claims platform on 31 March. Its regulator requires evidence that customer records have been destroyed. The provider stores each tenant's data encrypted under a per-tenant key on shared arrays it also uses for 900 other customers, and its immutable backups expire on a fixed 90-day cycle that cannot be shortened. Merrow's contract lets it specify the exit deliverable. Which deliverable is the BEST one to require?

options.A: A certificate of destruction listing the media on which Merrow's records resided.
options.C: A written attestation that the tenant key was destroyed, with the backup expiry date.
options.B: An independent audit witnessing the provider degauss the arrays holding Merrow's records.
options.D: An overwrite of Merrow's records in the production database before the tenant closes.

questionsV2.explanation:
Two of these are the same regulator's answer in different worlds. On dedicated media a certificate naming the drives is the artifact, which is what makes that reading tempting. On arrays shared with 900 other tenants there are no drives to name, and no provider will destroy them.
The data was encrypted from the moment it was written, and each tenant holds its own key. Destroying that key renders every copy unrecoverable, immutable backups included, even though those will not expire until the 90-day cycle runs out. NIST SP 800-88 Rev 1 recognizes cryptographic erase as a purge technique on exactly that condition. The attestation paired with the backup expiry date (C) is therefore the honest deliverable, because it shows the regulator the residual window up front.
When you cannot reach the media, reach the key, and disclose the window.
questionsV2.recallLine: A multi-tenant SaaS provider cannot destroy shared arrays, and immutable backups run 90 days. Which exit deliverable is the BEST evidence of destruction?

optionsShort.A: Certificate of destruction naming the media
optionsShort.C: Attested tenant key destruction and backup expiry
optionsShort.B: Independent audit witnessing the arrays degaussed
optionsShort.D: Overwrite the records in production

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Would have to be signed by a provider that destroyed nothing, which is worse than no certificate at all.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Asks for 900 live tenants' hardware to be degaussed. It will be refused, and it would be an outage if granted.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Clears the live rows and leaves every backup intact, the failure that persuades people deleted means gone.

sources: NIST SP 800-88 Rev 1 | Guidelines for Media Sanitization, cryptographic erase as a purge technique
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.4.7 Data destruction

questionsV2.question: Kestrel Mortgage keeps borrower contact details in a servicing platform that the business treats as the system of record. A compliance review finds that when a call-center agent corrects an address, the correction survives until the nightly feed from the retired origination database overwrites the field with the value captured at closing. Statements have gone to superseded addresses for eleven months, and 900 borrowers are affected. The data owner has funded one fix. Which data maintenance action MOST directly ends the recurrence?

options.A: Retire the origination feed and make the servicing platform the sole authoritative source.
options.B: Run a monthly reconciliation report listing addresses that differ between the two systems.
options.C: Add a validation rule rejecting malformed addresses at the point the agent types them.
options.D: Bulk-update the 900 borrower records in both systems from the postal address file.

questionsV2.explanation:
Two systems both claim the borrower address, and the one the business calls authoritative loses every night to a database it has already decommissioned. Data maintenance means keeping information accurate and current across its life, and no correction is durable while a stale source holds write authority over the field. Naming one authoritative source and cutting the feed (A) removes the mechanism.
When two systems write the same field, settle the authority before you clean the values.
questionsV2.recallLine: A nightly feed from a retired origination database keeps overwriting corrected borrower addresses. Which data maintenance action MOST directly ends the recurrence?

optionsShort.A: Make the servicing platform the sole authoritative source
optionsShort.B: Reconcile the two systems every month
optionsShort.C: Validate address format at the point of entry
optionsShort.D: Bulk-update the 900 affected borrower records

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Finds the divergence a month late and queues corrections the next overnight run undoes. Detective, over a live fault.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Improves what agents type. These addresses were never malformed, only replaced by a system that knew no better.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Repairs the 900 records and leaves the loop intact. The postal file cannot know which value is the newer one.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SI-18 Personally Identifiable Information Quality Operations
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PM-22 Personally Identifiable Information Quality Management
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.4.4 Data maintenance

questionsV2.question: Ashgrove Utilities runs a smart-meter program. Its meter-reading table is classified Internal: half-hourly consumption per meter, carrying no names. Its customer master is classified Confidential. An analytics team joins the two into a new table so it can model tariff take-up, and asks the data governance board to classify the joined table Internal on the grounds that it adds no field the utility did not already hold. The board must rule before the table is provisioned. Which principle should MOST influence the level the board assigns?

options.A: Originator control: each source owner's label continues to govern its own columns.
options.B: Data minimization: the join should be labeled after unnecessary fields are removed.
options.C: Aggregation: combined data may warrant a higher level than any contributing source.
options.D: Least privilege: the label should match what the analytics team needs to read.

questionsV2.explanation:
Joining a consumption series to a customer master turns half-hourly readings that identified nobody into a behavioral record of a named household: occupancy, working hours, when the shower runs. That is a different order of harm from either input on its own, and aggregation (C) is the principle that names it. The Confidential source also sets a floor the product cannot sit beneath.
Classify what the combination reveals.
questionsV2.recallLine: A utility joins Internal meter readings to a Confidential customer master. Which principle should MOST influence the level the governance board assigns the joined table?

optionsShort.A: Originator control keeps each source owner's label
optionsShort.B: Minimize the fields before labeling the join
optionsShort.C: Combined data may warrant a higher level
optionsShort.D: Fit the label to the team's access

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Real doctrine. Originator control governs release and onward sharing, not the single label one table must carry.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Sound practice, and the team should drop fields it does not need. It says nothing about what to call the rest.

D.label: true of a different thing
D.wouldAnswer: Confuses classification with authorization. The label states the harm; access is then granted against the label.

sources: NIST SP 800-122 | Section 3.2 PII confidentiality impact levels, including aggregation
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | RA-2 Security Categorization
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.5.12 Classification of information

questionsV2.question: Pennistone Rail is categorizing the 40 systems inside its signaling enclave. One is a bastion host: it stores no operational data and runs no application, and its disk holds an operating system and an SSH daemon. Every engineer who changes a signaling controller works through it. The infrastructure team proposes categorizing it Low, because losing it would cost a rebuild and nothing else. Which consideration should MOST influence the categorization the security architect assigns to the bastion host?

options.A: The volume of authentication data the host writes into its local log files.
options.B: The sensitivity of the signaling controllers an attacker could reach through the host.
options.C: The replacement cost and rebuild time if the bastion host itself were destroyed.
options.D: The number of engineers who hold interactive privileged accounts on the host.

questionsV2.explanation:
A categorization that reads only what an asset holds misses what it commands. Every change to a signaling controller passes through this host, so whoever owns it owns the administrative path into systems whose failure stops trains. The impact of compromising the bastion is the impact of compromising them (B).
FIPS 199 sets a system's category at the high-water mark of what it supports, and NIST SP 800-60 applies that to the function a component serves, not to the bytes on its disk.
Categorize an administrative asset by what it can reach.
questionsV2.recallLine: A bastion host stores no data but fronts every change to rail signaling controllers. Which consideration should MOST influence its security categorization?

optionsShort.A: Volume of authentication data in local logs
optionsShort.B: Sensitivity of the controllers reachable behind it
optionsShort.C: Cost and time to rebuild the host
optionsShort.D: Number of engineers with privileged accounts

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: A genuine input. Log volume sizes the retention, and the logs exist because of the host's role.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: The availability half, and the team is right that the rebuild is cheap. Silent on confidentiality and integrity.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Measures the population that can use the host, which drives recertification effort once the level is set.

sources: FIPS 199 | High-water mark for system security categorization
NIST SP 800-60 Vol 1 Rev 1 | Section 3.3 Assigning a system security category
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.1.2 Asset classification

questionsV2.question: Marlin Ridge Credit Union has agreed to pilot a fraud-scoring service. The vendor needs two years of member transaction history, classified Confidential, copied into its own cloud tenant; the master services agreement already carries a data processing addendum. The information security manager read the vendor's SOC 2 report, judged the controls adequate, and signed a release authorizing the extract, and the pilot began on Monday. At the quarterly governance meeting the internal auditor raises the release. Which is the PRIMARY reason the auditor is right to raise it?

options.A: A SOC 2 report evidences vendor controls but does not substitute for due diligence.
options.B: The vendor tenant holding the extract does not appear in the credit union's register.
options.C: Two years of transaction history exceeds what the fraud-scoring pilot needs to run.
options.D: Release of the member data was the data owner's decision, not the security manager's.

questionsV2.explanation:
Accountability for an information asset sits with its owner, and putting a copy of it beyond the institution's control is the plainest exercise of that accountability there is. Security advises on whether a recipient's controls are adequate. The owner decides whether the business will carry the exposure at all. Here the release was signed by the wrong role (D), so nobody who bears the loss ever agreed to it, and that defect stands whatever the evidence pack contained.
Ask who owns the asset before you ask how good the recipient is.
questionsV2.recallLine: A security manager signed the release sending two years of member transactions to a fraud-scoring vendor. What is the PRIMARY reason an auditor should challenge it?

optionsShort.A: A SOC 2 report is not due diligence
optionsShort.B: Vendor tenant absent from the asset register
optionsShort.C: Extract exceeds what the pilot needs
optionsShort.D: The data owner should have decided

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Fair criticism of the evidence. Reading a SOC 2 report is not the same as running third-party due diligence.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: A real register gap, and a bookkeeping consequence of a decision taken outside the process.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: A minimization finding worth raising. It argues over the size of a transfer nobody authorized.

sources: NIST SP 800-18 Rev 1 | Section 2.2 Information Owner responsibilities, retained when data are shared
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.5.9 Inventory of information and other associated assets, including ownership
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 2.3.1 Information and asset ownership

questionsV2.question: Balfern Housing Trust records every laptop, server and virtual machine in its configuration management database and reconciles it monthly. It records nothing about the 140 software-as-a-service tenancies the trust pays for. In March a tenancy-inspection application lapsed because the department that bought it had been reorganized and no renewal was raised; the vendor purged the tenant after 30 days and 4,000 inspection reports went with it. The IT director wants one change to the asset process. Which change MOST directly prevents a repeat?

options.A: Extend discovery scanning so the CMDB records every endpoint and virtual machine agentlessly.
options.B: Record each hosted tenancy as an asset with a named owner and renewal date.
options.C: Deploy a cloud access security broker so shadow applications appear in the register.
options.D: Route every recurring software invoice through the asset team before finance pays it.

questionsV2.explanation:
An asset register that stops at hardware and virtual machines describes the estate the trust can touch, and not the estate it depends on. A hosted tenancy is an intangible asset: it holds records, it has a lifecycle, and it dies on a renewal date. Recording each one with a named owner and that date (B) treats it as the asset it is.
What failed here was stewardship. The subscription was known, invoiced and paid, and it lapsed because a reorganization left nobody answerable for it.
Inventory what you cannot see as carefully as what you can trip over.
questionsV2.recallLine: A housing trust inventories hardware but not its 140 hosted tenancies, and lost 4,000 reports when one lapsed. Which change MOST directly prevents a repeat?

optionsShort.A: Extend discovery scanning across endpoints and virtual machines
optionsShort.B: Register each subscription with owner and renewal date
optionsShort.C: Deploy a broker to surface shadow applications
optionsShort.D: Route recurring software invoices through the asset team

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Widens discovery across the class the CMDB already covers. The 140 tenancies have no agent and no address.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Aimed at applications the trust does not know about. This one was procured, approved and budgeted.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Catches the money. A payment record names a cost center, and nobody in finance answers for the reports.

questionsV2.question: Redmayne Consulting issues a laptop to every consultant and records its serial number against that person in the asset system. An audit covering two years finds 61 laptops still assigned to people who have left, 14 of them holding client engagement files. Leavers surrender their building pass to reception and the service desk disables their accounts on the last day, but neither step consults the asset system. Which change to asset management MOST directly closes the gap?

options.A: Tie the asset system to the leaver workflow so device return is a mandatory step.
options.B: Encrypt every laptop at rest so a device retained by a leaver stays unreadable.
options.C: Run a quarterly report comparing asset assignments against the active employee directory.
options.D: Ask consultants to confirm annually that they still hold the device assigned to them.

questionsV2.explanation:
The asset system already knows who holds which laptop, and nothing in the departure process ever asks it. Asset management is the discipline that keeps a recorded custodian true through every change of hands, and departure is the change most likely to go unrecorded, because the person holding the device has no further reason to appear. Tying the asset system to the leaver workflow (A) puts the check at the one moment the firm still has both leverage and attention.
Attach the asset record to the event that moves the asset.
questionsV2.recallLine: Sixty-one laptops remain assigned to consultants who have left, because leaver offboarding ignores the asset system. Which asset management change MOST directly closes the gap?

optionsShort.A: Make device return a required leaver workflow step
optionsShort.B: Encrypt laptops so retained devices stay unreadable
optionsShort.C: Quarterly report of assignments against active employees
optionsShort.D: Annual self-attestation that consultants still hold devices

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Worth doing on its own merits, and it blunts the consequence. A device nobody can account for is still off the books.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Finds the drift up to three months late, when the machine is unrecoverable. It measures the failure.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Asks the population least likely to reply, on a cycle slower than the quarterly report it would displace.

questionsV2.question: Stanmoor Dental Group, a UK chain of 90 practices, uses a hosted appointment-reminder service. The contract instructs the supplier to send reminders and to delete each record 30 days after the appointment. At a renewal review the supplier's engineers explain that they also keep the reminder data for two years to train a no-show prediction model they license to other dental groups. Stanmoor was not told, receives nothing from the model, and its contract permits no such use. Which characterization of the supplier's role for that training is MOST accurate?

options.A: The supplier remains a processor, because Stanmoor still decides why the reminders are sent.
options.B: The supplier acts as a controller for the model training, having chosen that purpose itself.
options.C: Stanmoor and the supplier are joint controllers, having jointly determined purposes and means.
options.D: The supplier remains a processor but has breached the contractual retention instruction.

questionsV2.explanation:
Whoever determines the purpose of a processing operation is its controller for that operation, and nobody at Stanmoor chose to build a commercial prediction model. The supplier picked the purpose, picked the means, set its own retention period and sells the result. For the training it is a controller in its own right (B), while it remains a processor for the reminders, one acting outside instruction.
Read the purpose, not the plumbing, when you assign a data role.
questionsV2.recallLine: A reminder supplier keeps client records beyond its instruction to train a model it licenses elsewhere. Which characterization of its role for that training is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: A processor, since the customer sets purposes
optionsShort.B: A controller for the training it chose
optionsShort.C: Joint controllers, purposes and means settled together
optionsShort.D: A processor that breached the retention instruction

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Holds for the reminder messages themselves, and would be the whole answer had the supplier stopped there.

C.label: true of a different thing
C.wouldAnswer: Needs both parties to have settled purposes and means together. Stanmoor was not told and agreed to nothing.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Names the visible contract failure and stops there. The retention breach follows from a purpose the supplier adopted.

questionsV2.question: Ferrymead Broadband holds installation addresses, fault histories and payment dates for 400,000 subscribers, and its privacy notice says these are kept to provide and bill for the service. A data science team now wants the same records to train a churn model that will drive retention offers. Nothing further would be collected and the records would not leave the company. The privacy lead must advise the steering group before the project is approved. Which requirement should she raise FIRST?

options.A: Pseudonymize the subscriber identifiers before the training set is extracted from billing.
options.B: Assess whether retention modeling is compatible with the purpose the subscribers were given.
options.C: Restrict access to the training set to the data science team's service accounts.
options.D: Add the training set to the records schedule with a defined disposal date.

questionsV2.explanation:
Personal data gathered for one purpose does not become available for another because it stays inside the building. Purpose limitation binds the use, and a retention-marketing model is a different purpose from providing and billing for broadband, however convenient the records are. Until compatibility has been judged, or another lawful basis secured and the subscribers told, every downstream design choice serves a project that may not be permitted to exist. Assessing that compatibility (B) comes first.
Settle whether the use is allowed before engineering how it will be done safely.
questionsV2.recallLine: A broadband provider wants to train a churn model on records collected to provide and bill for service. Which requirement should the privacy lead raise FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Pseudonymize identifiers before extracting the training set
optionsShort.B: Test the new use against the stated purpose
optionsShort.C: Restrict training-set access to service accounts
optionsShort.D: Give the training set a disposal date

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: A real safeguard. Pseudonymized personal data stays personal data while the company holds the key.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Sound access control over an artifact whose legitimacy is unsettled. Restricting readers does not permit it.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Proper lifecycle hygiene. A schedule governs how long you may keep what you were entitled to create.

questionsV2.question: Norvane Provincial Health Authority must keep resident health records inside the province and must be able to demonstrate that no foreign authority can compel their disclosure. Its chosen analytics platform is a hyperscaler service. The authority has selected the provider's in-province region, and the provider encrypts every volume at rest using keys held in its own managed key service, which also runs in-province. The provider is incorporated abroad. Which measure BEST satisfies the second requirement?

options.A: Add a contractual undertaking that the provider will resist and notify foreign disclosure orders.
options.B: Enable the provider's customer-managed key option, with key material generated in-province.
options.C: Replicate the encrypted volumes to a second in-province region operated by the same provider.
options.D: Hold the encryption keys in a hardware security module the authority alone operates.

questionsV2.explanation:
The requirement is not where the bytes sit. It is who can be ordered to turn them into plaintext. A provider incorporated abroad can be served an order in its home jurisdiction, and the question becomes whether it retains the technical means to comply. Keys held in a module the authority alone operates (D) give the platform a wrapped, revocable path to them, so the provider holds ciphertext and answers an order by inability.
Residency answers where the data is. Key custody answers who can be made to open it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A provincial health authority must show that no foreign authority can compel disclosure of records held on a foreign-owned cloud. Which measure BEST satisfies that?

optionsShort.A: Contract to resist and notify disclosure orders
optionsShort.B: Customer-managed keys inside the provider's key service
optionsShort.C: Replicate to a second in-province region
optionsShort.D: Keys in a module the authority operates

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: Worth having. A contract binds the provider to the authority and binds no court, and notice comes after the fact.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: A genuine improvement, and the key material still lives in the provider's key service. It can still decrypt.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Addresses durability and regional availability. Compellability is exactly where it was, now with a second copy.

questionsV2.question: Ostley Recruitment operates in two markets. In one, an employment regulator requires interview notes and scoring sheets to be kept for six years so that discrimination complaints can be tested. In the other, a privacy regulator requires unsuccessful candidates' data to be erased within twelve months unless the candidate consents to a talent pool. The records manager applies a single six-year rule to every applicant record in one shared system. Which change to the retention approach is BEST?

options.A: Set the period per record class and market, and segregate the records accordingly.
options.B: Apply the twelve-month rule to every applicant record, as the more restrictive period.
options.C: Keep the six-year rule and ask every candidate to consent to a talent pool.
options.D: Move all applicant records to the six-year market's system and apply its schedule.

questionsV2.explanation:
Two obligations bind two different populations, and one number cannot be right for both. A retention schedule works at the level of a record class: what the record is, whose it is, and which regime reaches it. Splitting applicant records by market (A) gives each class the period its own regulator names, with disposal automated against the class.
Where two schedules collide, subdivide the records until each piece has one clock.
questionsV2.recallLine: One regulator requires interview notes kept six years, another requires erasure within twelve months. Which retention approach is BEST for a recruiter subject to both?

optionsShort.A: Set periods per record class and market
optionsShort.B: Apply the shorter twelve-month period everywhere
optionsShort.C: Seek talent-pool consent and keep six years
optionsShort.D: Consolidate onto the six-year market's system

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: The reflex of taking the shortest period. It destroys the scoring sheets the employment regulator expects to see.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: The privacy regulator's own carve-out, and it should be offered. Consent is the candidate's to refuse and withdraw.

D.label: true of a different thing
D.wouldAnswer: Changes the address of the data without changing the candidate. The privacy regulator's claim follows the person.

NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SI-12 Information Management and Retention

questionsV2.question: Whitcombe Legal Services agreed with a corporate client that all case data would be destroyed within 60 days of the matter closing, under a signed certificate naming what was destroyed. The matter closed in April. The document system holds the master set; nightly backups hold copies on a fixed 35-day rotation; and a partner exported a working extract to a departmental file share at some point during the matter, which nobody logged. Which factor presents the GREATEST obstacle to issuing an accurate certificate?

options.A: The 35-day backup rotation, which retains copies beyond the agreed destruction date.
options.B: The absence of a cryptographic erase capability in the document system's storage.
options.C: The unlogged departmental extract, whose existence and contents nobody has established.
options.D: The 60-day window, which is shorter than the firm's standard disposal cadence.

questionsV2.explanation:
A destruction certificate is a statement about a population, and this population has a member the firm cannot describe. Backups that rotate on a published cycle can be bounded and disclosed: the client is told the last copy expires on a named date under unchanged access controls, and most destruction clauses accept exactly that. An export nobody recorded cannot be described at all. Whitcombe does not know how many documents it holds, who has read it since, or whether it was copied onward, which makes the unlogged extract (C) the obstacle. Signing over a set you have not enumerated is the failure; the delay is not.
Enumerate the copies before you certify anything about them.
questionsV2.recallLine: A law firm must certify destruction of client case data held in a document system, rotating backups and an unlogged export. Which factor is the GREATEST obstacle?

optionsShort.A: Backups rotating past the agreed destruction date
optionsShort.B: No cryptographic erase in the document storage
optionsShort.C: An export nobody has enumerated
optionsShort.D: A sixty-day window shorter than normal disposal

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: A real constraint that needs disclosing, and probably a variation. It is arithmetic on a known process.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: A capability question. Deleting logical records discharges a contractual destruction clause perfectly well.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Inverts the problem. A tight window pressures the process without making the resulting statement untrue.

questionsV2.question: Rothsay Trust is moving a client reporting store into a managed cloud database. The store holds account balances and beneficiary details; a batch job writes it overnight and scheduled report generation reads it. The risk assessment singles out one threat: a storage administrator employed by the provider reading the tables directly. TLS 1.3 already protects every connection to the service. Which protection BEST addresses the state in which the assessed threat acts?

options.A: Transparent volume encryption at rest, managed by the provider's own storage service.
options.B: A confidential-computing enclave so the batch job's working memory stays opaque.
options.C: Application-layer encryption of the sensitive columns, with keys held outside the provider.
options.D: Database activity monitoring alerting on direct reads of the beneficiary tables.

questionsV2.explanation:
The named threat is a person with legitimate access to the stored copy, so the state at issue is data at rest, and the test of any control is whether it denies plaintext to somebody the platform already trusts. Encrypting the sensitive columns before they are written, with key custody outside the provider (C), leaves that administrator looking at ciphertext through every path the platform offers.
Name the state the adversary reaches before comparing controls. At rest and in use call for different machinery.
questionsV2.recallLine: A cloud database holds client balances, and the assessed threat is a provider storage administrator reading the tables. Which protection BEST fits that state?

optionsShort.A: Provider-managed transparent encryption of the volumes
optionsShort.B: A confidential-computing enclave for the batch job
optionsShort.C: Encrypt columns in the application, keys held outside
optionsShort.D: Alert on direct reads of beneficiary tables

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The same state, and right for a stolen disk. The platform applies and removes it, so the engine serves plaintext.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Protects data in use, right where a hypervisor or host operator inspects live memory. Not where this adversary sits.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Finds the administrator afterwards, worth having for deterrence and evidence. The alert arrives after the read.

questionsV2.question: Braysdon Manufacturing runs its design review in a sanctioned cloud collaboration suite. Contract engineers, working on their own laptops that Braysdon does not manage, need to view drawings during review calls. Twice this quarter a contractor has copied a full drawing set to a personal machine. Braysdon will not issue managed laptops for a six-week engagement, and cutting contractor access off would stop the reviews. Which control BEST meets both constraints?

options.A: A cloud access security broker in reverse proxy mode, blocking download to unmanaged devices.
options.B: Endpoint data loss prevention agents on the contractors' laptops, blocking local file writes.
options.C: Rights management on each drawing, with licenses the firm can revoke after review.
options.D: Conditional access requiring device compliance before the collaboration suite grants a session.

questionsV2.explanation:
Both constraints are constraints on where a control can live. Braysdon governs the service and not the laptops, so the only place it can interpose is the session between the two. A broker sitting in the authenticated flow to the sanctioned suite sees that the device is unmanaged, lets the drawing render, and denies the file transfer, with nothing installed on the contractor's machine (A).
Put the control where you hold authority. For somebody else's endpoint, that is the session.
questionsV2.recallLine: A manufacturer must let contractors on unmanaged laptops view drawings in a sanctioned cloud suite while stopping downloads. Which control BEST achieves that?

optionsShort.A: Broker in reverse proxy blocking unmanaged downloads
optionsShort.B: Endpoint DLP agents on the contractors' laptops
optionsShort.C: Revocable rights management licenses on each drawing
optionsShort.D: Require device compliance before granting a session

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: The textbook answer where the endpoints are yours. These belong to the contractors, so nothing can be installed.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Protects a drawing after it has moved. The requirement here is that the full set stops leaving in the first place.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Enforces posture properly, and an unmanaged device fails the check and receives nothing. The reviews stop.

domains.title: Security Architecture & Engineering
domains.caseStudy:
Domain 3 is how secure systems are designed: security models, trusted computing, cryptography and its lifecycle, and the physical protections around the hardware. It is the most technical domain, and the one where ATM hardware makes the abstractions concrete.

Case Study: The "Phantom Key" Hardware Shim Attack

### Context

Nexus Bank launched a fleet of compact "SlimLine" ATMs for subway stations. The design is modular: a PC core running Windows 10 IoT talks to the cash dispenser and to the encrypting PIN pad (EPP) over standard USB cables. The service panel opens with a standard key. The EPP ships with a legacy compatibility mode that sends the first 50 milliseconds of each keystroke burst in plaintext before switching to encrypted mode, and the mode is on by default.

### What went wrong

A transnational gang built a small USB interceptor, a hardware shim, and installed it in seconds behind a service panel opened with a stolen key. Sitting between the EPP and the PC core, the shim captured the plaintext burst of every PIN. It also spoke directly to the dispenser, sending dispense commands that never touched the PC, its operating system, or its security software.

Two things made this work. The PIN left the tamper-resistant device in clear, so the cryptographic boundary the EPP exists to provide was broken by a configuration switch. And the dispenser accepted commands from anything on the bus, because it had no way to authenticate the controller it was supposed to be talking to. Nothing in the boot chain, no Secure Boot or TPM measurement, noticed unfamiliar hardware.

This is the black box attack the white paper describes: the attacker bypasses the PC core entirely, connects a device (a laptop, a phone, or a Raspberry Pi) to the dispenser, and issues native commands. Because the PC is out of the loop, whitelisting, antivirus and host authorization never fire, and the software logs stay clean. The paper adds the physical precondition: standardized top-hat keys can be bought online, so the cabinet lock is often the whole defense.

### What a practitioner does differently

Draw the trust boundary where the standards draw it. PCI PTS POI certification exists so the PIN is encrypted inside the EPP and never leaves it in clear; a legacy plaintext mode should be disabled at commissioning, and better, absent from the product. Keys move under TR-31 and TR-34 key-block rules, which the white paper notes had a compliance deadline of 1 January 2025.

Treat the peripheral bus as a network. The dispenser should authenticate the PC core before it dispenses; the white paper lists secure peripheral communication and dispenser-level protections (image bonding, high-level dispenser settings) as the controls that answer black box attacks, and rates them High against that vector. Measured boot with a TPM lets the platform refuse to run when the hardware inventory changes.

Then the physical layer: unique or electronic locks on the top hat, a key management policy with named custodians, and a tamper alarm on the service panel that raises a ticket the moment it opens outside a scheduled visit.

### Outcome

Nexus pulled the legacy mode from the fleet by configuration push, replaced the service-panel locks, and added dispenser authentication in the next firmware. The PINs captured before detection forced card reissue on every account that had used a SlimLine unit in the exposure window.

### What the exam tests

Scenario questions here go to security models and where the trusted computing base ends: a dispenser that obeys any device on the bus is an integrity failure in the Biba sense, and the PIN path is a trusted path that was broken by a default. Expect questions on fail-safe defaults, on the roles of TPM, HSM and Secure Boot, on the cryptographic lifecycle (why key blocks matter), and on physical security as part of engineering instead of a separate discipline.

### Related reading

The bank in this scenario is a composite. The attack and the controls are documented in:

- [Technical Risks and Attack Vectors Targeting ATMs](https://portfolio.atmavailability.com/atm-technical-risks-white-paper.pdf), the sections on black box attacks, on peripheral security, and on compliance and standards (PCI PTS POI, TR-31/TR-34).
- [ATM Security Capability Maturity Worksheet](https://portfolio.atmavailability.com/atm-capability-maturity-worksheet.pdf), Domain 1 (physical) and Domain 2 (logical) controls.
- [ATM research on ATM Availability](https://portfolio.atmavailability.com/atm-research/), including the 3D model of what sits behind the fascia.

questions.question: During a post-incident review of the SlimLine shim attack, Nexus Bank's engineers confirm that the cash dispenser executed 'Dispense' commands received from an unauthenticated device on the internal USB bus. Which design change would MOST directly address this failure?

options.A: Require the dispenser and the PC core to establish a mutually authenticated, encrypted session before commands are accepted.
options.B: Deploy application allow-listing on the Windows core so unauthorized executables are unable to run.
options.C: Install a firewall between the ATM and the bank host to filter suspicious dispense traffic.
options.D: Fit tamper-evident seals to every service panel so that any future shim installation is discovered during scheduled servicing.

questions.explanation: The dispenser obeyed any device on the bus because nothing required the sender to prove its identity, so the fix must make the dispenser verify its controller. A does exactly that: with mutual authentication and session encryption, a future interposer can neither read PIN traffic nor issue commands the dispenser will accept. Option B is a real hardening step but the right control for the wrong problem. The shim never executed code on Windows, so allow-listing would never engage; it wins when the threat is malware dropped onto the core. C guards the wrong boundary: the attack lived entirely on the internal USB link and never crossed the external network a firewall inspects. Option D is detective where a preventive control is asked for. Seals reveal the intrusion at the next inspection, after the cash is gone; they are the right answer for detecting panel entry, not for stopping command injection. Physical presence on a bus must never be treated as authorization; peripherals should authenticate their controller.

questions.question: Nexus Bank's architects must decide where customer PINs will be encrypted, so that even an attacker with full control of the ATM's Windows core can never observe a key or a cleartext PIN. Which placement BEST meets this requirement?

options.A: Store the keys inside a TPM on the motherboard and let the operating system perform the PIN encryption.
options.B: Encrypt PINs with a software library on the core, keeping the keys obfuscated inside the application binary.
options.C: Perform encryption inside the PIN pad's dedicated hardware security module, so keys and cleartext never reach the core.
options.D: Hold the keys on a self-encrypting drive that unlocks automatically once the ATM boots successfully.

questions.explanation: Because the requirement assumes the core itself is compromised, the encryption must happen before data ever touches the core, inside a tamper-resistant boundary that performs the cryptography and refuses to export its keys. That is precisely what an HSM-class PIN pad (C) provides. A fails because a TPM protects keys at rest, but the encryption operation would still run in the operating system, exposing the cleartext PIN and the working key in host memory; a TPM is the right answer for sealing disk or boot secrets to platform state. Option B is security through obscurity: obfuscated keys in a binary can be extracted by anyone who owns the OS. D protects stored data on the drive, and its automatic unlock at boot means a running, compromised system reads everything. A SED answers media theft, not runtime compromise. If the host is untrusted, the cryptography must live in hardware the host cannot see into.

questions.question: An analyst is mapping the shim incident to a formal security model: a low-integrity, unauthorized device successfully wrote 'Dispense' commands to the high-integrity dispenser. Which model MOST directly describes the rule that was violated?

options.A: Bell-LaPadula, whose simple security property forbids reading data at a higher classification.
options.B: Biba, whose star integrity axiom forbids a subject writing up to higher-integrity objects.
options.C: Brewer-Nash, which partitions access to prevent conflicts of interest between clients.
options.D: Clark-Wilson, which channels every change through certified well-formed transactions enforcing separation of duties.

questions.explanation: The violated rule concerns the integrity of a trusted component accepting input from an untrusted one: a low-integrity subject writing to a high-integrity object, which is exactly what Biba's *-integrity axiom ('no write up') prohibits. A addresses confidentiality, not integrity. Bell-LaPadula's rules govern who may read secrets, and nothing was read up here; it is the right model when the concern is disclosure of classified data. C solves a different problem entirely, dynamically walling off datasets so one consultant cannot serve competing clients. Option D is the strongest distractor because Clark-Wilson is also an integrity model, but it describes integrity through certified transformation procedures and separation of duties, not a lattice rule about write direction; it would be the right answer if the question asked how to constrain balance updates to certified application code. When the fault is 'untrusted wrote to trusted', name Biba; when changes bypassed certified procedures, name Clark-Wilson.
