options.C: Remote wipe, letting the fleet console erase any unit reported stolen in the field.
options.D: Fail-safe defaults, forcing the device into a locked state whenever power is removed.

questionsV2.explanation:
A tamper-responding module that detects enclosure breach and erases its keys is performing zeroization, the FIPS 140-3 Level 3 behavior. What it saves is the key material, which would otherwise let the thieves decrypt PIN traffic or impersonate the device fleet-wide (A).
For hardware holding keys, plan on the device being taken. Tamper-triggered zeroization is what makes physical theft yield a worthless brick.
questionsV2.recallLine: Thieves carried off a pad, but the module erased its key material before extraction finished. Which capability acted, and which risk did it MOST reduce?

optionsShort.A: Zeroization on tamper, denying thieves the keys
optionsShort.B: Full-disk encryption keeping stored records unreadable
optionsShort.C: Remote wipe of a unit reported stolen
optionsShort.D: Fail-safe defaults locking the device on power loss

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: A different asset by a different means. Disk encryption erases nothing, and an EPP's crown jewels are its live keys.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Needs what a ripped-out module lacks: connectivity, and someone noticing in time. Remote wipe suits managed devices that stay reachable.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Describes defaulting to a safe state on failure, a passive posture. The EPP detected an attack and destroyed its secrets.

questionsV2.question: Which factor MOST determines how long the offline recovery attempt needs before it succeeds?

options.A: The effective key space of the encryption algorithm protecting the blocks.
options.B: The account lockout threshold configured at the card issuer's host.
options.C: The entropy of the four-digit PIN values the customers selected.
options.D: The collision resistance of the hash function used by the terminals.

questionsV2.explanation:
Exhaustive key search runs at the attacker's own pace against captured ciphertext. Its duration follows how many keys must be tried, the effective key space (A). That is why 56-bit DES falls in hours while 128-bit AES stays beyond feasible computation.
For any brute-force question, fix what is being enumerated and where. Offline key search answers only to key space, and no online control touches it.
questionsV2.recallLine: Thieves captured encrypted PIN blocks and are trying every possible key offline. Which factor MOST determines how long that recovery attempt takes to succeed?

optionsShort.A: Effective key space of the encryption algorithm
optionsShort.B: Account lockout threshold at the issuer's host
optionsShort.C: Entropy of the customers' four-digit PINs
optionsShort.D: Collision resistance of the terminals' hash function

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: The classic online and offline confusion. Lockout thresholds throttle guesses sent to a live host, and this attacker never talks to it.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Misidentifies the search target. The thieves are trying keys. Find the key and every PIN in the batch falls at once.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Names a property the scheme does not use here. PIN blocks are reversibly encrypted for translation between hosts, and nothing hashes them.

questionsV2.question: Which security service makes that demonstration to the regulator possible after the fact?

options.A: Confidentiality, because the order traveled through an encrypted channel end to end.
options.B: Integrity, because any alteration of the order after signing would break the signature.
options.C: Authentication, because the session verified her identity when she first logged in.
options.D: Non-repudiation, because the signature is provable to a third party after the fact.

questionsV2.explanation:
The bank needs evidence that stands up in front of a regulator, against the signer's own denial. That service is non-repudiation (D). A digital signature binds the order to the sole holder of the private key, so origin cannot be plausibly disclaimed later.
Authentication convinces the counterparty now. Non-repudiation convinces a third party later. The private-key signature upgrades the first into the second.
questionsV2.recallLine: An administrator denies sending a transfer order that only her smart card's private key could have signed. Which security service lets the bank demonstrate that to a regulator?

optionsShort.A: Confidentiality from the end-to-end encrypted channel
optionsShort.B: Integrity: alteration after signing breaks verification
optionsShort.C: Authentication verified her identity at login
optionsShort.D: Non-repudiation: provable to a third party

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Orthogonal to the demonstration. Encryption hides the order from outsiders and proves nothing about who created it.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: True, and a narrower claim. The signature does prove the order was unaltered, and the administrator is denying authorship, not modification.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Session authentication is evidence between the two parties at that moment. A third party reviewing events later gets less.

questionsV2.question: Which mechanism is the MOST direct fit for two gateways agreeing a session key with no pre-shared secret?

options.A: AES in Galois/Counter Mode, negotiated through an initial handshake message.
options.B: Diffie-Hellman key agreement, preferably using ephemeral parameters per session.
options.C: A one-time pad distributed to both gateways during their initial commissioning.
options.D: Kerberos tickets issued to both gateways by the carrier's authentication server.

questionsV2.explanation:
The stem lists Diffie-Hellman's defining conditions. No pre-shared secret, an untrusted channel, and a key that is derived, never sent. Each side combines its private value with the other's public value and both arrive at the same secret (B).
Agree on a key without sending it, with no prior secret: that is Diffie-Hellman. It establishes keys; ciphers and modes consume them.
questionsV2.recallLine: Two gateways must agree a session key across an untrusted network with no pre-shared secret, and the key must never cross the wire. Which mechanism fits MOST directly?

optionsShort.A: AES-GCM negotiated in an initial handshake message
optionsShort.B: Diffie-Hellman agreement with ephemeral parameters
optionsShort.C: One-time pad distributed at commissioning
optionsShort.D: Kerberos tickets from the carrier's authentication server

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Names a cipher mode. AES in Galois/Counter Mode is what a session key is used for once it exists, not how two sides agree one.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Contradicts the stem twice. Commissioning-time distribution is pre-sharing, and the pad material must itself travel securely.

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: Outsources trust to the carrier's server. Kerberos needs every party to pre-share keys with that KDC, over infrastructure called untrusted.

questionsV2.question: Malware gained user-mode execution but the processor refused its attempts to modify kernel memory. Which mechanism was MOST directly responsible for stopping it?

options.A: Address space layout randomization concealing the kernel's memory layout from the process.
options.B: Protection rings separating privileged kernel mode from unprivileged user mode.
options.C: Application sandboxing policies applied by the kiosk's managed runtime environment.
options.D: Data execution prevention marking writable memory pages as non-executable.

questionsV2.explanation:
The CPU itself rejected privileged operations from unprivileged code. That is hardware enforcement of privilege levels, the protection-ring model, where user-mode code in ring 3 cannot execute ring 0 instructions or touch kernel structures (B).
Attribute the block to the layer that issued the refusal. A processor rejecting a privileged instruction names ring-based CPU privilege separation.
questionsV2.recallLine: Malware ran in user mode, but the processor refused its attempts to modify kernel memory. Which mechanism was MOST directly responsible for that refusal?

optionsShort.A: ASLR concealing the kernel's memory layout
optionsShort.B: Protection rings separating kernel from user mode
optionsShort.C: Sandboxing policies from the managed runtime
optionsShort.D: Data execution prevention marking pages non-executable

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Protects by hiding. ASLR makes kernel addresses hard to find, and a process that guesses right is still stopped by the privilege check.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: A software policy layered far above the CPU. A sandbox escape leaves ring enforcement as the surviving barrier, which the stem describes.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Governs whether data pages may execute, which blocks injected shellcode. Here the malware was already executing and failed on privilege.

questionsV2.question: The design must conceal even the existence of the covert rows. Which database technique MOST directly addresses this?

options.A: Views restricting each role to approved subsets of columns and rows.
options.B: Row-level encryption whose keys are held by the investigation team.
options.C: Referential integrity constraints enforced across the investigation tables.
options.D: Polyinstantiation, letting rows at different classification levels share one key.

questionsV2.explanation:
This is the classic multilevel-database inference attack. A low-cleared user inserts at a key, the insert is rejected because a classified row already sits there, and the rejection leaks that something secret exists. Polyinstantiation permits two rows, one at each level, to coexist at the same key, so the low-level insert simply succeeds (D).
When the secret is that data exists, filtering and encryption are the wrong tools. Existence-hiding in multilevel databases is what polyinstantiation is for.
questionsV2.recallLine: A warehouse table holds covert investigation records that lower-clearance staff must not even learn exist. Which database technique MOST directly conceals their existence?

optionsShort.A: Views restricting each role to approved rows
optionsShort.B: Row-level encryption keyed to the investigation team
optionsShort.C: Referential integrity constraints across investigation tables
optionsShort.D: Polyinstantiation: two rows share one key

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Hides content and leaves existence exposed. A filtered view still cannot let the insert proceed at an occupied key without lying or leaking.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: The same boundary. Ciphertext in a visible row conceals values and confirms the row is there, and a key conflict still surfaces.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Works against the design goal. Integrity constraints exist to expose conflicts loudly, and that signal is exactly what has to be suppressed.

questionsV2.question: Which risk does the unsalted storage create, and which fix is MOST appropriate?

options.A: Hash collisions; migrate the console from SHA-256 to SHA-3 to restore output uniqueness.
options.B: Key reuse; issue each administrator a distinct symmetric key for encrypting credentials.
options.C: Precomputed-table cracking; add a unique random salt per password and use a slow, iterated hash.
options.D: Pass-the-hash replay; encrypt the stored hash values at rest under the console's TLS private key.

questionsV2.explanation:
Unsalted fast hashes fail exactly as the auditor observed. Identical passwords collapse to identical digests, so one rainbow table or one cracked value breaks every account sharing it. The remedy is a per-user random salt to make every digest unique, plus a deliberately slow function such as PBKDF2, bcrypt, scrypt or Argon2 to price out bulk guessing (C).
Stored passwords take two words: salted and slow. Uniqueness defeats precomputation, cost defeats scale.
questionsV2.recallLine: The console stores administrator passwords as unsalted SHA-256 hashes, and two admins with the same password share a digest. Which risk follows, and what fix is MOST appropriate?

optionsShort.A: Hash collisions; migrate from SHA-256 to SHA-3
optionsShort.B: Key reuse; give each admin a symmetric key
optionsShort.C: Precomputed-table cracking; add per-password salt, slow hash
optionsShort.D: Pass-the-hash replay; encrypt stored hashes at rest

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Picks the scariest-sounding word. A collision is two different inputs hashing alike; these are identical inputs, and SHA-3 would too.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Applies key-management vocabulary to a storage problem. Password verification needs no per-admin keys, and wrapping hashes moves the secret.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Borrows a Windows lateral-movement attack about authenticating with a stolen hash. A key held on the same host protects little.

questionsV2.question: Which change MOST directly corrects the weakness of encrypting every record under one fixed initialization vector?

options.A: Move the routine to a longer key so the cipher is more resistant to brute force.
options.B: Compress each record before encryption so repeated plaintext patterns are reduced.
options.C: Generate a fresh, unpredictable initialization vector for every record encrypted.
options.D: Append a keyed hash to each record so any later modification becomes detectable.

questionsV2.explanation:
An initialization vector exists to randomize the first block so equal plaintexts encrypt to unequal ciphertexts. A fixed IV in CBC restores the pattern leakage the mode was built to remove. The direct fix is a fresh, unpredictable IV for every record (C).
Name the cryptographic service that actually failed, here confidentiality of patterns, and fix that parameter.
questionsV2.recallLine: Every log record is encrypted in CBC mode under one fixed IV, so identical entries produce identical ciphertext. Which change MOST directly corrects that weakness?

optionsShort.A: Longer key for more brute-force resistance
optionsShort.B: Compress records before encryption to reduce repeats
optionsShort.C: Fresh unpredictable initialization vector per record
optionsShort.D: Keyed hash appended so modification becomes detectable

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Strengthens a dimension that was never weak. Key length governs resistance to key search, and hides no two matching ciphertexts.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Masks the symptom. Compression makes repeats less likely and deterministic encryption stays deterministic. It also leaks plaintext length.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Adds integrity, a different service. A keyed hash proves records were unaltered and never stops an observer correlating identical entries.

questionsV2.question: Which platform protection MOST directly defeats executing shellcode from a data buffer?

options.A: Address space layout randomization, hiding the buffer's location from the exploit.
options.B: Data execution prevention, marking data pages in memory as non-executable.
options.C: Full-disk encryption, protecting the driver binary from tampering at rest.
options.D: Stack canaries, detecting corruption of saved return addresses before they are used.

questionsV2.explanation:
The essential step is executing instructions out of a memory region that holds data. Non-executable page protection refuses precisely that: control transfers into the buffer, the processor faults, and the shellcode never runs, however the redirect was achieved (B).
Map the mitigation to the exploit step it interrupts. Data execution prevention (DEP) kills execute-from-data; ASLR and canaries harass the steps that lead there.
questionsV2.recallLine: Exploit developers have shown shellcode placed in a driver's data buffer and then executed. Which platform protection MOST directly defeats that step?

optionsShort.A: ASLR hiding the buffer's location from the exploit
optionsShort.B: Data execution prevention marking data pages non-executable
optionsShort.C: Full-disk encryption protecting the driver binary at rest
optionsShort.D: Stack canaries detecting corrupted saved return addresses

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: A genuine obstacle aimed at a different step, and a probabilistic one. Once a leak or a spray recovers the address, the page still executes.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Protects the wrong copy at the wrong time. The binary on disk was never modified; the corruption happens in live memory.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Watches one specific structure. Overwrite a function pointer, or use a heap buffer, and no canary is disturbed.

questionsV2.question: Which property is missing from the proprietary cipher, and why does its absence matter MOST?

options.A: Collision resistance; two distinct inputs could be found that produce the same output.
options.B: The avalanche effect; localized changes let analysts map ciphertext structure back to plaintext.
options.C: Forward secrecy; a stolen long-term key would expose previously recorded traffic.
options.D: Key-generation entropy; predictable keys would narrow an attacker's search space.

questionsV2.explanation:
A strong cipher shows the avalanche effect: a one-bit input change flips roughly half the output bits. That is the visible evidence of diffusion. When a change stays localized, ciphertext regions correspond to plaintext regions, so an analyst recovers structure, spots repeated fields and mounts statistical attacks without the key (B).
Diffusion failures show up exactly this way in testing. Treat a missing avalanche as proof the cipher leaks structure, and reject it.
questionsV2.recallLine: Flipping one plaintext bit changes only the corresponding ciphertext byte in a vendor's proprietary cipher. Which property is missing, and why does its absence matter MOST?

optionsShort.A: Collision resistance; distinct inputs share one output
optionsShort.B: Avalanche effect; localized change exposes plaintext structure
optionsShort.C: Forward secrecy; stolen long-term key exposes recordings
optionsShort.D: Key-generation entropy; predictable keys narrow the search

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Imports a hash-function requirement. Collision resistance matters where distinct inputs must never share an output, as in signatures.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Concerns key-management architecture, not cipher internals. No block cipher supplies forward secrecy on its own.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: A real and fatal weakness when present. This test held the key fixed and varied the plaintext, so what it measured was mixing.

questionsV2.question: Which security model BEST fits the requirement that access history dynamically bars a consultant from the competitor's files?

options.A: Brewer-Nash, enforcing dynamic conflict-of-interest classes over datasets.
options.B: Bell-LaPadula, enforcing hierarchical confidentiality labels and clearances.
options.C: Clark-Wilson, enforcing well-formed transactions with separation of duties.
options.D: Biba, preventing lower-integrity information from contaminating higher levels.

questionsV2.explanation:
Permissions here change as a consequence of the subject's own past reads: touch one competitor's data and the other's walls off. That history-dependent, conflict-of-interest behavior is what Brewer-Nash, the Chinese Wall model, was built to formalize (A).
When permissions depend on what the subject already accessed, conflict of interest and dynamic should trigger Brewer-Nash before any of the classic static models.
questionsV2.recallLine: A consultant who opens one bank's engagement files must be barred from its competitor's, on the strength of that access history. Which security model BEST fits?

optionsShort.A: Brewer-Nash: dynamic conflict-of-interest classes over datasets
optionsShort.B: Bell-LaPadula: hierarchical confidentiality labels and clearances
optionsShort.C: Clark-Wilson: well-formed transactions and duty separation
optionsShort.D: Biba: keep low-integrity data out of high

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Static by comparison. Bell-LaPadula grants access from fixed clearances and labels, however much the consultant read yesterday.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Protects how data is modified: certified procedures, duty separation, reconciliations. It has no notion of one dataset excluding another.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Governs the direction of information flow for integrity, and it never consults access history either.

questionsV2.question: Which mechanism BEST provides a guaranteed route to the genuine login screen?

options.A: A secure attention key that invokes a trusted path directly to the operating system.
options.B: A password manager configured to auto-fill on the legitimate login screen.
options.C: A login banner warning users against disclosing credentials to unofficial prompts.
options.D: An inactivity timeout that locks the kiosk session after a period of idle use.

questionsV2.explanation:
The team needs a route to the real OS that user-mode software can neither fake nor intercept. That is the secure attention key, the Ctrl+Alt+Del pattern. The keystroke is reserved by the kernel, so pressing it tears down whatever is on screen and yields the authentic secure desktop: a trusted path no fake login page survives (A).
Trusted path beats spoofed logins. Give users one reserved gesture that always reaches the kernel.
questionsV2.recallLine: Kiosk staff typed credentials into full-screen fakes. Which mechanism BEST guarantees users a route to the genuine login screen that malware cannot imitate or suppress?

optionsShort.A: Secure attention key invoking a trusted path
optionsShort.B: Password manager auto-filling the legitimate screen
optionsShort.C: Login banner warning against unofficial credential prompts
optionsShort.D: Inactivity timeout locking the idle kiosk session

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Real protection in browsers, where fill logic binds to a verified origin. A full-screen native fake is pixels with no URL to bind to.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Administrative only. A banner instructs the very users the simulation proved will comply, and the fake can display its own banner.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Limits how long a hijacked or abandoned session stays open. No help at all in telling a real login screen from a counterfeit.

questionsV2.question: Which algorithm family is MOST appropriate for the constrained device program, given the power and certificate-size limits?

options.A: RSA with 4096-bit moduli, buying the security margin of the larger key.
options.B: Triple-DES with frequent rotation, avoiding asymmetric operations altogether.
options.C: Diffie-Hellman over a 1024-bit prime group, minimizing the computation per exchange.
options.D: Elliptic-curve cryptography, matching RSA-grade security at far smaller key sizes.

questionsV2.explanation:
Elliptic-curve algorithms deliver equivalent strength to RSA at a fraction of the key length. A 256-bit curve corresponds to roughly a 3072-bit RSA modulus. That buys cheaper computation, lower power draw and compact certificates: the three constraints the stem names (D).
Constrained devices are ECC's home ground. Shrink the key and keep the strength.
questionsV2.recallLine: A battery-powered device program needs asymmetric cryptography on a tight processor budget, with certificates small enough for a slow link. Which algorithm family is MOST appropriate?

optionsShort.A: RSA with 4096-bit moduli for margin
optionsShort.B: Triple-DES rotated often, avoiding asymmetric operations
optionsShort.C: Diffie-Hellman over a 1024-bit prime group
optionsShort.D: Elliptic-curve: RSA-grade strength at smaller key sizes

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Secure, and it maximizes every cost the platform must avoid. 4096-bit private-key operations are expensive and the certificates are bulky.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Ignores a stated requirement. Symmetric schemes presuppose the shared secret, so frequent rotation leaves the bootstrap problem in place.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Economizes into known weakness. 1024-bit finite-field groups are within reach of precomputation and are deprecated by standards bodies.

questionsV2.question: Which security model MOST directly formalizes those creation, deletion and transfer rules?

options.A: Harrison-Ruzzo-Ullman, analyzing whether a given right can ever leak to an unauthorized subject.
options.B: Bell-LaPadula, constraining how information may flow between clearance levels.
options.C: Graham-Denning, defining the primitive operations for managing subjects, objects, and rights.
options.D: Sutherland, addressing inference by constraining permissible information flows.

questionsV2.explanation:
Create and delete subjects and objects; grant, transfer and revoke rights. That lifecycle is the set of eight protection rules Graham-Denning formalizes over the access-control matrix, the model about administering protection state independent of any one policy (C).
Sort the matrix models by their question. Graham-Denning says how to manipulate rights safely, HRU asks whether the rules can leak them, and the flow models stay silent on administration.
questionsV2.recallLine: The console needs formal rules for creating and deleting administrator subjects and device objects, and for granting, transferring and revoking rights. Which model MOST directly formalizes them?

optionsShort.A: Harrison-Ruzzo-Ullman: can a right ever leak
optionsShort.B: Bell-LaPadula: flow between clearance levels
optionsShort.C: Graham-Denning: primitive operations for subjects, objects, rights
optionsShort.D: Sutherland: constrain flows to prevent inference

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The close descendant and the tempting near-miss. Harrison-Ruzzo-Ullman asks whether a right can escape, and proves that undecidable.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Supplies a specific confidentiality policy with no vocabulary for creating subjects or transferring rights.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Aims at the inference problem, keeping low-level observations from revealing high-level facts. Rights administration never comes up.

questionsV2.question: Which security consequence of the local-authorization design should the risk assessment weigh MOST heavily?

options.A: Authorization logic and sensitive data become distributed across many physically exposed endpoints.
options.B: Delayed reconciliation can postpone the detection of duplicate or over-limit withdrawals.
options.C: The management platform must now scale to synchronize state with thousands of units.
options.D: Customers may experience slower transaction responses while the carrier link is down.

questionsV2.explanation:
Moving authorization to the edge relocates the crown jewels. Decision logic, approval authority and cached account data now live on thousands of machines standing unattended in public space, the least defensible tier the bank owns. Compromise one unit and you hold capabilities that used to exist only in the data center (A). That structural change is what creates the reconciliation exposure and several others besides.
When a design pushes function toward the edge, ask first what new value now sits on the most exposed devices.
questionsV2.recallLine: A redesigned field unit will authorize transactions locally during outages and reconcile later. Which security consequence should the risk assessment weigh MOST heavily?

optionsShort.A: Authorization and data spread to exposed endpoints
optionsShort.B: Delayed reconciliation postpones detecting duplicate withdrawals
optionsShort.C: Platform must scale to synchronize thousands of units
optionsShort.D: Customers see slower responses during link outages

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: The strongest competitor and a real, quantifiable exposure. It is bounded by design: stand-in limits and reconciliation windows cap it.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: A genuine engineering cost with no direct security dimension. Scalability planning belongs in the architecture review.

D.label: true of a different thing
D.wouldAnswer: Backwards on the facts. Local authorization is what keeps responses fast during outages, and customer latency is a service metric.

questionsV2.question: Under the cloud shared-responsibility model, which duty remains MOST squarely with the firm?

options.A: Testing and applying patches to the application platform and middleware serving the management console.
options.B: Hardening the host operating systems running in the vendor's data centers.
options.C: Governing its user accounts, their entitlements, and the data it places in the service.
options.D: Maintaining the hypervisor layer that isolates tenants from one another.

questionsV2.explanation:
Consuming a finished application over the network with no visibility into its stack is SaaS. The customer's retained duties compress to the two things no provider can own: who may access the tenant and with what privileges, and the classification and handling of the data placed in it (C).
Climb from IaaS to SaaS and the provider absorbs layer after layer. Identity governance and data accountability stay with the customer throughout.
questionsV2.recallLine: The firm subscribes to a vendor-hosted fleet application in which the vendor runs the servers, operating systems and code. Which duty remains MOST squarely with the firm?

optionsShort.A: Patch the application platform and middleware
optionsShort.B: Harden host operating systems in vendor data centers
optionsShort.C: Govern its accounts, entitlements and data
optionsShort.D: Maintain the tenant-isolating hypervisor layer

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: Sits on the provider's side of the SaaS line. The customer cannot see the middleware, and platform patching is its duty only at IaaS.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Fails the same test one layer lower. OS hardening belongs to the customer in IaaS; here the vendor runs the operating systems.

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: Provider territory in every service model. No tenant administers the hypervisor, which is why isolation assurance comes through audits.

questionsV2.question: Which property of a well-designed biometric system should the team cite to the regulator?

options.A: Raw scans are retained, but encrypted under keys lodged with an independent escrow agent.
options.B: Mathematical templates are stored instead of images, and the original fingerprint is not recoverable.
options.C: Fingerprint images are hashed with SHA-256 at enrollment and compared by digest thereafter.
options.D: Scans are held solely at the central host instead of on the individual ATM units.

questionsV2.explanation:
Well-designed biometric systems keep no picture. Enrollment extracts a template, a mathematical summary of minutiae features, and matching compares fresh templates against it. A stolen database then yields feature vectors and no reproducible fingerprint images, which is the assurance the regulator asked for (B).
Biometric privacy comes from storing derived, non-reversible templates. Encrypting or relocating a raw image leaves the irrevocable secret intact.
questionsV2.recallLine: Regulators want assurance about what a breach of the planned fingerprint enrollment database would expose. Which property of a well-designed biometric system should the team cite?

optionsShort.A: Raw scans kept, encrypted under escrowed keys
optionsShort.B: Templates stored instead of images, not reversible
optionsShort.C: Images hashed with SHA-256 and compared by digest
optionsShort.D: Scans held centrally and not on each unit

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Keeps the dangerous artifact and bets everything on key custody. Escrowed keys can be compelled, leaked or stolen, and full images spill.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Misapplies a password technique to fuzzy data. Two scans of one finger never match bit-for-bit, so digests of images never compare.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Changes where the images sit. They still exist, and pooling every customer's biometric in one place may raise the stakes.

questionsV2.question: Which classical concept is the engineer applying with that single enforcement component?

options.A: A security perimeter, drawing the boundary that separates the TCB from the rest of the system.
options.B: An audit subsystem, recording every access decision for later independent review.
options.C: A trusted recovery process, returning the platform to a secure state after any failure.
options.D: A reference monitor, mediating every access by subjects to objects under a defined policy.

questionsV2.explanation:
Tamper-proof, always invoked, small enough to verify. Those three are the textbook requirements of the reference monitor concept, the abstract mediator that checks every subject-to-object access against policy and gets implemented concretely as a security kernel (D).
Complete mediation by something verifiable and untamperable names the reference monitor. Everything else in the TCB supports it.
questionsV2.recallLine: Every request to reach the dispenser interface must pass one enforcement component that is tamper-proof, unbypassable and small enough to verify. Which classical concept is the engineer applying?

optionsShort.A: Security perimeter bounding the trusted computing base
optionsShort.B: Audit subsystem recording every access decision
optionsShort.C: Trusted recovery returning to a secure state
optionsShort.D: Reference monitor mediating every subject-object access

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Describes where trust ends. A perimeter delimits the TCB and mediates no individual request.

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Consumes the mediator's work. Logging decisions supports accountability and forensics, and a recorder that can be bypassed enforces nothing.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Belongs to a different phase of the lifecycle, governing how a system fails and restarts without exposing protected state.

questionsV2.question: Which approach is MOST appropriate for the bulk encryption of those logs on constrained hardware?

options.A: A symmetric block cipher such as AES, operating under the pre-provisioned shared keys.
options.B: RSA public-key encryption applied directly to each log record as it is written.
options.C: An elliptic-curve digital signature over each record to protect it from disclosure.
options.D: Hybrid encryption that wraps a freshly generated session key for every individual record.

questionsV2.explanation:
Bulk data on a weak processor calls for symmetric cryptography. AES runs orders of magnitude faster than public-key operations, often with hardware acceleration, and the stem removes the usual objection by guaranteeing secure key provisioning (A).
Asymmetric cryptography establishes trust and keys. Symmetric cryptography moves the bytes.
questionsV2.recallLine: High-volume transaction logs must be encrypted on a constrained processor, and each unit can be given its keys securely in advance. Which approach is MOST appropriate?

optionsShort.A: AES block cipher under pre-provisioned shared keys
optionsShort.B: RSA applied directly to each log record
optionsShort.C: Elliptic-curve signature over each record
optionsShort.D: Hybrid encryption wrapping a fresh key per record

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Misuses the expensive primitive. RSA is slow and encrypts only inputs smaller than its modulus, so it is kept for key transport.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Confuses two services. A signature proves origin and integrity while the record itself stays readable to anyone.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: The near-winner, since hybrid encryption is standard practice. Per-record key generation squanders the exact CPU budget the stem constrains.

questionsV2.question: Holiday photos emailed to a personal account carried fragments of a key database in their pixel data. Which technique was used, and which gateway countermeasure would MOST likely disrupt it?

options.A: Encryption; quarantine outbound messages whose attachments show abnormally high entropy.
options.B: A covert timing channel; normalize the transmission intervals of outbound messages.
options.C: Digital watermarking; strip identifying metadata from images at the mail gateway.
options.D: Steganography; recompress or transform outbound images so hidden payloads are destroyed.

questionsV2.explanation:
Hiding data inside an innocuous carrier file so the existence of the message itself stays hidden is steganography. Pixel-level payloads rarely survive lossy recompression or resizing, so transforming every outbound image breaks the channel and lets legitimate mail through (D).
Steganography defeats inspection by hiding existence. Effective countermeasures alter the carrier: recompress, resize, transcode.
questionsV2.recallLine: Holiday photos emailed to a personal account carried key-database fragments in their pixel data. Which technique was used, and which gateway countermeasure MOST likely disrupts it?

optionsShort.A: Encryption; quarantine high-entropy outbound attachments
optionsShort.B: Covert timing channel; normalize transmission intervals
optionsShort.C: Watermarking; strip image metadata at the gateway
optionsShort.D: Steganography; recompress outbound images to destroy payloads

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Misreads the evidence. Encryption announces itself as noise, and these files still displayed as valid holiday photos.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Names the wrong covert medium. Timing channels signal through when packets are sent, so interval normalization leaves the pixels untouched.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Inverts the technology. Watermarking embeds marks to assert ownership, and stripping EXIF leaves the payload woven into the image data.

questionsV2.question: Which classification fits the embedded routine, and which practice is MOST likely to catch it before release?

options.A: A worm, best caught by network anomaly detection as it propagates between systems.
options.B: Ransomware, best caught by monitoring for mass file encryption on the build servers.
options.C: A logic bomb, best caught by peer code review and change control over the build pipeline.
options.D: A rootkit, best caught by comparing shipped boot images and drivers against known-good vendor reference hashes.

questionsV2.explanation:
Malicious code that lies dormant until a condition is met, here a date tied to the author's departure, is a logic bomb. Nothing observable happens until it fires, so runtime defenses rarely see it. The realistic catch point is human and procedural: review of source changes and enforced change control expose an unexplained time-conditioned branch before it ships (C).
Insider code defeats integrity checking that trusts the source. What works is scrutiny of changes before they become the trusted baseline.
questionsV2.recallLine: A developer embedded a routine that corrupts a driver on the first business day after his contract ends. Which classification fits, and which practice MOST likely catches it pre-release?

optionsShort.A: Worm; network anomaly detection as it spreads
optionsShort.B: Ransomware; monitor build servers for mass encryption
optionsShort.C: Logic bomb; peer code review and change control
optionsShort.D: Rootkit; compare shipped images against vendor hashes

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Misclassifies on mechanism. A worm self-replicates across systems; this routine spreads only by being compiled into the product.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Pattern-matches the wrong payload. Destruction on a trigger date is sabotage, and there is no mass-encryption signal to monitor.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Fails on location. Rootkits conceal an intruder inside a running system, and this code is in the build, so the image hashes match perfectly.

questionsV2.question: Which term BEST describes an exfiltration route that uses a component never intended to carry data?

options.A: A covert channel, deliberately communicating in violation of the security policy.
options.B: A side channel, leaking secrets through unintended physical emissions of the hardware.
options.C: An out-of-band channel, an alternate interface authorized for management traffic.
options.D: A backdoor, an undocumented function granting remote administrative access.

questionsV2.explanation:
Two cooperating parties, the implanted malware sending and the nearby receiver listening, move information over a path the security policy never authorized for communication. That is a covert channel, here a storage-style channel built on an LED (A).
Classify leakage by intent. An unwitting device leaks via a side channel; a willing sender abusing an unintended path creates a covert one.
questionsV2.recallLine: Malware signaled captured card numbers to a nearby receiver by modulating the fascia status LED. Which term BEST describes that exfiltration route?

optionsShort.A: Covert channel violating the security policy deliberately
optionsShort.B: Side channel leaking through unintended physical emissions
optionsShort.C: Out-of-band channel authorized for management traffic
optionsShort.D: Backdoor granting undocumented remote administrative access

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: The near-miss that decides this. A side channel has no cooperating sender: the attacker observes leakage the device produces naturally.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Fails on authorization. Out-of-band channels such as a dedicated management network are sanctioned. This one is illicit by design.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Describes the access method an attacker might have used to plant the malware, not the route the data left by.

questionsV2.question: Which recommendation BEST reflects crime prevention through environmental design for the new sites?

options.A: Screen each ATM behind fencing and dense planting so customers enter their PINs shielded from onlookers.
options.B: Move the ATMs into interior corridors reachable only through staffed building entrances.
options.C: Rotate ATM placements every month so criminals cannot learn local traffic patterns.
options.D: Site the ATMs in open, well-lit locations with clear sightlines and steady natural foot traffic.

questionsV2.explanation:
CPTED works three levers: natural surveillance, natural access control and territorial reinforcement. Shape the environment so ordinary people's presence and sightlines make crime feel observable and risky. Open, well-lit, well-trafficked siting does that for the robber and for the skimmer installer who needs unobserved minutes at the fascia (D).
CPTED asks what the place itself makes easy. Design for eyes on the asset.
questionsV2.recallLine: City planners must site new walk-up machines to discourage skimmer installation and robbery without paying for guards. Which recommendation BEST reflects crime prevention through environmental design?

optionsShort.A: Fencing and dense planting screening each machine
optionsShort.B: Interior corridors reached through staffed building entrances
optionsShort.C: Rotate placements monthly to defeat pattern learning
optionsShort.D: Open, well-lit sites with sightlines and foot traffic

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Applies a security instinct backwards. Concealment protects PIN privacy, and screening the machine builds the workspace attackers want.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Does reduce crime, through staffing and access control by personnel, which the stem explicitly set aside.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Confuses environmental design with unpredictability tactics. Moving targets inconvenience customers and buy no surveillance benefit.

questionsV2.question: Which remediation MOST directly addresses the root cause of the driver crash?

options.A: Deploy endpoint anti-malware on the core, tuned to recognize known USB exploit payloads.
options.B: Validate the length and structure of every descriptor in the driver before processing it.
options.C: Enable data execution prevention so injected code placed in data pages is unable to run.
options.D: Fit locking covers over the core's accessible USB ports to keep rogue devices off the bus.

questionsV2.explanation:
The driver trusts input from the wire. It copies an attacker-controlled length into a fixed buffer, and the crash, the overwrite and the exploitability all flow from that missing check. Bounds and structure validation at the trust boundary is the root-cause fix (B).
Fix injection-class findings where untrusted data enters. Validation at the boundary removes the flaw; data execution prevention, anti-malware and port locks argue with its consequences.
questionsV2.recallLine: A USB driver crashes and overwrites adjacent memory whenever a peripheral sends a malformed descriptor longer than 64 bytes. Which remediation MOST directly addresses the root cause?

optionsShort.A: Anti-malware tuned to known USB exploit payloads
optionsShort.B: Validate every descriptor's length and structure first
optionsShort.C: Data execution prevention stopping code in data pages
optionsShort.D: Locking covers over the core's accessible USB ports

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: Detective and signature-bound. The fuzzer just showed the flaw falls to arbitrary malformed input that no signature anticipates.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: Genuinely raises the exploitation bar and cures nothing. The overflow still corrupts memory, and return-oriented programming beats DEP.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Shrinks the attack surface and leaves the trusted path wide open. The EPP and dispenser cables stay on the bus.

questionsV2.question: On which principle should the architect ground the recommendation between the proprietary cipher and standard algorithms?

options.A: Defense in depth: deploy both ciphers in layers so each covers the other's weaknesses.
options.B: Security through obscurity: an unpublished algorithm denies attackers the starting point that any practical cryptanalysis requires.
options.C: Kerckhoffs's principle: assume the algorithm is known and let security rest on the key alone.
options.D: Crypto-agility: select whichever cipher will be easiest to swap out in later years.

questionsV2.explanation:
A system must stay secure when everything about it except the key is public. That is Kerckhoffs's principle, and it decides the vendor choice cleanly (C). AES has survived decades of open, worldwide analysis. The proprietary cipher's secrecy is its only defense and a guarantee that nobody has seriously reviewed it.
Trust ciphers that survive publication. Secrecy belongs in keys, because keys can be changed.
questionsV2.recallLine: A vendor pitches a cipher whose strength rests on keeping the algorithm secret. On which principle should the architect ground a recommendation between it and standard algorithms?

optionsShort.A: Defense in depth: layer both ciphers together
optionsShort.B: Security through obscurity: keep the algorithm unpublished
optionsShort.C: Kerckhoffs: security rests on the key alone
optionsShort.D: Crypto-agility: pick whatever is easiest to replace

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Misuses a sound principle as a tiebreaker dodge. Layering a weak cipher adds complexity and a false sense of margin.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: The vendor's pitch restated. Algorithms leak through reverse engineering and departing staff, and a leaked algorithm cannot be rotated.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: A genuine engineering virtue that presupposes the question answered. Agility would argue for the standard option anyway.

questionsV2.question: Tailgating keeps occurring at the cash-loading room door. Which physical control MOST directly defeats it?

options.A: A camera covering the doorway, with footage retained for ninety days of review.
options.B: An upgraded reader requiring a PIN in addition to the badge at the door.
options.C: A guard posted to review the door's access log at the end of each shift.
options.D: A mantrap of two interlocked doors that admits one person at a time.

questionsV2.explanation:
Tailgating exploits the interval when an open door admits more bodies than credentials. The direct counter meters passage physically. A mantrap's interlocked doors create a holding space where one person is authenticated before the far door releases, so the piggyback becomes impossible (D).
Match the control to the exploited mechanism. Tailgating is a throughput problem at the doorway, and only single-person interlocks close it.
questionsV2.recallLine: Tailgating keeps occurring at the bank's cash-loading room door. Which physical control MOST directly defeats that entry?

optionsShort.A: Camera on the doorway with ninety-day retention
optionsShort.B: Reader requiring a PIN alongside the badge
optionsShort.C: Guard reviewing the access log each shift
optionsShort.D: Mantrap admitting one person at a time

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: Records the violation without resisting it. Footage supports investigation, and the intruder is inside either way.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Strengthens the authentication of whoever badges anyway. The tailgater was never authenticating, and the same open door still admits them.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Doubly detective. The log never saw the tailgater, and end-of-shift review adds hours to a record of an event it cannot contain.

questionsV2.question: To stop one lost key exposing the whole estate again, which control should the operator implement FIRST?

options.A: Relocate the ATMs into bank branches where staff can keep the service panels under observation.
options.B: Fit each unit with a uniquely keyed or electronically credentialed lock that records every opening.
options.C: Add camera coverage of every unit and review the recorded footage after each service visit.
options.D: Engrave serialized asset identifiers on the panels so any tampering can be traced to a specific site.

questionsV2.explanation:
Keying the whole fleet alike turns one stolen key into a master credential. Fit each unit with a uniquely keyed or electronically credentialed lock (B), which adds the accountability of logged openings as well.
When a single shared secret protects many assets, diversify the secret before layering monitoring around it.
questionsV2.recallLine: One stolen vendor key opened dozens of machines. Which control should the operator implement FIRST so a single lost key can never expose the estate again?

optionsShort.A: Relocate machines into branches under staff observation
optionsShort.B: Unique or credentialed lock per unit, openings logged
optionsShort.C: Cameras on every unit, footage reviewed afterwards
optionsShort.D: Serialized asset identifiers engraved on the panels

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Abandons the business model in place of fixing the control. Relocation moves the exposure, and the shared-key failure survives the move.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Detective, and the review happens after entry. Cameras investigate incidents and deter casual tampering. They stop no keyed entry.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Neither prevents nor detects an opening. Engraving supports inventory and forensics.

questionsV2.question: Which statement is the MOST accurate guidance on what the higher assurance level actually buys?

options.A: EAL4 certifies that fewer exploitable vulnerabilities will remain in the product during live operation.
options.B: EAL4 reflects deeper design review and testing rigor on a scale running to EAL7.
options.C: EAL4 doubles the cryptographic strength requirements that were applied at EAL2.
options.D: EAL4 products are approved for classified environments, while EAL2 products remain commercial.

questionsV2.explanation:
Evaluation Assurance Levels grade the depth of the evaluation. EAL2 is structurally tested, EAL4 is methodically designed, tested and reviewed, and the scale tops out at EAL7's formally verified design. The premium buys higher confidence that the product meets its stated security target (B).
Read an EAL as how hard the evaluators looked. Then check what the security target actually claimed.
questionsV2.recallLine: Two shortlisted pads are evaluated at different assurance levels, and the finance director asks what the higher number buys. Which statement is the MOST accurate guidance?

optionsShort.A: Fewer exploitable vulnerabilities will remain in operation
optionsShort.B: Deeper design review and testing rigor
optionsShort.C: Cryptographic strength requirements double relative to EAL2
optionsShort.D: Approved for classified environments, unlike lower-level products

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: The misconception the CISO must be warned about. EAL4-certified products have shipped with exploitable bugs, and no EAL is a warranty.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Invents a linkage. Cryptographic strength comes from the algorithms and any FIPS validation, not from the assurance level.

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: Imports the retired TCSEC habit of mapping levels to authorized environments. Accreditation rests with each scheme and authorizing official.

questionsV2.question: Which element of the model BEST describes the certified application every balance update must pass through?

options.A: A transformation procedure, the certified program permitted to modify constrained data items.
options.B: An integrity verification procedure, confirming data items remain valid at defined checkpoints.
options.C: A constrained data item itself, protected against modification by unauthorized subjects.
options.D: An access triple, binding an authenticated user to the operations that user may invoke.

questionsV2.explanation:
In Clark-Wilson, users never touch protected data directly. They act through certified programs that carry data from one valid state to another, and that mediating certified program is the transformation procedure (A). Here it is the banking application.
Remember the division of labor. TPs change data, IVPs check data, triples say who may run what.
questionsV2.recallLine: In the consultant's Clark-Wilson model of the payment platform, which element BEST describes the certified application every balance update must pass through?

optionsShort.A: Transformation procedure: certified program modifying constrained data
optionsShort.B: Integrity verification procedure confirming data stays valid
optionsShort.C: A constrained data item, protected from unauthorized change
optionsShort.D: Access triple binding user, operation and data

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: An integrity verification procedure audits that constrained data items are in a valid state, like a nightly reconciliation. It changes none.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Mislabels the actor as the object. The application manipulates CDIs such as balances, and is not one of them.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Names the model's bookkeeping. The triple of user, TP and CDI records who may run which procedure against which data.

questionsV2.question: Which suppression arrangement BEST protects the racks without giving up the sprinkler coverage this building's code requires?

options.A: Keep the wet risers charged above the racks and fit drip pans under each joint.
options.B: Convert the hall's sprinkler branch to double interlock pre-action, released by aspirating smoke detection.
options.C: Install clean agent total flooding for the hall and remove it from the sprinkler system.
options.D: Install carbon dioxide total flooding in the hall, discharging on cross-zoned heat detection.

questionsV2.explanation:
Water above a live data hall is a hazard to be engineered. A double interlock pre-action branch keeps the pipe dry until both the aspirating detectors and a fused head agree there is a fire (B). That removes the leak and accidental-discharge risk and leaves the hall inside the building's sprinkler envelope. A gaseous agent alone would also leave re-ignition unaddressed once the agent disperses.
Choose the suppression whose failure mode you can live with.
questionsV2.recallLine: A data hall sits under the landlord's wet sprinkler risers, which cannot be rerouted. Which suppression arrangement BEST protects the racks while keeping code coverage?

optionsShort.A: Keep wet risers charged, add drip pans
optionsShort.B: Double interlock pre-action released by aspirating detection
optionsShort.C: Clean agent flooding, drop sprinkler coverage
optionsShort.D: Carbon dioxide flooding on cross-zoned heat detection

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Leaves charged water over the racks. Drip pans catch a weeping joint and nothing catches a sheared head.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Right in a purpose-built shell whose authority having jurisdiction accepts gaseous protection alone. Here the landlord's riser stays.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: A proven total flooding agent for spaces nobody occupies. Carbon dioxide at extinguishing concentration is lethal in a hall people work in.

sources: NFPA 75 Standard for the Fire Protection of Information Technology Equipment | automatic sprinkler and gaseous agent protection
NFPA 13 Standard for the Installation of Sprinkler Systems | pre-action systems
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PE-13 Fire Protection

questionsV2.question: Which power investment MOST reduces the chance that the claims platform loses supply during a long utility outage?

options.A: Bring in a second utility feed from a different substation on the far side.
options.B: Extend UPS autonomy at full load from ten minutes to thirty by adding batteries.
options.C: Load bank the generator and run automatic transfer switch tests on a fixed schedule.
options.D: Dual-cord each rack to two power distribution units drawing on separate UPS modules.

questionsV2.explanation:
The single feed is the visible weakness, and the design already answers it with a generator and fuel under contract. That answer has never been proven. A transfer switch that has not operated since installation, in front of a generator that has never carried load, is the failure a site discovers at minute eleven of an outage. Load banking and scheduled transfer tests (C) buy more availability per pound here than any new hardware.
Test the link in the chain that has never run. Untested redundancy is a plan.
questionsV2.recallLine: A data hall has one utility feed and a 750 kVA generator never transfer-tested. Which power investment MOST reduces the chance of losing supply?

optionsShort.A: Second utility feed from another substation
optionsShort.B: Extend UPS autonomy to thirty minutes
optionsShort.C: Load bank and transfer-test the generator
optionsShort.D: Dual-cord racks to separate UPS modules

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: Removes the single point of failure at the utility, the right spend where outage history is long. It changes nothing if the transfer fails.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Lengthens the bridge the UPS provides, which matters when outages run to minutes. A longer bridge to a dead generator goes nowhere.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Protects against a failed cord, breaker or distribution unit inside the hall. A different failure from loss of supply to the building.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PE-11 Emergency Power
NFPA 110 Standard for Emergency and Standby Power Systems | routine maintenance and operational testing
Uptime Institute Tier Standard: Topology | engine generator commissioning

questionsV2.question: Which behavior for the two hall doors when controller power fails BEST balances egress against unauthorized entry?

options.A: Both doors release so occupants can leave and responders can reach the racks quickly.
options.B: Both doors stay locked until a keyholder opens them with the mechanical override key.
options.C: The doors hold their locked state on controller batteries, releasing when the batteries run flat.
options.D: Egress hardware releases while the entry side stays locked, with both doors alarmed and logged.

questionsV2.explanation:
Life safety comes first. People have to leave a room whose door hardware has lost power, and mechanical egress hardware does that without waiting on a controller. What is left to design is the other direction: let the door out, hold the door in, and alarm and log the position of both leaves (D). An open door during an outage then becomes an event somebody sees.
Decide what a control does when it dies. It will die at an inconvenient hour.
questionsV2.recallLine: Badge-controlled doors on an occupied data hall lose controller power. Which failure behavior BEST balances safe egress against unauthorized entry?

optionsShort.A: Both doors release for occupants and responders
optionsShort.B: Both stay locked pending a mechanical override
optionsShort.C: Batteries hold locks until they run flat
optionsShort.D: Egress releases, entry stays locked, doors alarmed

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Gets the egress half right and gives the racks away. A released entry side during an outage is when nobody watches the corridor.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: The classic fail-secure posture, and it belongs on a cage or vault that people do not occupy. On an occupied hall it can trap a technician.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Defers the decision to a battery. The eventual release then arrives unannounced, hours later.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-24 Fail in Known State
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PE-3 Physical Access Control
NFPA 101 Life Safety Code | door openings on means of egress

questionsV2.question: Which change MOST directly closes the path the testers used from one clinical workstation to another?

options.A: Give every workstation a unique local administrator password, rotated automatically by a managed solution.
options.B: Set a sixteen-character minimum on the shared local administrator password and rotate it quarterly.
options.C: Stop help desk staff from signing in to workstations with domain administrator credentials.
options.D: Deploy endpoint detection that alerts when a process reads credentials out of LSASS memory.

questionsV2.explanation:
Reuse is the mechanism. A hash lifted from the first machine authenticates to every other machine that shares the secret. What ends the technique is a different secret on every host, rotated without a human touching it (A).
When a credential works in more than one place, the number of places it works is the control.
questionsV2.recallLine: One local administrator password is shared by 4,200 workstations. Which change MOST directly closes the lateral path between those workstations?

optionsShort.A: Unique rotating local administrator password per workstation
optionsShort.B: Longer shared local administrator password, rotated quarterly
optionsShort.C: Stop domain admin logons on workstations
optionsShort.D: Alert on credential dumping from LSASS

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Changes how hard the password is to guess. Nobody guessed anything, and a sixteen-character shared secret replays just as well.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Genuinely necessary, and it belongs in the same plan. It closes workstation to domain while the workstation-to-workstation route stays open.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Would have shown the credential theft as it happened. Detection removes none of the reachability that made one dump worth 4,200 machines.

sources: MITRE ATT&CK | T1550.002 Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash
Microsoft | Mitigating Pass-the-Hash and Other Credential Theft, version 2
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-5 Authenticator Management

questionsV2.question: Which change to the sixty service accounts BEST removes the value of any service ticket an attacker requests?

options.A: Have the application owners choose new twelve-character passwords for the accounts and rotate annually.
options.B: Disable RC4 for Kerberos so that tickets for the accounts are encrypted with AES.
options.C: Convert the accounts to group managed service accounts whose passwords the directory generates and rotates.
options.D: Add the accounts to Protected Users so their credentials receive the group's restrictions.

questionsV2.explanation:
Any authenticated user may ask a domain controller for a ticket to an account carrying a service principal name, and that ticket comes back encrypted under a key derived from the account's password. The attack is offline cracking of the ticket. So the whole question is whether the password can be cracked, and a 240-byte password the directory generates and rotates on its own cannot be (C).
Ask what the attacker carries away, then make it uncrackable.
questionsV2.recallLine: Sixty service accounts hold service principal names with passwords set in 2019. Which change BEST removes the value of a requested service ticket?

optionsShort.A: Owners choose twelve-character passwords, rotated annually
optionsShort.B: Disable RC4 so tickets use AES
optionsShort.C: Group managed service accounts, directory-generated passwords
optionsShort.D: Add the accounts to Protected Users

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Leaves a human choosing the secret. A twelve-character password picked by an application owner is what a modern cracking rig is built for.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Worth doing, and it removes RC4. An AES-encrypted ticket wrapped around a weak password still yields that password.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Protected Users blocks delegation, caching and weak ciphers for interactive accounts. Microsoft warns against service accounts in it.

sources: MITRE ATT&CK | T1558.003 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Kerberoasting
Microsoft | Group Managed Service Accounts overview
NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev 5 | key strength and cryptoperiods

questionsV2.question: Which krbtgt rotation step MOST reliably invalidates Kerberos tickets an intruder could have forged already?

options.A: Reset the krbtgt password once and force immediate replication to every domain controller.
options.B: Reset the krbtgt password twice, leaving a full replication cycle between the two resets.
options.C: Reset the krbtgt password twice in succession inside a single overnight maintenance window.
options.D: Reset the domain controller computer accounts and the built-in Administrator password across the forest.

questionsV2.explanation:
A domain controller accepts a ticket signed with either the current ticket-granting key or the one before it. That pair is why a partial rotation leaves a forged ticket working: the old key becomes the previous key, and a golden ticket minted from it stays valid until a second rotation pushes it out. Run the second reset only after the first has replicated everywhere (B) and the operation stays survivable.
Keys trusted in pairs have to be rotated in pairs.
questionsV2.recallLine: A forest's krbtgt account has not been reset since 2014. Which rotation step MOST reliably invalidates tickets an intruder may already hold?

optionsShort.A: Reset krbtgt once, replicate immediately
optionsShort.B: Reset krbtgt twice, a replication cycle apart
optionsShort.C: Reset krbtgt twice in one window
optionsShort.D: Reset DC computer accounts and Administrator

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: The half of the job that feels finished. The old key becomes the previous key, so a forged ticket works until a second rotation.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Has the arithmetic right and the sequencing wrong. Controllers that lack the first new key are handed tickets they cannot validate.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Removes other credentials the testers may hold. A forged ticket is signed by the ticket-granting account, not the Administrator password.

sources: MITRE ATT&CK | T1558.001 Steal or Forge Kerberos Tickets: Golden Ticket
Microsoft | AD Forest Recovery: resetting the krbtgt password twice with replication between resets
NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev 5 | cryptoperiods and key rotation

questionsV2.question: Calder Trust Bank runs its core deposit platform on 41 Oracle databases. Twenty-four members of the database team hold permanent db_owner on every production instance, granted the week each engineer joined and never reduced since; the internal audit has raised the standing rights three years running. Around nine of the twenty-four touch production in a given month, and then during change windows. The bank already licenses a privileged access management platform but uses it to store the passwords and nothing else. Which change should the security architect require FIRST to bring the arrangement into line with least privilege?

options.A: Split the twenty-four engineers into four role groups, each holding db_owner on a subset of instances
options.B: Recertify the twenty-four privileged accounts quarterly and not annually, with the data owner attesting
options.C: Broker db_owner as a time-boxed session issued against an approved change and withdrawn at its close
options.D: Require a hardware security key at every interactive logon to a production database instance

questionsV2.explanation:
Twenty-four standing grants across 41 instances is 984 permanent authorizations to reach production deposit data. Roughly nine get exercised in a month. Least privilege is the state of the entitlement between reviews. Have the vault issue db_owner against an approved change and take it back when the change closes (C), and the authorization exists while the work does. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-6 and AC-2(6) describe exactly that.
Where an entitlement is permanent, make it temporary before you make it smaller or better assured.
questionsV2.recallLine: Twenty-four engineers hold permanent db_owner on 41 production databases. What should a security architect require FIRST under least privilege?

optionsShort.A: Four role groups, each over some instances
optionsShort.B: Recertify the privileged accounts each quarter
optionsShort.C: Time-boxed sessions issued against approved changes
optionsShort.D: Hardware security key at production logon

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Worth doing, and four groups of six still hold permanent rights over fewer instances. It narrows the blast radius, not the grant.

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: A detective control over a state nobody has changed. Attesting to a permanent entitlement quarterly confirms it faster and removes nothing.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Strengthens the evidence that the right person arrived at the door. It says nothing about what they may do once inside.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-6 Least Privilege
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-2(6) Dynamic Privilege Management
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 3.1.2 Least privilege

questionsV2.question: Kestrel Mutual's treasury systems team has five engineers. The same engineer who creates a vendor master record in the payments application can also release the twice-weekly outbound payment file to the bank, because both rights sit inside one application role that the software vendor will not let anyone split. Finance has refused headcount and the release window is fixed by the bank's cut-off. An internal audit finding calls the arrangement a segregation of duties failure and asks for remediation within the quarter. Which control BEST addresses that finding?

options.A: Rotate the payment release duty among the treasury systems team on a published monthly schedule
options.B: Require an approver outside the treasury systems team to release each assembled payment file
options.C: Write vendor creations and payment releases to a write-once log that internal audit samples quarterly
options.D: Grant the release right just for the two-hour cut-off window and withdraw it afterwards

questionsV2.explanation:
One engineer can create the payee and send money to it, carrying a fraudulent payment end to end with nobody else in the path. The vendor's refusal to split the role only means the separation has to be imposed around the application. Put an approver from outside the treasury systems team at the release step (B) and the second pair of hands is back, before the money leaves. NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 AC-5 and AC-3(2) pair exactly this way: where the duty cannot be divided, require two authorized individuals for the privileged action.
Ask whether a control puts another human into the chain.
questionsV2.recallLine: One engineer can both create a vendor record and release the payment file, and the role cannot be split. Which control BEST closes the gap?

optionsShort.A: Rotate the release duty each month
optionsShort.B: Approver outside the team releases the file
optionsShort.C: Write-once log sampled by audit quarterly
optionsShort.D: Release right granted for the cut-off window

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Spreads the conflicting rights across the calendar and never removes them. Whoever holds the duty this month holds both halves of it.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: The instrument to reach for when no preventive separation is available at all. A quarterly sample reads the payment after settlement.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Shortens the period in which one person holds both rights and adds no second person to the transaction.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-5 Separation of Duties
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3(2) Dual Authorization
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 3.1.6 Segregation of Duties

questionsV2.question: Halden Fitness is three sprints from launching a running app for 200,000 users. A data protection impact assessment finds that the app records precise coordinates every four seconds for as long as it is installed, including when no activity is being tracked, and retains them indefinitely. The single feature that consumes location is a weekly map of the routes the user ran. Product management wants to ship on the announced date and has asked the assessment to name one change it will accept. Which change MOST reflects privacy by design?

options.A: Collect location at run-tracking resolution and just while an activity is being recorded
options.B: Present a consent dialogue at first launch explaining the continuous collection and its purpose
options.C: Encrypt the stored coordinates under a per-user key held in the handset's platform keystore
options.D: Delete stored coordinates automatically ninety days after the activity they belong to

questionsV2.explanation:
All four are genuine privacy controls, and three of them govern data the app should not be holding. Privacy by design is a decision about the collection (A). A weekly route map needs coordinates while somebody is running. It does not need a continuous trace of where they sleep, work and worship. ISO/IEC 29100's collection limitation principle and Article 25 of the GDPR, which requires data protection by design and by default, both put that decision at the design stage.
When a finding names a collection, the answer that changes the collection outranks the ones that dress it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A running app records four-second coordinates continuously to draw a weekly route map. Which change MOST reflects privacy by design?

optionsShort.A: Collect location while an activity is recording
optionsShort.B: Consent dialogue explaining the continuous collection
optionsShort.C: Encrypt coordinates under a per-user key
optionsShort.D: Delete coordinates ninety days after the run

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Makes the collection transparent and arguably lawful without making it smaller. Consent to excessive collection is still excessive.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Protects the coordinates from an attacker and from other apps on the handset. What Halden itself knows is unchanged.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Bounds the exposure in time, which is worth having. Ninety days of four-second location on 200,000 people is the same holding, shorter.

sources: ISO/IEC 29100:2011 | Privacy principle: collection limitation
Regulation (EU) 2016/679 | Article 25, data protection by design and by default
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 3.1.9 Privacy by design

questionsV2.question: Ardent Retail runs 140 stores, each with a broadband circuit and an IPsec tunnel home to one of two datacenters, where all internet and software-as-a-service traffic is inspected before it leaves. The concentrators sit at 80 percent of capacity, a point-of-sale replacement will add 900 more devices, and store managers report that the hosted till application is slow. Security wants any redesign to keep inspection uniform and to stop treating a device's presence on the store network as evidence that the device is trusted. Which architecture BEST satisfies both requirements?

options.A: A next-generation firewall in every store with local breakout and rule sets managed centrally
options.B: A third datacenter inspection hub with added concentrator capacity for the growing device estate
options.C: A reverse proxy in the datacenter publishing the till application to stores across the existing tunnels
options.D: A cloud-delivered edge applying identity and device-posture policy per session at a regional point of presence

questionsV2.explanation:
Two requirements pull against each other. Inspection has to stay uniform, and the store LAN has to stop conferring trust. A cloud-delivered edge satisfies both (D). The secure web gateway, the broker for sanctioned software-as-a-service and the access proxy sit in one policy plane at a regional point of presence. A till, a handheld or a manager's laptop is evaluated on who and what it is, and traffic never has to reach a datacenter to be inspected. NIST SP 800-207 describes that move of the policy decision point away from network location.
When a redesign carries a trust requirement as well as a capacity one, the capacity answers look adequate until you re-read the trust sentence.
questionsV2.recallLine: A retailer backhauls 140 stores through two datacenters and wants to stop trusting devices by network location. Which architecture BEST fits?

optionsShort.A: Firewall per store with central rule management
optionsShort.B: Third inspection hub with more concentrator capacity
optionsShort.C: Datacenter reverse proxy across the existing tunnels
