B.wouldAnswer: Misplaces the mechanism. A5/1 encrypts user traffic after the downgrade, and radio signaling never transits the center's sensors.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Invents an action the attacker did not need. A relay that quietly forwards traffic is precisely why on-path interception is hard to spot.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Fails on the facts. The fleet had no TLS configured, which is what made the cleartext capture possible.

questionsV2.question: Which change would MOST directly restore call quality on the shared links?

options.A: Increasing the TCP window size on the replication servers so the nightly transfers complete sooner each evening.
options.B: Re-encoding the branch calls with a noticeably higher-bitrate audio codec to improve their perceived sound fidelity.
options.C: Enabling compression on the WAN links to reduce the total volume of traffic they must carry.
options.D: Applying quality-of-service policies so voice packets are queued and forwarded ahead of bulk transfer traffic.

questionsV2.explanation:
The symptom pair is diagnostic. Bulk TCP transfers ride out congestion by retransmitting and reordering, so they complete without error. Voice cannot wait for a retransmission, and every delayed or jittered packet is a gap the listener hears.
So the fix is scheduling (D). Quality-of-service classifies voice into a priority queue, which crosses the congested link with bounded delay and jitter while the replication absorbs the slack it tolerates so well.
Real-time traffic fails on latency and jitter, elastic traffic on throughput. Share a link between them and priority queueing is what reconciles them.
questionsV2.recallLine: Voice on CityBank's shared site links turns choppy every evening while bulk replication runs. Which change would MOST directly restore call quality?

optionsShort.A: Raise TCP window size on replication servers
optionsShort.B: Re-encode calls with a higher-bitrate codec
optionsShort.C: Compress the WAN links to cut volume
optionsShort.D: Queue voice ahead of bulk transfers

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Does the opposite of helping. A larger window lets the transfers fill the path harder, deepening the queues voice is stuck behind.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Raises fidelity per packet and makes the stream heavier and just as delayed. The garbling here is loss and jitter.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Buys headroom at the cost of processing delay. An already-compressed replication stream yields little at the moment of contention.

questionsV2.question: What is the MOST accurate account of what the attackers learned from the subscriber identity captures alone?

options.A: The cardholder PIN blocks queued up for onward transmission by each of the affected festival ATMs.
options.B: The contents of calls and data sessions that passed through the rogue base station while it operated.
options.C: The unique subscriber identity of each nearby SIM, letting individual devices be identified and tracked.
options.D: The street-level home addresses registered by the carrier against each captured subscriber account in its own records.

questionsV2.explanation:
An IMSI is the identifier a SIM presents to the network, and an IMSI catcher harvests exactly that: which subscriber identities are present, when, and where. That supports identification and movement tracking of everyone near the rogue tower, a privacy harm independent of any decryption (C). It is what counsel needs stated.
Identifiers leak presence and movement. Metadata is a privacy breach in its own right, even when every payload stays sealed.
questionsV2.recallLine: Privacy counsel asks what the rogue base station learned from subscriber identity captures alone, before any traffic was decrypted. Which account is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Cardholder PIN blocks queued by festival machines
optionsShort.B: Contents of the calls and data sessions
optionsShort.C: Unique identity of every nearby SIM
optionsShort.D: Home addresses held against each subscriber account

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Confuses the identifier layer with the payload. PIN blocks are application data, obtainable only after the traffic was captured.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Likewise needs interception and decryption of session content. Capturing identities opens no sessions.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Reaches into the carrier's subscriber database, which the radio interface never transmits.

questionsV2.question: Which assessment of the engineer's IPsec claim is MOST accurate?

options.A: The tunnel would have stopped the rogue base station from forcing the modems down to 2G in the first place.
options.B: The interception would still have occurred, but the captured traffic would have been unreadable ciphertext instead of cardholder data.
options.C: IPsec's added overhead would have made transactions over a 2G link time out, so the ATMs would simply have gone offline.
options.D: The tunnel would have alerted the SOC as soon as the peer's identity could no longer be cryptographically verified.

questionsV2.explanation:
Encryption at a layer the bank controls changes what the attacker obtains. It changes nothing about whether the attacker can sit on the path. The rogue tower would still relay traffic, and every intercepted packet would be ESP ciphertext, so the loss event, cardholder data exposure, is averted while the attack itself proceeds (B). That is why 'prevented entirely' overstates.
Encrypting the payload changes what an on-path attacker carries away. It does not remove the attacker.
questionsV2.recallLine: A review-board engineer claims an IPsec tunnel to the processing center would have prevented the machine interception entirely. Which assessment of that claim is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Tunnel would have blocked the 2G downgrade
optionsShort.B: Interception proceeds, but yields only ciphertext
optionsShort.C: Overhead would time out 2G transactions
optionsShort.D: Tunnel would alert on peer-verification failure

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: Puts IPsec at the wrong layer. The downgrade is negotiated in the radio stack beneath the tunnel. Refusing 2G fallback is a modem setting.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: A performance guess. IPsec's overhead is modest, and 2G, while slow, carries small transaction messages.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Misunderstands a relay attack. The attacker forwards the IKE exchange untouched between the true endpoints, so peer authentication succeeds.

questionsV2.question: Two support laptops on one switch exchange transfers that never appear in the site router's flow logs, while their sessions to the center always do. Which statement BEST explains the difference?

options.A: The laptops negotiate a direct transport-layer session with each other that bypasses the lower network layers entirely.
options.B: The switch routes the local traffic itself using private internal IP addresses that the site's flow-logging router is configured to silently ignore.
options.C: An access list on the router discards the laptops' local traffic before the flow exporter can record it, while permitting their processing-center sessions.
options.D: Frames between hosts on one segment are switched by MAC address and reach the router only when traffic leaves the network.

questionsV2.explanation:
The router never sees the local traffic. Within a segment, delivery is a data link function: the switch forwards frames by learned MAC address, and the network-layer device participates only when a packet's destination lies in another network (D). Sessions to the processing center cross that boundary and get logged. Laptop-to-laptop transfers do not.
Knowing which device touches traffic at which layer tells you where visibility exists. Some monitoring blind spots are architectural.
questionsV2.recallLine: Two support laptops on one switch exchange transfers the site router's flow logs never show, though their sessions to the processing center appear. Which explanation is BEST?

optionsShort.A: Transport session bypasses the lower layers
optionsShort.B: Switch routes local traffic the router ignores
optionsShort.C: Router ACL drops the traffic before export
optionsShort.D: Same-segment frames are forwarded by MAC address

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Impossible as described. Transport sessions are carried inside network and data link layers. Layers encapsulate; they cannot be skipped.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Misassigns roles. A layer 2 switch forwards frames and consults no routing logic, and ignoring private addresses is not router behavior.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Conceivable in some other network, and it presumes an access list nobody mentioned. Dropped traffic would also typically still be countable.

questionsV2.question: A customer portal must be reachable from the internet and query an internal database. Where should the web server be placed?

options.A: On the internal LAN beside the database server, keeping their connection short and simple.
options.B: In a screened subnet (DMZ), with only its specific database port permitted through the inner firewall.
options.C: With an external hosting provider, keeping the exposed service outside the bank's perimeter entirely.
options.D: On the firewall's outside interface, relying on the server's own hardening as its protection.

questionsV2.explanation:
Anything internet-reachable must be assumed compromisable, so the design question is what that compromise is adjacent to. A screened subnet puts the portal in a buffer zone with filtering on both sides (B): the internet reaches only the portal, and the portal reaches the internal network on the one database port it needs. An attacker who wins the web tier inherits a nearly empty room.
Place exposed services at the end of a corridor. Segmentation is designed for the day the host falls.
questionsV2.recallLine: CityBank's customer portal must be reachable from the internet and query an internal database. Where should the web server be placed?

optionsShort.A: Internal LAN, beside the database server
optionsShort.B: Screened subnet, one port permitted inward
optionsShort.C: External hosting provider, outside the perimeter
optionsShort.D: Firewall's outside interface, hardened by itself

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The worst adjacency. From a compromised portal on the internal LAN, the database and directory are one hop away with no screen between.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Sounds like risk transfer and breaks on the requirement. The database query path returns as a tunnel the bank cannot monitor.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Leaves one host's hardening as the entire defense, with no filtered zone around it. Hardening is necessary and it is not architecture.

questionsV2.question: One handheld received an unsolicited anonymous Bluetooth message; another had its contact list retrieved. Which assessment is MOST accurate?

options.A: The second event is the more serious: unauthorized retrieval of data (bluesnarfing) breaches confidentiality, while unsolicited messages (bluejacking) are a nuisance.
options.B: The first event is the more serious, because successful message delivery proves the attacker has already completed a pairing relationship with the handheld.
options.C: The two events deserve equal priority, since each one demonstrates the same unauthorized radio-layer reach to devices carried by festival staff.
options.D: Neither event warrants a response, because Bluetooth's short operating range means the attacker will already have moved on and left the venue.

questionsV2.explanation:
Triage ranks by impact. Pushing an unwanted message at a device, bluejacking, alters nothing and takes nothing: an annoyance and a warning sign. Pulling data off a device, bluesnarfing, is a completed confidentiality breach of whatever was reachable, here a contact list and possibly more (A).
Prioritize by what the attacker achieved against confidentiality, integrity and availability. Same radio, very different losses.
questionsV2.recallLine: One festival handheld received an unsolicited anonymous Bluetooth message; another had its contact list pulled off. Which triage assessment of the pair is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Retrieval outranks the nuisance message
optionsShort.B: Delivery proves a completed pairing relationship
optionsShort.C: Equal priority: identical radio-layer reach
optionsShort.D: No response needed; short operating range

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Rests on a false technical premise. Bluejacking abuses object push precisely because it works on discoverable devices without pairing.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Flattens the distinction triage exists to draw. Shared attack surface is not shared impact, and spam is not data theft.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Turns a targeting constraint into a dismissal. Short range means the attacker was on-site, which argues for sweeps and a notice.

questionsV2.question: Which evaluation of the private access point name is MOST accurate?

options.A: It separates the fleet's traffic from other subscribers, but by itself encrypts nothing end to end.
options.B: It encrypts each modem's traffic all the way through to the processing center using keys the carrier manages.
options.C: It makes the cellular towers authenticate themselves to the modems, closing the rogue-base-station attachment path at the radio layer.
options.D: It places a carrier-managed stateful firewall between the fleet and the internet, making any further transit protection redundant.

questionsV2.explanation:
A private APN is a segregation construct. The carrier gives the fleet its own access point and routing context, keeping its traffic logically apart from other subscribers and often off the public internet. Valuable containment, and the data still crosses radio and carrier infrastructure protected only by whatever the link layer offers, which the incident proved breakable (A). Separate was mistaken for encrypted.
Segmentation controls who shares your path. Encryption controls who can read it. Test every private network claim against that pair.
questionsV2.recallLine: CityBank's design file skipped transit protection because a private access point name supposedly kept the traffic private. Which evaluation of that reasoning is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Segregates subscriber traffic; encrypts nothing itself
optionsShort.B: Encrypts end to end with carrier keys
optionsShort.C: Makes towers authenticate themselves to modems
optionsShort.D: Adds a carrier firewall, so protection is redundant

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Asserts a service the APN does not provide. There is no APN-level end-to-end cryptography, and believing there is is the design error.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Confuses the APN, which lives in the carrier's core, with radio-layer authentication. The APN stopped nothing during the downgrade.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Overstates a side effect. Private APNs commonly restrict inbound reachability, which does nothing for confidentiality of data in transit.

questionsV2.question: Transaction messages must arrive intact and in order; status telemetry can lose a sample but must be fresh. Which transport-layer design is MOST appropriate?

options.A: UDP for both flows, because its lower overhead maximizes battery life and bandwidth on cellular links.
options.B: TCP for the transaction messages and UDP for the telemetry, matching each flow's delivery requirements.
options.C: TCP for both flows, because a connection-oriented protocol is required before traffic can be encrypted.
options.D: UDP for the transactions and TCP for the telemetry, keeping time-critical payments off the slower protocol.

questionsV2.explanation:
Transport selection is requirements matching. Transactions need what TCP's connection, sequencing, acknowledgment and retransmission machinery provides: guaranteed, ordered delivery. Telemetry inverts the trade, because a retransmitted stale sample is worth less than the next fresh one, so connectionless UDP fits (B).
Match the transport to what each flow cannot afford to lose.
questionsV2.recallLine: Machine transaction messages must arrive intact and in order; status telemetry may lose a sample but must be fresh. Which transport-layer design is MOST appropriate?

optionsShort.A: UDP for both flows, for lower overhead
optionsShort.B: TCP for the payments, UDP for samples
optionsShort.C: TCP for both; encryption needs a connection
optionsShort.D: UDP for the payments, TCP for samples

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Optimizes the wrong variable. The efficiency gain is real, and a dropped withdrawal message would simply vanish.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Rests on a false premise. DTLS and IPsec protect datagram traffic routinely, so encryption needs no connection-oriented transport.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Reverses the analysis, treating TCP's reliability as mere slowness. Payments are exactly the traffic that must not be lost.

questionsV2.question: Which evaluation of the dark fiber argument is MOST accurate?

options.A: It holds: traffic on a point-to-point fiber that the bank alone lights is not realistically observable anywhere in transit.
options.B: It holds, provided the fiber's full physical route is inspected on a regular schedule for evidence of splices or taps.
options.C: It fails: dark fiber carries other tenants' wavelengths on the same strand, so their equipment can observe the bank's frames.
options.D: It fails: fiber can be tapped with minimal signal loss along uncontrolled ground, so traffic in transit still requires encryption.

questionsV2.explanation:
Leasing dark fiber buys exclusivity of the strand. It buys no custody of the path. The glass runs through ducts, vaults and rights-of-way the bank neither owns nor watches, and an optical tap, a bend coupler leaking a fraction of the light, extracts traffic with losses small enough to hide in normal attenuation. Encryption of data in transit stays required (D).
Control of the endpoints is not control of the ground between them. Data crossing territory you cannot secure gets encrypted, whatever the contract says about the medium.
questionsV2.recallLine: The wide-area team argues replication needs no encryption because the bank lights and operates the leased dark fiber itself. Which evaluation of that argument is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Holds: nobody can observe fiber we light
optionsShort.B: Holds if the route is inspected regularly
optionsShort.C: Fails: other tenants share the strand's wavelengths
optionsShort.D: Fails: taps draw light with negligible loss

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Mistakes a commercial arrangement for a physical guarantee. Lighting the strand says who transmits, not who can listen along the route.

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Converts a preventive requirement into detective comfort. Route inspections are periodic and taps are built to be unobtrusive.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Reaches the right verdict through the wrong facts. Sharing a strand by wavelength describes a lit service; a dark strand is the bank's.

questionsV2.question: Which set of measures is MOST appropriate for the handheld fleet?

options.A: Disable Bluetooth across the whole handheld fleet by written policy until the current festival season has completely ended.
options.B: Rely on Bluetooth's frequency-hopping physical layer, whose channel changes defeat attempts to intercept the pairing and data traffic.
options.C: Instruct staff to keep handhelds within arm's reach and to decline any pairing prompt they were not expecting.
options.D: Make the handhelds non-discoverable, require authenticated pairing, and remove the Bluetooth profiles the sleds do not use.

questionsV2.explanation:
The constraint rules out amputation, so the risk gets engineered down while the radio stays up (D). Non-discoverable mode removes the fleet from casual scanning. Authenticated pairing stops unknown devices establishing the relationship bluesnarfing rides on. Deleting unused profiles removes the very services, object exchange and file transfer, that data-theft attacks call. Three cuts into the attack path, and the sleds keep working.
When a risky capability must stay enabled, shrink it. Visibility, authentication and surface are the three dials that turn.
questionsV2.recallLine: Handhelds still need Bluetooth for the card sleds, yet further Bluetooth data theft has to stop. Which set of measures is MOST appropriate for that fleet?

optionsShort.A: Disable Bluetooth fleet-wide by written policy
optionsShort.B: Trust frequency hopping to defeat interception
optionsShort.C: Tell staff to decline unexpected pairing prompts
optionsShort.D: Hide the devices, authenticate pairing, strip profiles

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Meets the security goal by failing the business one. The sleds depend on Bluetooth, so a blanket disable trades an incident for an outage.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Mistakes a coexistence mechanism for a security control. Frequency hopping fights interference, and every chipset follows the hop sequence.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: Worth issuing and worthless alone. It depends on busy staff noticing prompts, and attacks on discoverable services never prompt.

questionsV2.question: Which classification BEST fits what the interposed device did during that event?

options.A: A denial-of-service attack, because the ATMs were forced away from the legitimate 4G network they should have used.
options.B: A replay attack, because the transactions captured by the rogue station could be resubmitted at a later time.
options.C: An on-path (man-in-the-middle) attack, because the adversary sat between the endpoints and observed live traffic in transit.
options.D: An injection attack, because the rogue station inserted itself into the carrier's trusted infrastructure.

questionsV2.explanation:
An adversary interposed between two communicating parties, relaying their traffic while reading it, is an on-path attack (C). Full relay, silent recording, uninterrupted service: the stem's details match exactly.
An on-path attack's hallmark is service that keeps working while confidentiality quietly fails.
questionsV2.recallLine: An interposed device relayed live traffic between the machines and the carrier while recording it, and service never faltered. Which classification BEST fits that event?

optionsShort.A: Denial of service: forced off legitimate 4G
optionsShort.B: Replay: captured transactions could be resubmitted
optionsShort.C: On-path: adversary sat between the endpoints
optionsShort.D: Injection: device inserted into trusted infrastructure

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Fixes on the forced network change and draws the wrong conclusion. Availability was preserved deliberately, to keep victims transacting.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Names a real follow-on risk of holding captured transactions. Nothing was resubmitted during the event itself.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Stretches injection, which means crafted data pushed into an application or protocol stream. A device placed in a path is something else.

questionsV2.question: Which control MOST directly addresses the compromised certificate authority risk?

options.A: Purchasing extended-validation certificates for the processing center's public hostname from one of the largest and best-known public certificate authorities.
options.B: Increasing the public key length on the processing center's certificate to strengthen its cryptography against attack.
options.C: Checking each certificate's revocation status through OCSP before the session is established, so known mis-issued certificates are rejected.
options.D: Embedding the expected certificate or public key in the ATM software so any other certificate is rejected.

questionsV2.explanation:
The threat is mis-issuance: some other trusted CA signing a certificate the bank never requested. Pinning removes the CA ecosystem from the trust decision (D). The ATM accepts only the certificate or key it was built to expect, so a technically valid rogue certificate fails. A closed fleet of bank-owned clients is the ideal place for it.
When the CA ecosystem itself is the threat, pin the identity you expect.
questionsV2.recallLine: Architects fear a compromised public certificate authority issuing attackers a valid certificate for the processing center's hostname. Which control MOST directly addresses that risk?

optionsShort.A: Buy extended-validation certificates from a major authority
optionsShort.B: Lengthen the public key on the certificate
optionsShort.C: Check revocation by OCSP before each session
optionsShort.D: Accept only the identity built into the fleet

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Changes the vetting tier of the bank's own certificate and constrains no other CA. A compromised authority can still issue for the hostname.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Hardens against cryptanalysis of a key nobody is attacking. The rogue certificate carries its own perfectly good key.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Helps once the bad certificate is discovered and revoked, and an on-path attacker can often suppress the OCSP check.

questionsV2.question: A flood of large responses arrives from thousands of legitimate servers the authority never queried. Which property of UDP MOST directly makes that possible?

options.A: It performs no handshake, so a request carrying a forged source address is answered as though the victim had sent it.
options.B: It provides no delivery guarantee, so attack packets lost in transit are simply gone instead of retransmitted.
options.C: It has lower per-packet header overhead than TCP, so each response consumes less of the attacker's own bandwidth.
options.D: It supports broadcast and multicast delivery, letting a single request reach many amplifying servers at once.

questionsV2.explanation:
Reflection depends on servers answering someone who never asked, and that takes a forgeable victim address. UDP exchanges datagrams with no connection establishment, so a server has no handshake in which the claimed source must prove it can respond. It obligingly sends its large reply to the spoofed address (A). TCP's three-way handshake is exactly what defeats this, since a spoofed SYN never completes.
Connectionless protocols accept unverified source addresses. Every reflection and amplification attack is built on that one fact.
questionsV2.recallLine: A flood of large responses arrives from thousands of legitimate servers the authority never queried. Which property of UDP MOST directly makes that possible?

optionsShort.A: No handshake, so forged sources get answered
optionsShort.B: No delivery guarantee; lost packets stay lost
optionsShort.C: Smaller headers, so each response costs less
optionsShort.D: Broadcast and multicast reach many servers at once

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: A true UDP property, and irrelevant to the mechanism. Unreliable delivery describes lost packets, not why reflectors answer forged ones.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: Also true, and it improves the attacker's amplification economics. A secondary efficiency, worth nothing without spoofability.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Misdescribes the technique. Reflectors are queried unicast, one request per server.

questionsV2.question: Which change MOST directly shrinks how far broadcasts propagate while keeping the existing switch hardware?

options.A: Enable port security, so each switch port accepts frames from a single learned hardware address.
options.B: Enable spanning tree on the switches, removing the redundant paths that broadcasts can loop across.
options.C: Define VLANs on the switches, dividing the flat network into several smaller broadcast domains.
options.D: Replace the busiest access switches with faster models that can process broadcasts with less delay.

questionsV2.explanation:
Broadcast reach is defined by the broadcast domain, and a flat network is one giant domain: every ARP request touches all 500 hosts. VLANs partition the same physical switches into several logical domains, so each broadcast floods only its own segment (C). Propagation shrinks by design, on existing hardware.
To limit how far broadcasts travel, cut the domain into pieces. VLANs resize broadcast domains without new hardware or new cabling.
questionsV2.recallLine: A flat operations network of 500 devices slows under legitimate broadcast traffic. Which change MOST directly shrinks how far broadcasts propagate, keeping the existing switches?

optionsShort.A: Port security: one hardware address per port
optionsShort.B: Spanning tree, cutting redundant looping paths
optionsShort.C: Define VLANs, splitting one flat domain
optionsShort.D: Replace the busiest switches with faster models

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Polices who may send on a port. The number of hosts a legitimate broadcast reaches is unchanged, and so is the volume.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: The closest miss. Spanning tree blocks forwarding loops, and the stem describes legitimate broadcast load in a network that has none.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Treats propagation as a performance problem. Faster switches forward the same broadcasts to the same 500 hosts, sooner.

questionsV2.question: Which assessment of the parked laptop and a proportionate first response is BEST?

options.A: An active intrusion is underway; disable the branch wireless network until law enforcement arrives on site.
options.B: Probable wireless reconnaissance (war driving); review how far the branch SSIDs propagate and confirm the strength of the authentication they require.
options.C: Harmless behavior; passively observing radio signals from a parking lot yields nothing of value to an attacker.
options.D: An evil twin attack is already in progress; direct branch staff to move every handheld onto its cellular fallback connectivity at once.

questionsV2.explanation:
The evidence supports collection. Hours of dwell with a high-gain antenna and zero association attempts is the profile of war driving: passively mapping SSIDs, security modes and signal reach (B). The proportionate response treats it as a warning about exposure. Measure how far the branch networks bleed past the walls, trim transmit power where warranted, and verify that what is reachable from a parking lot demands strong authentication.
Reconnaissance observed is your prompt to shrink what an observer can learn and harden what an observer can reach.
questionsV2.recallLine: Mall security reports someone parked outside a station for hours with a laptop and a roof antenna. Which assessment and proportionate first response is BEST?

optionsShort.A: Active intrusion: shut branch wireless down
optionsShort.B: Likely war driving; check reach and authentication
optionsShort.C: Harmless: passive listening yields nothing useful
optionsShort.D: Evil twin: move handhelds onto cellular immediately

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Declares an intrusion the logs refute, then answers it with an availability loss on the branch.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Waves away the collection phase. SSIDs, hardware vendors, security modes and coverage maps are targeting data, and passive is not valueless.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Names an attack whose evidence, duplicate SSIDs, client disruptions and certificate warnings, is entirely absent.

questionsV2.question: Which upgrade MOST directly addresses both the slowdowns and the sniffing, and why?

options.A: Replace the hub with a switch, giving each port its own collision domain and forwarding unicast frames to the destination port.
options.B: Replace the hub with a small router, so that every PC is placed into a separate IP subnet of its own.
options.C: Cascade a second hub off the first and split the PCs between the two devices, halving the shared load.
options.D: Upgrade to a faster hub, so the shared medium offers more headroom to every attached station.

questionsV2.explanation:
Both complaints have one cause. A hub is a shared medium that repeats every bit out of every port, so contention throttles throughput and every NIC in promiscuous mode hears everything.
A switch fixes both with one change (A). Per-port collision domains end the contention, and MAC-learned forwarding delivers unicast frames only where they belong, so a sniffer on another port sees broadcasts and its own traffic.
Shared-medium problems, collisions and universal sniffing alike, are solved by per-port forwarding.
questionsV2.recallLine: A workshop's five diagnostic machines share an old Ethernet hub: transfers crawl when several are busy, and one port sniffs everyone. Which upgrade MOST directly fixes both?

optionsShort.A: Switch: per-port collisions, unicast forwarding
optionsShort.B: Small router, each PC its own subnet
optionsShort.C: Cascade a second hub, splitting the machines
optionsShort.D: Faster hub, more headroom for everyone

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Would also isolate traffic, at the wrong layer and cost. Per-PC subnets add complexity a five-PC workshop does not need.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Misunderstands cascading. Hubs joined to hubs still form one collision domain and one listening zone, so both problems survive intact.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Buys speed for a medium that stays shared. Contention scales down and persists, and the confidentiality exposure is untouched at any speed.

questionsV2.question: After a failed gateway was replaced with a spare using the same address, some machines could reach it only after minutes. Which mechanism BEST explains the delay?

options.A: The kiosks' DNS caches kept resolving the gateway's hostname to the address of the old device.
options.B: The kiosks' ARP caches still mapped the gateway's IP address to the old MAC address until those entries expired.
options.C: Spanning tree kept the replacement's switch port in a blocking state until the topology reconverged.
options.D: The kiosks' DHCP leases still named the failed device as default gateway until each lease renewed.

questionsV2.explanation:
The capture is the tell. Frames addressed to a hardware address that no longer exists on the wire mean the IP-to-MAC mapping is stale, and that mapping is ARP's. Each kiosk cached the old resolution and kept using it until the entry timed out or was refreshed (B), which is exactly a minutes-long outage that heals by itself.
Layer 2 reachability lives in ARP caches. Swap a device behind a retained IP and stale ARP entries are the first suspect.
questionsV2.recallLine: A failed gateway was replaced by a spare keeping the same IP address, yet some kiosks reached it only after minutes. Which mechanism BEST explains that delay?

optionsShort.A: DNS caches still resolved the old device
optionsShort.B: ARP caches still held the old MAC
optionsShort.C: Spanning tree blocked the replacement's port
optionsShort.D: DHCP leases still named the failed gateway

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Works at the wrong translation. DNS maps names to IP addresses, and the gateway's IP never changed, so no DNS record was invalidated.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: A real convergence delay when new switch links come up. It would block the replacement wholesale, and the capture shows a stale MAC.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Fails the same way. The lease hands out a gateway IP, and that IP is unchanged, so renewal alters nothing.

questionsV2.question: The backup path must stay in place. Which mechanism MOST directly stops the frames circulating while keeping it available?

options.A: Spanning Tree Protocol, which detects the loop and blocks one segment of it until a working path fails.
options.B: Storm control, which caps the incoming rate of broadcast and multicast traffic accepted on each individual switch port.
options.C: Link aggregation, which bundles parallel cables between two switches into one logical link.
options.D: Port security, which limits which hardware addresses may be learned on the new uplink port.

questionsV2.explanation:
Ethernet frames carry no hop count, so a physical loop recirculates broadcasts forever, amplifying them each lap. That is the storm in the captures.
The requirement is to keep the redundant path and forward over a loop-free topology, which is spanning tree's whole function (A). Elect a topology, place the loop-forming port in a blocking state, unblock it automatically when the primary path dies. Redundancy and stability together.
Layer 2 redundancy is safe only under a loop-management protocol. Without spanning tree or a modern equivalent, every backup cable is a scheduled outage.
questionsV2.recallLine: A second uplink patched through a third switch created a ring, and the same broadcast frames now circulate endlessly. Which mechanism keeps the redundant path safely?

optionsShort.A: Spanning tree blocks the loop-forming port
optionsShort.B: Storm control caps broadcast rate per port
optionsShort.C: Link aggregation bundles the parallel cables
optionsShort.D: Port security limits addresses on the uplink

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: A damage limiter. Rate caps blunt the storm's peak while the loop keeps regenerating traffic, and legitimate broadcasts are throttled too.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Fails on topology. Aggregation bundles parallel links between the same two devices, and this ring runs through a third switch.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Filters which hardware addresses may speak on a port. Nothing about it detects or breaks a forwarding loop.

questionsV2.question: Which observed packet sequence confirms an inbound connection was fully established?

options.A: A SYN from the client, a RST from the server, then a fresh SYN from the client.
options.B: A SYN from the client followed by a SYN-ACK from the server, with nothing further exchanged.
options.C: A SYN from the client, a SYN-ACK from the server, then an ACK from the client.
options.D: An ACK from the client answered by a FIN from the server shortly afterwards.

questionsV2.explanation:
Establishment is the three-way handshake completing. The client proposes (SYN), the server agrees and proposes back (SYN-ACK), and the client's final ACK confirms both directions are synchronized (C). Only after that third packet does either side hold an established connection.
SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK is the signature of establishment. Its missing final ACK is the signature of the attack that abuses it.
questionsV2.recallLine: An analyst's rule must match only inbound connections that were fully established. Which observed packet sequence confirms establishment?

optionsShort.A: SYN, server RST, then another SYN
optionsShort.B: SYN and SYN-ACK, nothing further
optionsShort.C: SYN, SYN-ACK, then the client's ACK
optionsShort.D: Client ACK answered by a server FIN

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Shows the opposite outcome. A RST is the server refusing or aborting the attempt, and the client simply trying again.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: A half-open connection. The server has committed state and is waiting for an ACK that never comes.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Belongs to a different phase. A FIN initiates orderly teardown, so it presupposes a connection that already exists.

questionsV2.question: Which risk statement about the readers' short operating range is MOST accurate?

options.A: The range is a hard physical ceiling, so capturing a transaction requires physically tampering with the reader itself.
options.B: The NFC standard already encrypts each session on its own, so the operating range question is largely irrelevant to the workshop's risk analysis.
options.C: Short range raises attacker difficulty, but relay and skimming equipment can still extend or capture transactions, so transaction-layer cryptographic protection remains necessary.
options.D: Interception is a practical concern chiefly in crowded environments, so readers installed in well-supervised branch locations need no additional protective controls beyond supervision.

questionsV2.explanation:
Range is an attacker-cost parameter (C). Purpose-built antennas read NFC from further than the nominal few centimeters, skimming hardware can sit at the reader, and relay attacks defeat proximity entirely by piping the exchange between a victim's card and a distant terminal in real time. Treat short range as difficulty and put the real protection in the payment protocol's cryptography, the dynamic per-transaction cryptogram.
Proximity limits are attack-cost assumptions. Price them as difficulty and put the defense in cryptography that does not care where the attacker stands.
questionsV2.recallLine: A risk workshop is weighing how much protection the tap-to-pay readers' few centimeters of operating range really buy. Which risk statement is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Physical ceiling; capture needs reader tampering
optionsShort.B: NFC already encrypts every session itself
optionsShort.C: Difficulty rises, but cryptography still required
optionsShort.D: Crowded venues mainly; supervision covers branches

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Converts a nominal figure into a physics guarantee. Eavesdropping and relay both work without ever touching the reader.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Misattributes the protection. Baseline NFC communication is not encrypted; the anti-replay strength lives in the payment application.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Turns risk into a seating chart. Supervision perceives neither a radio-layer relay nor a skimmer inside the housing.

questionsV2.question: A tester on an access port now captures only broadcasts and their own sessions, where the old hub captured everything. Which explanation is MOST accurate?

options.A: The switch encrypts frames traveling between its ports, so other stations' traffic is still present in the capture but cryptographically unreadable.
options.B: The switch forwards unicast frames only to the learned destination port, so other conversations no longer reach the tester's port.
options.C: The switch's VLAN configuration has isolated every access port into its own separate per-port broadcast domain.
options.D: The switch performs routing between its ports, so frames cross from one port to another only when a gateway forwards them.

questionsV2.explanation:
A switch learns which MAC address lives on which port from source addresses, then forwards each unicast frame only toward its destination (B). Traffic between two other stations has no reason to appear at the tester's port, and broadcasts still flood to all ports of the VLAN. That matches the capture contents exactly.
The report should carry the caveat: this is a forwarding behavior, and MAC flooding and ARP spoofing exist precisely to defeat it.
Knowing why the sniffer went quiet is knowing which attacks make it loud again.
questionsV2.recallLine: A tester on an access port now captures only broadcasts and their own sessions, where the old hub captured everything. Which explanation is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Switch encrypts frames between its ports
optionsShort.B: Unicast reaches only the learned destination port
optionsShort.C: Every access port is its own VLAN
optionsShort.D: Switch routes between ports via a gateway

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Invents a service switches do not provide. Traffic that is simply absent contradicts an unreadable theory, which would show garbled bytes.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Refuted by the tester's own evidence. Broadcasts were captured, so the port shares a broadcast domain with their senders.

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: Moves the device up a layer. A layer 2 switch forwards frames by MAC address with no gateway involved.

questionsV2.question: Which explanation BEST fits the ward segment receiving no addresses, and points to the standard fix?

options.A: The DHCP scope is exhausted, so the server has no addresses left to offer the branch clients; extend the pool.
options.B: The WAN provider is filtering the lease traffic somewhere in transit; request an exception for those flows.
options.C: The branch clients' requests carry addressing the server does not recognize; renumber the branch to match the server's scopes.
options.D: DHCP discovery is broadcast, and routers do not forward broadcasts; configure a relay agent on the branch router.

questionsV2.explanation:
The evidence isolates the variable. Same clients, same server, success on the local LAN, failure across a routed boundary, healthy link. What changes at that boundary is broadcast reach. A client's DHCPDISCOVER is broadcast because the client has no address yet, and routers terminate broadcasts at the segment edge, so the plea for an address dies on the branch wire.
The cure is a relay agent, the IP helper, on the branch router (D), which converts the broadcast into a unicast aimed at the headquarters server. Relays exist in every centralized-DHCP design for this reason.
Protocols that begin from nothing must broadcast, and broadcasts stop at routers.
questionsV2.recallLine: Machines on a newly routed ward segment get no addresses, though the same laptops lease instantly at headquarters and the link tests clean. Which explanation and fix BEST fit?

optionsShort.A: Scope exhausted; extend the address pool
optionsShort.B: Provider filters the traffic; request an exception
optionsShort.C: Client addressing unrecognized; renumber the ward
optionsShort.D: Routers drop broadcasts; add a relay agent

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Cannot survive the control case. An exhausted scope would refuse the same laptops at headquarters too, and exhaustion appears under load.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Contradicts the clean bidirectional link test. Without a relay, no lease traffic enters the WAN to be filtered at all.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Reverses DHCP's premise. Clients request precisely because they have no addressing, and scope selection follows the relay's tagged source.

questionsV2.question: A web server compromised through a plugin probed for a week without reaching the database. Which design property MOST directly accounts for the containment?

options.A: The inner screen permitted the web server one database port inward, so every other probe from it was dropped.
options.B: Address translation at the perimeter hid the internal numbering plan, leaving the attacker unable to identify any internal targets worth probing.
options.C: The portal host's hardening baseline had already removed the scanning and enumeration tooling an intruder would need to probe internal ranges.
options.D: The outer firewall's alerting brought the SOC in early, and its containment actions cut the probing short.

questionsV2.explanation:
The screened subnet earned its keep on the inward side. Its premise is that exposed hosts eventually fall, so the inner screen restricts what a fallen host may initiate: here, one database port to one destination (A). A week of probing becomes a week of drops at a policy boundary the attacker cannot alter from the web server.
Measure a DMZ by its inner rules. The design succeeds when a compromised exposed host finds almost nothing inward will answer it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A web server compromised through a plugin probed for a week without ever reaching the database. Which design property MOST directly accounts for the containment?

optionsShort.A: Inner screen permitted one port inward
optionsShort.B: Translation hid the internal numbering plan
optionsShort.C: Hardening had removed the enumeration tooling
optionsShort.D: Firewall alerting brought responders in early

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Overrates obscurity. Translation hides numbering from the outside, and the attacker was inside the DMZ, reading real addresses.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Worthwhile friction that cannot carry the outcome. Attackers fetch tooling, and hardening a host says nothing about where its packets go.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Contradicted by the timeline. A week of unimpeded probing is the opposite of early detection, and the stem credits design.

questionsV2.question: To justify replacing the scanners urgently, which statement of the obsolete standard's risk is MOST accurate?

options.A: WEP's short initialization vectors force keystream reuse, letting an attacker who captures traffic recover the key within minutes and join the network.
options.B: WEP's weakness is chiefly short passphrases, so configuring the longest supported key makes it acceptable for scanner traffic.
options.C: WEP's flaw is primarily its one-way authentication, so adding MAC-address filtering restores adequate protection for the warehouse fleet.
options.D: WEP's break requires prolonged physical access to an access point, so the risk stays confined to the warehouse floor and its equipment.

questionsV2.explanation:
The budget case has to survive technical challenge, and one statement does. WEP's 24-bit initialization vector space is so small that busy traffic repeats IVs quickly. RC4 keystream reuse and related-key weaknesses then yield the shared key to passive capture in minutes with public tooling, and the recovered key is the network key, so the attacker joins the same LAN the settlement traffic crosses (A). Mechanism, feasibility and consequence, each correct.
Argue legacy-crypto findings from the mechanism of the break. An accurate one-paragraph mechanism is what makes replace it now unanswerable.
questionsV2.recallLine: Warehouse scanners still run WEP, and the case for replacing them now must survive technical challenge. Which statement of that standard's risk is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Short IVs repeat; passive capture recovers key
optionsShort.B: Longest supported key makes it acceptable
optionsShort.C: Address filtering restores adequate protection
optionsShort.D: Breaking it needs prolonged physical access

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Misdiagnoses. The attacks recover whatever key is configured, and 104-bit keys fall the same way. A longer key fixes guessable secrets.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Pairs a real observation with a useless remedy. MAC filters fall to address spoofing in seconds, and a reviewer refutes it in a sentence.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Inverts the exposure. The attack is passive radio capture from anywhere in range, parking lot included.

questionsV2.question: Which switch capability MOST directly defeats a host announcing itself as the gateway?

options.A: Dynamic ARP inspection, validating ARP replies against trusted address bindings before forwarding them.
options.B: Port security, limiting each access port to a single learned hardware address at a time.
options.C: Storm control, rate-limiting the volume of broadcast and multicast traffic accepted on access ports.
options.D: 802.1X authentication, requiring devices to authenticate successfully before their switch port forwards any traffic.

questionsV2.explanation:
The technique is ARP spoofing: unsolicited or false ARP messages claim the gateway's IP maps to the attacker's MAC. Dynamic ARP inspection attacks it at the root (A). The switch checks every ARP reply against known-good IP-to-MAC bindings, typically from DHCP snooping, and drops the forgeries, so the poisoning never reaches victim caches. It works even against an authorized, already-admitted device.
Admission control and protocol validation are different layers. ARP spoofing is stopped by validating ARP.
questionsV2.recallLine: A penetration tester's laptop in a meeting room announced itself as the default gateway and silently proxied other hosts' traffic. Which switch capability MOST directly defeats that technique?

optionsShort.A: Validate address replies against trusted bindings
optionsShort.B: Port security: one address per port
optionsShort.C: Storm control rate-limits broadcast and multicast
optionsShort.D: 802.1X authentication before the port forwards

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Sounds apt and misses. The attacking laptop uses one MAC of its own, so a one-address limit is satisfied while the poisoning proceeds.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Governs traffic volume. Gratuitous ARP is a trickle, nowhere near storm thresholds.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: The strongest-sounding distractor. What it authenticates is admission, and a compromised authenticated host runs the identical attack.

questionsV2.question: Fragmented packets whose offsets overlap so they can never reassemble have crashed a legacy controller twice. Which attack does the evidence MOST specifically indicate?

options.A: Ping of death: fragments that reassemble into a datagram beyond the maximum legal size.
options.B: Smurf: amplified echo replies converging on the controller from a broadcast network.
options.C: Teardrop: deliberately overlapping fragment offsets that crash a vulnerable reassembly implementation.
options.D: SYN flood: connection requests that exhaust the controller's half-open session table.

questionsV2.explanation:
The IPS already isolated the discriminating feature: offsets that overlap. Teardrop-class attacks craft fragment sequences whose offset arithmetic is self-contradictory, and reassembly code that mishandles the overlap corrupts memory and crashes (C). Malformed input plus a crashing legacy stack is this evidence exactly.
Fragmentation attacks are told apart by their lever, oversize against overlap. Naming the lever turns an alert into the right remediation.
questionsV2.recallLine: Fragments whose offsets overlap so they can never reassemble have crashed a legacy controller twice. Which attack does the evidence MOST specifically indicate?

optionsShort.A: Ping of death: oversized reassembled datagram
optionsShort.B: Smurf: amplified echo replies converging inward
optionsShort.C: Teardrop: overlapping fragments crash reassembly
optionsShort.D: SYN flood: half-open session table exhausted

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The sibling fragmentation attack. Its lever is a reassembled datagram exceeding 65,535 bytes, a different check in the same reassembly path.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Fails on traffic type and mechanism both. A smurf is a flood of well-formed echo replies that saturates capacity, and it kills by volume.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: TCP state exhaustion: a rising tide of SYNs and half-open sessions, degrading service progressively.

questionsV2.question: Which approach MOST directly addresses the exhaustion mechanism behind the flood?

options.A: Block the flood's source addresses at the perimeter firewall as the SOC identifies them.
options.B: Raise the servers' connection-table limits so that more half-open sessions can be held at once.
options.C: Shorten the servers' keep-alive timers so established HTTP sessions are released sooner.
options.D: Enable SYN cookies, so the servers commit no connection state until a client's final handshake acknowledgment arrives.

questionsV2.explanation:
The flood's lever is asymmetry. Each spoofed SYN costs the attacker one packet and costs the server a table entry held open for a timeout.
SYN cookies remove the lever (D). The server answers with a SYN-ACK whose sequence number cryptographically encodes the pending connection, and stores nothing. State gets created only when a real client returns the final ACK. Spoofed SYNs, whose ACKs come from nowhere, now cost the server nothing, and legitimate handshakes complete normally.
Durable denial-of-service mitigations attack the attacker's asymmetry. Make the unverified party carry the cost of state and a flood of fakes loses its purchase.
questionsV2.recallLine: Spoofed connection attempts are filling the web tier's tables with half-open sessions while real patients time out. Which approach MOST directly addresses the exhaustion mechanism?

optionsShort.A: Block the flood's source addresses as identified
optionsShort.B: Raise the tables' limits to hold more
optionsShort.C: Shorten keep-alive timers on established sessions
optionsShort.D: Commit no state until the final acknowledgment

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Chases addresses that are forged and rotating. Each block lags the flood by design, and the rule base becomes its own exhaustion problem.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Enlarges the bucket under an open tap. The flood fills any finite table, minutes later.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Tunes the wrong lifecycle phase. Keep-alive governs established sessions after the handshake, and the damage here is all pre-establishment.

questionsV2.question: A partner campus eighteen router hops away must reroute within seconds. Which limitation of the proposed distance-vector protocol MOST justifies rejecting it?

options.A: RIP carries its routing updates in cleartext, so route advertisements can be captured and read off the wire by listeners.
options.B: RIP treats 16 hops as unreachable and converges slowly, so both the 18-hop path and the recovery target fail.
options.C: RIP requires a backbone-area hierarchy to scale, which a merged campus network would struggle to support.
options.D: RIP floods complete topology maps on every change, consuming bandwidth on the WAN links between the merged sites.

questionsV2.explanation:
RIP breaks both requirements at once (B). Its metric counts to 15, with 16 meaning unreachable, so an 18-hop destination is administratively nonexistent. Its periodic-update, distance-vector convergence takes minutes with hold-downs, and the target is seconds.
Reject a protocol on the requirements it measurably fails. For RIP that is its 15-hop diameter and its convergence time.
questionsV2.recallLine: A merged network must reach a segment eighteen router hops away and reroute within seconds. Which distance-vector limitation MOST justifies rejecting RIP?

optionsShort.A: Cleartext updates can be read off-wire
optionsShort.B: Sixteen means unreachable, and convergence crawls
optionsShort.C: Needs a backbone-area hierarchy to scale
optionsShort.D: Floods full topology maps on every change

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: A real hygiene concern. RIPv2 supports authentication, and confidentiality of advertisements is not among the stated requirements.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Belongs to the wrong protocol. The backbone-area design, area 0, is OSPF's architecture, and RIP has no areas at all.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Also describes the other family. Flooding link-state advertisements is OSPF and IS-IS behavior; RIP sends distance vectors.

questionsV2.question: A branch rule set permits all inbound traffic above port 1023 so replies can return. Which firewall capability MOST directly admits only genuine return traffic?

options.A: An application-layer proxy gateway terminating each session and re-originating it toward the destination on the client's behalf.
options.B: Restricting the inbound high-port rules to source addresses inside the ISP's own network space.
options.C: Stateful inspection, tracking outbound connections and admitting inbound packets that match an existing session.
options.D: Network address translation, hiding branch addressing behind a single public address at the perimeter.

questionsV2.explanation:
The gap is memory. A static packet filter judges each packet in isolation, so 'replies must get back in' degenerates into 'leave the high ports open'.
A stateful firewall records each outbound connection in a state table and admits inbound packets only when they correspond to a tracked session (C). That is word-for-word the reviewer's requirement, and it closes the hole without breaking return traffic.
A rule that has to remember something needs a device that keeps state.
questionsV2.recallLine: A branch rule set permits all inbound traffic above port 1023 so replies can return. Which firewall capability MOST directly admits only genuine return traffic?

optionsShort.A: Application proxy terminating and re-originating each session
optionsShort.B: Limit high ports to the ISP's addresses
optionsShort.C: Track outbound sessions; admit matching packets
optionsShort.D: Address translation behind one public address

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Would achieve it and more, since a proxy fully mediates the protocol. The heavier instrument, bought for content inspection.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Narrows who can exploit the standing hole. Any host in that ISP space still reaches branch high ports, and addresses can be spoofed.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Does incidentally drop unsolicited inbound flows for want of a translation entry. An addressing mechanism whose filtering is a side effect.

questionsV2.question: Which IPsec configuration BEST meets the trailer's requirements for hidden internal addresses and gateway-terminated cryptography?

options.A: Transport mode using AH, authenticating each packet's origin while leaving its payload readable in transit.
options.B: Tunnel mode using ESP, encrypting each original packet whole inside a new outer header between the gateways.
options.C: Transport mode using ESP, encrypting the payload while the original addresses stay visible for routing.
options.D: Tunnel mode using AH alone, protecting header integrity without concealing the packet contents.

questionsV2.explanation:
Two requirements decide this: hide internal addressing, and terminate the cryptography on the gateways. Tunnel mode encapsulates the entire original IP packet, internal source and destination included, inside a new packet addressed gateway-to-gateway. ESP encrypts that inner packet, so the carrier sees only the gateways talking (B). Tunnel-mode ESP is the standard site-to-site construction for exactly this reason.
Tunnel mode hides the original packet; transport mode hides its payload. Pick by whether topology itself is sensitive.
questionsV2.recallLine: The trailer's link must keep internal host addresses off the carrier network, with a gateway at each end terminating the cryptography. Which IPsec configuration BEST fits?

optionsShort.A: Transport AH: origin proven, payload readable
optionsShort.B: Tunnel ESP: whole packet wrapped and encrypted
optionsShort.C: Transport ESP: payload sealed, addresses visible
optionsShort.D: Tunnel AH: header integrity, no concealment

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Fails on both axes. Transport mode leaves the original header exposed, and AH gives authentication and integrity with no confidentiality.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Does encrypt the data. Transport mode preserves the original header, so the internal addresses ride the carrier network in the clear.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Wraps the packet and never encrypts it. AH-only tunnels prove origin and conceal nothing.

questionsV2.question: A live all-hands video will go to 2,000 desktops by multicast. Which protocol delivers the stream only where there are viewers?

options.A: IGMP, letting hosts join and leave multicast groups so the network forwards the stream to segments that have subscribers.
options.B: ICMP, reporting delivery errors and diagnostic information about the stream's path back to its source.
options.C: SNMP, letting the operations team watch link utilization on each distribution switch in real time while the broadcast is running.
options.D: BGP, advertising the multicast group's addresses outward to each of the campus routers ahead of the event.

questionsV2.explanation:
Multicast saves the core only if the network knows where the viewers are. IGMP is the membership protocol: hosts announce joining or leaving a group, and routers, with switches snooping the exchanges, replicate the stream solely onto segments holding subscribers (A). One copy in the core, fan-out at the edges, silence on segments with no viewers.
Efficient one-to-many delivery is two problems: replication, and audience discovery. The design fails without the second.
questionsV2.recallLine: A live all-hands video will reach 2,000 desktops by multicast. Which protocol makes the network carry the stream only where viewers actually are?

optionsShort.A: IGMP: hosts join and leave groups
optionsShort.B: ICMP: reports errors and path diagnostics
optionsShort.C: SNMP: watch link utilization during the event
optionsShort.D: BGP: advertise the group outward to routers

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Trades on the one-letter similarity. ICMP carries error and diagnostic messages, unreachables among them, and manages no group membership.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: How the team would watch the rollout succeed. Management-plane telemetry with no role in forwarding decisions.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Routes between autonomous systems at internet scale. An interior campus stream needs none of it, and BGP carries no membership.

questionsV2.question: Which routing protocol BEST fits a 60-site network needing fast reconvergence and regional aggregation, and why?

options.A: RIP, because a simple hop-count metric stays easy to reason about across all 60 sites.
options.B: Static routes pushed to every site by configuration management, avoiding dynamic routing protocols and their failure modes.
options.C: BGP, because a protocol that scales to the entire global internet will comfortably handle routing for a 60-site network.
options.D: OSPF, because routers recompute from a full topology map for fast reconvergence, and its areas match regional aggregation.

questionsV2.explanation:
Both requirements select link-state (D). OSPF routers share a synchronized topology map and recompute paths locally the moment a failure is flooded, which gives the seconds-scale reconvergence asked for. Its area hierarchy exists to summarize regions into a backbone, and the addressing plan maps onto it directly.
Interior networks needing fast failover want link-state protocols.
questionsV2.recallLine: A 60-site network needs reconvergence within seconds and routing that aggregates by region. Which routing protocol BEST fits, and for what reason?

optionsShort.A: RIP: hop count is easy to reason about
optionsShort.B: Static routes pushed by configuration management
optionsShort.C: BGP: it scales to the entire internet
optionsShort.D: OSPF: local recomputation, areas match regions

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Fails the speed requirement. Distance-vector convergence with hold-down timers runs to minutes, and hop count ignores link capacity.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Removes reconvergence altogether. Static routes do not react to failures, so within seconds becomes when an operator intervenes.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Capable, mis-reasoned and mis-fit. BGP is a path-vector policy protocol between autonomous systems, tuned for stability over speed.

questionsV2.question: Users will authenticate with directory passwords that must stay protected over the air. Which method BEST fits?

options.A: EAP-TLS, mutually authenticating the client and the server with X.509 certificates issued to each side.
options.B: EAP-MD5, hashing the password exchange so the credential itself is not transmitted over the air.
options.C: LEAP, using a lightweight proprietary vendor challenge-response protocol designed specifically for early wireless deployments.
options.D: PEAP, opening a server-authenticated TLS tunnel and passing the password exchange inside it.

questionsV2.explanation:
The constraints are explicit: password authentication, no client PKI, credentials protected over the air. PEAP is shaped to them (D). The client validates the server's certificate and builds a TLS tunnel, which puts one server-side certificate on the entire PKI bill, then runs the password exchange inside that encrypted, server-authenticated channel. Credentials neither travel exposed nor get offered to an impostor access point.
When passwords must cross wireless, wrap them in a server-authenticated tunnel. Read constraints as hard requirements: the strongest method is wrong when it needs infrastructure the design cannot have.
questionsV2.recallLine: Branch wireless is moving to 802.1X with directory passwords, no client certificate infrastructure and none budgeted. Which authentication method BEST protects those credentials over the air?

optionsShort.A: EAP-TLS: certificates issued to both sides
optionsShort.B: EAP-MD5: hashed challenge instead of password
optionsShort.C: LEAP: proprietary lightweight challenge-response
optionsShort.D: PEAP: password inside a server-authenticated tunnel

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: The stronger method and the wrong fit. Mutual certificate authentication needs a certificate per client, the PKI the stem rules out.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Fails the transit requirement it pretends to meet. An unprotected challenge-response hash invites offline guessing and proves no server.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: A broken legacy proprietary method whose challenge-response fell to practical cracking tools years ago.

questionsV2.question: The bank must block uploads to personal cloud storage and strip risky methods while allowing ordinary browsing. Which control is BEST suited to decisions at that level of detail?

options.A: A stateful inspection firewall filtering each connection by source address, destination address and destination port.
options.B: An access control list applied directly to the router at each branch office's internet uplink.
options.C: A circuit-level gateway that relays outbound TCP sessions to the internet after validating each connection handshake.
options.D: An application-layer proxy gateway that terminates sessions and applies policy to methods and content.

questionsV2.explanation:
The policy is written in the vocabulary of the application protocol: this HTTP method and not that one, this action on a site while the site itself stays permitted. Enforcement therefore takes a device that reads that vocabulary. An application-layer proxy terminates the client's session, sees full requests and payloads, and can strip a method or block an upload while passing the page view (D).
Match the enforcement point to the vocabulary the policy is written in.
questionsV2.recallLine: The bank must block uploads to personal cloud storage and strip risky HTTP methods while allowing ordinary browsing. Which control suits decisions at that level of detail?

optionsShort.A: Stateful firewall filtering addresses, ports, session state
optionsShort.B: Router access list at each branch uplink
optionsShort.C: Circuit-level gateway relaying validated TCP sessions
optionsShort.D: Proxy terminating sessions, judging methods and payloads

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: An excellent connection gatekeeper. Its decision space is addresses, ports and state, where upload and page view look identical.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: The same limitation with less. Stateless address-and-port matching at the uplink is right for coarse boundary hygiene and blind to content.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: One layer higher than a packet filter and still below the need. It vets and relays sessions without interpreting the data inside them.

questionsV2.question: Which configuration is MOST appropriate for the two application servers?

options.A: Transport mode using ESP, encrypting the payload end to end while the original IP headers route the packets.
options.B: Tunnel mode using ESP terminated on the data center's perimeter firewalls and not on the two servers themselves.
options.C: Tunnel mode using ESP running directly between the two servers, wrapping every packet inside a second, outer IP header.
options.D: Transport mode using AH, signing each packet so any modification in transit is detected on receipt.

questionsV2.explanation:
The communicating hosts are the security endpoints and the path between them is routable as it stands. Transport mode fits: ESP encrypts the payload, the original headers keep doing the routing, and no second IP header is added (A). Confidentiality at minimum overhead.
Mode follows the endpoints: hosts take transport, gateways take tunnel. Protocol follows the property needed: ESP for secrecy, AH for origin integrity alone.
questionsV2.recallLine: Two application servers in one data center must exchange settlement files confidentially, terminate the cryptography themselves, and add as little overhead as possible. Which configuration is MOST appropriate?

optionsShort.A: Transport ESP: payload sealed, original headers route
optionsShort.B: Tunnel ESP terminated on the perimeter firewalls
optionsShort.C: Tunnel ESP server to server, outer header added
optionsShort.D: Transport AH: tampering detected, contents readable

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Moves the crypto boundary to devices the requirement excluded. Firewall-terminated tunnels leave the server-to-firewall legs unprotected.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Works and protects the data, and it fails the stated tiebreaker. The redundant outer header carries the same addresses as the inner one.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Chooses the wrong service. AH detects tampering and transmits the settlement data readable, so confidentiality goes unmet.

questionsV2.question: Which design BEST implements the single hardened entry point for enclave administration?

options.A: Firewall rules permitting SSH and RDP only from administrators' registered workstations to the enclave hosts.
options.B: A bastion (jump) host in a controlled segment, the only source permitted to reach enclave management interfaces.
options.C: Individual VPN profiles on administrator laptops, each terminating inside the enclave's server network.
options.D: A dedicated management VLAN trunked from the administrators' desk switches into the enclave switches.

questionsV2.explanation:
The architecture asked for is a choke point: one hardened system every management session must traverse, where multi-factor authentication is enforced once and session logging is complete. That is a bastion or jump host, made effective by firewall policy that admits management traffic from it alone (B).
Privileged access wants concentration. Every additional path into a sensitive zone is a full copy of the risk.
questionsV2.recallLine: Every administrative session into the card-processing enclave must cross one hardened, fully logged entry point behind a second factor. Which design BEST implements that requirement?

optionsShort.A: Firewall rules from administrators' registered workstations
optionsShort.B: Jump host, the only source permitted inward
optionsShort.C: Per-laptop VPN profiles terminating inside the enclave
optionsShort.D: Management VLAN trunked from desk switches inward

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Creates as many entry points as there are administrators. One compromised desktop reaches the servers, and MFA must be replicated.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Multiplies entry points too, tunneled. A stolen laptop carries the enclave with it, and the sessions bypass any central recording.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Extends layer 2 adjacency across the boundary. A trunked VLAN is connectivity, with no authentication and no session capture.

questionsV2.question: After a circuit failed, two routers re-advertised the dead network to each other for minutes, the metric climbing. Which underlying behavior BEST explains the episode?

options.A: Each router floods a complete topology map after every change, so a failure generates duplicated route advertisements.
options.B: The two routers' update timers fell out of synchronization, so each advertised stale route information on a different periodic refresh cycle.
options.C: Routers see their neighbors' summarized distances but not the topology, so two of them can keep re-advertising a failed path.
options.D: The failed circuit kept flapping between up and down states, and every transition triggered a fresh advertisement.

questionsV2.explanation:
The stair-step metric is the fingerprint. In distance-vector routing no router sees the topology; each believes whatever distances its neighbors summarize (C). When the network died, each router took the other's stale advertisement as evidence of an alternate path and re-advertised it back one hop worse. The pair inflated the metric in lockstep until the protocol's infinity ceiling declared the route unreachable. That mutual loop is count-to-infinity, and it is why split horizon, poison reverse and a small maximum metric exist.
Routing by rumor fails by believing your own echo. Read a steadily inflating metric as count-to-infinity.
questionsV2.recallLine: After a circuit failed, two routers re-advertised the dead network to each other for minutes with the metric climbing. Which underlying behavior BEST explains the episode?

optionsShort.A: Each router floods a full topology map
optionsShort.B: Update timers drifted out of synchronization
optionsShort.C: Routers see neighbors' distances, not the topology
optionsShort.D: The circuit kept flapping up and down

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Describes the other protocol family. Link-state routers flood topology advertisements and would each compute the loss locally in seconds.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Blames scheduling for a structural problem. Timer alignment changes when stale routes are spoken, not why each router believes the other's.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Predicts a different trace. Flapping yields alternating advertisements, and this was a monotonic climb on a link that stayed dead.

questionsV2.question: Which point in the resolution chain was MOST likely compromised?

options.A: The bank's authoritative name servers, altered to serve the attacker's address for the portal's name.
options.B: The registrar account, with the domain's delegation quietly repointed at attacker-controlled name servers.
options.C: The recursive resolvers' caches, poisoned to return the attacker's address for the portal hostname.
options.D: The customers' local hosts files, each overwritten by malware to pin the portal to the attacker's address.

questionsV2.explanation:
Work the chain against the evidence. Answers are wrong at the clients, the zone's source of truth is clean, and the delegation still points at it. The corruption sits between authority and client, at the recursive resolver layer, where forged answers get cached and then served to every user of that resolver (C). That also explains many customers being hit through a shared point.
