DNS trouble localizes by comparing answers at each tier: client, resolver, authority. Cache poisoning lives in the middle tier that everyone shares.
questionsV2.recallLine: Customers get an attacker's address for the portal, though the bank's authoritative records and its registrar delegation are both verified intact. Which point was MOST likely compromised?

optionsShort.A: Bank's authoritative servers altered for that name
optionsShort.B: Registrar account repointed the domain's delegation
optionsShort.C: Recursive resolver caches serving forged answers
optionsShort.D: Customers' hosts files overwritten by malware

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Directly contradicted. The stem verifies the authoritative records unchanged; this is the finding in a zone-tampering incident.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Excluded by the intact delegation. A registrar hijack typically redirects the whole domain, visible in WHOIS and NS records.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Could produce identical symptoms on one machine, and it needs separate malware on every affected customer.

questionsV2.question: The manager wants every device authenticated against corporate identity before its traffic is admitted. Which control BEST meets that?

options.A: 802.1X port-based access control, with a RADIUS server validating each device's credentials or certificate.
options.B: Static MAC-address filtering, maintained by hand by the network team for every access port in the building.
options.C: Assignment of all the lobby wall jacks to a segregated guest VLAN restricted to internet access.
options.D: DHCP reservations for known machines, so unrecognized devices receive no usable address.

questionsV2.explanation:
The requirement has two parts: authenticate against corporate identity, and enforce before any traffic passes. 802.1X pairs them (A). The switch port stays closed to everything except the authentication exchange until the RADIUS server accepts the device's credentials or certificate, so admission becomes an identity decision.
Enforcement sits at the point of connection and keys on identity. Anything that filters after admission, or keys on spoofable attributes, is a courtesy.
questionsV2.recallLine: A lobby audit found unauthenticated devices receiving corporate addresses, and every device must now prove corporate identity before its traffic is admitted. Which control BEST meets that?

optionsShort.A: Port-based control, with RADIUS vetting every device
optionsShort.B: Hand-maintained address filtering on every port
optionsShort.C: Lobby jacks moved to a guest internet VLAN
optionsShort.D: DHCP reservations, so strangers get nothing usable

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Identity by hardware address, which is no identity. MACs are observed on the wire and spoofed in seconds, and a hand-kept list decays.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: Worthwhile containment, and it pairs well as the destination for failed authentications. On its own it authenticates nobody.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Merely declines to hand out configuration. A visitor who statically assigns an address bypasses it entirely, since the port forwards freely.

questionsV2.question: Audits keep finding branch firewall and routing policies drifting from the corporate standard. Which capability MOST directly addresses that?

options.A: It replaces the branches' broadband and LTE circuits with uniformly provisioned MPLS.
options.B: It raises each branch's usable bandwidth by bonding whatever links the site has available.
options.C: It applies centrally defined policy to every branch edge device, independent of each site's underlying transport.
options.D: It encrypts traffic between branches using keys that each site's edge device manages for itself.

questionsV2.explanation:
The finding is configuration drift: 200 hand-tended devices diverging from standard. The SD-WAN property that answers it is the separation of control plane from transport (C). Policy is authored once in the orchestrator and pushed to every edge, so the architecture enforces the standard and an audit compares every site against one source of truth. Independent of transport is what lets one policy span MPLS, broadband and LTE alike.
Recurring drift across many sites is a management-plane problem. Buy centralization of control.
questionsV2.recallLine: Audits keep finding branch firewall and routing policies drifting from the corporate standard across 200 hand-tended edge devices. Which SD-WAN capability MOST directly addresses that finding?

optionsShort.A: Replace branch circuits with uniformly provisioned MPLS
optionsShort.B: Bond the site's links to raise bandwidth
optionsShort.C: Central policy to every edge, any transport
optionsShort.D: Encrypt between branches with locally managed keys

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Reverses SD-WAN's economics. The technology exists to use cheap heterogeneous links safely, and uniform circuits would stop no local drift.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: A genuine SD-WAN benefit aimed at a different complaint. More bandwidth fixes congestion findings.

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: Undercuts itself in the second clause. Per-site self-managed keying is exactly the decentralization the finding indicts.

questionsV2.question: Which control MOST directly provides that assurance to resolvers?

options.A: DNS over HTTPS between customers' machines and their resolvers, encrypting every query and response in transit.
options.B: Shorter TTL values on the bank's records, so poisoned cache entries expire and are replaced more quickly.
options.C: Restricting zone transfers so that the bank's own secondary name servers can copy the zone.
options.D: DNSSEC on the bank's zone, publishing signed records that resolvers validate for origin and integrity.

questionsV2.explanation:
The requirement is data authenticity: proof that an answer is what the zone owner published. That is DNSSEC's exact function (D). Records are cryptographically signed in a chain anchored at the root, so a validating resolver detects a forged or altered answer whichever cache or path supplied it.
Encrypting the channel and signing the data are different guarantees. Only signatures survive whatever path the data took.
questionsV2.recallLine: The architect must let resolvers verify that answers for the bank's zone are genuine and unmodified, wherever those answers were obtained. Which control MOST directly provides that?

optionsShort.A: DNS over HTTPS from clients to resolvers
optionsShort.B: Shorter record lifetimes, so poison expires sooner
optionsShort.C: Restrict zone transfers to the bank's secondaries
optionsShort.D: DNSSEC: signed records, validated on receipt

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Protects a different property on a different segment. A poisoned resolver serves its forgery over beautifully encrypted transport.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Shrinks the damage window and adds no verification. Poison expires sooner and can be re-inserted.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Guards bulk zone disclosure and copy integrity between the bank's own servers. Resolvers can verify nothing from it.

questionsV2.question: A branch design justifies no inbound filtering because the site is behind address translation. Which evaluation of that is MOST accurate?

options.A: NAT is equivalent to a stateful firewall, since both maintain per-connection state tables that gate what may enter the network.
options.B: NAT obscures internal addressing and incidentally drops unsolicited inbound traffic, but enforcing security policy still requires a firewall.
options.C: NAT reduces security overall, because rewriting packet headers strips the very fields that inspection devices depend on.
options.D: NAT gives translated sessions confidentiality, since outside observers see the rewritten public addresses on the wire.

questionsV2.explanation:
NAT was built to stretch IPv4 addresses. It rewrites headers and keeps translation state so replies find their way back. Two side effects look like security: internal numbering is invisible outside, and unsolicited inbound packets die for lack of a mapping (B).
Side effects carry no policy. No rule language, and no logging designed for security decisions. The protection evaporates wherever mappings exist: port forwards, hairpins, protocol helpers. It evaporates wherever traffic is solicited, which is how phishing-delivered malware connects out and NAT obligingly sustains the session. What is missing is enforced, auditable policy, and that is a firewall's job.
Classify controls by what they were designed to decide. NAT decides address rewriting.
questionsV2.recallLine: A branch design leaves out inbound filtering on the grounds that the site sits behind address translation. Which evaluation of that justification is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Equivalent to a stateful firewall; both keep state
optionsShort.B: Hides addressing incidentally; policy still needs enforcing
optionsShort.C: Reduces security: rewriting strips fields inspection needs
optionsShort.D: Gives sessions confidentiality behind the public address

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The equivalence the design note depends on, and it fails at the definition. Both keep state; only one consults policy.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Manufactures a downside from a real nuisance. NAT complicates some inspection and end-to-end protocols, which is not a net reduction.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Confuses hiding an address with protecting a payload. Translated traffic is as readable in transit as any other cleartext.

questionsV2.question: As an interim measure using only the existing access switches, which control MOST directly curbs the mini-switches?

options.A: Reassign the affected wall jacks into an isolated guest VLAN limited to internet access.
options.B: Configure port security, limiting each access port to a small fixed number of learned hardware addresses.
options.C: Deploy 802.1X authentication on every access port, with each connecting device's credentials checked against the corporate directory service.
options.D: Enable DHCP snooping, blocking lease offers that originate from any port not designated as a server port.

questionsV2.explanation:
A desk mini-switch shows up as several source MAC addresses on one access port, and port security acts on exactly that signal (B). Cap the learned addresses at one or two, violate into shutdown or restrict, and the fan-out stops working the moment a second device speaks. It is configured on the switches already in place, which honors both constraints.
Pick controls whose trigger condition matches the behavior you want to stop. Multiple hardware addresses on one port is the fingerprint here.
questionsV2.recallLine: Staff at a branch with no certificate infrastructure are fanning wall jacks out with unmanaged mini-switches. Using only the existing access switches, which control MOST directly curbs that?

optionsShort.A: Move the jacks to a guest internet VLAN
optionsShort.B: Cap learned addresses on each access port
optionsShort.C: Authenticate every port against the directory
optionsShort.D: DHCP snooping, blocking offers from user ports

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Changes what the extra devices can reach and leaves them free to connect. The mini-switch keeps working inside the guest VLAN.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: The better end-state and the wrong answer today. 802.1X needs the RADIUS infrastructure the stem rules out.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Watches a different protocol. Snooping polices rogue DHCP servers; personal laptops taking leases through a mini-switch never trip it.

questionsV2.question: Which measure BEST keeps the promotional site available through the spike and the attack traffic?

options.A: Double the origin's web servers behind the existing load balancer ahead of the launch window.
options.B: Add a second internet circuit at the origin data center, roughly doubling the total ingress bandwidth available for the launch.
options.C: Set aggressive browser-caching headers, so returning visitors render the promotional pages from their own local caches.
options.D: Front the site with a content delivery network, serving cached content from edge locations near the traffic's sources.

questionsV2.explanation:
Fiftyfold plus a flood is a scale problem no single origin can meet at the origin. A content delivery network moves the serving edge outward (D). Promotional content is cached across many distributed points, each visitor is served nearby, and the legitimate spike and the volumetric attack traffic both spread across the provider's aggregate capacity. The origin keeps its architecture and sees a trickle of cache fills. Static promotional content is the ideal cacheable workload, and nothing gets re-platformed.
Availability at internet scale comes from distributing where demand is absorbed. Capacity added at a single point is spent the moment the internet aims at it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A fiftyfold spike plus probable volumetric attack is heading for a promotional site served from one origin that cannot be re-platformed. Which measure BEST keeps it available?

optionsShort.A: Double the origin's web servers before launch
optionsShort.B: Add a second circuit at the origin
optionsShort.C: Aggressive browser caching for returning visitors
optionsShort.D: Serve cached copies from edge locations nearby

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Buys 2x against 50x, and compute was never the choke point a volumetric flood aims at. The pipe is.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Widens that pipe finitely and leaves every packet converging on one location. Volumetric attacks are sized in multiples of any circuit pair.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Helps visitors already served once, and launch traffic is first visits by definition. Attack tools ignore cache headers entirely.

questionsV2.question: Which wireless configuration MOST directly removes the offline guessing exposure?

options.A: WPA2-Personal with a forty-character random passphrase that is rotated every week.
options.B: WPA3-Personal, whose SAE exchange gives a captured handshake no material for offline password guessing.
options.C: Hiding the staff SSID from broadcast and filtering client hardware addresses at each access point.
options.D: WPA2 with TKIP disabled, so every access point requires AES-CCMP for the data frames.

questionsV2.explanation:
The exposure is structural to WPA2-PSK. Its four-way handshake lets anyone who captures it test passphrase guesses offline, off the air, at hardware speed.
Simultaneous Authentication of Equals (SAE) redesigns the exchange so each guess takes a live interaction with the network (B). A capture yields nothing to grind on, which removes the offline attack as a class.
When an attack is inherent to a protocol's design, the fix is the successor protocol that redesigned the exchange.
questionsV2.recallLine: Attackers in the crowd captured four-way handshakes from the shared-passphrase network and ground on them offline at leisure. Which wireless configuration MOST directly removes that exposure?

optionsShort.A: WPA2-Personal, forty-character passphrase rotated weekly
optionsShort.B: WPA3-Personal, whose SAE exchange yields nothing capturable
optionsShort.C: Hide the SSID and filter hardware addresses
optionsShort.D: WPA2 with TKIP disabled, AES-CCMP required

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: Respectable hardening, and the best available where WPA3 hardware cannot be had. The captured handshake stays attackable offline.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Visibility theater. SSIDs appear in probe frames anyway, MAC filters fall to trivial spoofing, and neither touches the handshake.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Hardens the data cipher. The dictionary attack targets the key derivation.

questionsV2.question: Which protocol change MOST directly prevents the replayed authorization being accepted a second time?

options.A: Upgrading to a stronger cipher, so captured authorization messages take far longer to decrypt.
options.B: Rotating the encryption keys used by each ATM on a daily schedule instead of monthly.
options.C: Hashing each message body, so any modification made to it in transit is detected on receipt.
options.D: Adding timestamps and sequence numbers that the processing center validates, so a repeated message is recognized and refused.

questionsV2.explanation:
This is a replay attack, and the lesson is that the attacker read nothing. A captured ciphertext, re-sent intact, is decrypted and honored like the original. The missing property is freshness: the receiver cannot tell a first presentation from a repeat.
Validated timestamps, sequence numbers or nonces supply it (D), and make the duplicate detectably stale.
Confidentiality, integrity and freshness are separate guarantees. A protocol can encrypt and authenticate flawlessly and still pay twice, until something in each message proves it is new.
questionsV2.recallLine: Testers re-sent a captured, fully encrypted withdrawal authorization an hour later and the processing center paid out again. Which protocol change MOST directly prevents that second acceptance?

optionsShort.A: Stronger cipher, so decryption takes longer
optionsShort.B: Rotate each machine's keys daily, not monthly
optionsShort.C: Hash each body so modification is detected
optionsShort.D: Timestamps and counters the center validates

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Strengthens a lock the attacker never picks. Replay works on unread ciphertext, so cipher strength is orthogonal.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Narrows the replay window to the key's lifetime, and an hour-old message sails through a daily rotation.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Protects integrity, and the replayed message is unmodified, so a hash over it verifies perfectly and endorses the fraud.

questionsV2.question: Packets shuttled between two misconfigured routers until a header field reached zero and an error returned. Which mechanism limited the damage?

options.A: The TCP retransmission timer, which bounds how long any unacknowledged segment stays in flight before the sending host finally gives up.
options.B: The fragmentation offset field, which forces malformed or oversized packets to be discarded at each hop along the forwarding path they traverse.
options.C: The IP time-to-live field, decremented at each router so that packets caught in forwarding loops are eventually discarded.
options.D: The Ethernet frame check sequence, which discards any frame whose contents were corrupted somewhere in transit between two directly adjacent devices.

questionsV2.explanation:
The capture narrates the mechanism: a field decreasing at each router, a discard when it runs out, and time-exceeded notifications. That is the IP time-to-live field, the hop limit in IPv6 (C). Every forwarding hop decrements it, so a routing loop degrades into discarded packets and error messages instead of a link-saturating storm of immortal traffic. The mutual default routes made the loop; TTL made it survivable. Traceroute exploits the same expiry deliberately.
Networks assume routing will sometimes be wrong, so packets carry a hop budget. Read TTL expiry and time-exceeded backscatter as a loop being safely bled off.
questionsV2.recallLine: Packets shuttled between two misconfigured routers until a header field reached zero and an error was returned to the sender. Which mechanism limited the damage?

optionsShort.A: TCP retransmission timer bounding unacknowledged segments
optionsShort.B: Fragmentation offset field discarding malformed packets
optionsShort.C: IP time-to-live, decremented at every hop
optionsShort.D: Ethernet frame check sequence catching corruption

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: Lives in the endpoints. Retransmission timers govern when a sender tries again and cannot expire a packet already circling between routers.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: A reassembly bookkeeping field. Fragmentation offsets count no hops and expire no looping datagrams.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Checks integrity per link. The shuttling packets were perfectly intact, and corruption detection has no opinion about forwarding sanity.

questionsV2.question: Engineering proposes split tunneling to relieve saturated concentrators. What is the MOST accurate statement of the trade-off?

options.A: The tunnel's cryptography is weakened, because the concentrator must maintain two separate policies for every connected client.
options.B: There is no meaningful change, because traffic to the corporate ranges remains encrypted exactly as it was before the split tunnel was introduced.
options.C: Exposure is doubled, because corporate traffic now traverses both the tunnel and the public internet on every request.
options.D: Corporate traffic stays protected, but the endpoint's internet traffic bypasses corporate inspection while the device holds a path into the internal network.

questionsV2.explanation:
A trade-off statement names what is gained and what is genuinely given up. Split tunneling leaves the corporate flow encrypted and relieves the concentrators. It also sends the endpoint's general internet traffic outside the corporate security stack, past web filtering, data loss prevention and monitoring, on a device that simultaneously holds an authenticated route into the LAN (D). A browser compromise then sits one hop from the internal network with the defenses unsighted.
Evaluate tunneling changes by where traffic stops being watched. Protection and visibility are separate properties.
questionsV2.recallLine: Engineering proposes split tunneling to relieve saturated remote-access concentrators. What is the MOST accurate statement of the trade-off that change makes?

optionsShort.A: Cryptography weakens under two policies per client
optionsShort.B: No real change; corporate traffic stays encrypted
optionsShort.C: Exposure doubles: everything takes both paths
optionsShort.D: Corporate flow protected; browsing escapes corporate inspection

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Invents a cryptographic cost. Policy routing decides which packets enter the tunnel and leaves the cipher untouched.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: The engineer's half-truth. The encryption claim is correct, and it ignores the inspection bypass, which is the whole trade-off.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Reverses the mechanism. Corporate traffic still travels only the tunnel, and nothing is sent twice.

questionsV2.question: Which statement of the push-button setup risk is MOST accurate?

options.A: It weakens the encryption in use, forcing access points to fall back from AES to TKIP for all clients.
options.B: It broadcasts the network passphrase in cleartext during every new client association handshake, so anyone capturing the exchange can read it directly.
options.C: Its PIN can be brute-forced in hours because each half is validated separately, after which the passphrase is recoverable.
options.D: It lets joining clients bypass captive-portal authentication on nearby guest wireless networks that gate access through a web page.

questionsV2.explanation:
Findings survive challenge only when the mechanism is stated correctly. WPS's external-PIN design confirms the two halves of its eight-digit PIN independently, which collapses the search space to a few thousand tries per half. An online brute force completes in hours, and the protocol then hands over the network passphrase (C). That is why disable WPS is standard remediation.
State the mechanism exactly. A finding that gets the mechanism wrong dies in review, and takes the remediation with it.
questionsV2.recallLine: Consumer access points in the offices have push-button setup enabled, and the finding must survive a vendor's challenge. Which statement of that risk is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Forces a fallback from AES to TKIP
optionsShort.B: Broadcasts the passphrase at every association
optionsShort.C: PIN halves checked separately, passphrase then recoverable
optionsShort.D: Bypasses captive portals on nearby guest networks

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Invents a cipher interaction. WPS automates enrollment and has no effect on the AES or TKIP suite the access point negotiates.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Also misstates the mechanism. The passphrase is delivered inside the WPS exchange after PIN authentication, not broadcast in the clear.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Connects WPS to captive portals, which are unrelated web-layer gating on open networks.

questionsV2.question: Which response to the network team's argument about individual accounts is MOST accurate?

options.A: The team is right: per-administrator accountability addresses the principal risk, which is untraceable shared access to devices.
options.B: The team is right if management traffic is confined to a dedicated VLAN, since that separation is functionally equivalent to encryption.
options.C: The team is wrong: Telnet carries those individual credentials and every session in cleartext, so interception yields working administrator access; replace it with SSH.
options.D: The team is wrong about switches but right about routers, which sit behind the perimeter and face less interception risk.

questionsV2.explanation:
The argument defends the wrong property. TACACS+ gives attribution: who logged in, what they typed. Telnet transmits the login and the session as cleartext on the wire, so anyone positioned to capture branch traffic collects the very credentials the accounting system so carefully individualizes, plus every configuration detail that scrolls by (C). Accountability and confidentiality are independent, and SSH is the encrypted equivalent that preserves the TACACS+ model intact.
Evaluate a protocol against each property separately. Knowing who logged in does not answer who else was reading.
questionsV2.recallLine: The network team argues per-administrator accounts make managing routers and switches over an unencrypted terminal protocol acceptable. Which response to that argument is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Right: accountability was the principal risk
optionsShort.B: Right if management traffic gets its own VLAN
optionsShort.C: Wrong: those logins cross in clear; use SSH
optionsShort.D: Wrong for switches, tolerable for routers

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: Names a real risk that Telnet with TACACS+ does solve, then stops one property short. Attribution of readable sessions is cold comfort.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: The segmentation-equals-encryption fallacy. A management VLAN narrows who is positioned to listen, and whoever gets there reads everything.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Invents a perimeter distinction with no basis. Both device classes carry credentials in the clear, and interception risk follows the path.

questionsV2.question: An external scan shows a remote-shell port open on forty hosts, permitted inbound from any source. Which risk assessment is MOST accurate?

options.A: The exposure is minor, because the service listening on that port encrypts every session between client and server.
options.B: Forty hosts offer remote administrative shells to the whole internet; that access belongs behind one hardened, MFA-protected entry point.
options.C: A false positive in effect: an open port carries no real risk until a vulnerability is published for the service.
options.D: The principal risk is information disclosure through service banners, which changing the daemon's banner text will resolve.

questionsV2.explanation:
Port 22 is SSH, which is remote administrative shell access. So the finding reads: forty separately maintained doors to command-line control, reachable by every address on the internet, each accepting credential-guessing at line rate and each exposed to the next pre-auth vulnerability in its daemon.
Collapse the surface to a single bastion with multi-factor authentication, logging, and firewall rules admitting enclave SSH from it alone (B). Forty exposures become one instrumented chokepoint.
Assess an open port by the capability behind it and the audience in front of it.
questionsV2.recallLine: An external scan shows a remote administrative shell port open on forty hosts, permitted inbound from any source. Which risk assessment is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Minor: the service encrypts every session
optionsShort.B: Forty global shells; collapse behind one door
optionsShort.C: No real risk until a vulnerability appears
optionsShort.D: Banner disclosure; reword the daemon's banner

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Mistakes the session's property for the exposure's. Encryption protects traffic from observers and says nothing about who may connect.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Inverts the discipline. Brute force works against weak credentials with no advisory required, and waiting concedes the race.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Trims the leaf. Banners ease reconnaissance slightly, and rewording them changes no attacker's ability to connect.

questionsV2.question: Which control MOST directly protects the telephony signaling traffic?

options.A: Transporting SIP over TLS, so call setup and teardown exchanges are encrypted between the endpoints and call servers.
options.B: Enabling SRTP, so the media streams carrying the audio between endpoints are encrypted and authenticated.
options.C: Moving the handsets onto a dedicated voice VLAN, separated from the workstation segments of the LAN.
options.D: Enforcing 802.1X on handset ports, so each telephone authenticates before joining the branch network.

questionsV2.explanation:
What leaked is signaling: the SIP conversation that sets calls up and tears them down. Encrypt that channel (A). SIP over TLS wraps the setup exchange, hiding numbers, extensions and, critically, the session keys the endpoints negotiate for the media.
Telephony has two channels and two protections: TLS for the signaling, SRTP for the media. Encrypt one and the other stays exposed.
questionsV2.recallLine: A red-team capture showed telephony call-setup traffic in clear: dialed numbers, extensions and negotiated session parameters. Which control MOST directly protects that signaling?

optionsShort.A: SIP setup carried over TLS
optionsShort.B: SRTP encrypting the audio media streams
optionsShort.C: Dedicated voice VLAN away from workstations
optionsShort.D: 802.1X authenticating handsets before they join

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Guards the other half of a call. SRTP encrypts the audio stream, and unprotected signaling can expose the very keys SRTP depends on.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Reduces who can easily reach the packets. A VLAN is containment, and traffic inside the voice VLAN stays cleartext to anyone who gets there.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Governs which devices may join. An authorized but compromised host still reads cleartext signaling.

questionsV2.question: Which attack sequence BEST explains the drops, reconnections and warnings together?

options.A: A deauthentication flood pushed clients off the legitimate network so they would re-associate to an evil twin carrying the same SSID.
options.B: A WPS PIN attack recovered the staff passphrase overnight, after which the attacker quietly joined the staff network as one more ordinary client.
options.C: Wideband jamming across the festival Wi-Fi channels overwhelmed the access points and temporarily forced the staff handhelds onto their cellular fallback connectivity.
options.D: DHCP pool exhaustion on the staff network denied new leases until the access points were power-cycled by staff.

questionsV2.explanation:
A good explanation covers every observation. Forged deauthentication frames account for the sudden drop. Auto-rejoin plus a stronger same-SSID signal accounts for clients landing on the impostor. Traffic now traversing an attacker's network accounts for the TLS certificate warnings. The deauth-then-evil-twin sequence strings all three together (A), corroborated by the survey.
Certificate warnings after an unexplained Wi-Fi bounce are the signature of traffic re-homed through an impostor.
questionsV2.recallLine: Handhelds dropped off, rejoined by themselves, then showed certificate warnings, while a survey found a stronger second network broadcasting the staff name. Which sequence BEST explains that?

optionsShort.A: Deauthentication flood, then re-association to an impostor
optionsShort.B: WPS PIN attack recovered the staff passphrase
optionsShort.C: Wideband jamming pushed handhelds onto cellular
optionsShort.D: DHCP pool exhaustion denied new leases

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Explains at most a quiet attacker presence on the real network. A joined client causes no mass disconnects, and WPS is access-point side.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Fails on the reconnect. Jammed handhelds falling back to cellular would not re-associate, and jamming advertises no second staff SSID.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: An availability fault with the wrong footprint: no drop of already-associated clients, no rogue SSID, no TLS warnings.

questionsV2.question: Which statement BEST captures the primary risk the unlabeled access point creates?

options.A: The open network lets passers-by consume the corporate internet connection's bandwidth without any usage accounting.
options.B: The device's radio may interfere with the sanctioned access points operating on nearby channels in the same band.
options.C: It creates an unauthenticated radio bridge into the wired LAN that bypasses the perimeter and network access controls.
options.D: Its consumer firmware will fall behind on security patches, since no one in the organization owns its ongoing maintenance.

questionsV2.explanation:
Rank the harms and one dwarfs the rest. An open access point bridged to the corporate wired network extends that network, unauthenticated, into radio range (C). Anyone in the parking lot obtains what amounts to an inside jack: behind the firewall, behind admission control, invisible to perimeter monitoring. Nullifying the boundary architecture is why rogue access points are treated as incidents.
Severity ranking asks what the finding gives an attacker. Interior network access from outside the walls outranks every operational side effect.
questionsV2.recallLine: A survey found an unlabeled consumer access point plugged into a corporate wall jack behind a printer, broadcasting an open network. Which statement BEST captures the primary risk?

optionsShort.A: Passers-by consume bandwidth with no accounting
optionsShort.B: Its radio interferes with sanctioned access points
optionsShort.C: Unauthenticated radio bridge past every perimeter control
optionsShort.D: Unowned consumer firmware falls behind on patches

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Real, and trivial by comparison. Bandwidth and acceptable use would top the list for an access point isolated from every corporate asset.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: An airtime-management concern for the wireless team. Interference degrades performance and confers no access.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: A genuine secondary finding, since unowned devices do rot. Unmanaged lifecycle is the chronic issue; the open bridge is the acute one.

questionsV2.question: Ransomware at a subsidiary is traced to a remote desktop port opened for a vendor and forgotten. Which pairing of lesson and remediation is MOST appropriate?

options.A: The password policy failed; require substantially longer and more complex vendor-account passwords, rotated regularly, while keeping the existing access path unchanged.
options.B: Vendor management failed; terminate the vendor's contract and permanently disable the account that was brute-forced.
options.C: External visibility failed; raise the frequency of the bank's perimeter vulnerability scanning so that temporary firewall openings are discovered and closed sooner.
options.D: Remote desktop was internet-reachable; move it behind an MFA-protected gateway and give every firewall exception an owner and expiry.

questionsV2.explanation:
Port 3389 is RDP, interactive desktop control, and the causal chain has two links a report must break. The service was exposed to the whole internet, and the exposure was created ad hoc with no expiry, so it outlived its purpose silently.
One answer fixes both (D). Remote desktop reachable only through an authenticated, MFA-protected gateway ends internet-facing password guessing as an access route, and exceptions carrying owners and expiry dates end the temporary-and-forgotten pattern that created the target.
Incident lessons should name the decision that created the exposure. Administrative interfaces belong behind authenticated gateways, and every temporary rule needs a mechanism that ends it.
questionsV2.recallLine: Ransomware at a subsidiary is traced to a remote desktop port opened for a vendor and forgotten. Which pairing of lesson and remediation is MOST appropriate?

optionsShort.A: Longer vendor passwords, same access path
optionsShort.B: Terminate the vendor; disable the account
optionsShort.C: Scan the perimeter far more often
optionsShort.D: Behind a gateway; exceptions get owners, expiry

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Hardens the credential and preserves the exposure. Longer passwords slow guessing against a service that should not be reachable.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Punishes a party the analysis does not blame. The vendor needed access, the bank chose the mechanism, and the pattern survives.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Buys faster discovery of mistakes the process will keep making. Worth having as the compensating control, not as the lesson.

questionsV2.question: Which control MOST directly prevents an eavesdropper recovering conversation content from captured streams?

options.A: SIP over TLS, encrypting the call-setup channel between the handsets and the call servers.
options.B: SRTP, encrypting and authenticating the media streams that actually carry the audio.
options.C: Disabling port mirroring on branch switches except during approved troubleshooting windows.
options.D: Transcoding calls with a proprietary audio codec so captured streams resist casual decoding.

questionsV2.explanation:
The recovered artifact is audio, and audio travels in the media stream, RTP, separate from signaling. SRTP encrypts and integrity-protects the media packets themselves (B), so a mirrored copy yields ciphertext wherever it was collected.
Protect the data, not the vantage point. Cleartext on the wire always leaves somewhere to stand and listen.
questionsV2.recallLine: Recorded call audio was reassembled from a mirrored switch port. Which control MOST directly prevents an eavesdropper recovering conversation content from captured streams?

optionsShort.A: SIP over TLS protecting the setup channel
optionsShort.B: SRTP encrypting and authenticating the media packets
optionsShort.C: Disable port mirroring outside approved windows
optionsShort.D: Transcode calls with a proprietary codec

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The complement. TLS on SIP hides call metadata and protects key negotiation, and the audio still travels unencrypted while SRTP is off.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Attacks one collection method. Taps, compromised switches or any on-path position hear the same cleartext.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Obscurity with a shelf life. Codecs are identified from RTP headers and decoders are public or reversible.

questionsV2.question: Which characterization of the label-switched service is MOST accurate?

options.A: MPLS encrypts each labeled packet between the provider's edge routers using carrier-managed keys.
options.B: MPLS separates customers' traffic using labels but applies no encryption, so confidentiality rests on trust in the provider.
options.C: MPLS wraps traffic in IPsec automatically whenever a label-switched path crosses the provider's shared core.
options.D: MPLS varies each packet's path through the core unpredictably, which makes interception impractical in the first place.

questionsV2.explanation:
MPLS is a forwarding technology. Labels steer each customer's packets down its own label-switched paths and keep tenants' traffic logically separated across a shared core, and the payload rides exactly as submitted: cleartext in, cleartext through (B). Private here means separated, and confidentiality reduces to trusting the provider's staff, equipment and interconnects. The consequence is standard: run IPsec or TLS over the MPLS service for data that matters.
Like the private APN before it, a carrier's private network is a separation claim. Ask who could read the payload, and encrypt at a layer you control when the answer includes anyone but you.
questionsV2.recallLine: A carrier calls its label-switched service a private network on which encryption is unnecessary. Which characterization of what that service actually provides is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Encrypts labeled packets with carrier-managed keys
optionsShort.B: Labels separate tenants; confidentiality rests on trust
optionsShort.C: Wraps traffic in IPsec across the core automatically
optionsShort.D: Unpredictable paths make interception impractical

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Asserts a service plain MPLS has no mechanism to perform. Label operations are header manipulation, and no carrier keys touch the payload.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Imagines a default that does not exist. IPsec over MPLS is the customer-side overlay the accurate characterization leads to.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Inverts MPLS's behavior to manufacture comfort. Traffic engineering makes paths deterministic, and one observer reads everything.

questionsV2.question: Echo replies arrive from hundreds of hosts the group never contacted, each having received requests appearing to come from it. Which technique BEST explains this traffic pattern?

options.A: A SYN flood launched against the bank's internet gateway with the university's address space forged as the source of every packet.
options.B: A teardrop attack sending overlapping packet fragments through many separate hosts inside the university network.
options.C: A smurf attack, in which echo requests forged with the bank's address reached a broadcast address and every host replied.
options.D: A ping sweep of the bank's public address range conducted from a set of compromised university hosts.

questionsV2.explanation:
Every detail is the smurf signature (C). The victim receives echo replies it never solicited, so its address was forged on someone else's requests. The repliers are ordinary legitimate hosts, so they were used as amplifiers. They all sit in one network, so one broadcast-addressed request reached them at once. One spoofed request, hundreds of replies.
Read amplification attacks from the victim's inbox. Unsolicited replies from many honest hosts in one network mean your address was borrowed and a broadcast did the multiplying.
questionsV2.recallLine: Echo replies arrive from hundreds of hosts the group never contacted, each having received requests that appeared to come from it. Which technique BEST explains the pattern?

optionsShort.A: SYN flood with the university's addresses forged
optionsShort.B: Teardrop fragments sent through many hosts
optionsShort.C: Smurf: forged requests hit a broadcast address
optionsShort.D: Ping sweep from compromised university hosts

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Has the spoofing backwards and the protocol wrong. A SYN flood shows TCP SYNs arriving, and forged addresses send backscatter elsewhere.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: A malformed-fragment crash attack against one target's reassembly code. Nothing about it recruits hundreds of repliers.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Would produce echo requests arriving at the bank and replies flowing back out. The observed direction is inverted.

questionsV2.question: Which remote-access approach BEST fits auditors who cannot install software and work from networks allowing only web ports?

options.A: An IPsec VPN, with a preconfigured client software profile distributed to each visiting auditor before the engagement begins.
options.B: PPTP, selected because every major desktop operating system already supports it natively with no additional client software required.
options.C: A clientless TLS (SSL) VPN portal, published on TCP port 443 and reached through a standard browser.
options.D: L2TP over IPsec, relying on the operating system's built-in virtual private network client support.

questionsV2.explanation:
Both constraints point the same way. No installable software means the access method has to live in what the laptops already have, a browser. Restrictive egress means it has to ride the one port those networks reliably pass, 443.
A clientless TLS VPN portal satisfies both (C), brokering the three web applications through an authenticated gateway without touching the endpoint. Web apps are exactly the workload such portals serve.
Remote-access selection is constraint-driven. Who controls the endpoint, and what the intervening networks pass, decide the technology before security preferences do.
questionsV2.recallLine: Auditors cannot install software on their firms' laptops and work from networks allowing only web ports outbound. Which remote-access approach BEST fits them?

optionsShort.A: IPsec VPN with a preconfigured client profile
optionsShort.B: PPTP, natively supported on every desktop
optionsShort.C: Clientless TLS portal reached through a browser
optionsShort.D: L2TP over IPsec using built-in clients

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Fails the first constraint outright. A client profile is the software the auditors' firms forbid, and strict egress commonly drops IPsec.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Clears the install hurdle and fails the security one. PPTP's MSCHAPv2 and MPPE with RC4 are broken, and the protocol is deprecated.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Still needs per-laptop VPN configuration, and the same firewall-unfriendly IPsec transport underneath.

questionsV2.question: Which measure gives handhelds the MOST reliable way to tell the legitimate network from an impostor?

options.A: Rename the staff SSID to an obscure value and suppress it from the access points' beacon broadcasts.
options.B: Brief staff to join manually when the displayed signal strength is high and steady.
options.C: Lock the handhelds to 5 GHz channels, which inexpensive rogue equipment less commonly serves.
options.D: Deploy WPA3-Enterprise (802.1X), with client profiles that validate the authentication server's certificate before connecting.

questionsV2.explanation:
An SSID is a self-declared name any radio can claim. Telling twin from truth takes an identity the network can prove and an attacker cannot copy.
Under 802.1X the handheld's supplicant validates the authentication server's certificate before it will complete the join (D). An evil twin can echo the SSID and cannot present the certificate's private key, so a properly pinned client refuses it. Cryptographic distinction, enforced by configuration.
Names and signal properties are claimable. Only a key-backed identity check lets a client refuse a perfect imitation.
questionsV2.recallLine: Staff handhelds join any network broadcasting the staff name, which an attacker exploited with a stronger transmitter. Which measure MOST reliably lets them tell an impostor apart?

optionsShort.A: Obscure the staff SSID and stop beaconing
optionsShort.B: Brief staff to join strong, steady signals
optionsShort.C: Lock the handhelds to 5 GHz channels
optionsShort.D: Enterprise 802.1X clients validating the server certificate

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Concealment, and thin. Clients probe for hidden SSIDs, advertising the name, and the twin answers with whatever name it hears.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Delegates authentication to a bar graph. The incident's premise is an attacker who transmits stronger, so signal strength favors the twin.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Raises the equipment bill trivially, since dual-band hardware is commodity. A band is a venue, not an identity.

questionsV2.question: Which explanation of the red team's result is MOST accurate?

options.A: The red team tunneled the data out inside TLS on the permitted port, indistinguishable at the firewall from ordinary encrypted web traffic.
options.B: The rule set must also have been permitting a second port, since one allowed port would not carry both browsing and exfiltration.
options.C: The red team split the dataset into small transfers spaced across many days, staying beneath volume-based alerting thresholds.
options.D: The red team routed the data out through the firewall's own management interface, which egress policy does not evaluate.

questionsV2.explanation:
A port-only egress policy asks one question: is this TCP to 443? An attacker's TLS tunnel answers it identically to a browser. The red team wrapped its exfiltration in encrypted traffic to a server it controlled, and at the firewall's level of inspection there is nothing to distinguish stolen gigabytes from a long video call (A). No rule was broken, so no alert fired.
That exposes the assumption: port filtering was treated as data-loss control, a job that needs TLS-inspecting proxies, egress destination reputation, or data loss prevention with visibility into the tunnel.
An allowed encrypted port is a tunnel anyone may use. Egress control by port number decides only where traffic may go.
questionsV2.recallLine: A red team moved a large dataset out through an egress firewall permitting only the standard encrypted web port, and nothing alerted. Which explanation is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Tunneled inside TLS, indistinguishable from ordinary browsing
optionsShort.B: A second port must also have been permitted
optionsShort.C: Split into small transfers spread across days
optionsShort.D: Routed out through the firewall's management interface

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Misunderstands multiplexing. One permitted port carries unlimited concurrent sessions to unlimited destinations, which the tunnel uses.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: A real evasion technique the stem's facts exclude. A single afternoon session is the opposite of low-and-slow.

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: Invents a bypass with the wrong direction of risk. Management interfaces are an attack surface for reaching the firewall.

questionsV2.question: Which statement BEST justifies the architect's objection to the wireless design document?

options.A: EAP is a proprietary protocol controlled by a single wireless vendor, and it has since been superseded by newer open standard alternatives.
options.B: EAP mandates RC4 for its inner encryption, which current corporate cryptographic policy no longer permits anywhere in the bank.
options.C: EAP is only an authentication framework; its security depends on the method carried inside it, which may be strong or weak.
options.D: EAP applies only to wired 802.1X deployments and therefore offers no real protection on wireless networks.

questionsV2.explanation:
Secured by EAP specifies nothing yet. EAP is a carrier framework, an envelope in which some concrete method performs the actual authentication (C). The methods span mutual certificate authentication with strong key derivation, EAP-TLS, down to legacy exchanges with no server authentication and no usable keying, EAP-MD5. Until the method is named, the design's security properties are indeterminate, and that is a reviewable defect.
Naming a framework in a design is a decision deferred. Uses EAP constrains security exactly as much as uses encryption does.
questionsV2.recallLine: A wireless design document says only that the network is secured by EAP. Which statement BEST justifies the architect's objection to that wording?

optionsShort.A: It is proprietary and since superseded
optionsShort.B: It mandates RC4, which policy forbids
optionsShort.C: Framework only; the method inside decides security
optionsShort.D: It applies to wired deployments only

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Confuses the framework with LEAP, a vendor's lightweight method that was proprietary and broken. EAP itself is an open IETF standard.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Invents a mandate. EAP specifies no cipher at all, and that indifference is the very reason the method choice carries all the weight.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Simply false. Carrying EAP over the air, 802.1X on WLANs, is the flagship enterprise Wi-Fi architecture.

questionsV2.question: Which explanation BEST connects the clock drift to the authentication failures?

options.A: Kerberos rejects authenticators whose timestamps fall outside the permitted clock skew, a freshness check that keeps captured tickets from being replayed.
options.B: Kerberos derives its session keys from the current clock value, so drifted machines compute mismatched keys.
options.C: Ticket lifetimes are measured by the client alone, so a drifted client discards its own still-valid tickets before they have truly expired.
options.D: The domain controllers sign tickets with time-based one-time codes that drifted servers can no longer generate.

questionsV2.explanation:
Kerberos builds replay resistance out of time. Each request carries an encrypted authenticator whose timestamp the verifier checks against its own clock, and anything outside the allowed skew, five minutes by convention, is refused as possibly re-sent (A). Twenty minutes of drift puts every honest authenticator outside that window, so authentication fails wholesale until the clocks agree.
When authentication breaks in step with clock drift, you are watching an anti-replay freshness check do its job. Time synchronization is a security dependency.
questionsV2.recallLine: Domain machines began failing authentication after a hypervisor migration left clocks drifting. Which explanation BEST connects the drift to the failures?

optionsShort.A: Authenticators outside the permitted skew are refused
optionsShort.B: Session keys are derived from the current clock
optionsShort.C: Clients judge their own tickets' lifetimes
optionsShort.D: Controllers sign tickets with time-based codes

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Misplaces time in the cryptography. Session keys come from the KDC's key distribution; the clock gates validity and is no key material.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Has the arbiter wrong. Lifetimes are stamped into the ticket by the KDC and enforced at validation, not adjudicated by the holder.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Imports TOTP, a different authentication family, into a protocol that uses plain timestamps inside encrypted structures.

questionsV2.question: Meridian will fund one filtering change this quarter. Which of these traffic flows should the new controls constrain FIRST?

options.A: North-south traffic arriving from the internet at the public subnet
options.B: East-west traffic between workloads inside the application and data subnets
options.C: Traffic crossing the peering connection into the analytics account's payroll estate
options.D: Egress traffic from application workloads outbound to arbitrary internet destinations

questionsV2.explanation:
The tester's three hops all began inside the perimeter, and the flat security group is what let them continue. Constrain movement between the application and data subnets (B) and the hop that reached the claims record goes away. That is the loss the 42 carriers care about.
Rank flows by what they let an attacker reach.
questionsV2.recallLine: An insurer's flat cloud security group let one container reach the claims database. Which traffic flow should new filtering constrain FIRST?

optionsShort.A: North-south traffic from the internet
optionsShort.B: East-west traffic between application and data subnets
optionsShort.C: Traffic crossing the peering connection to analytics
optionsShort.D: Egress traffic to arbitrary internet destinations

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Already enforced. The edge permits 443 to the load balancer and nothing else, so tightening it buys nothing the tester exploited.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: Real, and it is the second change to fund. That path reached payroll, a narrower boundary, and the claims data sat elsewhere.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Would blunt exfiltration and the metadata call. It treats the exit and leaves the movement that reached the data.

sources: NIST SP 800-207 | Zero Trust Architecture §3.1
ISC2 CISSP Outline 2024 | 4.1.8 Traffic flows

questionsV2.question: The board asks how one container reached 179 peers. Which design change MOST directly removes that lateral path without re-architecting the application?

options.A: Move the data subnet into a separate VPC joined by a new peering connection
options.B: Deploy an intrusion detection sensor fed by a mirror of intra-subnet traffic
options.C: Replace the shared security group with per-workload policy permitting named flows
options.D: Terminate application traffic at an internal load balancer that inspects requests

questionsV2.explanation:
Lateral movement here is a policy problem. 180 workloads sit in one group that permits any member to reach any other, so the container inherited the reach of every peer.
Policy written per workload and keyed to workload identity shrinks the reachable set to the flows the application actually makes (C), and it can be built incrementally from the flow logs already being written.
Segmentation belongs where the workload is.
questionsV2.recallLine: One flat security group let a compromised container reach 179 peers. Which design change MOST directly removes the lateral path?

optionsShort.A: Separate VPC for data, joined by peering
optionsShort.B: Intrusion detection sensor on mirrored intra-subnet traffic
optionsShort.C: Per-workload policy permitting named flows between identities
optionsShort.D: Internal load balancer inspecting application requests

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Moves the boundary and leaves the rule. A peering connection between the two would carry the same traffic across it.

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Would have shown the movement afterwards. The board asked for it to stop.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Inspects one protocol at one hop and leaves every other path between workloads open.

sources: NIST SP 800-207 | Zero Trust Architecture §3.1.1
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-7(21) Boundary Protection, Isolation of Components

questionsV2.question: Analytics must read two claims tables in near real time, and nothing else. Which change to the peering arrangement BEST enforces that boundary?

options.A: Restrict the peered route table and security groups to the two database endpoints
options.B: Remove the peering connection and export nightly extracts to a bucket analytics reads
options.C: Replace the peering connection with a transit gateway carrying every account's routes
options.D: Keep the peering connection and enable flow logging on both sides of it

questionsV2.explanation:
A peering connection is a route. It makes two address spaces mutually reachable and leaves the filtering to the route tables and security groups on each side. Narrow those to the two database endpoints analytics genuinely needs (A) and it keeps the live read while the rest goes dark, which is the path the tester walked to reach payroll.
Reachability and authorization are separate decisions, and peering settles the first alone.
questionsV2.recallLine: An analytics account needs live read access to two claims tables and nothing more. Which change to a VPC peering arrangement BEST enforces that?

optionsShort.A: Narrow route tables and groups to two endpoints
optionsShort.B: Drop peering; export nightly extracts to a bucket
optionsShort.C: Transit gateway carrying every account's routes centrally
optionsShort.D: Keep peering; enable flow logging both sides

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Enforces the boundary and breaks the requirement. A nightly extract is no near-real-time read, and it makes a second copy to protect.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Centralizes routing for many accounts, and is worth doing at scale. A transit gateway forwards whatever the attached route tables allow.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Records the crossing without narrowing it. A log is evidence, not a boundary.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-4 Information Flow Enforcement
ISC2 CISSP Outline 2024 | 4.1.12 Edge networks

questionsV2.question: A director proposes giving each business unit its own VPC to fix the finding. Which objection should the architect raise FIRST?

options.A: Peering between the new VPCs is non-transitive, so shared services would need a hub
options.B: Each new VPC consumes another allocation from the address plan and another endpoint set
options.C: Flow logs would be produced per VPC, multiplying storage that nobody currently reads
options.D: Workloads inside each new VPC would still share one flat group, leaving movement open

questionsV2.explanation:
Splitting the estate does nothing to the mechanism the tester used. The finding was that a single security group permits every member to reach every other. Carve the estate into six parts and each one still contains a flat group, so a compromised workload still reaches its neighbors (D). The blast radius shrinks by a factor of six and the failure mode survives intact.
Ask first whether a proposal changes the mechanism. Then argue about its cost.
questionsV2.recallLine: A director wants one VPC per business unit to stop lateral movement in a flat cloud estate. Which objection should an architect raise FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Peering is non-transitive; shared services need a hub
optionsShort.B: More address allocations and endpoints per VPC
optionsShort.C: Per-VPC flow logs multiply unread storage
optionsShort.D: Each VPC still holds one flat group

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: A genuine design constraint the architect will raise. A hub is an engineering cost, and no reason the proposal fails to treat the finding.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: True of any multi-account design, and it belongs in the address plan review.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Multiplies telemetry nobody reads, which is a symptom of the same neglect.

sources: NIST SP 800-210 | General Access Control Guidance for Cloud Systems §3.3
ISC2 CISSP Outline 2024 | 4.1.17 Virtual Private Cloud

questionsV2.question: Calder Foundry runs 61 programmable logic controllers on its plant network. A process historian polls them with Modbus/TCP through a firewall that permits TCP 502 from the historian and denies everything else. An intruder who reached the historian through a compromised engineering workstation used it to issue write-single-coil commands that opened two cooling valves during a pour. The firewall recorded the session as permitted and raised nothing. The plant manager asks how a device the firewall was policing could change plant state. Which limitation of the inspection point MOST directly explains the outcome?

options.A: The firewall matches the transport header, leaving the Modbus function code in the payload unexamined
options.B: The firewall has no way to bind the session to a human operator, leaving writes unattributable
options.C: The firewall lacks decryption, so the contents of the encrypted Modbus session pass uninspected
options.D: The firewall permits the reply direction automatically, so traffic returning from controllers escapes examination

questionsV2.explanation:
Modbus/TCP wraps an industrial protocol inside an ordinary TCP session, and that stacking is the whole problem. A read and a write look identical at layer 4, differing by a function code one byte into the payload. A rule written in terms of ports can express who may talk (A). It can never express what they may say, so a legitimate session from a legitimate host carried an illegitimate command and the log was right to call it permitted.
Where a protocol rides inside another, a control that cannot read the inner one is filtering an envelope.
questionsV2.recallLine: A firewall permits TCP 502 from a plant historian, and a write command in that session opened valves. Which limitation MOST directly explains it?

optionsShort.A: Transport header matched; payload function code unexamined
optionsShort.B: Session not bound to a human operator
optionsShort.C: Encrypted session contents pass without inspection
optionsShort.D: Return direction permitted automatically, escaping examination

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Names a real gap in operational technology protocols. Attribution answers who, afterwards, and would not have stopped the valves opening.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Misreads the protocol. Modbus/TCP carries no encryption, and no ciphertext hides the function code.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Concerns the return direction. The damaging commands traveled toward the controllers, through the direction that was examined.

sources: NIST SP 800-82 Rev 3 | Guide to OT Security §6.2.4
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-7(11) Restrict Incoming Communications Traffic

questionsV2.question: Ridgeline Surgical Group is consolidating three server rooms. Its imaging array's iSCSI traffic will move off dedicated storage switches onto the same 10-gigabit Ethernet fabric that carries clinical workstations and VoIP handsets. The storage team notes that the array authenticates initiators by their iSCSI qualified name, that CHAP was left disabled because the old fabric was physically separate, and that jumbo frames must be preserved. The network team wants the change approved for a maintenance window nine days away. Which condition should the security architect require be met BEFORE the cutover?

options.A: Jumbo frames configured end to end so the imaging array's throughput survives the move
options.B: A quality-of-service policy that keeps VoIP handsets ahead of bulk storage replication
options.C: Traffic mirroring from the converged fabric into the security operations sensor
options.D: Mutual CHAP on every initiator-target pair, with the storage VLAN denied from clinical subnets

questionsV2.explanation:
Converging storage onto the production fabric removes the control that was quietly doing the work. On a separate fabric, physical separation was the authentication: an initiator had to be cabled into it. Once the targets are reachable from clinical VLANs, a qualified name is a claim anyone can make, because it is configured and never proved, and the array will present imaging volumes to a workstation that asserts the right one.
Mutual CHAP proves both ends, and denying the storage VLAN from clinical subnets keeps the reachable set small (D).
Ask what the old design's separation was silently providing, then replace it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A hospital is moving iSCSI storage onto the same Ethernet fabric as clinical workstations. What must be required BEFORE the cutover?

optionsShort.A: Jumbo frames configured end to end
optionsShort.B: Quality-of-service policy prioritizing voice over storage
optionsShort.C: Traffic mirroring into the security operations sensor
optionsShort.D: Mutual CHAP, storage VLAN denied from clinical subnets

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: A genuine cutover requirement that protects throughput, and no part of the security gate.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Addresses the other face of convergence, contention between voice and bulk transfer. That degrades calls; it exposes no volumes.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Would show the exposure being used. It is not the gate.

sources: RFC 7143 | iSCSI Protocol §9.2 (CHAP authentication)
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-3 Device Identification and Authentication

questionsV2.question: Harbor Point Water Authority manages 240 switches, its firewall pair and its virtualization hosts across the same production network that carries plant traffic. During a ransomware event in March, the operations team could not reach the management interfaces to isolate segments, because the malware had saturated the very links those management sessions traversed. Recovery took 31 hours. The authority has budget for one network change this year, and a director argues for air-gapping the control network instead. Which change would BEST improve the authority's ability to contain a repeat event?

options.A: An air gap between the control network and the business network, with data moved by removable media
options.B: A dedicated out-of-band management network with its own switching and console servers reaching each device
options.C: A second internet circuit from a different provider terminating on the existing firewall pair
options.D: Higher-capacity core links so that management sessions keep working when production traffic floods them

questionsV2.explanation:
Containment during an event depends on reaching the devices that do the containing, and the March failure was that management shared fate with the traffic it was meant to control.
A separate management path, with its own switching, console servers and addressing, survives a production flood because it carries no production (B).
Ask what the control plane depends on before an event, not during one.
questionsV2.recallLine: A utility could not reach switch management interfaces during a flood because management runs in-band. Which network change BEST improves containment?

optionsShort.A: Air gap between control and business networks
optionsShort.B: Dedicated out-of-band management network with console servers
optionsShort.C: Second internet circuit from a different provider
optionsShort.D: Higher-capacity core links carrying management sessions

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The director's proposal and a real control, at a different boundary. An air gap managed in-band would have failed the same way.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Protects against a provider outage. The flood was inside the authority's own links.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Raises the ceiling the malware has to reach and leaves the shared path in place.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-7(4) Boundary Protection, External Telecommunications Services
CISA | Layering Network Security Through Segmentation (out-of-band management)

questionsV2.question: Ballantyne Regional Airport's departures and baggage systems depend on a pair of core switches installed in 2014. Vendor support on one of them lapsed in January and the model reached end of software maintenance in June; the second switch is covered until 2027. Both draw from the same rack power distribution unit, and the on-site spare was consumed after a failure last autumn. The airport's risk register carries the pair as one entry rated moderate, and the infrastructure manager has funding for a single item this quarter. Which condition presents the GREATEST risk to continuity of departures?

options.A: The lapsed vendor support contract on the older of the two core switches
options.B: The end of software maintenance, which stops security patches for the older switch
options.C: Both switches drawing from one rack power distribution unit with no second feed
options.D: The consumed on-site spare, leaving no like-for-like replacement in the building

questionsV2.explanation:
Redundancy is worth only as much as the things the two halves do not share, and this pair shares its power (C). Every other item on the list degrades one switch and leaves the other carrying the airport. A distribution unit failure, or an electrician working the wrong breaker, takes both at once and departures stop. That is the difference between a degraded state and an outage.
Look for common-mode dependencies before counting devices.
questionsV2.recallLine: A pair of 2014 core switches is out of support, out of spares and on one power feed. Which condition is the GREATEST continuity risk?

optionsShort.A: Lapsed vendor support on the older switch
optionsShort.B: End of software maintenance stopping security patches
optionsShort.C: Both switches on one power distribution unit
optionsShort.D: On-site spare consumed, no replacement in building

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: Lengthens repair time once something breaks, which makes it the second item to fund.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: A security exposure, unpatched code on a reachable switch, and it belongs on the register under a different heading.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Also lengthens repair, and it matters most in the situation the lapsed support contract already describes.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PE-11 Emergency Power; SA-22 Unsupported System Components
ISC2 CISSP Outline 2024 | 4.2.1 Operation of infrastructure

questionsV2.question: Vesper Analytics moved to a permanent hybrid arrangement: 400 consultant laptops now spend most weeks on home and client networks, and they reach company systems through a SaaS identity broker and not a VPN. The security team's detection still rests on a datacenter intrusion prevention appliance and egress filtering at two offices, which between them now see under a fifth of the fleet's traffic. A phishing campaign last month installed a credential stealer on nine laptops; the appliance saw none of it, and the compromise surfaced when a client reported odd sign-ins. Which shift in control placement MOST directly restores visibility of what runs on the fleet?

options.A: Host-based endpoint detection and response on every laptop, reporting to a central console
options.B: A full-tunnel VPN client forcing laptop traffic back through the datacenter inspection point
options.C: A secure web gateway delivered as a cloud service, enforced by an agent on each laptop
options.D: Device posture checks in the identity broker, evaluated each time a laptop signs in

questionsV2.explanation:
Once the fleet stopped passing through the chokepoints, the chokepoints stopped being the security architecture. What stays constant is the laptop.
An agent on the endpoint sees process execution, persistence and outbound connections wherever the device happens to be (A). That is the class of evidence that would have caught a credential stealer nine times over before a client noticed.
Put monitoring where the asset is, not where the network used to be.
questionsV2.recallLine: A consultancy's 400 laptops rarely touch its offices, and a credential stealer went unseen. Which control placement MOST directly restores visibility?

optionsShort.A: Endpoint detection agent on every laptop
optionsShort.B: Full-tunnel VPN back to the datacenter appliance
optionsShort.C: Cloud secure web gateway with laptop agent
optionsShort.D: Device posture checked at each broker sign-in

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Restores network visibility by dragging traffic back to the appliance. It costs performance and shows nothing about what executed locally.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Follows the laptop and covers web traffic, a narrower slice than the question asks about.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: A check at a moment. A device that passes posture at sign-in can be compromised an hour later.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SI-4(23) System Monitoring, Host-Based Devices
NIST SP 800-207 | Zero Trust Architecture §3.2

questionsV2.question: Alderway Credit Union buys managed wide-area connectivity for 38 branches. The provider owns the customer premises routers, holds their administrative credentials, and reaches them over a management tunnel that terminates inside the credit union's core, because that is how the provider's monitoring platform collects statistics. The contract predates the current security program: it carries an availability service level and a confidentiality clause, and says nothing about who at the provider may connect, from where, or what is logged. An examiner has asked how this access is supervised. Which change should the credit union pursue FIRST?

options.A: Add a right-to-audit clause and schedule an annual assessment of the provider's security program
options.B: Terminate the provider's management tunnel in a screened segment and require named accounts with logging
options.C: Require the provider to carry cyber liability insurance sized to the credit union's exposure
options.D: Require the provider to test the managed router estate before the next contract renewal

questionsV2.explanation:
Third-party connectivity is an access path before it is a contract term, and this one lands inside the core with shared credentials and no record of who used them.
Terminate the tunnel in a screened segment and require named accounts with logging (B). The screened segment bounds what the provider can reach; named accounts make each session attributable to a person. Both are within the credit union's own gift, need no renegotiation, and answer the examiner directly.
Where a supplier's access is technical, treat the path first and the paperwork next.
questionsV2.recallLine: A telecom provider manages branch routers over a tunnel into a credit union's core with shared credentials. Which change should the union pursue FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Right-to-audit clause and annual provider assessment
optionsShort.B: Screened tunnel termination with named, logged accounts
optionsShort.C: Cyber liability insurance sized to the exposure
optionsShort.D: Provider tests the router estate before renewal

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: The right instrument for assurance over the provider's program, and it should follow. An annual assessment constrains no live path.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: A treasury judgment about how much loss to transfer, made by the board.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Buys evidence at renewal about a path that is open today.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SA-9 External System Services; AC-17 Remote Access
FFIEC IT Examination Handbook | Outsourcing Technology Services

questionsV2.question: Northgate Exchange runs an advertising auction whose bidders must receive a quote and return a bid inside 90 milliseconds round trip. Security wants inline TLS inspection on the bidder-facing path. A proof of concept shows the appliance sustaining the required 8 gigabits per second and adding a median 4 milliseconds, but its tail figure at the 99th percentile reaches 61 milliseconds whenever it reloads policy, which operations expects to do twice a week. The network team argues the appliance meets the throughput specification. Which measure is the PRIMARY basis for the acceptance decision?
