options.A: Sustained throughput in gigabits per second across the bidder-facing path at peak hour
options.B: Added delay at the 99th percentile, measured through the appliance during a policy reload
options.C: Median added delay measured through the appliance across a representative bidding session
options.D: Signal-to-noise ratio measured on the fiber spans that carry the bidder-facing path

questionsV2.explanation:
A deadline is a promise about the worst case. Bids arriving after 90 milliseconds are lost, so the statistic that decides this appliance is the one describing the tail (B). 61 milliseconds added twice a week, on top of the path's own delay, is scheduled lost revenue.
Choose the statistic the business requirement is written in.
questionsV2.recallLine: An inspection appliance meets its throughput specification but adds 61 milliseconds at the tail during reloads. Which measure is the PRIMARY acceptance basis?

optionsShort.A: Sustained throughput at peak hour
optionsShort.B: Added delay at the 99th percentile
optionsShort.C: Median added delay across a session
optionsShort.D: Signal-to-noise ratio on the fiber spans

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: Answers the sizing question, and is why the network team is comfortable. Capacity says nothing about when the appliance hands traffic back.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: A fair acceptance measure once the tail clears the deadline, and misleading before it, because a median hides the breaking event.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Characterizes the medium. The equipment is what is under decision.

sources: RFC 2679 | A One-way Delay Metric for IPPM
ISC2 CISSP Outline 2024 | 4.1.7 Performance metrics

questionsV2.question: Pellerin Books put its storefront behind a content delivery network with a web application firewall at the edge. Two weeks later a tester reported that the origin's public address, still present in an old certificate transparency entry and in the mail server's DNS records, accepts HTTPS directly, and that requests sent to it are served normally without touching the edge. Traffic through the edge is clean and the firewall's block counts look healthy. The team is preparing to enable rate limiting and bot management at the edge as well. Which weakness should Pellerin close BEFORE adding more edge controls?

options.A: Remove the historical certificate transparency entry that still discloses the origin's address
options.B: Require the delivery network to rewrite the Host header on every request it forwards
options.C: Restrict the origin to accept connections from the delivery network, proved by a client certificate
options.D: Enable logging at the origin so requests arriving without traversing the edge are recorded

questionsV2.explanation:
An edge control is worth what its bypass is worth. Every rule Pellerin adds at the delivery network, the firewall today and rate limiting tomorrow, is optional for an attacker who resolves the origin directly. The healthy block counts measure only the traffic that chose to come through the front door.
Bind the origin to connections it can prove came from the delivery network (C). The edge becomes the sole path, and the new controls get something to enforce.
Close the bypass before buying more of what it bypasses.
questionsV2.recallLine: A storefront's origin address is public and serves HTTPS directly, skipping the delivery network. What should be closed BEFORE adding more edge controls?

optionsShort.A: Remove the certificate transparency entry disclosing the origin
optionsShort.B: Rewrite the Host header on forwarded requests
optionsShort.C: Origin accepts the delivery network, proved by certificate
optionsShort.D: Log origin requests that skipped the edge

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Treats disclosure. An address published once should be assumed known, and rotating it buys weeks.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: A sound cache-integrity control against host-header abuse, which is a different attack.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Would tell Pellerin the bypass is being used, and leave it usable.

sources: OWASP | Web Application Firewall bypass via origin exposure
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-7(5) Boundary Protection, Deny by Default

questionsV2.question: Kestrel Logistics replaced its campus switching with a software-defined fabric: 90 switches take their forwarding state from a controller cluster reached over a REST API. The automation pipeline's service accounts hold API tokens with write scope over the whole fabric, kept in the pipeline's variable store, and four platform engineers hold administrator logins. During a tabletop exercise someone asked what an attacker holding one automation token could do. The answer was that the token rewrites any switch's policy within seconds, and the change appears in the audit log as a routine push. Which control MOST directly reduces that exposure?

options.A: Scope automation tokens to named switch groups and require a second approval for fabric-wide pushes
options.B: Move the controller cluster onto an out-of-band management network reached through jump hosts
options.C: Require a design review before any new automation pipeline is granted controller access
options.D: Rotate the automation tokens every 30 days and hold them in a managed secrets store

questionsV2.explanation:
Software-defined networking concentrates in one API the authority that used to be spread across 90 login sessions. The exposure the tabletop found is the size of what a single valid credential may do.
Scope each token to the switch groups its pipeline actually touches, and gate fabric-wide change behind a second human (A). A stolen token then buys a fraction of the fabric, and the dangerous class of push cannot be made alone.
On a control plane, scope the credential before hardening the console.
questionsV2.recallLine: One automation token can rewrite policy on all 90 switches of a software-defined fabric. Which control MOST directly reduces that exposure?

optionsShort.A: Scope tokens to groups; approval for fabric-wide pushes
optionsShort.B: Controller on an out-of-band management network
optionsShort.C: Design review before granting new pipelines access
optionsShort.D: Rotate tokens monthly into a secrets store

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Protects the controller from being reached by the wrong people. The automation token is already inside and reaches the API by design.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: The right gate for the next pipeline. The tokens already issued are already sitting in a variable store.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Shortens the window in which a leaked token works and leaves untouched what it can do.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-6(1) Least Privilege, Authorize Access to Security Functions
ISC2 CISSP Outline 2024 | 4.1.16 Software defined networks

questionsV2.question: Tannerhill Health Network collects NetFlow from its two internet routers and takes full packet capture at its datacenter core. After a laboratory server was found beaconing to an external host for six weeks, the review established why nothing had fired: the laboratory sits in a colocation suite whose traffic reaches the internet through the colocation provider's own uplink and returns to the hospital over a private circuit that lands behind the capture point. Ninety-two percent of the laboratory's outbound traffic crossed neither sensor. The team can fund one addition. Which addition to the monitoring design MOST directly closes the blind spot?

options.A: Full packet capture on the private circuit where it lands in the hospital datacenter
options.B: SNMP polling of the colocation switches' interface counters, alerting on sustained utilization
options.C: NetFlow sampling on the two internet routers raised from one-in-1000 to one-in-100
options.D: NetFlow export from the colocation suite's edge switch toward the provider's uplink

questionsV2.explanation:
Observability is a question about placement before it is a question about tooling. A sensor sees what crosses it, and 92 percent of this laboratory's outbound traffic crossed neither of the two the hospital owns.
Take flow records where the suite hands traffic to the provider (D), which is the path the beacon actually took. Flow records suffice: six weeks of small regular connections to one external address is a pattern that shows in five-tuples and timing, with no payload needed.
Ask which link the traffic uses before choosing what to record on it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A colocated laboratory's outbound traffic reaches the internet through the provider's uplink, unseen by either hospital sensor. Which addition MOST directly closes the gap?

optionsShort.A: Packet capture where the private circuit lands
optionsShort.B: SNMP counters alerting on sustained utilization
optionsShort.C: Higher NetFlow sampling on the internet routers
optionsShort.D: NetFlow at the colocation edge toward the uplink

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Tempting, because packet capture is richer. The private circuit carries hospital-bound traffic, and the beacon left through the provider.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Watches volume on the colocation switches. A beacon is quiet by design and never moves the counters.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Sharpens the fidelity of a sensor the laboratory's outbound traffic never reaches.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SI-4(4) System Monitoring, Inbound and Outbound Communications Traffic
RFC 7011 | IPFIX Protocol Specification

questionsV2.question: Corvine Title Company leases the ninth floor of a multi-tenant tower. Its two 10-gigabit links to a datacenter run as unshielded twisted pair through a shared riser and a basement telecom closet that building engineering, three other tenants and the incumbent carrier all hold keys to. An assessor recorded errors on one pair that coincide with the freight elevator's motor cycling, and noted that a listening device attached in that closet would look like ordinary patching. The company can fund one remediation this year. Which change addresses both findings BEST?

options.A: Replace the copper runs with shielded twisted pair terminated in the same basement closet
options.B: Encrypt both links with MACsec on the switch pairs at either end of the runs
options.C: Replace the copper runs with single-mode fiber in a locked, alarmed conduit
options.D: Install a badge reader and camera covering the basement closet, with monthly access reviews

questionsV2.explanation:
Two findings, one medium. Unshielded copper picks up the elevator motor's field, which is why the errors track its cycling, and copper radiates enough that a clip-on tap in a closet a dozen people can enter is easy and unremarkable.
Glass carries no current, so the interference disappears. A fiber tap needs the run cut or bent and shows itself in loss, and a locked, alarmed conduit adds the second barrier (C).
When one medium causes both findings, change the medium.
questionsV2.recallLine: Unshielded copper in a shared riser shows interference errors and could be tapped unnoticed. Which single remediation addresses both findings BEST?

optionsShort.A: Shielded twisted pair in the same closet
optionsShort.B: MACsec encryption on the switch pairs
optionsShort.C: Single-mode fiber in a locked, alarmed conduit
optionsShort.D: Badge reader, camera and monthly access reviews

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Cures the interference and leaves the tap. Shielding raises the effort a little, and the closet is still shared.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Makes an intercepted frame useless, which is a strong answer to the tap alone, and does nothing for the error rate.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Records who entered the closet, afterwards. Neither finding changes.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PE-4 Access Control for Transmission
IEEE 802.1AE | MAC Security (MACsec)

questionsV2.question: Ostrander Minerals operates four remote pits whose sole connectivity is a geostationary satellite link with a 620-millisecond round trip. The provider's terminals run a performance-enhancing proxy that terminates TCP at each end and rewrites window sizes; without it, transfers to head office collapse to a fraction of the link's capacity. Security now requires traffic between the pits and head office to be encrypted end to end, and the network engineer reports that switching on the site-to-site tunnel makes those transfers unusable again. Which account of the conflict is MOST accurate?

options.A: The tunnel hides the TCP headers the proxy rewrites, so acceleration must move inside the encrypted path
options.B: The tunnel's per-packet overhead consumes the link's capacity, so the transfers need compression instead
options.C: The 620-millisecond delay is the real constraint, so the pits need a low-earth-orbit provider
options.D: The tunnel discards packets the satellite path reorders, so its replay window must be widened

questionsV2.explanation:
A performance-enhancing proxy works by lying to both ends about a connection it has quietly split in two, and it can do that because it reads and rewrites the TCP header. Encrypt the packet and that header is hidden or integrity-protected (A). The proxy falls back to plain forwarding, and the transfers meet the satellite's real bandwidth-delay product with a window sized for a terrestrial link.
The design question is where the optimization lives: in appliances at each pit and at head office that see cleartext inside the crypto boundary, or in the carrier's terminals outside it.
Ask what a middlebox must see before encrypting past it.
questionsV2.recallLine: Turning on end-to-end encryption over a satellite link makes transfers unusable because a carrier proxy accelerates TCP. Which account is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: Encryption hides headers the proxy rewrites; move acceleration inside
optionsShort.B: Tunnel overhead consumes capacity; use compression
optionsShort.C: Propagation delay is the constraint; change orbit
optionsShort.D: Reordering trips the replay window; widen it

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: The wrong order of magnitude. Tunnel overhead costs a few percent, not the collapse described.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: A real remedy for latency, and a much larger procurement. The conflict arrived with the tunnel.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Describes a genuine effect on reordering paths. Nothing about reordering changed here.

sources: RFC 3135 | Performance Enhancing Proxies Intended to Mitigate Link-Related Degradations
NIST SP 800-77 Rev 1 | Guide to IPsec VPNs §3.3

questionsV2.question: The telephones tag their traffic onto a voice VLAN, and each workstation plugs into the passthrough port on the handset in front of it. Which change MOST directly stops a workstation reaching the voice VLAN?

options.A: Configure the handsets to strip tags on their passthrough ports, and the switch to reject tagged ingress
options.B: Move the telephones onto their own physical switches, cabled back to a separate distribution pair
options.C: Apply an access list between the voice and data VLANs at the campus core router
options.D: Require each handset to authenticate to the switch port before it is admitted

questionsV2.explanation:
A workstation plugged into a handset's passthrough port shares one switch port with the phone. Where that port accepts tagged frames, the workstation can label its own traffic with the telephony identifier and be switched straight into a VLAN it was never meant to see.
Strip tags at the handset and refuse tagged ingress at the switch (A). That closes the path where the path exists and leaves the phone's own tagged uplink working.
Enforce a VLAN boundary at the port that honors the tag.
questionsV2.recallLine: IP telephones share access ports with the workstations behind them. Which switch-port change MOST directly stops a workstation reaching the voice VLAN?

optionsShort.A: Strip tags at the handset, reject tagged ingress
optionsShort.B: Move telephones onto separate physical switches
optionsShort.C: Filter between voice and data VLANs at the router
optionsShort.D: Require handsets to authenticate to the port

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Separates the two networks in copper and would work. Re-cabling 90 handsets spends the approved quarter on one risk.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Filters what is routed between the two VLANs. A hopped frame is switched inside one VLAN and never reaches the router.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Belongs in the design and settles which handsets may be present. It decides nothing about a frame the workstation sends.

sources: NIST SP 800-58 | Security Considerations for Voice Over IP Systems
IEEE 802.1Q-2022 | Virtual Bridged Local Area Networks

questionsV2.question: Engineering wants the pasteurizer controllers isolated from everything on the office side, where the historian sits, without the historian losing its readings. Which arrangement BEST preserves that isolation?

options.A: A firewall pair between the two networks permitting the historian's polling protocol inbound
options.B: An air gap, with readings carried to the historian on removable media each shift
options.C: A unidirectional gateway passing readings out of the process network with no return path
options.D: A separate VLAN for the controllers with an access list at the campus core switches

questionsV2.explanation:
The requirement has two halves that pull against each other. Nothing on the office network may reach the controllers, and the historian must keep getting readings.
A gateway that carries data one way electrically satisfies both (C). There is no path back for a compromised office host to use, and the readings keep flowing.
Physical segmentation is a property of the wiring.
questionsV2.recallLine: Process controllers must be isolated from an office network while a historian keeps receiving their readings. Which arrangement BEST preserves that isolation?

optionsShort.A: Firewall permitting the historian's poll inbound
optionsShort.B: Air gap with removable media each shift
optionsShort.C: Unidirectional gateway with no return path
optionsShort.D: Controller VLAN with an access list

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: The right control for a boundary meant to stay two-way. Here the permitted poll is itself the return path a foothold rides inward.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Isolates the controllers thoroughly, abandons the second half of the requirement and puts removable media on the plant floor.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: What the cooperative already runs. A VLAN on shared switches is logical separation, and a misconfigured trunk reopens the path.

sources: NIST SP 800-82 Rev 3 | Guide to Operational Technology Security, §5 OT cybersecurity architecture
IEC 62443-3-3 | SR 5.1 Network segmentation

questionsV2.question: Which action BEST reduces the plant's exposure to the unsupported core switch failing during the autumn peak?

options.A: Renew extended vendor support on the switch, with a four-hour parts and engineer response
options.B: Buy a matching switch, hold it as a configured cold spare, and rehearse the swap
options.C: Replace both core switches with a currently supported model during the approved engineering quarter
options.D: Add a second power feed to the core rack from a separate distribution unit

questionsV2.explanation:
Exposure here is the length of the outage. Hardware of that age fails eventually, and with no spare and no vendor obligation the cooperative's recovery time in October is however long procurement takes.
A matching chassis on the shelf, already configured, with the swap rehearsed by the people who would do it at 03:00 (B), turns weeks into an hour.
Where the failure cannot be prevented, buy back the recovery time.
questionsV2.recallLine: A core switch is out of vendor support with no spare on hand. Which action BEST reduces exposure to it failing during a peak?

optionsShort.A: Renew extended vendor support with four-hour response
optionsShort.B: Configured cold spare, with the swap rehearsed
optionsShort.C: Refresh both core switches this quarter
optionsShort.D: Second power feed to the core rack

A.label: wrong phase
A.wouldAnswer: Assumes a manufacturer will sell support on a model it declared end of life, and parts obligations thin out first. Buy that earlier.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: The right destination reached by the wrong authority. A capital refresh of both switches is the board's call, not engineering time.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Hardens the rack against a supply failure. A real single point of failure, and not the one named here.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SA-22 Unsupported System Components
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | MA-6 Timely Maintenance

questionsV2.question: The machine builder's cellular modem reaches the filling line without crossing the plant firewall. Which requirement should the cooperative place on that arrangement FIRST?

options.A: Require the builder to apply its own remote-access standard to the modem and attest annually
options.B: Add the modem's address range to the plant firewall's outbound filtering rules
options.C: Require the builder to log every diagnostic session and send the cooperative monthly reports
options.D: Route the builder's diagnostics through the plant's remote-access gateway and disable the modem

questionsV2.explanation:
An access path the plant does not own and cannot observe is not a path it can govern, whatever the contract says.
Bring the builder's diagnostics in through the cooperative's own gateway (D) and each session becomes subject to the plant's authentication, logging and filtering. Switching the modem off removes the alternative route.
Govern the path before the paperwork. A control nobody can observe is a promise.
questionsV2.recallLine: A machine builder's cellular modem reaches new plant equipment without crossing the site firewall. Which requirement should the plant place on that arrangement FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Builder applies its own standard and attests annually
optionsShort.B: Filter the modem's addresses at the site firewall
optionsShort.C: Builder logs each session and reports monthly
optionsShort.D: Route diagnostics through the plant's remote-access gateway

A.label: not the decision-maker's
A.wouldAnswer: Hands the control decision to the party whose access is being controlled. The cooperative cannot audit an attestation it did not write.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Assumes the modem's traffic passes the firewall. The radio path leaves the building without touching it.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Produces a record after the fact. Valuable on a path already mediated, and no help in stopping the next session.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SA-9 External System Services
NIST SP 800-82 Rev 3 | Guide to Operational Technology Security

questionsV2.question: Brightmoor Insurance runs 900 virtual machines across two datacenters on a VXLAN overlay, so tenant traffic between hypervisors is encapsulated in UDP and carried over the physical fabric. The firewall pair sits between the fabric and the campus core, where it sees the outer headers of that traffic and nothing else: hypervisor address to hypervisor address, one transport port. An audit found the pair holds no record of any session between two claims applications that exchange data all day. The network team must give inspection of the inner flows back to security. Which change MOST directly delivers that?

options.A: Configure the firewall to decapsulate and re-inspect frames arriving on the overlay's transport port
options.B: Route the tenant subnets through the firewall pair by removing them from the overlay
options.C: Enforce policy at the virtual switch on each hypervisor, before the traffic is encapsulated
options.D: Mirror the encapsulated fabric traffic to an intrusion detection sensor for offline analysis

questionsV2.explanation:
Encapsulation moves the decision point. Wrap tenant traffic in an outer header between two hypervisors and an appliance downstream sees a conversation between hypervisors, learning nothing about the applications inside it. East-west traffic between two machines on the same fabric may never reach that appliance at all.
Apply policy in the virtual switch (C). Enforcement then sits inside the tenant's own address space, where source, destination and application are still visible.
Enforce policy where the addresses still mean something.
questionsV2.recallLine: Tenant traffic between hypervisors is encapsulated, so the firewall sees outer headers alone. Which change MOST directly gives the inspection point the inner flows?

optionsShort.A: Decapsulate and re-inspect at the firewall
optionsShort.B: Remove the subnets from the overlay and route
optionsShort.C: Enforce policy at the hypervisor's virtual switch
optionsShort.D: Mirror encapsulated traffic to a detection sensor

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: A real capability on modern firewalls, and it inspects only what is steered to it. The claims traffic never leaves the fabric.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Works, and it is what you do when one tenant genuinely needs perimeter inspection. Hairpinning 900 workloads re-creates the old bottleneck.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Produces a record of the outer conversation for an analyst to unwrap afterwards. It answers what happened.

sources: RFC 7348 | Virtual eXtensible Local Area Network (VXLAN)
NIST SP 800-125B | Secure Virtual Network Configuration for VM Protection

questionsV2.question: Redbank Health Analytics built its datacenter for a web tier that answers clinicians and a database tier behind it, so every subnet's default gateway is an interface on the perimeter firewall pair. A claims-modeling cluster added in March now moves 40 terabytes a night between 60 nodes in two adjacent subnets. That traffic leaves a node, crosses the firewall pair and returns to a node in the same rack. The pair runs at 94 percent of forwarding capacity at 02:00, and operations has begun disabling inspection to keep the job inside its window. Which change BEST resolves the bottleneck without giving up inspection of the cluster?

options.A: Increase the firewall pair's throughput license and add a second link to each leaf
options.B: Place the cluster's subnets on a leaf pair that routes between them, with distributed enforcement
options.C: Exempt the cluster's subnets from inspection and log the flows at the leaf switches
options.D: Schedule the modeling job across the working day so its traffic no longer coincides

questionsV2.explanation:
The traffic is east-west, node to node inside one tier, riding a path designed for north-south flows in which every packet from a client outside the datacenter passes a single enforcement point. Sixty nodes in adjacent racks have no reason to use that path.
Route the subnets locally at the leaf, with enforcement distributed to the leaves or the hosts (B). The traffic stays where it belongs and a policy stays on it.
Put the enforcement point on the path the traffic actually takes.
questionsV2.recallLine: A modeling cluster's node-to-node traffic hairpins through the perimeter firewall pair and saturates it. Which change BEST resolves the bottleneck while keeping inspection?

optionsShort.A: More firewall throughput and extra leaf links
optionsShort.B: Route the subnets locally with distributed enforcement
optionsShort.C: Exempt the cluster and log flows instead
optionsShort.D: Spread the job across the working day

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Buys headroom and leaves the hairpin intact, so the next cluster reopens the same finding at a higher license tier.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: What the team already reaches for at 02:00. It trades inspection for a flow record that shows who spoke without showing what was said.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Moves the load instead of the design, and the overnight window exists because the source data lands overnight.

sources: NIST SP 800-215 | Guide to a Secure Enterprise Network Landscape, §4 traffic flows
NIST SP 800-125B | Secure Virtual Network Configuration for VM Protection

questionsV2.question: Thackeray Group has bought two regional distributors in eighteen months. All three companies numbered their sites out of 10.10.0.0/16, and 400 duplicate addresses are already in production. The group wants one managed wide-area network and one router pair per hub site, but each company's traffic must stay in its own routing domain until its applications are consolidated, which finance has spread over three years. Renumbering before then is not funded. The architect has to carry three overlapping address spaces across shared hardware. Which segmentation approach BEST meets that requirement?

options.A: A VLAN for each company, trunked into one routing table on the hub routers
options.B: A virtual routing and forwarding instance per company, with controlled route leaking
options.C: Address translation at each hub, mapping every duplicate range onto unique group addresses
options.D: Separate physical routers for each company at every hub, sharing no hardware

questionsV2.explanation:
Three copies of one prefix cannot coexist in a single forwarding table, and that arithmetic rules out most of the alternatives before policy is discussed.
A separate routing and forwarding instance per company gives each its own table on the same physical router (B), so 10.10.5.0/24 exists three times without collision, and a deliberate leak publishes the shared services all three need.
Overlapping address space is a forwarding-table problem before it is a policy one.
questionsV2.recallLine: Three merged companies use overlapping address space on one shared router pair per site. Which segmentation approach BEST keeps their routing domains apart?

optionsShort.A: One VLAN per company into one table
optionsShort.B: A routing instance per company, with leaking
optionsShort.C: Translate duplicate ranges onto unique addresses
optionsShort.D: Separate physical routers for each company

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Divides the companies at layer 2 and hands every VLAN to a router that still holds one table. The duplicates collide at the first hop.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: What an integration team reaches for when two networks must talk despite overlap. 400 mappings are a permanent operational tax.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Keeps the domains apart and discards the consolidation the group is paying for, tripling the hardware at every hub.

sources: RFC 4364 | BGP/MPLS IP Virtual Private Networks
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-7 Boundary Protection

questionsV2.question: Orenda Payments enforces micro-segmentation across 1,100 cloud workloads with a distributed firewall. Its rules were written two years ago against source and destination address ranges. The estate has since moved to autoscaling groups: instances live for hours, released addresses are reissued within minutes, and three outages this year were traced to a new instance inheriting an address whose rules belonged to a decommissioned service. Two of those instances reached a cardholder subnet they had no business reaching. The architect is rewriting the policy. On what basis should the rules identify a workload to MOST reliably survive instances being replaced?

options.A: The address range of the subnet in which the instance launches
options.B: The DNS name registered for the instance when it starts
options.C: The hardware address presented by the instance's virtual interface
options.D: The workload identity carried in tags the platform assigns at launch

questionsV2.explanation:
Micro-segmentation is as stable as the thing its rules name, and in an autoscaling estate an address names whatever launched most recently.
A tag the platform attaches at launch travels with the workload (D). A replacement instance of the payments service is labeled as the payments service before it can send a packet, and the existing rule applies to it with nobody editing anything.
Name a workload by something that outlives the instance.
questionsV2.recallLine: Addresses are recycled within minutes in an autoscaling estate. On what basis should distributed firewall rules identify a workload to MOST reliably survive replacement?

optionsShort.A: The subnet range the instance launches in
optionsShort.B: The DNS name registered at start-up
optionsShort.C: The virtual interface's hardware address
optionsShort.D: Platform tags assigned to the workload at launch

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Stable, and a subnet is a neighborhood. Every instance in it inherits one policy, the flat blast radius micro-segmentation breaks up.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Also moves with the workload, and it depends on registration completing. A rule can be unenforced through an instance's first minutes.

C.label: true of a different thing
C.wouldAnswer: How a switch admits a device to an access port. It means nothing to a distributed firewall inside a routed overlay.

sources: NIST SP 800-207 | Zero Trust Architecture, §3.1.2 micro-segmentation
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-7(21) Isolation of System Components

questionsV2.question: Marlow Data Services multihomes its colocation edge to two internet providers and peers directly with a regional exchange. It announces one /21 of its own address space. During a maintenance window an engineer removed an outbound filter from the session to the second provider. For nineteen minutes the routers re-announced 4,000 prefixes learned from the first provider, traffic between two unrelated networks began transiting Marlow's 10-gigabit links, and both were saturated before the session was shut. Which control at the edge MOST directly prevents that recurring?

options.A: An outbound prefix list on each peer session, permitting the company's own aggregate
options.B: A maximum-prefix limit that shuts a session receiving more routes than expected
options.C: Route origin validation, dropping prefixes whose announcements lack a published authorization
options.D: Alerting from a public routing monitor when unexpected prefixes appear from the company

questionsV2.explanation:
What failed was an announcement. The routers told a neighbor they could reach 4,000 networks that were never theirs, and the neighbor believed them.
A list of the prefixes the company is permitted to announce, applied outbound on every session (A), matches that failure and fails closed. Anything absent from the list is not announced, including whatever the next engineer forgets.
Every edge session needs a policy in both directions, and the outbound half is the half that protects everyone else.
questionsV2.recallLine: A multihomed network re-announced 4,000 prefixes learned from one provider to another and became transit. Which edge control MOST directly prevents that recurring?

optionsShort.A: Outbound prefix list of the company's own aggregate
optionsShort.B: Maximum-prefix limit on inbound announcements
optionsShort.C: Origin validation of prefixes learned from peers
optionsShort.D: Alerting from a public routing monitor

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Counts what arrives. It would not have examined a single outbound update.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Checks that a prefix somebody else announces is authorized. Marlow's neighbors were the ones who needed protecting.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Would have raised the alarm in two minutes instead of nineteen. An alarm is not a filter.

sources: RFC 7454 | BGP Operations and Security, §6
NIST SP 800-189 | Resilient Interdomain Traffic Exchange: BGP Security and DDoS Mitigation

questionsV2.question: Kettleman Terminal runs 22 automated stacking cranes and 60 yard tractors over a private 5G network it operates itself, with its own core and its own SIM provisioning. Crane control sits on a dedicated slice; tractor telemetry and the yard office share a second. A subcontractor reported a tablet stolen from a tractor cab. Its SIM was issued for the tractor slice, and the terminal's own testing showed that the same SIM, moved into an unrelated handset, attaches to the network and reaches the yard office in seconds. Which control MOST directly stops a SIM removed from its issued device attaching at all?

options.A: Shortening the re-authentication interval so sessions on the tractor slice expire more frequently
options.B: Moving the yard office applications behind a gateway that requires a device certificate
options.C: Binding each subscriber identity to its device identity, refusing attachment from an unpaired device
options.D: Alerting when a subscriber identity attaches from a cell it has not used before

questionsV2.explanation:
The credential the network checks lives on the card, so a card in a different handset is still a valid subscriber unless the core has been told otherwise.
Pair the subscriber identity with the device's own identity and refuse an attachment where the pair does not match (C). A stolen card is then useless by itself, which is exactly the failure the terminal reproduced in its own testing.
Because the terminal operates the core itself, it holds the subscriber database. Admission decisions a public carrier could not offer are available to it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A SIM issued for a private 5G network is stolen and moved into another device. Which control MOST directly stops it attaching at all?

optionsShort.A: Re-authenticate slice sessions more frequently
optionsShort.B: Device certificate at the application gateway
optionsShort.C: Pair subscriber identity with device identity
optionsShort.D: Alert on attachment from an unfamiliar cell

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Re-runs an authentication that the stolen card passes, only more often.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: A sound control that protects one destination. The card still attaches, holds an address on the tractor slice, and reaches its neighbors.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Converts an attachment into an alert. That shortens the response, not the access.

sources: 3GPP TS 33.501 | Security architecture and procedures for 5G system
NIST SP 800-187 | Guide to LTE Security

questionsV2.question: Halverson Lending keeps its loan-origination workloads in private subnets of one cloud VPC. They write customer documents to the provider's object storage service, and they reach it over that service's public endpoint through a NAT gateway and the internet gateway. An examiner has asked the bank to show two things: that customer documents do not traverse the public internet, and that a workload compromised by an attacker could not write them to a bucket outside the bank's own account. Which VPC change BEST satisfies both halves of that finding?

options.A: A private endpoint for the storage service, with an endpoint policy naming the bank's buckets
options.B: A gateway rule allowing the storage service's published address ranges outbound from the subnets
options.C: A forward proxy in a public subnet, allowing requests to the bank's storage hostnames
options.D: A peering connection to a shared services VPC that fronts the storage service

questionsV2.explanation:
Both halves of the finding are about where traffic goes, and the examiner wants a control the bank can evidence.
A private endpoint inside the VPC keeps the request on the provider's own network, so no packet reaches an internet gateway (A). The policy attached to that endpoint enumerates the accounts and buckets the workloads may write to, so a compromised instance holding credentials for an outside bucket is refused at the network.
Where traffic goes and what it may reach are both properties of the endpoint, so settle them there.
questionsV2.recallLine: An examiner wants object storage traffic kept off the public internet and confined to the bank's own buckets. Which VPC change BEST satisfies both?

optionsShort.A: Private endpoint with a policy naming the buckets
optionsShort.B: Allow the service's address ranges outbound
optionsShort.C: Forward proxy permitting the storage hostnames
optionsShort.D: Peering to a shared services VPC

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Leaves the path public and permits writes to any tenant's bucket in those ranges, because the addresses belong to the service.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: The right control for governing and logging general outbound web traffic. The documents still cross the internet to reach the service.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: A genuine building block. Peering by itself moves the problem into another VPC that still needs an endpoint and a policy of its own.

sources: NIST SP 800-210 | General Access Control Guidance for Cloud Systems
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-7(4) External Telecommunications Services

questionsV2.question: Sandover Trust mirrors traffic from its datacenter distribution switch to an intrusion detection sensor, using a session that copies both directions of four 10-gigabit uplinks to one 10-gigabit monitor port. An investigation into a 40-minute transfer to an external host found the sensor held no record of it. The engineers then compared counters: the switch had been discarding mirrored frames during the nightly backup window for months, and the sensor's own capture statistics showed no gap, because frames it never received were never counted. Which change MOST reliably gives the sensor every frame during peak load?

options.A: A second monitor port on the switch, splitting the mirrored traffic across two sessions
options.B: Sampled flow export from the distribution switch, delivered to the sensor for correlation
options.C: A larger capture buffer and faster storage on the sensor to absorb bursts
options.D: Passive taps on the uplinks feeding a broker that load-balances across the sensor's interfaces

questionsV2.explanation:
Two things went wrong and both follow from mirroring. Copying eight directions of 10-gigabit traffic into one 10-gigabit port oversubscribes the monitor path by design, and a switch under load discards mirrored frames before forwarded ones, silently, because monitoring is best effort on the same forwarding hardware.
Passive taps sit in the physical path and copy at line rate whatever the switch is doing, and a broker in front of the sensor spreads that aggregate across enough interfaces to carry it (D).
A sensor that cannot tell you what it missed is reporting on its own inbox.
questionsV2.recallLine: A mirrored session copies four uplinks into one monitor port, and the sensor silently missed traffic. Which change MOST reliably delivers every frame at peak?

optionsShort.A: A second monitor port and session
optionsShort.B: Sampled flow export for correlation
optionsShort.C: Bigger capture buffer on the sensor
optionsShort.D: Passive taps into a load-balancing broker

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Halves nothing that matters. The same aggregate exceeds the mirror capacity, and both sessions compete with production forwarding.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Answers a different question well, giving metadata at a fraction of the volume. Sampled records reconstruct no uncaptured payload.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Enlarges a buffer at the wrong end of the wire. The frames the switch dropped were never sent to the sensor to be buffered.

sources: NIST SP 800-94 | Guide to Intrusion Detection and Prevention Systems, §4.1 sensor placement
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SI-4 System Monitoring

questionsV2.question: Fennimore Health District has finished an 802.1X rollout across 4,000 access ports. Two hundred and ten devices cannot run a supplicant: badge readers, label printers, and patient monitors whose vendor forbids configuration changes. The network team admits these by MAC authentication bypass. A tester then showed that copying a printer's hardware address onto a laptop put the laptop on the clinical VLAN in under a minute, with the same reach as any nurse's workstation. Replacing the devices is a four-year capital program. Which arrangement BEST limits what that spoofing can reach in the meantime?

options.A: Continuous profiling that re-checks each device's fingerprint and quarantines a port on change
options.B: Bypassed ports placed in a restricted VLAN permitted to reach their management servers
options.C: Port security limiting each bypassed port to a single learned hardware address
options.D: A monthly audit comparing the bypass list against the clinical asset inventory

questionsV2.explanation:
Bypass is an admission decision taken on an identifier the device broadcasts and anybody can copy. While those 210 devices remain, the exposure cannot be closed. It can be made small.
Put bypassed ports in their own VLAN that reaches the print and monitoring servers and little else (B). A spoofed address then buys an attacker a segment with a handful of destinations in it.
Where admission cannot be trusted, make what it admits people to small.
questionsV2.recallLine: Devices that cannot run 802.1X are admitted by MAC bypass, and the address is trivially spoofed. Which arrangement BEST limits what a spoofer reaches?

optionsShort.A: Continuous profiling that quarantines on fingerprint change
optionsShort.B: Restricted VLAN reaching their management servers
optionsShort.C: Port security limiting one learned address
optionsShort.D: Monthly audit of the bypass list

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: Worth running, and it acts after the fact. Fingerprints are forgeable too, and a quarantine follows a session that has already started.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Counts addresses without checking them. An attacker presenting one copied address presents exactly the single address the port expects.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Keeps the bypass list honest as devices come and go. Inventory hygiene on a monthly rhythm, and no limit on what a laptop reaches.

sources: IEEE 802.1X-2020 | Port-Based Network Access Control
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-7(21) Isolation of System Components

questionsV2.question: Lambert and Crowe, a 300-person accountancy firm, lost 40 workstations to ransomware in ninety minutes. The forensic timeline is short: one user opened an attachment, and the malware then authenticated as that user to file shares on 39 other workstations, all reachable from each other on a flat office LAN, and encrypted the documents it found on each. Every machine already runs a managed endpoint agent, and re-imaging started within the hour. Re-segmenting the office LAN is two quarters of work. Which host-based control would MOST directly have stopped the spread from workstation to workstation?

options.A: A host firewall policy denying inbound file sharing between workstations on the office LAN
options.B: An endpoint agent rule terminating processes that rename many documents in quick succession
options.C: Application allow-listing that permits signed executables from an approved publisher list
options.D: Removing local administrator rights from every user's day-to-day account on the workstations

questionsV2.explanation:
The spread used a network service the workstations were offering each other, with credentials the malware already held. The control that stops it closes that service between peers.
A host firewall policy refusing inbound file sharing from other workstations (A) leaves the machines able to reach servers, leaves the malware nothing to authenticate to sideways, and ships this quarter instead of in the two that re-segmentation needs.
Where the network cannot be segmented yet, the host can refuse its neighbors.
questionsV2.recallLine: Ransomware spread between workstations over file shares using one user's credentials on a flat LAN. Which host-based control MOST directly stops that hop?

optionsShort.A: Host firewall denying peer-to-peer file sharing
optionsShort.B: Agent rule killing mass renaming processes
optionsShort.C: Allow-listing signed executables from approved publishers
optionsShort.D: Remove local administrator rights from users

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Fires after encryption has begun on each machine in turn. It cuts the loss and prevents no hop.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Would have stopped the attachment executing at all, one step earlier. It does nothing once code is already running as the user.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Limits privilege. The shares reached here were ordinary user shares, so an unprivileged account was enough for every hop.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-7(12) Host-Based Protection
NIST SP 800-83 Rev 1 | Malware Incident Prevention and Handling, §3

questionsV2.question: Whitlock Partners holds its quarterly partnership meetings on a conferencing platform. Every meeting is created from one partner's personal meeting room, whose identifier has not changed in three years, and telephone dial-in is enabled so partners can join from court. A journalist published a verbatim account of a partnership discussion the following day. The platform's log shows 14 telephone participants in a meeting with 11 invited partners, and it records dial-in participants by caller identifier and nothing more. Which change to the meeting arrangements MOST directly closes the path that was used?

options.A: End-to-end encryption enabled for the partnership meetings on the platform
options.B: Single sign-on required for the desktop and mobile clients before joining
options.C: Per-meeting identifiers and passcodes, with a lobby the host admits participants from
options.D: Recording disabled and transcripts retained for thirty days on the platform

questionsV2.explanation:
A standing meeting identifier that has not changed in three years is a password shared with every participant the firm has ever had, and the telephone bridge reaches it without touching the firm's identity system.
Generate a fresh identifier and passcode for each meeting, and hold arrivals in a lobby the host admits from (C). Last quarter's number stops working, and an unexpected caller waits somewhere a human can see them.
A credential that never changes is a credential everyone still has.
questionsV2.recallLine: A standing personal meeting room with telephone dial-in admitted three uninvited callers to a confidential meeting. Which change MOST directly closes that path?

optionsShort.A: End-to-end encryption for the meetings
optionsShort.B: Single sign-on for the desktop clients
optionsShort.C: Per-meeting passcode with a host-admitted lobby
optionsShort.D: Recording disabled, transcripts kept thirty days

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Protects the media in transit from an eavesdropper on the network. The extra callers here were admitted participants.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: A real improvement that governs the application clients. A telephone bridge does not authenticate against a directory.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Governs the artifact after the meeting ends. What was published was the discussion itself.

sources: CISA | Guidance for Securing Video Conferencing (2020)
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3 Access Enforcement

questionsV2.question: Northcliff Energy gives 65 engineers at an analytics contractor access to one internal application, a reservoir modeling tool published on a web server in the corporate datacenter. Each contractor connects today with the corporate VPN client, which places their laptop on a routable address inside the corporate network; an access list on the concentrator is meant to hold them to the one server, and last month's review found 31 rules on it matching no current contract. The architect wants the contractors' reach cut to that single application. Which remote-access design BEST achieves that?

options.A: The existing VPN, with the concentrator's access list rebuilt and reviewed each quarter
options.B: A jump host in a screened segment from which contractors open the application
options.C: A clientless portal on the concentrator presenting the modeling tool through a browser
options.D: An identity-aware proxy publishing the modeling tool, with no network route to anything else

questionsV2.explanation:
Any of these can be made correct on the day it is built. What separates them is what the design leaves behind when nobody is watching it.
A proxy that publishes the application authorizes each request against the user and the device, and never hands the laptop a route into the network (D). There is no list whose decay quietly widens access.
Prefer the design that has no maintained list to decay.
questionsV2.recallLine: Contractors reach one internal application over a VPN that places them on the corporate network behind a stale access list. Which design BEST cuts their reach?

optionsShort.A: The same VPN with a rebuilt access list
optionsShort.B: A jump host in a screened segment
optionsShort.C: A clientless browser portal on the concentrator
optionsShort.D: An identity-aware proxy publishing one application

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: The same architecture with a tidier list. Keeping 65 contractors' rules current is work nobody owns, so it will decay again.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Trades a network route for an interactive session on a host inside the estate. Right for administrators, too much for one application.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: Removes the client software and still terminates on the concentrator, so reach is governed by the list that just failed its review.

sources: NIST SP 800-207 | Zero Trust Architecture, §3.2.3 resource portal-based deployment
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-17(3) Managed Access Control Points

domains.title: Identity & Access Management (IAM)
domains.caseStudy:
Domain 5 is identification, authentication, authorization and accountability, applied to people, devices and services. It covers access control models, the identity lifecycle, federation, and privileged access.

Case Study: The "Omni-Key" Insider Threat

### Context

QuickCash Inc. operates 300 ATMs. To save time, the regional manager created one administrative account, "SuperAdmin", password "Welcome123!", and shared it among the five field technicians. The account had unrestricted rights on the ATM management console, including PIN resets and account limits. The physical master keys for the ATM safes lived in an unlocked desk drawer in the regional office, in an envelope labelled "ATM Keys".

### What went wrong

A technician who knew he was about to be dismissed logged in as SuperAdmin from home. There was no MFA. He created ten customer accounts with high withdrawal limits, took the master keys from the drawer, drove to five ATMs, put each into service mode with the shared key, and withdrew $200,000 in cash using the accounts he had made.

The logs showed SuperAdmin logging in and SuperAdmin creating accounts. Five people could have been SuperAdmin. QuickCash could not prove which one until the cash was gone.

The white paper's access-management controls read like a list of what QuickCash lacked: MFA for technicians, administrators and any remote access; role-based access limiting each user to the minimum their job needs; default and shared passwords replaced. Its physical controls add key management and unique locks, and it notes that attackers installing malware may pose as technicians precisely because a technician's access is rarely questioned.

### What a practitioner does differently

One identity per person, always. Privileged access goes through a PAM system: the technician checks out a time-limited credential for a named task, the session is recorded, and the credential expires. MFA on every remote and privileged path. Roles split by job: a field technician gets service-mode rights on assigned machines, not console administration; account creation and limit changes belong to a separate role, and setting a limit above a threshold needs a second approver. That is separation of duties, and it would have stopped the fake accounts on the first day.

The leaver process starts when the decision to dismiss is made, before the employee is told. Access ends with the decision, not with the exit interview.

Physical keys are credentials. They live in a key cabinet with a log, under dual control, and a machine entering service mode outside a scheduled ticket raises an alert. The white paper's monitoring section lists exactly the transaction signals that would have fired here: rapid maximum withdrawals and unusual frequency from a single card.

### Outcome

The technician was identified from the ATM's camera, not from the logs. QuickCash retired the shared account, issued individual credentials with MFA, moved the keys into a controlled cabinet, and rewrote its termination procedure so revocation precedes notification.

### What the exam tests

Scenarios like this test IAAA and non-repudiation (shared accounts destroy accountability), least privilege and separation of duties, the account lifecycle and why deprovisioning is time-critical, the access control models and where RBAC fits, the factor types behind MFA, and the idea that physical access is part of identity management, not a separate concern.

### Related reading

The company in this scenario is a composite. The controls are documented in:

- [Technical Risks and Attack Vectors Targeting ATMs](https://portfolio.atmavailability.com/atm-technical-risks-white-paper.pdf), the sections on access management, on physical security controls (key management), and on monitoring.
- [ATM Security Capability Maturity Worksheet](https://portfolio.atmavailability.com/atm-capability-maturity-worksheet.pdf), Domain 1 (physical) and Domain 4 (process and governance) controls.

questions.question: Forensic investigators reviewing the QuickCash breach can see that 'SuperAdmin' logged in from a residential IP address and created the fake customer accounts, yet no individual can be charged. Which IAAA failure is the PRIMARY cause of this inability to attribute the actions?

options.A: Authentication - the account was protected by a single weak password
options.B: Identification - five people operated the console under one user identity
options.C: Authorization - the account held far more rights than technicians needed
options.D: Accountability - the console failed to log administrative sessions

questions.explanation: Attribution collapsed because the log could name only an identity, and that identity was shared: with five people behind one account, even perfect logging cannot say who acted. (A) is a real weakness - 'Welcome123!' with no MFA made compromise easy - but even a strong, MFA-protected shared account would still leave five suspects; it explains ease of entry, not loss of attribution. (C) is also true of this environment, but excessive rights widened what the insider could do; that goes to impact and does nothing to name him. (D) misreads the evidence: sessions were logged - the record said 'SuperAdmin logged in' - so accountability failed downstream of shared identification; the logging itself worked. Accountability can only ever be as granular as identification; unique identities are the foundation the other IAAA elements stand on.

questions.question: QuickCash Inc.'s five field technicians share a single 'SuperAdmin' account on the ATM management console. After a technician used it from home to create fake customer accounts and withdraw $200,000, the logs showed only that 'SuperAdmin' logged in, and no individual could be tied to the transactions. The security manager has budget for one change this quarter. Which change should the security manager recommend FIRST?

options.A: Enforce a 16-character password on the shared account and rotate it monthly
options.B: Issue each technician a uniquely named account and disable the shared account
options.C: Require multi-factor authentication for all remote logins to the console
options.D: Reduce the technicians' rights from SuperAdmin to a scoped field-service role

questions.explanation: Identification precedes authentication, authorization and accountability: until each person has a distinct identity, none of the other controls can produce an attributable log entry - MFA on a shared account still writes 'SuperAdmin logged in', and a scoped role shared by five people is still shared. The word FIRST decides it: A, C and D are all correct controls, and all three become fully effective only once B exists; that dependency, not managerial preference, makes B first. (A) strengthens the secret without changing whom the secret identifies - the right answer once accounts are individual and the finding is credential guessability. (C) is a genuinely serious gap, but five technicians sharing one account would share the MFA enrolment, so attribution stays broken - the right answer once unique identities exist and the concern is remote credential theft. (D) limits blast radius and not restoring attribution - the right answer to how you would limit the damage one compromised account can do.

questions.question: The QuickCash technician reached the ATM console from his home computer using only the shared password. Which additional control would have been MOST effective at stopping this remote use of a credential the attacker already knew?

options.A: A stricter complexity policy applied to every administrative password
options.B: Quarterly security-awareness training on credential handling for technicians
options.C: A second authentication factor, such as a hardware token, for remote sessions
options.D: An intrusion detection sensor alerting the SOC whenever administrative logins originate from residential networks

questions.explanation: Because the attacker legitimately knew the password, the only listed control that stops the session at the point of entry is one demanding evidence he did not have: possession of an enrolled token. Hardening the secret itself (A) still leaves a single factor already known to all five technicians; that would fix a finding of guessability by outsiders. (B) targets negligence, but no amount of training restrains an insider acting deliberately - it belongs where the failure is accidental disclosure. (D) is detective, firing while or after the abuse occurs, and would be the right choice if the question asked how to detect anomalous administrative logins. Against a credential the attacker already holds, prevention must come from a second, different factor.

questions.question: An organization has rolled out app-generated time-based one-time codes as a second factor on its webmail after a wave of account takeovers in which employees typed their passwords into lookalike login sites. Which attack technique is MOST likely to still succeed against the upgraded login?

options.A: Credential stuffing that replays username and password pairs harvested from breaches of unrelated services
options.B: Offline cracking of stolen password hashes using precomputed tables
options.C: A scripted brute-force loop guessing all possible six-digit codes against the login endpoint
options.D: A proxy page that captures and instantly relays both the password and current code

questions.explanation: A TOTP code is bound to a clock, not to the site the user types it into, so an adversary-in-the-middle page can capture the password and the current code and replay both to the real service inside the validity window - the newly deployed control does not break that flow. (A) now fails because a stolen password alone no longer completes login; stuffing would be the residual threat had MFA been skipped. (B) yields passwords and then hits the same second-factor wall; it would be the concern if the question were about theft of an unsalted credential database. (C) is defeated by the 30-second code lifetime combined with ordinary attempt throttling; it would matter only on an endpoint with no rate limiting at all. OTP-based MFA raises the bar yet stays phishable in real time; closing the gap takes an origin-bound, phishing-resistant method such as FIDO2/WebAuthn.

questions.question: An auditor is reviewing QuickCash's proposed console login upgrade, which the standard requires to be genuine multi-factor authentication. Which combination should the auditor accept as meeting that requirement?

options.A: A smart card inserted at the console together with a memorized PIN
options.B: A primary password backed by answers to personal challenge questions
options.C: A fingerprint scan confirmed by an iris scan at the same panel
options.D: A console password plus a second passphrase held by the same technician

questions.explanation: Multi-factor means evidence from two different categories - something you know, have, or are - because credentials of the same category tend to fall to the same attack. A card plus a PIN pairs possession with knowledge: a shoulder-surfed PIN is useless without the card, a stolen card useless without the PIN. (B) stacks knowledge on knowledge; challenge answers are memorized facts, often researchable from social media, and one phishing call can harvest both. (C) stacks inherence on inherence - two strong biometrics, but one category, so it remains single-factor; the second biometric buys accuracy, nothing more. (D) is two knowledge secrets in one head; a single keylogger session captures both. Count the factor categories, not the number of prompts.

questions.question: QuickCash is deploying a second authentication factor for field technicians who service ATMs in rural areas where mobile coverage is unreliable, and company policy bars personal phones from work use. Which factor is MOST appropriate for this workforce?

options.A: One-time codes delivered to each technician by SMS text message
options.B: Push-notification approvals sent to a corporate smartphone application
options.C: A dedicated hardware token displaying time-based one-time codes
options.D: One-time codes emailed to each technician's corporate mailbox

questions.explanation: A hardware TOTP token computes codes locally from a synchronized clock and stored seed, so it needs no signal, no phone and no mailbox - the only option compatible with both stated constraints. Codes over SMS (A) depend on cellular coverage at exactly the sites where it is unreliable, and NIST SP 800-63B additionally classes SMS delivery as a restricted, weaker out-of-band channel; that option suits consumer populations in covered areas. (B) needs a data connection plus a smartphone, colliding with both constraints; it is a good choice for office staff with managed devices. (D) requires network reachability at the ATM site, and if the mailbox is protected by the same password under attack, both factors collapse into one channel. Offline sites need possession factors that compute their codes locally instead of receiving them.

questions.question: Following a rash of account takeovers, an analyst finds the helpdesk resets any password for a caller who can state the employee's birthday and manager's name - details attackers routinely harvest from social media. Which change to the reset process would MOST reduce this exposure?

options.A: Add several further personal questions about employment history to the verification script
options.B: Require reset callers to also state their employee ID number and department
options.C: Rotate the personal verification questions on a monthly schedule across the whole team
options.D: Confirm each request via a push prompt to the employee's enrolled device

questions.explanation: The flaw is structural: every check in the current script is knowledge that lives outside the company's control, so an attacker who researches the target passes it. Routing approval through a device already enrolled to the employee moves verification onto a possession factor the caller cannot fake from research. (A) adds more of the same failed category - employment history is exactly the kind of fact professional networking profiles publish, so it is researchable too - and would help only against unprepared opportunists. (B) fails the same way: employee IDs leak through email signatures and directory exports, so they remain harvestable knowledge. (C) changes which facts are asked without changing that facts are the medium - rotation is the right idea for shared secrets like passwords, misapplied here to identity proofing.

questions.question: Technicians complain that the fingerprint reader guarding the ATM service panel rejects them repeatedly in cold weather, so an administrator lowers the match-confidence threshold until the complaints stop. What is the MOST significant security consequence of this adjustment?

options.A: The false acceptance rate rises, so impostors will match more easily
options.B: The crossover error rate improves, making the sensor more accurate
options.C: The failure-to-enroll rate increases for users with worn fingerprints
options.D: The false rejection rate rises further, locking even more legitimate users out

questions.explanation: False accepts and false rejects sit at opposite ends of one tuning curve: relaxing the threshold to admit poorly captured legitimate prints necessarily also admits poorer impostor prints, trading Type I errors for Type II errors - and a false accept at an unattended cash machine is the expensive direction. (B) misunderstands CER, which is a fixed property of the device measured where FAR equals FRR; moving the operating threshold does not change the sensor's underlying accuracy. (C) confuses verification with registration - failure to enroll happens at enrolment time and is unaffected by the matching threshold. (D) inverts the direction of the change: rejections were the pre-change complaint, and lowering the threshold reduces false rejections; it cannot drive them up.

questions.question: A security team must set biometric matching thresholds for two doors: the unattended vault anteroom, and the staffed main entrance where a guard also checks badges. How should the team bias the two thresholds?

options.A: Apply one uniform threshold at both doors so error rates remain consistent
options.B: Bias the vault door toward acceptance to avoid delaying cash-handling operations
options.C: Bias the vault door toward false rejections and the guarded entrance toward false acceptances
options.D: Bias both doors toward acceptance because badge checks already provide a compensating control everywhere

questions.explanation: The surrounding controls decide which error type is tolerable at each point. At an unattended vault door a false acceptance is unrecoverable, so the threshold should be strict even though staff get rejected more often; at the guarded entrance an occasional false acceptance is caught by the guard, so a looser threshold that cuts queue-building rejections is the better trade. Option (A) treats tuning as a consistency exercise, ignoring that the cost of each error differs by location - uniformity is the right answer only where the doors protect equivalent assets. (B) optimizes convenience precisely where an admitted impostor does the greatest damage. (D) is half right, and 'everywhere' is where it fails: badge checks do compensate at the staffed entrance, but no compensating human control exists at the unattended vault anteroom.

questions.question: An analyst comparing three fingerprint products finds each vendor quotes impressive numbers measured at different threshold settings - one boasts the fewest false accepts, another the fewest rejects. Which figure gives the analyst the fairest single basis for comparing the systems?

options.A: The lowest false acceptance rate that each vendor quotes in its datasheet
options.B: The false rejection rate each vendor measured during its own pilot
options.C: The failure-to-enroll rate observed across the user population
options.D: The crossover error rate, where false accepts and false rejects are equal

questions.explanation: Since FAR and FRR both move with the threshold, any vendor can make either number look excellent by choosing where to measure; the crossover point removes that freedom by fixing the comparison at the setting where the two error rates meet, so a lower CER genuinely means a more accurate sensor. (A) and (B) are each one end of a tunable trade - quoting either alone is exactly the marketing trick the analyst has run into, though each becomes relevant again when tuning the chosen product for its site's risk bias. (C) measures how many users can register at all, which matters for usability and population coverage but says nothing about matching accuracy once enrolled.

questions.question: The post-incident review notes that QuickCash's field technicians only ever performed cash replenishment and diagnostics, yet every technician held full 'SuperAdmin' rights on the console, including PIN reset and account creation. Which principle did this rights assignment MOST directly violate?

options.A: Least privilege, because the accounts carried powers the job did not require
options.B: Separation of duties, because one team both requested and approved its access
options.C: Dual control, because sensitive operations could proceed without a second person
options.D: Need to know, because technicians could browse customer transaction records

questions.explanation: The mismatch the stem describes is between duties and powers: the job needed service functions, the account granted everything, and that surplus of capability is precisely what least privilege forbids. (B) names a real weakness of QuickCash's governance, but the stem describes excessive rights, not a missing split between requesting and approving - separation of duties would be the most direct answer if one person could both initiate and authorize a payment. (C) is about requiring two people for a single sensitive act - a compensating control layered on top, while the stem asks which principle the rights assignment breaks. (D) is the data-access sibling of least privilege and is arguably also violated, but the stem's examples - PIN reset, account creation - are capabilities, not data views, so it is the less direct fit. When powers exceed duties, cite least privilege; reserve need to know for surplus access to information.

questions.question: After the breach, QuickCash must overhaul how ATM safe master keys are managed; today they sit in an unlocked drawer that any office visitor could reach. Which replacement practice would BEST bring physical key handling into line with IAM principles?

options.A: Issue keys individually from an audited cabinet with per-person sign-out records
options.B: Install a camera covering the key storage area so removals can be reviewed
options.C: Move the keys into a locked cabinet whose combination all technicians share
options.D: Remove the identifying label so a visitor cannot tell what the keys open

questions.explanation: Physical keys are credentials, and the case study's core lesson - one identity per person, with attributable use - applies to them exactly as it does to logins. An audited cabinet with individual sign-out restores identification and accountability for every key movement. (B) is purely detective: footage may show who took a key after cash has gone, and cameras are a sound complement once issuance is controlled. (C) upgrades the container but recreates the SuperAdmin defect in physical form - a shared combination is a shared credential, so no removal can be attributed. (D) is security through obscurity; a labeled drawer made the attack easier, but an unlabeled unlocked drawer is still an uncontrolled credential store.

questions.question: A defense contractor is implementing a document system that must enforce government classification markings, with the operating system imposing every access decision so that no file owner can override or reclassify on their own authority. Which access control model fits this requirement?

options.A: Role-based access control driven by job assignments
options.B: Discretionary access control administered by resource owners
options.C: Mandatory access control enforced through security labels
options.D: Attribute-based access control evaluating contextual rules

questions.explanation: Two phrases in the stem are decisive: classification markings, and decisions imposed by the system beyond any owner's authority - the defining pair of properties of mandatory access control, where subjects hold clearances, objects hold labels, and policy is centrally enforced. (A) grants by job function and would let an administrator or role owner adjust assignments, which the requirement excludes; it fits an enterprise organizing access around positions. (B) is the direct opposite of the requirement, since discretion by the owner is exactly what must be removed. (D) could emulate labels among its attributes, but its purpose is dynamic, condition-based decisions and not a rigid lattice of clearances - the right answer when access must vary with time, location or device.

questions.question: An auditor discovers that spreadsheets holding cardholder data on a Windows file share were readable company-wide because the files' creators had granted 'Everyone' read access on their own initiative. Which characteristic of the environment's access control model made this possible?

options.A: Rule-based control applies one uniform policy to every subject
options.B: Discretionary control leaves grant decisions with each resource owner
options.C: Mandatory control ties every access decision to clearance levels
options.D: Role-based control links permissions to defined job functions

questions.explanation: Windows NTFS permissions follow the discretionary model: whoever owns a file may share it at will, so a well-meaning creator can quietly grant the world access to regulated data, and that owner discretion is the exact mechanism the auditor observed. Option (A) describes system-wide rules such as firewall-style conditions; had one uniform policy governed the share, individual creators could not have loosened it, and the finding would look different. (C) would have made the oversharing impossible, since labels and clearances remove the owner's choice; it explains a different environment, not this one. (D) would bound access by job function, and the finding shows access following individual grant decisions, not roles. DAC's convenience is its risk: owner-controlled sharing scales into uncontrolled sprawl unless monitored or replaced for sensitive data.

questions.question: A retail company with heavy seasonal turnover wants store associates' access created and removed automatically from HR job codes, so every cashier receives an identical, pre-approved permission bundle on day one. Which access control model BEST supports this goal?

options.A: Discretionary access control, letting each store manager grant what is needed
options.B: Mandatory access control, labeling every resource by sensitivity level
options.C: Attribute-based access control, evaluating dynamic conditions at request time
options.D: Role-based access control, mapping permission bundles to defined job functions
