B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Describes the older NTLM scheme, which Kerberos environments keep only as a fallback. Hash reuse is a weakness to minimize.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Would be a dangerous design, and one Kerberos was built to avoid. Tickets exist so the long-term secret is barely used.

questionsV2.question: Which remediation BEST addresses both findings on the service account?

options.A: Rotate the service account password and store it in the team's vault
options.B: Rename the account to obscure its function from observers
options.C: Enroll the service account in the company's standard MFA program
options.D: Scope the account to minimum required rights and block interactive logon

questionsV2.explanation:
The review surfaced two defects: excessive privilege, and human use of a machine identity. The remediation has to close both. Least-privilege scoping removes the domain-admin blast radius, and blocking interactive logon pushes technicians back onto their own accounts, restoring attribution (D).
Two findings need a remediation that closes both. Check the second one before accepting an answer that closes the first.
questionsV2.recallLine: A monitoring service account holds domain administrator rights, and technicians sign in with it interactively. Which remediation BEST addresses both findings?

optionsShort.A: Rotate the password and vault it
optionsShort.B: Rename the account to obscure its function
optionsShort.C: Enroll the service account in standard MFA
optionsShort.D: Scope rights down and block interactive logon

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: Sound hygiene that leaves both findings standing. The freshly rotated secret still carries domain admin.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Obscurity. An attacker enumerating privileged group membership finds the account whatever it is called.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Misfits the account type. Unattended software cannot answer an interactive MFA prompt.

questionsV2.question: Which account of the new operational risk this architecture introduces is MOST accurate?

options.A: An outage at the provider can block sign-in to every connected application at once
options.B: Each connected application must now hold and protect its own copy of user passwords
options.C: Multi-factor authentication can no longer be enforced on cloud logins
options.D: Password hashes must be replicated out to every application in the federation

questionsV2.explanation: Centralizing authentication concentrates availability risk. One provider brokers every login, so its outage - or the loss of connectivity to it - takes the whole application portfolio down at once (A). The previous per-application logins had no such shared fate. That is why IDaaS adoption should come with SLA scrutiny and break-glass access for critical systems.
questionsV2.recallLine: Workforce authentication is moving to a cloud identity provider. Which account of the new operational risk that architecture introduces is MOST accurate?

optionsShort.A: A provider outage blocks sign-in everywhere at once
optionsShort.B: Each application now stores its own password copies
optionsShort.C: MFA can no longer be enforced on cloud logins
optionsShort.D: Password hashes replicate out to every application

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Inverts how federation works. Applications receive signed assertions or tokens and are specifically relieved of holding passwords.

C.label: true of a different thing
C.wouldAnswer: Backwards in practice. IDaaS platforms make strong MFA easier to enforce uniformly than scattered legacy apps ever did.

D.label: true of a different thing
D.wouldAnswer: Confuses federation with credential synchronization. Trust flows through tokens; hashes stay in the identity platform.

questionsV2.question: Which term BEST describes entering fabricated records with inflated limits before making withdrawals?

options.A: A salami attack, accumulating value through many tiny skimmed amounts
options.B: Data diddling, manipulating records as they are entered into the system
options.C: A logic bomb, planting code that triggers on a preset condition
options.D: A race condition, exploiting the gap between a check and its use

questionsV2.explanation:
The fraud lived in the input step. Records were fabricated as they went into the system, and every downstream control then treated the poisoned data as legitimate. That is the defining shape of data diddling (B), or input fraud.
Classifying fraud by mechanism matters because each kind is caught by different controls.
questionsV2.recallLine: A technician entered fabricated customer records with inflated limits before withdrawing cash. Which term BEST describes that fraud?

optionsShort.A: Salami attack: value accumulated in tiny slices
optionsShort.B: Data diddling: records manipulated as they are entered
optionsShort.C: Logic bomb: code triggered by a preset condition
optionsShort.D: Race condition: exploiting the check-to-use gap

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: The tempting neighbor. Salami harvests value in slices too small to notice, and ten fake accounts and $200,000 is neither.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Requires planted code awaiting a trigger. The technician wrote no software. He wrote data.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Exploits timing between validation and use, a software flaw absent here.

questionsV2.question: What must happen BEFORE a directory account is issued to a seasonal adjuster?

options.A: A manager's attestation that the applicant is genuine is recorded in the onboarding ticket.
options.B: The license is validated with the issuing authority and matched to the applicant.
options.C: A hardware authenticator is issued and bound to the adjuster at first sign-in.
options.D: An email verification link is sent and clicked to confirm the applicant's address.

questionsV2.explanation:
Enrollment has an order, and the order is the control. NIST SP 800-63A resolves, validates and verifies the claimed identity; only then does SP 800-63B bind an authenticator to the subject that proofing produced. Validating the license with the issuing authority and matching it to the applicant (B) is what makes the resulting account refer to a human being.
Decide what an identity asserts before deciding how hard it is to steal.
questionsV2.recallLine: Before a seasonal adjuster's account is created, which step establishes that the applicant is the person hired?

optionsShort.A: A manager's attestation filed in the ticket
optionsShort.B: Validate the license with the issuing authority
optionsShort.C: Bind a hardware authenticator at first sign-in
optionsShort.D: Click an emailed verification link

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Authorization to create the account. It is no evidence of who will hold it, and a hiring manager can be socially engineered.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Necessary, and later. Bind a token to an unproven identity and you get a well-protected fiction.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Demonstrates control of an email address. Adequate for a newsletter, not for an adjuster who can release payments.

sources: NIST SP 800-63A-3 | §5 Identity Resolution, Validation, and Verification
NIST SP 800-63B-3 | §6.1 Authenticator Binding
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.2.4

questionsV2.question: Which control MOST directly limits an insurer's exposure to weak identity proofing inside Oakhaven's identity provider?

options.A: Require each assertion to carry its assurance level and refuse those below the threshold.
options.B: Sign the assertions with a certificate the insurers pin and rotate on schedule.
options.C: Ask Oakhaven for a monthly report of accounts created without a license check.
options.D: Issue portal accounts locally at each insurer and stop consuming Oakhaven's assertion.

questionsV2.explanation:
Federation divides one act of trust between two parties, and each controls a different half. The identity provider decides how hard it proofs. The relying party decides what it will accept, and it exercises that choice by requiring each assertion to carry its assurance level and refusing anything below the portal's floor (A). NIST SP 800-63C provides the mechanism for exactly this asymmetry.
Ask which party can act on the answer before choosing the control.
questionsV2.recallLine: A relying party consumes another firm's identity assertions. What MOST directly limits its exposure to weak proofing at the identity provider?

optionsShort.A: Reject assertions below a required assurance level
optionsShort.B: Pin and rotate the assertion signing certificate
optionsShort.C: Monthly self-report from the identity provider
optionsShort.D: Replace federation with locally issued accounts

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Protects the assertion in transit and at rest. A genuine assertion about a poorly proofed person passes every signature check.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Hands the assurance decision back to the party whose process is in doubt. A self-report is worth the reporter's controls.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Removes the assertion and keeps the risk. The person behind the local account is still whoever Oakhaven hired without checking.

sources: NIST SP 800-63C-3 | §4 Federation Assurance Level
NIST SP 800-63C-3 | §6 Assertions
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.2.5

questionsV2.question: Which design change BEST stops group membership from being decided by whichever adjuster a new hire resembles?

options.A: Name every group after the team it serves and record an owner for each.
options.B: Give each adjuster a personal group and attach that person's entitlements to it.
options.C: Copy a long-serving adjuster's account and remove the rights the new hire lacks.
options.D: Grant entitlements to roles derived from job codes and place people in roles.

questionsV2.explanation:
Cloning copies a decision nobody wrote down, and it compounds: each clone inherits the last clone's mistakes. Roles derived from job codes (D) break the chain, because the job carries the entitlements. The permission assignment lives on the role, the user assignment lives on the person, and the two are maintained separately, as ANSI INCITS 359 sets out.
Grant to a job description, not to a precedent.
questionsV2.recallLine: New joiners get access copied from an existing colleague. Which design change BEST stops membership being decided by resemblance?

optionsShort.A: Name and assign an owner to each group
optionsShort.B: A personal group for every adjuster
optionsShort.C: Clone a colleague's account, then trim rights
optionsShort.D: Entitlements on roles derived from job codes

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Worth doing, and it leaves the decision where it was. A well-named, well-owned group is still populated by resemblance.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Scales to 400 personal groups, each needing its own review. The individual entitlement problem with indirection on top.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Keeps cloning and adds a trim. The new hire starts from someone else's history, and the reviewer has to know what to subtract.

sources: ANSI INCITS 359-2004 | Role Based Access Control, core RBAC assignments
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-2 Account Management
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.2.1

questionsV2.question: Which change MOST directly stops entitlements accumulating when an adjuster moves to another team?

options.A: Add a quarterly recertification in which managers confirm the entitlements each adjuster holds.
options.B: Require a second approver for any payment release above a set amount.
options.C: Revoke the previous role's entitlements as part of granting the new role.
options.D: Ask the receiving manager to list rights the mover no longer needs.

questionsV2.explanation:
A transfer is two lifecycle events that organizations habitually run as one: a leave from the old job, a join to the new one. Tie revocation to the grant (C) and the mover becomes the same shape as a joiner. It is the one step here that acts at the moment the accumulation happens.
Look for the event that should have triggered the change, then attach the control to that event.
questionsV2.recallLine: An adjuster promoted to fraud review keeps the old payment-release right. Which change MOST directly stops entitlements accumulating at transfer?

optionsShort.A: Quarterly manager recertification of entitlements
optionsShort.B: Second approver on large payment releases
optionsShort.C: Revoke the old role when granting the new
optionsShort.D: Receiving manager lists rights to remove

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: Finds the leftover right up to three months later, and the March promotions show how long that window stays open.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Limits what the extra right can do, which is a real segregation-of-duties control. The stray entitlement stays granted.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: Puts the work after the move, and on the manager least likely to know what the old job required.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-2h Account Management, notification when users are terminated or transferred
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-6 Least Privilege
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.5.3

questionsV2.question: Which arrangement BEST lets Saltmarsh change an access rule without a release of each application?

options.A: Have the gateway forward each request to a policy service and enforce its verdict.
options.B: Encode the rules in the gateway's configuration so it decides and forwards together.
options.C: Publish a signed policy document that each application owner implements in their code.
options.D: Log every gateway verdict and alert when an application's own decision disagrees.

questionsV2.explanation:
Split the decision point from the enforcement point, because they change at different rates. Policy changes weekly; the places that enforce it change yearly. In the model NIST SP 800-162 describes, the gateway is a policy enforcement point that asks a policy decision point and applies the verdict (A). A new rule is deployed once, and every enforcement point obeys it at the next request.
Ask where a rule lives before asking who enforces it.
questionsV2.recallLine: An access gateway fronts three applications that each hold their own permission table. Which arrangement BEST lets one rule change reach all three?

optionsShort.A: Gateway asks a policy service and enforces
optionsShort.B: Rules encoded in the gateway's own configuration
optionsShort.C: A signed policy each team implements in code
optionsShort.D: Log verdicts and alert on disagreement

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Centralizes enforcement and marries the decision to it. A second gateway then needs its own rules and its own change window.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Leaves the decision with three development teams and three release trains. A policy shipped as a document gets built three ways.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Observes disagreement after the fact and changes nothing about who decides.

sources: NIST SP 800-162 | ABAC access control mechanism: policy decision and enforcement points
OASIS XACML 3.0 | §3.1 data-flow model (PEP, PDP, PAP, PIP)
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3 Access Enforcement

questionsV2.question: Which mechanism MOST directly enforces the $50,000 condition without depending on who the trader is?

options.A: Grant a role to the traders who are authorized to place large orders.
options.B: Let each desk head decide at their discretion who may exceed the limit.
options.C: Deny orders above the threshold when the request comes from an unmanaged device.
options.D: Label orders and workstations by sensitivity and let the system compare the labels.

questionsV2.explanation:
Access control models differ in what the decision is a function of. Role-based decisions are a function of the subject's job. Discretionary decisions are a function of an owner's choice. Mandatory decisions are a function of labels carried by subject and object. A rule-based decision is a function of the request's own attributes: amount, device state, network. Deny orders above the threshold from an unmanaged device (C) and the rule applies identically to the newest trader and to the head of the desk. That is what a compliance condition written about orders needs.
Read the requirement and ask what the decision has to be a function of.
questionsV2.recallLine: A rule applies to every trade over a set amount regardless of the trader. Which access control model MOST directly expresses it?

optionsShort.A: A role for large-order traders
optionsShort.B: Desk heads waive the limit at discretion
optionsShort.C: Deny above-threshold orders from unmanaged devices
optionsShort.D: Compare sensitivity labels on orders and workstations

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Puts the condition on the person, so a trader holding the role keeps it on an unmanaged laptop at home.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Makes the limit negotiable by the manager most motivated to waive it.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Would work, and it imposes a labeling scheme across every order and workstation to express one threshold.

sources: NISTIR 7316 | Assessment of Access Control Systems, access control policy classes
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3 Access Enforcement
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.4.2

questionsV2.question: Which control MOST reduces account-takeover losses while leaving an ordinary customer's sign-in unchanged?

options.A: Block sign-ins from countries where Saltmarsh has no retail customers, refreshed monthly.
options.B: Score each request on device, location and behavior, stepping up above a threshold.
options.C: Feed the gateway's signals into the fraud team's daily review queue for investigation.
options.D: Re-prompt for the account password before a transfer leaves the customer's account.

questionsV2.explanation:
Risk-based access control matches the strength of the challenge to the evidence in front of it. Score each request on device, location and behavior (B) and the sign-ins from the customer's usual device in the customer's usual city pass untouched, while the unusual few meet a second factor. NIST SP 800-53 IA-10 names this control, and it is the one choice here that spends friction where the risk actually is.
Match the challenge to the evidence.
questionsV2.recallLine: Account takeovers hit a retail brokerage. Which control MOST reduces the loss while leaving an ordinary customer's sign-in unchanged?

optionsShort.A: Geo-block countries with no retail customers
optionsShort.B: Score the request, step up above threshold
optionsShort.C: Send signals to a daily fraud queue
optionsShort.D: Re-prompt for the password before transfers

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Crude proxy for the same idea, failing both ways: it stops a customer on holiday and misses a rented domestic address.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Turns live signals into a queue read the next working day, by which time the trade has settled.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Asks for the credential the attacker already has. It obstructs the customer and nobody else.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-10 Adaptive Authentication
NIST SP 800-207 | §2.1 dynamic policy from observable state
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.4.6

questionsV2.question: Which change FIRST closes the path that lets a stolen session outlive the customer's password reset?

options.A: Expire the session cookie after thirty minutes without customer activity on the platform.
options.B: Mark the session cookie Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite to limit its exposure.
options.C: Require a second factor from the customer before a password change is accepted.
options.D: Invalidate every stored server-side session for the account when the password changes.

questionsV2.explanation:
A session is a second credential. It is issued at sign-in and valid on its own afterwards, which is why a password reset that leaves the old sessions running evicts nobody. Invalidating every stored server-side session for the account when the password changes (D) is what makes the reset mean something to a customer whose account is already being used. NIST SP 800-63B treats the session as a distinct binding with its own lifetime, and OWASP ASVS V3.3 requires termination on a credential change.
Any credential that survives revocation of the credential that created it has not been revoked.
questionsV2.recallLine: A customer resets a password while a hijacked session is live. Which change FIRST closes the path that keeps that session working?

optionsShort.A: Idle timeout of thirty minutes
optionsShort.B: Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite cookie flags
optionsShort.C: Second factor to change a password
optionsShort.D: Kill server-side sessions on password change

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: Shortens the window and does nothing about an attacker who keeps the session warm with activity.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Protects the cookie from theft in the browser. A cookie already stolen stays perfectly valid.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Hardens the reset event itself, which matters once the takeover has been discovered.

sources: NIST SP 800-63B-3 | §7.1 Session Bindings and §7.2 Reauthentication
OWASP ASVS 4.0 | V3.3 Session Termination
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.2.3

questionsV2.question: Which control MOST directly makes the tablet, and more than its user, an authenticated party?

options.A: Enforce a passcode and full-disk encryption on the tablets through device management.
options.B: Issue each enrolled tablet a certificate and require it on the sync connection.
options.C: Record every tablet's serial number in an inventory the supervisor reconciles monthly.
options.D: Route the sync through a VPN the tablets dial before reaching the platform.

questionsV2.explanation:
Kentmere authenticates a person and infers a device, which is why a tablet bought on an auction site syncs as happily as one of the 900. Issue each enrolled tablet a certificate and require it on the sync connection (B). A device credential held in the tablet's hardware key store, presented on the connection and checked against the enrollment record, makes the endpoint a subject the platform can accept or refuse. That is what NIST SP 800-53 IA-3 asks for.
Ask which party a system is actually authenticating.
questionsV2.recallLine: Any tablet with a valid crew password can sync to a billing platform. Which control MOST directly authenticates the device itself?

optionsShort.A: Passcode and disk encryption via device management
optionsShort.B: A certificate per enrolled tablet on sync
optionsShort.C: Serial numbers in a monthly reconciled inventory
optionsShort.D: Send the sync over a VPN

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Protects the meter data if a tablet is lost, and says nothing about which tablets may connect.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: The prerequisite nobody skips, since you cannot enroll what you have not listed. A list is not a gate.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Narrows the path to the platform and still admits anything holding a crew password at the far end of it.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-3 Device Identification and Authentication
NIST SP 800-124 Rev 2 | mobile device enrollment and device identity
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.1.3

questionsV2.question: Which change BEST reduces what an attacker gains by extracting the key from the mobile app?

options.A: Obfuscate the key and verify the app's signature before each call to the API.
options.B: Rotate the key each quarter and ship it in a new release of the app.
options.C: Have the app obtain a short-lived token per user through an authorization-code exchange.
options.D: Restrict the billing API to source addresses in the carrier's published ranges.

questionsV2.explanation:
Anything shipped inside a mobile binary is published. The app runs on hardware the attacker owns, so a compiled-in key is a secret shared with everyone who downloads the package.
RFC 8252 settles this by treating a native app as a public client that holds no secret of its own. It exchanges an authorization code, protected by PKCE, for a token scoped to one customer and expiring in minutes (C). What an attacker pulls out of the binary is then one person's short-lived access.
Ask whether a secret can survive where you are putting it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A mobile app authenticates to an API with a key compiled into the build. Which change BEST reduces what extracting that key yields?

optionsShort.A: Obfuscate the key, check the app signature
optionsShort.B: Rotate the key in each quarterly release
optionsShort.C: Short-lived per-user token from an authorization code
optionsShort.D: Restrict the API to carrier address ranges

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Raises the effort of extracting the key and leaves the key's value where it was.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Refreshes a secret that is disclosed again the moment the release ships, and older copies keep working until retirement.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Authenticates a network path whose carrier ranges carry every other subscriber too.

sources: RFC 8252 | OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps, §8.5 client authentication
RFC 7636 | Proof Key for Code Exchange
ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline | 5.1.5

questionsV2.question: Which step should Kentmere take FIRST on the unowned overnight service account?

options.A: Rotate the key and move it into the platform team's secrets manager.
options.B: Move the scheduled task onto the hardened jump host the platform team maintains.
options.C: Ask the billing manager to approve the account at the quarterly access review.
options.D: Record the account in the service-account register with a named owning team.

questionsV2.explanation:
A service credential nobody owns cannot be corrected safely. Every other step on this list needs someone who knows what breaks.
Recording the account in the service-account register with a named owning team (D) is what gives a credential a lifecycle. A team to right-size its rights. A team to answer at rotation time. A team to decommission it when the meter-data feed is retired. NIST SP 800-53 AC-2 assigns account managers for exactly that reason.
Give a non-human identity a human name before giving it anything else.
questionsV2.recallLine: An overnight service account holds full read and write rights and has no owner. What should the utility do FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Rotate the key into a secrets manager
optionsShort.B: Run the task on a hardened host
optionsShort.C: Manager approves it at quarterly review
optionsShort.D: Register the account with a named owner

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: The second step, and a good one. Rotate a key whose consumers are unknown and the nightly billing run stops at two.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Changes where the task executes and leaves a full read-write credential sitting in a scheduled job.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Asks a manager who does not own the account to certify it, converting an unowned account into an approved unowned one.

questionsV2.question: Talgarth Surveying issues laptops to twenty-eight field engineers who work from client sites and vehicles for weeks at a time. A laptop holding survey files was taken from a parked van and has not connected to any network since. The device policy relies on a fifteen-minute screen lock, a remote wipe command queued in the management console, and monthly patching. The security lead is asked what would have kept the survey files unreadable to whoever took the machine. Which control would MOST reliably have protected the data on that device?

options.A: A remote wipe command that erases the volume the next time the device reports in.
options.B: A screen-lock timeout that requires the engineer's password after fifteen minutes of inactivity.
options.C: Full-disk encryption with pre-boot authentication, so the volume stays sealed until a credential is presented.
options.D: An inventory report that flags laptops which have not checked in for seven days.

questionsV2.explanation:
The laptop never came back online, so whatever protects the survey files has to be on the device already. Full-disk encryption with pre-boot authentication (C) leaves the drive as ciphertext whether it is booted, pulled, or mounted elsewhere.
Ask of any device control whether it still works when the device is offline and in someone else's hands.
questionsV2.recallLine: A stolen field laptop has not been online since it was taken. Which control MOST reliably keeps the survey files on it unreadable?

optionsShort.A: Remote wipe on next device check-in
optionsShort.B: Screen lock after fifteen minutes idle
optionsShort.C: Full-disk encryption with pre-boot authentication
optionsShort.D: Report on laptops missing from check-in

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Depends on the laptop contacting the management service. A thief who never powers it on never delivers the command.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Guards a running session and is bypassed by booting from external media or reading the disk in another machine.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Would tell Talgarth sooner that a machine had gone missing. A notice changes nothing about what the finder can read.

questionsV2.question: Halvard Payments runs forty internal services in one Kubernetes cluster. Any pod can open a connection to any other, and each service accepts a request as authentic because it arrived on the cluster network. A penetration tester compromised a public-facing image-resizing service, called the settlement service directly, and issued a refund, because the settlement service had no way to tell one caller from another. The platform team wants each service to be an access-controlled asset in its own right. Which change BEST achieves that?

options.A: Issue each workload a certificate and require mutual TLS, then authorize calls by the caller's identity.
options.B: Place the services in separate network segments and permit connections the published design requires.
options.C: Route every internal call through an API gateway that applies rate limits and payload validation.
options.D: Record every service-to-service call in a central log and alert on unexpected caller-callee pairs.

questionsV2.explanation:
A service that trusts the network cannot tell a compromised neighbor from a legitimate caller. The fix has to give every caller a name the callee can verify, and a per-workload certificate with mutual TLS (A) does that. It holds even once the attacker is inside the cluster.
Where the network is the credential, every compromise becomes a lateral one.
questionsV2.recallLine: Any pod in a payments cluster may call any other and is trusted by network position. Which change BEST makes each service an access-controlled asset?

optionsShort.A: Mutual TLS with per-workload certificates
optionsShort.B: Segment the network by permitted connections
optionsShort.C: API gateway with rate limits
optionsShort.D: Log and alert on unexpected callers

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Narrows which pods can reach settlement, which is worth doing. Reachability is not identity, and the resizer stays on the list.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Inspects the shape and rate of traffic. It earns its place once you already know who the caller is.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Produces the record that would have shown the refund call the following morning.

questionsV2.question: An access review at Bracken Health finds that fourteen temporary ward clerks can approve drug orders. None was granted that permission directly. The entitlement is attached to a group named Pharmacy-Approvers, which contains a group named Clinical-Staff, which contains the Ward-Clerks group the clerks were added to on their first day. Each nesting was made by a different administrator, years apart, and each looked reasonable alone. Managers approve additions to the group they own and can see nothing above it. Which change MOST directly stops an entitlement from reaching people no one intended?

options.A: Require a second manager to approve each addition to a group before it takes effect.
options.B: Prohibit nesting beneath groups that carry entitlements, so membership in them stays direct and visible.
options.C: Recertify every group's membership quarterly and remove members whose managers do not confirm them.
options.D: Adopt a naming convention that records each group's purpose and owning department in its name.

questionsV2.explanation:
Nested membership is transitive, and each administrator in this chain saw one link of it. Prohibit nesting beneath the groups that actually carry entitlements (B) and the population holding a permission becomes the population you can read off the group. Every other control here assumes that property; none of them creates it.
Ask who can enumerate the holders of a permission.
questionsV2.recallLine: Temporary ward clerks inherited drug-order approval through three levels of nested groups. Which change MOST directly stops an entitlement reaching people nobody intended?

optionsShort.A: Second manager approves each group addition
optionsShort.B: Forbid nesting under entitlement-bearing groups
optionsShort.C: Quarterly recertification of group membership
optionsShort.D: Naming convention recording purpose and owner

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Adds a signature to the act that was never the problem. Both managers see Ward-Clerks and neither sees Pharmacy-Approvers.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Finds the fourteen clerks at the next review, a quarter of drug-order approvals later. Recertification is the backstop.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Makes the estate easier to read. A convention constrains nobody who does not stop and consult it.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-2 Account Management; AC-6(7) Review of User Privileges
ISO/IEC 27001:2022 | A.5.18 Access rights
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 5.2.1

questionsV2.question: Coldharbour Building Society's member portal issues a session identifier to every visitor who loads the sign-in page and keeps that identifier after the member authenticates. A fraud analyst reproduces an attack: the attacker sends a member a link carrying an identifier the attacker chose, the member signs in on that link, and the attacker replays the value and is inside the account. Sessions expire after thirty minutes of inactivity, cookies carry the Secure and HttpOnly attributes, and the portal is served over TLS. Which change FIRST closes the path the analyst demonstrated?

options.A: Reduce the inactivity timeout from thirty minutes to five for authenticated member sessions.
options.B: Bind each session identifier to the client address it was first seen from.
options.C: Add the SameSite attribute to the session cookie so cross-site requests omit it.
options.D: Issue a new session identifier at the moment authentication succeeds and discard the previous one.

questionsV2.explanation:
The attack works because the identifier the member ends up authenticated on is one the attacker already knows. Transport and cookie flags change nothing about that. Issue a new identifier the moment authentication succeeds and discard the previous one (D), and what the attacker planted is authenticated to nobody.
Fix who chose the credential before you shorten how long it lives.
questionsV2.recallLine: A portal keeps the same session identifier before and after a member signs in. Which change FIRST closes the fixation path an analyst demonstrated?

optionsShort.A: Cut idle timeout to five minutes
optionsShort.B: Bind the session to a client address
optionsShort.C: Add SameSite to the session cookie
optionsShort.D: Regenerate the identifier on successful authentication

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Shortens the window in which an idle session is useful. The attacker uses it at once, on an identifier he chose.

B.label: correct but not first
B.wouldAnswer: Would break this replay and is reasonable hardening. Member addresses move, and a shared carrier gateway defeats it.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Stops the browser volunteering the cookie cross-site, which answers request forgery. Here the member signs in willingly.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SC-23 Session Authenticity; SC-23(3) Unique System-generated Session Identifiers
OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet | Renew the Session ID After Any Privilege Level Change

questionsV2.question: Marchwood Credit Union onboards remote staff by post: a manager confirms the hire, the service desk creates the account, and the employee enrolls an authenticator app. Last month a caller reached the service desk claiming a new phone, gave the employee number and date of birth printed on an internal roster, and had the authenticator re-enrolled to a device the employee had never owned. The service desk followed its script exactly. The credit union is rewriting the recovery procedure. What must the desk establish BEFORE it re-enrolls an authenticator?

options.A: That the caller is the person the account was issued to, proofed again to the enrollment standard.
options.B: That the caller can supply the employee number and hire date the roster records for that person.
options.C: That the caller's manager has confirmed by email that the employee asked for a new device.
options.D: That the caller can receive a one-time code at the mobile number the directory holds.

questionsV2.explanation:
Re-enrolling an authenticator issues a new credential, so it repeats the identity-proofing step and inherits its assurance requirement. Anything weaker makes the service desk the cheapest way into any account. What the desk has to establish is that the caller is the person the account was issued to, proofed again to the enrollment standard (A).
Recovery is enrollment again, at the same assurance.
questionsV2.recallLine: A service desk re-enrolls an authenticator for a caller who reports a new phone. What must the desk establish BEFORE it re-enrolls?

optionsShort.A: Re-proof the caller to the enrollment standard
optionsShort.B: Employee number and hire date from the roster
optionsShort.C: Manager's email confirming a device change
optionsShort.D: One-time code to the directory's mobile number

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Asks for facts the internal roster publishes to everyone who can open it. Knowledge authenticates where the knowledge is secret.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Establishes that a device replacement is expected. A manager cannot see who is on the telephone.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: The ordinary out-of-band check, sound once the number of record is trusted. A caller reporting a new phone puts that in doubt.

sources: NIST SP 800-63A | Identity Proofing and Enrollment, §4 Identity Assurance Levels
NIST SP 800-63B | §6.1.2 Binding of an Authenticator Subsequent to Enrollment
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-4 Identifier Management; IA-5 Authenticator Management

questionsV2.question: Meridian Analytics federates a cloud business-intelligence application by SAML. Meridian runs the identity provider; the vendor runs the service provider. A contractor's directory account is disabled at 09:05 on his last day. At 11:40 he exports a client revenue report from the application. The investigation finds that he signed in at 07:50, that the service provider built its own twelve-hour application session from that sign-in, and that it does not consult Meridian again until the session ends. Which change MOST directly stops a disabled identity from continuing to use the application?

options.A: Shorten the identity provider's assertion validity window so each response expires within a few minutes.
options.B: Have the service provider cap its application session and require a fresh assertion before extending it.
options.C: Configure single logout so the identity provider notifies each service provider when a user signs out.
options.D: Rotate the identity provider's token-signing certificate whenever an administrator disables an account.

questionsV2.explanation:
Federation splits the decision in two. The identity provider states who the person is at the moment of sign-in; the relying party decides how long to keep acting on that statement. Meridian revoked the identity on time, and the vendor's twelve-hour session is what kept the contractor working, so the change belongs to the party holding the session (B).
Ask which party holds the thing that must change, then ask whether the change reaches sessions already in flight.
questionsV2.recallLine: A terminated contractor kept using a federated application for hours after the directory disabled him. Which change MOST directly ends a disabled identity's access?

optionsShort.A: Shorten assertion validity at the identity provider
optionsShort.B: Service provider revalidates before extending its session
optionsShort.C: Single logout notifies each service provider
optionsShort.D: Rotate the token-signing certificate on disablement

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Governs how long a SAML response may be presented after issue. That is replay protection, and it is already satisfied here.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Acts when a user signs out, which a terminated contractor has no reason to do. Disabling an account triggers no logout.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Would break federated sign-in for everyone and leave established sessions untouched. Key rotation answers a key compromise.

OASIS SAML 2.0 Core | §2.5.1 Conditions on assertion validity
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-12 Session Termination

questionsV2.question: Fenwick Logistics grants its cloud platform engineers no standing administrative rights. An engineer requests elevation, a peer approves, and the engineer holds the Contributor role for a four-hour window, after which the assignment is removed automatically. During an investigation a deleted storage container is traced to an engineer whose window had closed ninety minutes earlier. The access token his tooling was using had been minted during the window, carries an eight-hour lifetime, and the storage service honored it without re-checking role assignments. What is the PRIMARY reason the window failed to bound his access?

options.A: The approval was granted by a peer instead of by the engineer's own line manager.
options.B: The Contributor role carried more permissions than the engineer's task actually required.
options.C: The activation window was set to four hours as opposed to to the length of the task.
options.D: Authorization was decided when the token was issued and not re-evaluated while it was used.

questionsV2.explanation:
Just-in-time access bounds the assignment. The credential minted from it has a life of its own, and here the storage service decided once, at issue, then honored the resulting token for its full eight hours (D). Until the resource re-checks the assignment - through a short token lifetime, or evaluation that revokes on assignment change - a window is only as tight as the longest token issued inside it.
Bound the credential, more than the grant.
questionsV2.recallLine: An engineer's four-hour elevation expired, yet his tooling kept deleting cloud storage. What is the PRIMARY reason the window failed to bound his access?

optionsShort.A: A peer approved instead of a manager
optionsShort.B: The role was broader than the task
optionsShort.C: The window was four hours, not shorter
optionsShort.D: Authorization decided at issue, never re-evaluated

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Describes a weaker approval than many organizations want. A line manager's signature would have produced the same token.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Real finding, since Contributor is broader than deleting one container needs. It explains how much damage was possible.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Looks like the fix and is not. A one-hour window still mints an eight-hour token, and that gap is the whole failure.

NIST SP 800-207 | Zero Trust Architecture, §2 tenet 6 (dynamic authentication and authorization)

questionsV2.question: Calderwood Mutual runs an on-premises identity provider and federates to Brightwater Claims' on-premises claims application. Calderwood asserts a region attribute, and Brightwater's application treats whatever arrives in it as the adjuster's entitlement. An audit finds a Calderwood adjuster reading claims for three regions she does not cover, because a Calderwood claim rule maps a legacy group to the value ALL. Both organizations agree the mapping was wrong. Which arrangement BEST prevents an attribute error at one party from becoming excess access at the other?

options.A: Calderwood corrects the claim rule and reviews its other attribute mappings for similar errors.
options.B: Both parties sign and encrypt assertions so attribute values stay intact in transit.
options.C: Brightwater applies its own authorization policy to asserted attributes instead of treating them as entitlements.
options.D: Brightwater keeps a local copy of the region mapping and refreshes it from Calderwood monthly.

questionsV2.explanation:
A federation divides labor without transferring responsibility. The asserting party states facts about a person; the relying party decides what those facts entitle the person to do. Brightwater took an assertion as a decision, so every mapping error at Calderwood becomes an access error at Brightwater. Brightwater applying its own authorization policy to the asserted attributes (C) is what breaks that chain.
Sign what you assert; decide what you rely on.
questionsV2.recallLine: A relying party grants access straight from an attribute another organization asserts. Which arrangement BEST stops one party's attribute error becoming excess access at the other?

optionsShort.A: Fix the mapping at the asserting party
optionsShort.B: Sign and encrypt the assertions
optionsShort.C: Relying party authorizes and not trusting attributes
optionsShort.D: Copy the mapping locally, refresh monthly

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Repairs this instance and is plainly necessary. It leaves the relying party as trusting as before, until the next bad mapping.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Protects the integrity of the assertion in flight. It answers whether Brightwater received what Calderwood sent. It did.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Moves the mapping to the relying party and lets it go stale, replacing a wrong value with an old one.

sources: NIST SP 800-63C | Federation and Assertions, §5.3 attribute assertions and relying party responsibilities
OASIS SAML 2.0 Core | §2 Assertions, attribute statements
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3 Access Enforcement; AC-16 Security and Privacy Attributes

questionsV2.question: Pinnacle Freight federates its four hundred staff to a cloud contract-management service using SAML, with a phishing-resistant second factor at the identity provider and a rule that admits managed devices alone. An assessor reviews the service provider's own settings and returns four findings. The security committee can fund one this quarter and asks which finding leaves the largest opening for someone who has already stolen a member of staff's password. Which finding represents the GREATEST risk?

options.A: The service provider still accepts local username and password sign-in alongside the federated route.
options.B: The service provider's sign-in log is retained for thirty days instead of the required year.
options.C: Two dormant administrator accounts in the service provider have not signed in for eight months.
options.D: The service provider's session lasts eight hours, longer than the identity provider's four.

questionsV2.explanation:
Everything Pinnacle invested in sits on the federated path. A second door that avoids that path makes the whole investment optional for the attacker, and a stolen password is exactly the credential local sign-in accepts (A). That finding turns a password into a session.
Count the ways in before you shorten the time spent inside.
questionsV2.recallLine: A federated cloud service is assessed against a staff password an attacker already holds. Which finding represents the GREATEST risk?

optionsShort.A: Local password sign-in still accepted
optionsShort.B: Sign-in logs kept for thirty days
optionsShort.C: Two dormant administrator accounts
optionsShort.D: Eight-hour session at the service provider

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Affects what Pinnacle can reconstruct afterwards, which is an investigation and retention concern.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Real, and it should be cleaned up. Two accounts nobody signs into are not reachable with the staff password in question.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Lengthens the exposure that follows a successful sign-in. It does not decide whether he gets in.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-2 Identification and Authentication; IA-2(1) Multi-factor Authentication to Privileged Accounts
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-2(3) Disable Accounts
NIST SP 800-63B | §4 Authenticator Assurance Levels

questionsV2.question: Ravensworth Utilities keeps its on-premises directory authoritative for accounts and synchronizes them to a cloud tenant, where a policy demands a second factor and a compliant device at every sign-in. An attacker holding a lineworker's password reaches the payroll mailbox anyway. The logs show a mail protocol that authenticates with a username and password straight against the synchronized credential and has no way to prompt for a second factor, so the tenant policy never evaluated the request. Which change MOST directly closes that path?

options.A: Require a password change for every synchronized account and shorten the maximum password age.
options.B: Disable the older mail protocols that bypass the tenant's sign-in policy engine.
options.C: Extend multifactor authentication to the on-premises virtual private network and remote desktop gateway.
options.D: Require the conditional access policy to check device compliance for the mailbox application too.

questionsV2.explanation:
A hybrid identity has as many authentication paths as it has protocols, and a policy engine decides about the paths that reach it. The protocol in these logs authenticated straight against the synchronized password, so every requirement Ravensworth had written went unconsulted. Disabling those older mail protocols (B) is what makes the policy universal.
Enumerate the ways in before strengthening the one you already watch.
questionsV2.recallLine: A synchronized account was abused over a mail protocol that never reached the tenant's policy engine. Which change MOST directly closes that path?

optionsShort.A: Change every synchronized account password
optionsShort.B: Disable the older mail protocols
optionsShort.C: Extend multifactor to VPN and gateway
optionsShort.D: Add a device check to the policy

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Removes the credential the attacker holds and leaves the bypass waiting for the next phished lineworker.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Hardens a different front door, and is irrelevant to a mailbox reached over the internet without touching that network.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Asks a policy that was never evaluated to evaluate one more condition.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-7 Least Functionality; IA-2(1) Multi-factor Authentication
NIST SP 800-63B | §4.2 AAL2 authenticator requirements
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 5.3.3

questionsV2.question: Ashgrove Health System adopted role-based access control four years ago to make provisioning repeatable. It now maintains 2,400 roles for 1,900 staff. Most roles hold a single member, were built for one person's unusual combination of duties, and are copied whenever a similar hire arrives. Provisioning takes as long as it did before, nobody can say what a role means, and the annual review has become 2,400 separate conversations. The identity team has a year and a small budget. Which change BEST restores the benefit the model was adopted for?

options.A: Add an attribute-based layer above the existing roles to decide access at request time.
options.B: Delegate role creation to each department so requests stop queueing with the identity team.
options.C: Recertify all 2,400 roles annually and delete those whose owners do not confirm them.
options.D: Define roles from duties many staff share, and grant the remainder as time-bounded exceptions.

questionsV2.explanation:
Roles pay for themselves when one definition serves many people. A catalog with more roles than staff carries the administrative cost of the model and none of its leverage, because each role is a bespoke grant wearing a role's name.
Define roles from duties many staff share, and grant the remainder as time-bounded exceptions (D). That is the change that reduces how much anyone has to understand.
Ask what a role is meant to be reused for before deciding how many there should be.
questionsV2.recallLine: A hospital maintains 2,400 mostly single-member roles for 1,900 staff. Which change BEST restores the benefit role-based access control was adopted for?

optionsShort.A: Attribute layer above the existing roles
optionsShort.B: Departments create their own roles
optionsShort.C: Annual recertification of every role
optionsShort.D: Shared-duty roles plus time-bounded exceptions

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Leaves 2,400 definitions in place and adds a policy language on top of them.

B.label: not the decision-maker's
B.wouldAnswer: Moves the work to people who know the duties and cannot see the overlaps that make a role reusable. The count grows faster.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: Control on a catalog. The review is the very thing collapsing under the count.

sources: INCITS 359-2012 | Information Technology — Role Based Access Control
NIST IR 7316 | Assessment of Access Control Systems, §3 RBAC
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-2(7) Privileged User Accounts, role-based schemes

questionsV2.question: Harrowgate Defense Systems runs a mandatory access control environment: every document carries a classification label, every user a clearance, and the system enforces both. A cleared engineer working at Secret has written a two-page summary of a Secret test report for a supplier briefing to be held at the Restricted level. She saved the summary in her Secret workspace, believes it holds nothing sensitive, and has asked the system administrator to move the file to the Restricted share. What must happen NEXT?

options.A: An authorized reviewer must formally downgrade the summary before it leaves the Secret workspace.
options.B: The summary must pass through the guard that inspects content moving between the two levels.
options.C: The briefing's organizer must confirm that every supplier attendee holds a Restricted clearance.
options.D: The original test report's owner must grant the supplier's representatives read access to it.

questionsV2.explanation:
In a mandatory environment the label travels with the information, and no clearance lets a subject move information downward on their own judgment. An authorized reviewer must downgrade the summary formally, against the classification guide, and record the decision (A). Until that review happens the summary is Secret material whatever it appears to contain.
Derived content keeps the label of its source until someone with the authority to change it says otherwise.
questionsV2.recallLine: A cleared engineer wants a summary of a Secret report moved to a Restricted share. What must happen NEXT?

optionsShort.A: Authorized reviewer downgrades the summary
optionsShort.B: Send it through the cross-domain guard
optionsShort.C: Confirm attendees hold Restricted clearance
optionsShort.D: Report owner grants read access

B.label: correct but not first
B.wouldAnswer: The mechanism that carries a transfer out and inspects what crosses. A guard enforces a decision; it does not make one.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Matters before the briefing takes place. The audience's clearance says nothing about this document's label.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Applies discretionary thinking inside a mandatory model. The report's owner cannot release what the system classifies.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3(3) Mandatory Access Control; AC-16 Security and Privacy Attributes
Bell-LaPadula | the *-property, no write-down without a trusted downgrade
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 5.4.3

questionsV2.question: Thornbury Research keeps project data on a file server where each project folder is owned by the analyst who created it, and that analyst grants colleagues access as she sees fit. A senior analyst left in March and her leaver process disabled her account. Her three project folders now carry her disabled account as sole owner, no other account holds change-permission rights on them, and nobody in the department can grant access to the two colleagues who need the data. Which change MOST directly prevents this recurring?

options.A: Have an administrator take ownership of orphaned folders when a request is raised.
options.B: Report monthly on folders whose owning account has been disabled or deleted.
options.C: Make a team group, not an individual account, the owner at folder creation.
options.D: Require leavers to hand their folder permissions to a named colleague before departure.

questionsV2.explanation:
Discretionary control ties the authority to change a resource's permissions to a principal. When that principal is one person's account, the authority leaves with the person. Make a team group the owner at folder creation (C) and the authority survives any individual's departure. It is settled up front, so nothing depends on anyone remembering at resignation time.
Ask whether an access decision survives the person who made it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A departed analyst's disabled account is the sole owner of three project folders. Which change MOST directly prevents that recurring?

optionsShort.A: Administrator takes ownership on request
optionsShort.B: Monthly report of orphaned folders
optionsShort.C: A team group owns the folder
optionsShort.D: Leavers hand over folder permissions

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Restores access in minutes, and every environment needs the escalation path. It treats each orphan as it appears.

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Would have told Thornbury in April that three folders had lost their owner. Worth knowing. Still a report.

D.label: wrong phase
D.wouldAnswer: The right instinct at the wrong point. Handover assumes a planned exit, and the painful folders come from the sudden one.

questionsV2.question: Larkspur Bank scores every sign-in and steps up to a second factor when the score is high. The engine treats a request arriving from the bank's remote-access egress addresses as low risk, on the grounds that the user has already authenticated to the network. An attacker who phished a relationship manager's remote-access credentials signed in to the payments console from that range, scored low, and was never challenged. Device registration, typing cadence and time of day were all available to the engine. Which change should the bank make FIRST?

options.A: Raise the score threshold at which the engine steps up to a second factor.
options.B: Stop treating the remote-access egress range as evidence of low risk in the score.
options.C: Extend the risk engine's coverage to the bank's internal expenses and travel applications.
options.D: Add the payments console to the applications that require step-up at every sign-in.

questionsV2.explanation:
Risk scoring is worth what its signals are worth. A network address that any authenticated user - or anyone holding an authenticated user's credentials - can appear behind says nothing about the person. Stop treating the remote-access egress range as evidence of low risk (B) and the signals already collected regain their value: an unregistered device and an unusual cadence would both have scored this session high.
Fix the signal before special-casing the applications it misleads.
questionsV2.recallLine: A risk engine treats the bank's remote-access egress addresses as low risk. Which change should the bank make FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Raise the step-up threshold
optionsShort.B: Drop network egress as a trust signal
optionsShort.C: Extend the engine to more applications
optionsShort.D: Always step up on the payments console

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Moves the engine the wrong way for this failure. It is the adjustment for when genuine customers abandon transactions.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Widens the engine's reach to applications that were never involved. The payments console was already inside it.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Would have blocked this attack and should probably happen. It patches one destination while the rest keep inheriting trust.

questionsV2.question: Redhill Bioinformatics lets its eight operations staff run the nightly backup with sudo. The sudoers file grants each of them the find and tar binaries with any arguments, because the backup script calls both. An auditor demonstrates that the -exec option launches an interactive root shell, and that the sudo log records nothing beyond the name of the binary. The operators must keep running the backup by hand when the scheduler fails. Which change MOST directly stops an operator from obtaining a full root shell?

options.A: Require the operator's password on every sudo invocation instead of caching it briefly.
options.B: Ship the sudo log entries to the central collector as they are written.
options.C: Permit the sudo grants during the nightly backup window and deny them at other times.
options.D: Replace the command grants with one wrapper script that takes no arguments from the caller.

questionsV2.explanation:
A sudo entry that accepts arguments delegates whatever the named binary can be persuaded to do, and find, tar and several others can be persuaded to execute another program. The grant is effectively root, and the log names the binary while whatever it launched goes unrecorded. Replace the command grants with one wrapper script that takes no arguments from the caller (D): the argument stops being an attack surface, and the backup still runs by hand when the scheduler fails.
Judge a privilege grant by what the binary can be persuaded to do, not by what the script calls it for.
questionsV2.recallLine: Operators hold sudo rights on find and tar with any arguments. Which change MOST directly stops one of them obtaining a root shell?

optionsShort.A: Password on every sudo invocation
optionsShort.B: Stream sudo logs to a central collector
optionsShort.C: Grant sudo only in the backup window
optionsShort.D: One wrapper script accepting no caller arguments

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Narrows the window in which an unattended terminal serves somebody else. The operator who authenticates again gets the same escape.

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Makes the record tamper-resistant and reviewable, which matters after the fact.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Reduces the hours in which the escape is available. Inside the window the grant is unchanged.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-6(2) Non-privileged Access for Nonsecurity Functions; AC-6(9) Log Use of Privileged Functions
CIS Controls v8 | 5.4 Restrict Administrator Privileges to Dedicated Accounts

questionsV2.question: Kestrel Water's reporting platform runs under a domain service account whose password has not changed since 2019. The password is typed into forty scheduled tasks across eleven servers and appears in two configuration files in the deployment repository. The engineer who knew why it was built that way has left. An auditor asks how the credential will be rotated, and the operations lead answers that rotation was attempted once, broke nine jobs overnight, and was reversed. Which approach BEST resolves the finding?

options.A: Set a long passphrase, exempt the account from expiry, and record the exemption as accepted.
options.B: Rotate the password each quarter and update the scheduled tasks and files by hand.
options.C: Move to an account whose credential the platform rotates and each job retrieves at run time.
options.D: Record the account, its owner and its dependencies in the service account register.

questionsV2.explanation:
The finding is not that a password is old. One secret exists in forty-two places, and no process can change it in all of them at once.
An account whose credential the platform rotates, and which each job retrieves at run time (C), turns rotation into an operation on a single record. That is why the earlier attempt broke nine jobs: it was a coordinated edit across eleven servers.
Count the copies of a secret before planning to change it.
questionsV2.recallLine: A service account's password sits in forty scheduled tasks and two configuration files, unchanged since 2019. Which approach BEST resolves that?

optionsShort.A: Long passphrase with a documented expiry exemption
optionsShort.B: Quarterly manual rotation across the tasks
optionsShort.C: Platform-rotated credential fetched at run time
optionsShort.D: Register the account, owner and dependencies

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Formalizes the current state and buys nothing. The secret is still readable in a repository, still shared, still nobody's.

B.label: correct but not first
B.wouldAnswer: Repeats the change that already failed. Rotation is certainly required, and it succeeds once the credential lives in one place.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Proper hygiene, and Kestrel should do it. A register records a credential without rotating one.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | IA-5(7) No Embedded Unencrypted Static Authenticators; AC-2 Account Management
NIST SP 800-63B | §5.1.1 Memorized Secrets, storage and rotation
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 5.5.5

questionsV2.question: Northshore Clinical Research holds trial data for eleven sponsors in one analytics warehouse. Every analyst granted the query role can read all forty-one columns of the participant table, including name, medical record number and full date of birth, although the studies they support need age band, site and outcome alone. The warehouse is encrypted at rest, sits behind the corporate identity provider, and its access list is reviewed each quarter. An auditor asks how the participant identifiers themselves are protected. Which change MOST directly limits what an analyst can see inside the table instead of whether the table opens?

options.C: Apply masking policies to the identifying columns so each analyst sees values their purpose permits.
options.A: Move the participant table to a separate database with its own list of authorized analysts.
options.B: Encrypt the warehouse volumes with a key held by the sponsor instead of by Northshore.
options.D: Review the query role's membership monthly instead of quarterly and remove analysts who finished.

questionsV2.explanation:
Access to information has to be controlled at the granularity the information is classified at. The identifiers are the sensitive part; the outcome fields are not. A masking policy on the identifying columns (C) returns a redacted value to anyone whose purpose does not include re-identification, and the protection travels with the data.
Protecting information means deciding which fields a purpose justifies, beyond deciding who may open the container.
questionsV2.recallLine: Analysts with the query role can read every identifying column in a trial participant table. Which change MOST directly limits what they see inside it?

optionsShort.C: Mask the identifying columns by purpose
optionsShort.A: Move the table to a separate database
optionsShort.B: Encrypt the volumes with a sponsor key
optionsShort.D: Review the query role monthly

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Moves the same unrestricted read to a second place. A smaller population, and each of them still sees every identifier.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Protects the volumes against theft of the storage. An authorized query still returns plaintext to the analyst who ran it.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Shortens the window in which a departed analyst keeps the role. A currently authorized analyst still reads every identifier.

questionsV2.question: Bramfield Aerospace hardened interactive logon to the sixty servers behind its design and manufacturing systems: directory accounts, a hardware second factor at every sign-in, and no local administrator logons. A red team still reached those servers four other ways. The baseboard management controllers answer on the office VLAN with the credentials the vendor shipped. The hypervisor console authenticates against a standalone database the identity team does not administer. The backup agent runs under a domain account with full file access on every host. A monitoring agent reports host telemetry to a collector over an unauthenticated channel. Which finding represents the GREATEST weakness in logical access control to those systems?

options.A: The baseboard management controllers answer on the office network under the credentials the vendor shipped.
options.B: The hypervisor console authenticates against a database the organization's identity governance does not reach.
options.C: The backup agent holds a domain account able to read every file on the hosts it protects.
options.D: The monitoring agent reports host telemetry to a collector over a channel nobody authenticates.

questionsV2.explanation:
Out-of-band management sits beneath the operating system. A baseboard management controller reachable from any office desk, answering to the credentials the vendor shipped (A), hands an attacker power control, virtual media and keyboard-video access to the hardware. Every control Bramfield built above it - the directory accounts, the hardware factor - is simply not in that path.
Rank access findings by what the attacker gets, and by whether the controls you built are consulted on that path at all.
questionsV2.recallLine: Servers with hardened directory logon are also reachable through management controllers, a standalone hypervisor console and service agents. Which finding is the GREATEST weakness?

optionsShort.A: Management controllers on the office VLAN, default credentials
optionsShort.B: Hypervisor console on a standalone account store
optionsShort.C: Backup service account reads every protected file
optionsShort.D: Monitoring telemetry sent over an unauthenticated channel

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Real governance gap, and the worst finding here only if the office network were separated from the management interfaces.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: Excessive privilege in a service account. It is still an account the directory can disable, monitor and rotate.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: What an intruder exploits after arriving. Forged or suppressed metrics hide activity that has already begun.

questionsV2.question: Camborne Legal Systems sells a case-management application to 340 law firms. The browser interface shows a user the matters belonging to their own firm and hides the administration menu unless the account holds the supervisor role. A tester signs in as an ordinary paralegal, reads the matter identifier out of the address bar, and calls the application's REST endpoint directly with a different identifier; the endpoint returns another firm's matter. The same tester calls the administrative export endpoint and receives a full client list. Which change BEST closes what the tester demonstrated?

options.D: Have every endpoint check the caller's identity and firm against the record before returning it.
options.A: Remove the matter identifier from the address bar and pass an opaque reference instead.
options.B: Require the supervisor role at sign-in before the administration menu is rendered at all.
options.C: Rate-limit each account's endpoint calls and alert when a paralegal enumerates many matters.

questionsV2.explanation:
Authorization has to be decided where the request is served. The browser enforces nothing: anything the interface hides is one HTTP call away. Have every endpoint check the caller's identity and firm against the record before returning it (D). That is the whole control; the menu and the address bar are presentation.
When an interface hides a function, ask what happens when someone calls the function anyway.
questionsV2.recallLine: A paralegal calls a case-management application's REST endpoints directly and receives another firm's records. Which change BEST closes that gap?

optionsShort.D: Check identity and firm inside each endpoint
optionsShort.A: Replace the identifier with an opaque reference
optionsShort.B: Require the supervisor role before rendering the menu
optionsShort.C: Rate-limit calls and alert on enumeration

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Swaps a guessable identifier for an unguessable one, and leaves the endpoint willing to serve any identifier presented to it.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Strengthens a check that already runs in the wrong place. The tester never used the menu.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Notices the pattern after the records have been returned. A worthwhile second layer that refuses no call.

questionsV2.question: Halloran Precision manufactures turbine blades under an export-control license. The license obliges the company to stop the parts catalog leaving its network outside an approved review window, and the obligation binds every party: engineers, the two administrators who assign roles, and the nightly integration account that pushes drawings to a supplier portal. Halloran already runs role-based access control and can add conditions at its access gateway. The compliance officer wants a mechanism the administrators themselves cannot quietly step around by granting a role. Which mechanism BEST meets that obligation?

options.B: A gateway rule denying catalog export outside the window, evaluated for every request received.
options.A: A role granting catalog export, assigned to the engineers who need it during reviews.
options.C: Classification labels on catalog files, compared against each requester's clearance at export.
options.D: Folder permissions on the catalog, set by its owning engineering manager as required.

questionsV2.explanation:
Rule-based control evaluates a condition attached to the resource or the request, and it applies to whoever is asking. That is what an obligation binding every party needs. The window is a property of the request, so a gateway rule denying catalog export outside it (B) reaches the integration account and the two administrators as surely as it reaches the engineers.
Match the mechanism to the shape of the condition: identity, sensitivity, or circumstance.
questionsV2.recallLine: An export-control obligation must stop a parts catalog leaving outside an approved window, binding administrators and service accounts too. Which mechanism BEST meets it?

optionsShort.B: A gateway rule tied to the window
optionsShort.A: A role granting export to reviewing engineers
optionsShort.C: Labels compared against each requester's clearance
optionsShort.D: Folder permissions set by the owning manager

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Role-based control, the right mechanism for which duties a person performs. A role is something an administrator can grant.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Mandatory access control, which does bind administrators. A clearance-against-label test would bar the catalog at every hour.

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: Discretionary control, which puts the decision with the person most likely to be asked for an exception and least able to refuse.

NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-3 Access Enforcement

questionsV2.question: Wrekin Pharmaceuticals replaced most of its role grants with attribute-based policies. Access to a trial dataset is decided from four attributes: the requester's department, their assigned study, their training status, and whether the workstation is managed. Twelve months on, an internal audit finds staff reading datasets for studies they left long ago. The policy engine evaluates every rule exactly as written, the logs agree, and no policy has changed since launch. Department and study come from a self-service profile page; training status and device state come from the training system and the device manager. Which finding MOST likely explains the audit result?

options.A: Two of the four attributes are self-asserted and no process corrects them when work changes.
options.B: The policy engine caches each access decision for the length of the requester's session.
options.C: Attribute-based policies were written by the platform team and not by the dataset owners.
options.D: Nobody recertifies who currently holds access to each of the trial datasets in use.

questionsV2.explanation:
An attribute-based decision is only as good as the attributes it consumes, and two of these four are typed in by the people they govern (A). Nothing recomputes a researcher's study when they move, so the engine keeps returning permit for a condition that stopped being true. Correct behavior on stale input.
Attribute-based control does not remove access administration. It moves it from grants to attribute sources, each of which needs an owner and a refresh interval.
questionsV2.recallLine: Attribute-based policies still admit staff to studies they left a year ago, though every rule evaluates as written. Which finding MOST likely explains it?

optionsShort.A: Two attributes are self-asserted and go stale
optionsShort.B: Decisions are cached for the session's length
optionsShort.C: Platform team wrote the policies, not owners
optionsShort.D: No recertification of who holds dataset access

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Would explain access surviving for hours. This ran for a year, so decision caching is the wrong span for the finding.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Real governance question. A policy nobody objects to still evaluates the same way against the same stale input.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Applies a role-based habit to a model with no standing grants to recertify. The right instinct, aimed at the wrong object.
