The network team can re-cable the sensor, and the vendor license already includes prevention signatures. The security manager wants the next set of beacons stopped on the wire as opposed to reconstructed afterwards. Which change would MOST directly deliver that?

options.A: Forward the sensor's alerts into the SIEM with a 24-hour analyst triage target
options.B: Re-cable the sensor inline on the uplink and enable blocking on high-confidence signatures
options.C: Deploy endpoint detection and response agents to every branch file server and workstation
options.D: Keep six days of full packet capture so beacon traffic can be reconstructed later

questionsV2.explanation:
A sensor on a mirror port sees a copy of traffic that has already been delivered, so nothing it observes can be withheld from the destination. Move the same device into the path and observation becomes interdiction (B). With prevention enabled on the signatures the vendor rates as high confidence, a beacon gets dropped.
Detection and prevention differ by where the device sits.
questionsV2.recallLine: A credit union's intrusion sensor watches a mirror port and logged six days of attacker beacons unread. Which change MOST directly stops the next ones?

optionsShort.A: Send alerts to the SIEM for triage
optionsShort.B: Move the sensor inline with blocking enabled
optionsShort.C: Deploy endpoint detection and response agents
optionsShort.D: Keep more days of packet capture

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Attacks the six-day delay and is real value. A faster human reading a copy of a packet cannot unsend it.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: A sound investment that would likely catch the encryption stage. It acts on hosts, and the branch network stays unfiltered.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Buys evidence. More capture means a better reconstruction of what the manager has said he no longer wants to reconstruct.

sources: NIST SP 800-94 | §4.1.1 Network-based IDPS sensors — inline versus passive deployment
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.2.1 Intrusion detection and prevention system

questionsV2.question: Corviston Retail Group's security operations center receives about 1,400 alerts a day. Nine hundred come from one data loss prevention rule that matches sixteen-digit numbers, and a review shows 94 percent of those matches are the retailer's own test card range, generated by the payment team's nightly regression suite. Analysts now close the rule's alerts in bulk without reading them, and two genuine card-data emails were closed that way last quarter. The manager must cut the volume without giving up coverage of live cardholder data. Which change BEST achieves that?

options.A: Exclude the documented test card range from the rule and re-measure its hit rate weekly
options.B: Disable the data loss prevention rule until the payment team stops generating test traffic
options.C: Raise the rule's severity threshold so that lower-severity matches bypass the analyst queue
options.D: Add two analysts to the day shift so the alert queue can be worked in full

questionsV2.explanation:
Tuning changes what a rule matches. The test range is documented, so excluding it removes the ninety-four percent that is noise while every match on live card data still reaches the queue (A). The weekly hit-rate measurement is what proves the exclusion did not quietly take something else with it.
Measure a rule by what it catches.
questionsV2.recallLine: A retail SOC bulk-closes 900 alerts a day from one DLP rule that mostly matches its own test card numbers. Which change BEST cuts volume without losing coverage?

optionsShort.A: Exclude the test card range and re-measure
optionsShort.B: Turn the rule off for now
optionsShort.C: Raise the severity threshold for the queue
optionsShort.D: Add two analysts to the shift

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Trades a false-positive problem for a blind spot. The rule switched off is the one that catches genuine card email.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Keeps the matches and hides them. The real emails carry no special severity, so they fall below the line too.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Pays for two analyst-years of reading alerts that should never have been raised in the first place.

sources: NIST SP 800-137 | §3.2 Establishing and refining monitoring frequencies and metrics
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.2.4 Continuous monitoring and tuning

questionsV2.question: Ravensworth Mutual keeps thirty years of policy files on LTO tape. A courier collects a sealed case from the data center each Friday and returns the previous week's case, and the offsite vault sends a written manifest with every delivery. The annual audit has just compared the tape library with the vault's own inventory for the first time since the last audit, and found three tapes unaccounted for. Nobody can say when they went missing or whether they ever left the building. The operations director wants the next loss visible in weeks. Which control MOST directly delivers that?

options.A: Encrypt every tape with keys held in the data center's hardware security module
options.B: Degauss and destroy each tape at end of life under a witnessed disposal procedure
options.C: Reconcile the library against the vault manifest at every pickup, signed by both parties
options.D: Have internal audit count the library quarterly and report exceptions to the director

questionsV2.explanation:
Custody is a two-sided account, and it closes when both sides agree at each hand-off. Signing the library against the courier's manifest every Friday surfaces a missing tape within a week, against a named party, with a document that says who held it last (C).
Encryption protects the data. Custody records protect your knowledge of where it is.
questionsV2.recallLine: An insurer's annual audit found three backup tapes missing with no record of when. Which control MOST directly makes the next loss visible within weeks?

optionsShort.A: Encrypt every tape under HSM-held keys
optionsShort.B: Degauss and destroy tapes at end of life
optionsShort.C: Sign the library against the vault manifest weekly
optionsShort.D: Have internal audit count the library quarterly

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Limits what a found tape can disclose, which is why a lost encrypted tape is often not reportable. A cipher raises no hand.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Governs the end of a tape's life, a different point in the media lifecycle from the weekly journey between buildings.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Shortens the interval from twelve months to three and still counts only one side of the chain.

questionsV2.question: Halewood Actuarial encrypts its policyholder database with transparent database encryption, terminates TLS 1.3 at the application tier, and replicates backups between two data centers over a dedicated fiber circuit. A quarterly assessment finds one further flow: a nightly job runs a reporting extract, writes it as an uncompressed CSV into an SFTP landing directory on the same storage array, and leaves it there for fourteen days so that analysts can collect it. The array carries the same transparent encryption. Which change closes the GREATEST exposure of policyholder data at rest?

options.A: Terminate TLS 1.3 at the database listener so the application-to-database link is encrypted too
options.B: Encrypt the replication stream between the data centers instead of relying on the private circuit
options.C: Rotate the transparent encryption keys every ninety days instead of once a year
options.D: Encrypt the reporting extract under a key held outside the storage platform, and expire it nightly

questionsV2.explanation:
Transparent database encryption and array encryption both defend against a stolen disk. Neither defends against a process the operating system already trusts, because the storage layer decrypts for whoever can open the file. The extract is therefore readable for a fortnight and holds the same policyholder fields as the database. Wrap the file itself in a key the platform does not hold, and expire it each morning (D), and the copy becomes as protected as its source.
Ask who sits inside the trust boundary an encryption scheme assumes.
questionsV2.recallLine: An insurer's nightly reporting extract is left on a transparently encrypted array for fourteen days. Which change closes the GREATEST exposure of policyholder data at rest?

optionsShort.A: Terminate TLS at the database listener
optionsShort.B: Encrypt replication between the data centers
optionsShort.C: Rotate the encryption keys quarterly
optionsShort.D: Encrypt the extract and expire it nightly

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Closes a genuine gap on an internal link that carries rows for milliseconds. The file sits still for fourteen days.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Replaces physical isolation with cryptographic isolation on a circuit between two of the insurer's own buildings.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Sound key hygiene that would matter if a key had leaked. It changes nothing about who can read a decrypted file.

ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.5.3 Data at rest/data in transit

questionsV2.question: Ardenbrook Savings outsources 24-hour monitoring to a managed security service provider. The contract sets a fifteen-minute acknowledgment target, carries service credits for missed targets, and requires the provider to hold a SOC 2 Type II report. An intruder who entered through a container workload in the bank's new cloud tenancy operated for nineteen days before a customer complaint surfaced the fraud. The review finds the provider met every acknowledgment target it was measured on: the tenancy's logs were never forwarded, and nobody owned the question of what should be monitored. Which change addresses the PRIMARY cause of the nineteen-day dwell?

options.A: Increase the service credits so a missed detection costs the provider more than a late acknowledgment
options.B: Maintain a signed log-source catalog with an onboarding deadline and a monthly ingestion attestation
options.C: Require the provider to widen its SOC 2 Type II scope to cover cloud workload monitoring
options.D: Retain a second provider to run independent threat hunting across the bank's environment

questionsV2.explanation:
A monitoring provider detects what it is sent, and the duty to decide what gets sent stays with the customer. Every metric in this contract measured the provider's speed on alerts it received, so the agreement could be satisfied in full while an entire cloud tenancy stayed dark. A catalog of log sources, with a deadline for onboarding each new one and a monthly attestation naming what was actually ingested, turns coverage into an obligation with a date, an owner and evidence behind it (B).
Accountability for risk stays with the bank even when the work does not.
questionsV2.recallLine: A bank's outsourced monitoring met every response target while an intruder ran nineteen days in an unforwarded cloud tenancy. Which change addresses the PRIMARY cause?

optionsShort.A: Raise the service credits for missed detections
optionsShort.B: Catalog log sources with monthly ingestion attestation
optionsShort.C: Widen the provider's SOC 2 scope
optionsShort.D: Retain a second provider to hunt

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Raises the price of a failure the contract still cannot see. The provider would pay nothing, having missed no target.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: Audits how well the provider runs its own operation. Worth knowing, and silent on whether the container logs arrive.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Pays a second firm to hunt in the same data the first firm was already given.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | SA-9 External System Services — defined and monitored service coverage
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.7.4 Third-party provided security services

questionsV2.question: Pellworth Logistics deployed a user behavior analytics platform that builds its model of normal activity from a rolling ninety-day baseline. Six weeks after go-live it has raised nothing on the finance shared drive. During an unrelated audit an engineer finds that a contractor's account has been copying rate cards to a personal cloud folder every Tuesday since before the platform was installed, at a volume the model now treats as that account's ordinary behavior. The account was suspended within the hour. The security lead has one analyst, a threat-hunting notebook, and the vendor's offer to retrain. What should the security lead do FIRST?

options.A: Hunt the ninety-day baseline window with deterministic queries for behavior the model absorbed
options.B: Retrain the model on a window verified as clean before the contractor's copying began
options.C: Report the confirmed theft to the executive risk committee before any further analysis
options.D: Add a deterministic rule alerting on finance uploads to consumer cloud storage services

questionsV2.explanation:
The audit found something larger than one contractor: the platform learned its idea of normal during a period nobody had validated. Anything else running in those ninety days, a second account, a slower transfer, an internal share, was averaged into the same baseline and is equally silent today. Queries written against the raw logs do not depend on the model at all, which is why they can tell the lead how large this is (A).
Any learned baseline inherits every compromise that was already running when the learning started.
questionsV2.recallLine: A behavior analytics model learned its baseline during a period that included a contractor's ongoing data theft. What should the security lead do FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Hunt the baseline window with deterministic queries
optionsShort.B: Retrain the model on a clean window
optionsShort.C: Report the theft to the risk committee
optionsShort.D: Alert on finance uploads to consumer cloud

B.label: correct but not first
B.wouldAnswer: The right repair, and it belongs on the same worklist. A retrained model says nothing about the ninety days already absorbed.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Has to happen, and the committee will ask how many files and accounts. That answer comes from the hunt.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Narrows one path for the future and leaves the training window unexamined.

ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.7.8 Machine learning and artificial intelligence based tools

questionsV2.question: Sable Ridge Payments clears card transactions from two data centers eleven kilometers apart, both inside the same metropolitan area. The pair runs active-active, each carrying half the traffic and each able to carry all of it, with synchronous replication over dark fiber. A resilience review establishes that both buildings draw from one utility substation, sit within the hundred-year flood outline of the same river, and are served by two carriers along a shared duct. The board believes the design has removed single points of failure. Which change would MOST improve the resilience this two-site design is meant to provide?

options.A: Increase the dark fiber capacity so either site can absorb the other's peak load
options.B: Convert the second site to active-passive with automated failover and quarterly failover tests
options.C: Replicate a third copy of the transaction ledger to cloud storage in the same region
options.D: Add a third processing site outside the river basin, the grid region and the carrier duct

questionsV2.explanation:
Two sites are two sites to the extent that they fail independently. Eleven kilometers buys protection against a fire, a burst pipe or a failed switch. It buys nothing against a substation fault, a river or a backhoe in the shared duct, and this pair meets all three hazards together. A site outside all three exposure sets turns a redundant pair into a resilient estate (D), and it can be sized for the volume a regulator would expect to keep clearing.
Separation is counted in shared dependencies.
questionsV2.recallLine: A processor runs two active-active data centers eleven kilometers apart on one substation and one flood plain. Which change MOST improves the design's resilience?

optionsShort.A: Increase dark fiber capacity between the sites
optionsShort.B: Make the second site active-passive with tested failover
optionsShort.C: Copy the ledger to regional cloud storage
optionsShort.D: Add a site outside the shared hazards

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Raises the ceiling on a takeover that already works. A wider pipe between two flooded halls moves nothing.

B.label: symptom not cause
B.wouldAnswer: Swaps a topology that already carries live load for one that has to be triggered, in scenarios this pair survives.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Protects the record and leaves the service down, and storage in the same region shares the hazard.

sources: NIST SP 800-34 Rev 1 | §3.4.2 Alternate sites — a site should not be subject to the same hazards as the primary
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.10.3 Multiple processing sites

questionsV2.question: Kestrel Vale Health Trust lost its identity provider to ransomware at 03:40. Email, the collaboration platform, the softphone system and the intranet all authenticate against it and all are unavailable. The disaster recovery plan is a document library page reached through single sign-on, the call tree is a spreadsheet in the continuity manager's mailbox, and the vendor escalation numbers sit in a contact list that synchronizes from the same directory. Ninety minutes passed before enough of the response team could be reached on personal mobiles to open a bridge. Which provision would MOST directly have shortened that ninety minutes?

options.A: A mass notification service that draws its recipient list from the corporate directory
options.B: Satellite phones issued to the executive team and tested twice a year
options.C: A printed call tree and a standing bridge held with an unrelated provider
options.D: A requirement that staff install the collaboration application on their personal phones

questionsV2.explanation:
Every channel the trust reached for depended on the system that had failed. Out-of-band means a path whose dependencies do not overlap the ones being recovered (C). Paper does not authenticate, and a conference bridge bought from a supplier with no link to the trust's directory answers whether or not the identity provider is running.
Test a notification path by assuming the system you are recovering is already down.
questionsV2.recallLine: Ransomware took a health trust's identity provider, and with it email, the call tree and the softphones. Which provision MOST directly speeds the response?

optionsShort.A: Mass notification driven by the corporate directory
optionsShort.B: Satellite phones for the executive team
optionsShort.C: Printed call tree and an unrelated bridge
optionsShort.D: Collaboration app installed on personal phones

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Its recipient list is the very object that became unreachable at 03:40. A service that cannot resolve whom to call stays silent.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Reaches four or five people in an event with no radio problem. The shift engineers were the ones missing.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Changes the device and keeps the dependency. The application still asks the same identity provider for a token.

sources: NIST SP 800-34 Rev 1 | §4.2.2 Notification procedures — contact methods that survive the outage
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.11.3 Communications

questionsV2.question: Thornbury Water rewrote its disaster recovery plan after a failed audit. The new plan names 34 role holders, gives each a numbered task list, and was approved by the executive committee last week. Four of those 34 people have ever taken part in a recovery activity, eleven joined the utility within the past year, and the plan introduces a new emergency operations center together with a new declaration authority. The continuity manager has a budget, six months of clear space in the calendar, and pressure from the auditor to show progress. What should the continuity manager arrange NEXT?

options.A: Circulate the approved plan and require every role holder to acknowledge reading it
options.B: Book a full interruption test of the emergency operations center for the coming quarter
options.C: Run role-specific training so that each named holder can execute their own task list
options.D: Add a disaster recovery module to the utility's annual awareness training for all staff

questionsV2.explanation:
Awareness tells people a plan exists. Training makes a named person able to do the numbered thing beside their name at 03:00, with a stranger on the bridge (C). Thirty of the thirty-four have never done it once, the operations center is new, and the declaration authority has changed. Competence is the whole distance between an approved document and a working capability.
Train the role, then exercise the plan, in that order.
questionsV2.recallLine: A utility has approved a rewritten recovery plan naming 34 role holders, thirty of whom have never used one. What should the continuity manager arrange NEXT?

optionsShort.A: Circulate the plan and collect read acknowledgments
optionsShort.B: Book a full interruption test this quarter
optionsShort.C: Train each role holder on their tasks
optionsShort.D: Add a module to annual awareness training

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Produces an audit artifact and a signature. Reading is not rehearsal, and the finding was about capability.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: The most demanding exercise in the catalog. Run against untrained holders it fails for reasons that teach nothing.

D.label: wrong scope
D.wouldAnswer: Reaches the whole workforce with general content, worth having. It says nothing about whether the 34 can run their lists.

sources: NIST SP 800-34 Rev 1 | §3.6 Plan testing, training and exercises — training personnel in their plan roles
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.11.6 Training and awareness

questionsV2.question: Marchfield Building Society will run a parallel test of its core banking recovery on a Saturday, with the recovery site processing a copy of the day's transactions while production keeps running. Two hundred staff, the core banking vendor and an outsourced card processor are involved, and the prudential regulator has asked to observe. At the last test an operator's alert about failed settlement reached the fraud team, who froze thirty accounts believing a live incident was under way, and the incident line took calls from two branches. Which step must the test director complete BEFORE the test begins?

options.A: Schedule the run overnight so that fewer branches and customers can be affected by it
options.B: Route every test message through a distribution list that excludes customer-facing teams
options.C: Suspend the fraud team's alerting for the duration of the recovery site's processing
options.D: Issue a test communications plan naming stakeholders, the EXERCISE prefix, and start and stop calls

questionsV2.explanation:
A rehearsal that cannot be told apart from an incident produces incidents. What prevents that is agreed before anyone logs in (D): a named list of who is told, a marking convention that survives being forwarded, and a formal announcement opening and closing the exercise. Anything outside those two calls is treated as real. The regulator's attendance belongs in the same document, because an examiner watching what looks like an unannounced failure draws conclusions the society will spend months correcting.
Label the message. The recipient list is the wrong place to hide.
questionsV2.recallLine: A building society's last recovery test was mistaken for a live incident and froze thirty accounts. What must the test director complete BEFORE the next one?

optionsShort.A: Run the test overnight to limit exposure
optionsShort.B: Exclude customer-facing teams from test messages
optionsShort.C: Suspend fraud alerting during the run
optionsShort.D: Issue a test communications plan and announcements

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Shrinks the audience and leaves the ambiguity intact. A night operator has less help to hand at 02:00, not more.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Removes exactly the people who most need to know a test is running, and the branches would call again.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Buys silence at the price of a genuine blind spot in fraud detection for the length of the run.

sources: NIST SP 800-84 | Guide to Test, Training, and Exercise Programs — exercise coordination and participant notification
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.12.6 Communications

questionsV2.question: Calder Point Data Services runs a suburban colocation hall behind a 2.4-meter palisade fence, with card-controlled pedestrian doors and a single vehicle entrance closed by a barrier arm. Delivery drivers raise the barrier with a call button answered from reception. A penetration tester drove in behind a booked courier van while the arm was still up, parked, and reached the loading dock unchallenged, and nobody at reception noticed a second vehicle on the camera feed. Management wants the vehicle entrance to stop an uninvited car and not record it. Which perimeter change BEST meets that requirement?

options.A: A two-gate vehicle trap where the outer gate closes before the inner one opens
options.B: A second camera on the barrier with analytics that count vehicles per authorization
options.C: Raising the fence to three meters and adding razor topping along the boundary
options.D: A rule that reception verify each delivery against the day's booking before raising the barrier

questionsV2.explanation:
The gap here is geometric: one authorization raised one barrier and two vehicles passed under it. A vehicle trap removes the geometry (A). The outer gate must shut before the inner one opens, so a following car is held in a space it cannot drive out of, and admitting it becomes a deliberate decision.
Work out which part of the sequence failed before choosing the control.
questionsV2.recallLine: A colocation site's barrier arm let a tester's car follow a booked courier in unchallenged. Which perimeter change BEST stops the next uninvited vehicle?

optionsShort.A: A two-gate trap sequencing the outer gate
optionsShort.B: Camera analytics counting vehicles per authorization
optionsShort.C: A higher fence with razor topping
optionsShort.D: Reception verifies deliveries against the booking list

B.label: detective when preventive is asked
B.wouldAnswer: Counts the vehicles the tester's car was the second of. A count reaching reception after the car has parked is a record.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Strengthens a boundary the tester never touched. Razor wire is nothing to a driver who came through the gate.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Tightens the authorization of the first vehicle, which was legitimate. The barrier would have risen exactly as it did.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PE-3 Physical Access Control — controlling ingress at facility entry points
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.14.1 Perimeter security controls

questionsV2.question: Ashcombe Analytics leases four floors of a shared office tower. Each floor has a communications room holding the floor switch and the fiber patch to the building's carrier entry, and all four are opened by a facilities master key that the landlord issues to cleaning, catering and maintenance contractors. During a cable audit an engineer finds a passive optical tap spliced into the fourth-floor uplink, feeding a small transmitter cable-tied inside the rack. No door alarm, work ticket or camera records anyone entering that room. Which internal control MOST directly stops the next device being installed?

options.A: Tamper-evident seals on each patch panel, inspected against a checklist every month
options.B: Badge-controlled locks on the communications rooms, restricted to the network team and logged
options.C: Escorting all cleaning and catering contractors while they work on the leased floors
options.D: Re-keying the landlord's master suite annually and reissuing keys to the same contractors

questionsV2.explanation:
Nothing in the building recorded who opened that room, and a landlord set the population able to open it for reasons that had nothing to do with a fiber uplink. A badge reader on the door, with the list restricted to the network team, does two things at once (B). It shrinks entry to people with a reason to be there, and it produces a record that can be read against work orders when the next device turns up.
Passive taps authenticate to nothing, so the control that counts is the one on the door.
questionsV2.recallLine: A tenant found a passive fiber tap in a communications room opened by the landlord's contractor master key. Which internal control MOST directly prevents a repeat?

optionsShort.A: Tamper-evident seals on patch panels, inspected monthly
optionsShort.B: Badge locks restricted to the network team
optionsShort.C: Escort cleaning and catering contractors on site
optionsShort.D: Re-key the master suite each year

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: A good companion control. A seal is a report, and the transmitter is in the rack before anybody reads the checklist.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Covers two contractor groups and leaves maintenance, the landlord's own staff and everyone else holding a master key.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Changes the metal and keeps the distribution list exactly as it was.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | PE-4 Access Control for Transmission — securing wiring closets and distribution
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.14.2 Internal security controls

questionsV2.question: The examiner reaches the unlocked laptop with a write blocker and an evidence drive. Which acquisition step should be taken FIRST?

options.A: Shut the laptop down cleanly and image the drive through the write blocker
options.B: Photograph the screen, then capture volatile memory and the list of running processes
options.C: Copy the personal cloud sync folder onto the evidence drive and hash each file
options.D: Disconnect the laptop's network cable to stop any further synchronization to the cloud

questionsV2.explanation:
Everything that disappears when power is removed goes first. On a machine sitting unlocked that means the mounted cloud client, its session tokens, the open network connections and whatever is resident in memory. Photographing the screen records the state a defense expert will later ask about (B).
Order an acquisition by how fast the evidence decays.
questionsV2.recallLine: An examiner reaches a departing developer's laptop, powered on and unlocked, with a write blocker in hand. Which acquisition step should be taken FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Shut down and image through the write blocker
optionsShort.B: Photograph the screen and capture volatile memory
optionsShort.C: Copy the sync folder and hash it
optionsShort.D: Pull the network cable to stop syncing

A.label: correct but not first
A.wouldAnswer: The dead-box procedure, due within the hour. A clean shutdown flushes the volatile material that shows the folder syncing.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Collects the target files and nothing that explains how they got there. A hash proves integrity from the copy onward.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Stops further loss, which matters while data is still leaving. This injunction turns on what already left.

sources: IETF RFC 3227 | §2.1 Order of volatility
NIST SP 800-86 | §3.1 Collection — acquiring data from a live system
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.1.4 Digital forensics tools, tactics, and procedures

questionsV2.question: The investigator has one chance at a first interview. Which action should be completed BEFORE the developer is questioned?

options.A: Acquire and examine the laptop, the sync folder and the repository access logs
options.B: Withdraw her network access and her building badge before she reaches her desk
options.C: Search her corporate mailbox for contact with the competitor's recruiters
options.D: Interview the two colleagues who share the pricing repository with her

questionsV2.explanation:
An interview is worth what the interviewer already knows. With the machine imaged, the sync folder parsed and the repository's read history in hand, the investigator can put dates, file names and volumes to the developer and test her account against them (A). Go in without that and the meeting tells her what has been noticed, leaving three weeks to tidy.
Collect, then examine, then confront.
questionsV2.recallLine: An insider investigator gets one first interview with a developer suspected of copying pricing models. Which action should be completed BEFORE she is questioned?

optionsShort.A: Acquire and examine the laptop and logs
optionsShort.B: Withdraw her network access and badge
optionsShort.C: Search her mailbox for recruiter contact
optionsShort.D: Interview the colleagues who share the repository

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: Belongs at termination, or once the evidence is secured. Pulling access first announces the investigation to its subject.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: A reasonable line of inquiry into whether the competitor solicited the copy. Here the copy itself is the question.

D.label: correct but not first
D.wouldAnswer: Will be needed, and colleagues may confirm the copy was sanctioned. Taken early it puts the story into her own team.

sources: ISO/IEC 27043:2015 | §7 Incident investigation principles and processes
NIST SP 800-86 | §3.2 Examination and §3.3 Analysis
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.1.3 Investigative techniques

questionsV2.question: The examiner is writing the report outside counsel will rely on. Which practice MOST protects its value at the injunction hearing?

options.A: Write the report as a narrative timeline of the developer's actions that weekend
options.B: Attach the full disk image and the memory capture as appendices to it
options.C: Have the line manager review and sign the report before it is issued
options.D: Separate observed fact from examiner opinion and record every tool version and hash

questionsV2.explanation:
A report survives cross-examination when its factual claims can be reproduced by the other side's expert and its inferences are visibly labeled as inference (D). Recording the tool, its version and the hash of each acquisition lets an opposing examiner repeat the work and reach the same figures. Keeping opinion in its own section stops a court discounting the facts along with a conclusion it rejects.
Facts a stranger can reproduce, opinions a stranger can identify.
questionsV2.recallLine: A forensic examiner is writing an insider-theft report that outside counsel will rely on in court. Which reporting practice MOST protects its value?

optionsShort.A: Write it as a narrative timeline
optionsShort.B: Attach the disk and memory images
optionsShort.C: Have the line manager sign it
optionsShort.D: Separate fact from opinion; record tool hashes

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: How findings are made readable, and often the first section a judge reads. A narrative presents inference as sequence.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Confuses the report with the exhibit register. Images are held under chain of custody and referred to by hash.

C.label: not the decision-maker's
C.wouldAnswer: Would have a witness who contaminated the machine endorse the account of that contamination.

sources: NIST SP 800-86 | §3.4 Reporting
ISO/IEC 27037:2012 | §7.1 Documentation of digital evidence handling
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.1.2 Reporting and documentation

questionsV2.question: The developer works her notice for three more weeks and still has models to deliver. Which access decision BEST fits least privilege here?

options.A: Suspend her account today and reassign both live models to another developer
options.B: Leave her access unchanged so the investigation can observe any further copying
options.C: Cut her repository rights to the two live models and log every read
options.D: Move her to a supervised terminal with screen recording for the remaining weeks

questionsV2.explanation:
Need-to-know is measured against the work a person still has to do. Two models remain hers until month end, so the entitlement that matches the job is read and write on those two and nothing else, with reads recorded so any further collection is visible (C).
Least privilege is not a fixed setting. It tracks the assignment, and it moves again the day the handover finishes.
Reduce what is reachable before increasing what is watched.
questionsV2.recallLine: A developer under investigation works three more weeks of notice and still has pricing models to deliver. Which access decision BEST fits least privilege?

optionsShort.A: Suspend her account and reassign both models
optionsShort.B: Leave access unchanged to observe further copying
optionsShort.C: Cut rights to the two models, log reads
optionsShort.D: Move her to a supervised recorded terminal

A.label: wrong scope
A.wouldAnswer: Right once the handover is complete. Done today it strips access she still needs and tips off the investigation.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: A recognized investigative tactic. As an answer to a need-to-know question it runs backward.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Watches behavior and reduces no entitlement. A recorded session with the same rights leaks the same data.

sources: NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-6 Least Privilege
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | AC-2(3) Account Management — disable accounts
ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline 2024 | 7.4.1 Need-to-know/least privilege

questionsV2.question: Tarnwick Freight Systems runs 900 Linux servers built from a hardening baseline approved two years ago. A quarterly scan finds that 310 of them differ from it: SSH root login re-enabled on 40, audit daemons stopped on 96, unmanaged packages on the rest. Each finding is remediated by hand and the same drift reappears at the next scan. The platform team already builds every new server from a machine image and can rebuild any workload in under ten minutes. Which change would MOST durably keep the estate on its baseline?

options.A: Run the compliance scan weekly and open a ticket for each deviation
options.B: Rebuild servers from a versioned image on a fixed cycle, forbidding in-place edits
options.C: Deploy a configuration management agent in audit mode across the whole estate
options.D: Update the hardening baseline document and re-approve it through the change board

questionsV2.explanation:
Drift that returns after every remediation is a property of the process, and the 310 servers are innocent. Let a running server be edited in place and the edits accumulate between scans, so somebody is always reapplying them. Make the unit of change a new image, discard the old server, and the running estate is by construction whatever the last approved image contained (B). The ten-minute rebuild the platform team already has makes that affordable.
Enforcement lives in how systems are built.
questionsV2.recallLine: A fleet of 900 Linux servers drifts from its hardening baseline and the same deviations return after every manual fix. Which change MOST durably prevents that?

optionsShort.A: Scan weekly and ticket each deviation
optionsShort.B: Rebuild from a versioned image, no in-place edits
optionsShort.C: Deploy an audit-mode configuration agent
optionsShort.D: Update and re-approve the baseline document

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Shortens the window between drift and discovery, and is worth doing. It is the current process run more often.

C.label: detective when preventive is asked
C.wouldAnswer: Measures the gap accurately and continuously. In audit mode it changes nothing on any host.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Repairs the standard itself. A re-approved document still has no mechanism to reach a server.

sources: NIST SP 800-128 | §2.3 Configuration control and configuration monitoring
NIST SP 800-53 Rev 5 | CM-2 Baseline Configuration and CM-6 Configuration Settings

questionsV2.question: Orrenmoor Health Networks contracts a vendor to maintain its radiology archive. The vendor's four engineers share one domain account that belongs to Domain Admins, has no password expiry, and is used about twice a month for planned work. An internal audit finds the account authenticated at 02:00 on a Sunday against no change ticket, and nobody can say which of the four engineers held that session. The vendor refuses individual named accounts because its own staff rotate weekly. Which change would MOST directly restore accountability for the vendor's privileged work?

options.A: Expire the shared account's password every thirty days and notify the vendor
options.B: Reduce the account from Domain Admins to a scoped archive administrator role
options.C: Check the shared credential out of a vault per session, rotated afterwards
options.D: Record every privileged session and review the recordings at the monthly audit

questionsV2.explanation:
Accountability means naming the human behind a session, and nothing in the current arrangement does that, because the credential itself is the identity. Checking the password out of a vault binds a named engineer to a time window, records who held it, and rotates it on check-in so the standing secret stops existing between jobs (C). It works even though the vendor will not create individual directory accounts.
Attribution is created at the moment of use. Everything else reconstructs it.
questionsV2.recallLine: Four vendor engineers share one Domain Admins account used for planned archive maintenance. Which change MOST directly restores accountability for their work?

optionsShort.A: Expire the shared password every thirty days
optionsShort.B: Scope the account below Domain Admins
optionsShort.C: Vault checkout per session, rotated afterwards
optionsShort.D: Record and review privileged sessions monthly

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Shortens the life of a leaked password and leaves four people sharing whatever the current one is.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Least privilege, and it should follow. Scoping the rights still does not say who exercised them.

D.label: detective when preventive is asked
D.wouldAnswer: Captures what was done in rich detail, a month later. That is evidence; the question asks for attribution.

questionsV2.question: Duncastle Media streams video from a cloud provider whose service-level agreement promises 99.9 percent monthly availability, with a ten percent service credit if that is missed. A regional fault took the platform down for four hours on a Saturday evening, costing Duncastle an estimated 1.1 million in lost subscriptions and refunds. The provider paid the credit: 4,200. The agreement carries no data-restoration term, no incident-notification deadline and no right to audit. Renewal falls in three months and the chief operating officer wants terms that protect the business as opposed to rebate a fraction of a bill. Which change would MOST improve that protection?

options.A: Raise the service credit to fifty percent of the monthly fee
options.B: Tighten the availability commitment from 99.9 percent to 99.99 percent monthly
options.C: Add a notification deadline, a recovery-time commitment and a right to audit
options.D: Require the provider to carry indemnity insurance naming Duncastle as beneficiary

questionsV2.explanation:
The service credit is a discount. It is calculated from the fee, so it can never scale with what an outage costs the customer, and paying it discharges the provider's obligation. What changes behavior during the four hours is a commitment about the four hours (C): a deadline to say what has happened, a committed time to restore service, and the right to inspect whether the controls behind those commitments exist.
Negotiate the provider's behavior before negotiating the penalty.
questionsV2.recallLine: A cloud provider's four-hour outage cost a streaming business 1.1 million and returned a 4,200 service credit. Which change to the agreement MOST improves protection?

optionsShort.A: Raise the service credit to fifty percent
optionsShort.B: Tighten availability to 99.99 percent monthly
optionsShort.C: Add notification, recovery-time and audit terms
optionsShort.D: Require provider indemnity insurance naming the customer

A.label: symptom not cause
A.wouldAnswer: Raises the discount to a larger fraction of a small number, leaving 1.1 million uncovered.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Tightens the outage minutes permitted, and says nothing about what the provider must do once it has lost them.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Moves money after the fact through an insurer. That handles residual loss once the operational terms are settled.

questionsV2.question: Feldspar Imaging leases a flash storage array holding 18 months of diagnostic images. Every drive in it is a self-encrypting drive whose key is held in the array's key manager. Over the lease 214 drives failed and were swapped by the vendor; the contract requires each failed drive to go back to the lessor for warranty credit worth about 60,000 in total. Thirty-one of the failed drives will not power up, so no command can be sent to them. The information security manager must clear the images from all 214 before they ship. Which approach BEST achieves that?

options.A: Degauss each drive before shipment and log the serial numbers returned
options.B: Overwrite every drive three times with a purge utility, then verify a sample
options.C: Destroy the drives on site and negotiate credits against destruction certificates
options.D: Destroy the key manager's per-drive keys and record each cryptographic erase

questionsV2.explanation:
Sanitization has to work on media the organization can no longer address, and thirty-one of these drives will not accept a command at all. Every drive is self-encrypting and its key lives in the array, off the media, so destroying that key renders the ciphertext unrecoverable without touching the drive (D). That satisfies purge for all 214 and keeps them intact for the lessor.
Match the technique to the medium and to who holds the key.
questionsV2.recallLine: A leased flash array's 214 failed self-encrypting drives must go back to the lessor with the diagnostic images cleared. Which approach BEST achieves that?

optionsShort.A: Degauss each drive before shipment
optionsShort.B: Overwrite three times, then verify a sample
optionsShort.C: Destroy on site, negotiate destruction credits
optionsShort.D: Destroy the per-drive keys, log the erases

A.label: true of a different thing
A.wouldAnswer: A purge technique for magnetic media. A magnetic field does nothing to charge stored in flash cells.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Needs a responsive drive, and on flash it cannot reach blocks the controller has retired or over-provisioned.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: The highest-assurance route, and it destroys the asset the warranty credit depends on.

questionsV2.question: Wrayburn Telecom detonates every attachment its mail gateway cannot classify in an automated sandbox, which runs each sample for 90 seconds in a fresh virtual machine with no domain membership and a simulated internet. A phishing campaign is now reaching desktops with a loader the sandbox rates clean every time. On a real workstation the same file waits eleven minutes, checks that the host is joined to a domain, and only then contacts its controller. The security engineer must make the sandbox catch this family. Which change would MOST directly do that?

options.A: Hold every attachment the gateway leaves unclassified until an analyst reviews it
options.B: Extend the run time and give the images domain membership and realistic artifacts
options.C: Add the loader's file hashes to the gateway blocklist as they are reported
options.D: Detonate the samples on physical hardware instead of in virtual machines

questionsV2.explanation:
The sandbox is not failing to analyze. It is being told, correctly, that it is not a target. Eleven minutes exceeds a ninety-second run, and an unjoined machine fails the loader's domain check, so the sample does nothing and is scored on that. Lengthen the detonation, give the images the domain membership, user profile and document history a real desktop has, and both conditions the family tests for disappear (B).
Read what a sample checks for, then remove the check.
questionsV2.recallLine: A mail sandbox runs each sample ninety seconds in an unjoined virtual machine and rates a delayed, domain-checking loader clean. Which change MOST directly fixes that?

optionsShort.A: Hold unclassified attachments for analyst review
optionsShort.B: Extend run time, add domain and realistic artifacts
optionsShort.C: Blocklist the loader's file hashes
optionsShort.D: Detonate on physical hardware instead

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: A sound interim measure at the gateway. The sandbox will still rate the next variant clean.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: Blocks binaries already identified somewhere else, one hash at a time, and this family recompiles.

D.label: true of a different thing
D.wouldAnswer: Defeats sandboxes that are spotted through hypervisor artifacts. This sample looks for no such thing.

questionsV2.question: Inglewood Chemicals runs a flat plant network where a compromised engineering workstation gave an intruder ninety days of undetected lateral movement last year. The security team already has endpoint detection on servers, a SIEM and netflow. It now wants a signal that fires early, is almost never raised by ordinary work, and costs little to run. The plant will not accept anything that touches the availability of the process control network. Which deployment BEST meets that requirement?

options.A: Seed decoy credentials and unused file shares that no legitimate process should touch
options.B: Stand up an internet-facing honeypot to collect tooling aimed at the plant
options.C: Mirror the plant network into a honeynet that emulates the control systems
options.D: Raise SIEM alerting on failed logons across the engineering workstations

questionsV2.explanation:
The requirement is a signal with almost no legitimate traffic behind it, and deception supplies exactly that (A). A credential no process should ever use and a share no job should ever open produce alerts whose false-positive base rate is close to zero. They sit in the estate where the traversal happened, and the plant depends on none of them.
Deception is cheap because it is defined by traffic that should not exist.
questionsV2.recallLine: A flat plant network needs a cheap, low-noise early signal of lateral movement without touching process control availability. Which deployment BEST meets that?

optionsShort.A: Seed decoy credentials and unused shares
optionsShort.B: Run an internet-facing honeypot for tooling
optionsShort.C: Build a honeynet emulating the control systems
optionsShort.D: Alert on failed engineering-workstation logons

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Faces the internet and reports scanning from outside. Ninety days of internal movement looked nothing like that.

C.label: right control, wrong problem
C.wouldAnswer: The right instrument for studying industrial protocols, and it means standing a system beside the process network.

D.label: symptom not cause
D.wouldAnswer: Reports failed logons, the noise a clumsy attacker makes. This one held valid credentials and made none.

questionsV2.question: Portmadoc Ferries runs ticketing and berth scheduling from a single data center. At 04:50 a chilled-water main bursts, the hall's temperature climbs and servers begin shutting down on thermal protection. The disaster recovery plan gives ticketing a four-hour recovery time objective and names the duty operations manager as the person who declares a disaster once restoration inside that objective is no longer credible. At 06:20 the plumbing contractor says he can give no repair estimate until a valve is exposed, perhaps another two hours. Which action should the duty manager take FIRST?

options.A: Have facilities install portable cooling and keep the hall running
options.B: Wait for the contractor's estimate, then judge whether the objective can be met
options.C: Notify the maritime regulator and ticket holders of a service interruption
options.D: Declare a disaster and start the documented failover to the recovery site

questionsV2.explanation:
The plan never asks the duty manager to know when the cooling will be fixed. It asks whether restoration inside four hours is still credible. At 06:20, with the objective expiring at 08:50 and no estimate available before 08:20, it is not, and the trigger the plan wrote down has fired. Declaring converts a hopeful repair into an authorized failover with staff, budget and a documented sequence behind it (D).
Declare on the trigger.
questionsV2.recallLine: A cooling failure will breach a four-hour recovery objective and the repair time is unknown. Which action should the duty manager take FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Install portable cooling and keep running
optionsShort.B: Wait for the contractor's repair estimate
optionsShort.C: Notify the regulator and ticket holders
optionsShort.D: Declare a disaster and fail over

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Treats the heat. Right when the repair is minutes away; here it competes for the same two hours.

B.label: wrong phase
B.wouldAnswer: The instinct that costs organizations their objective. The estimate arrives after the decision window closes.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: Required, and it will be done. It also announces a position the duty manager has not yet taken.

questionsV2.question: Guildhaven Building Supplies failed its order-entry system over to a recovery site after a power event and, six hours later, the recovery team reports the system restored. The application answers on its published address, the monitoring dashboard is green, the database service is running and the backup software's restore job reported success. Branch staff have not yet been told to resume trading. The continuity plan requires a restoration to be confirmed before the incident is closed and the recovery clock stopped. Which confirmation BEST establishes that the service is actually restored?

options.A: The monitoring platform reports every component healthy for a continuous thirty-minute window
options.B: The business owner processes agreed test orders and reconciles results against expected values
options.C: The restore job log shows no errors and record counts match the backup
options.D: The infrastructure team confirms every server, service and network route is running

questionsV2.explanation:
Recovery is a statement about a business process, and the party who can make it is the one who runs the process (B). Putting a small set of agreed orders through the recovered system and reconciling the outputs against known-good values exercises the application, the data and the integrations together. It also produces a record the incident can be closed on.
Up is not the same as right.
questionsV2.recallLine: An order-entry system is reported restored at a recovery site with a green dashboard and a clean restore job. Which confirmation BEST establishes actual restoration?

optionsShort.A: Monitoring shows every component healthy thirty minutes
optionsShort.B: Business owner runs and reconciles test orders
optionsShort.C: Restore log clean and record counts match
optionsShort.D: Infrastructure team confirms all servers running

A.label: right control, wrong problem
A.wouldAnswer: Shows the platform has stopped moving, which operations needs. A green dashboard is a statement about heartbeats.

C.label: wrong scope
C.wouldAnswer: Checks that the restore was complete. Matching record counts say nothing about how the application computes.

D.label: not the decision-maker's
D.wouldAnswer: The layer report from the people who rebuilt it. Every server can be running while order entry prices wrongly.

questionsV2.question: Saltmarsh Mutual Insurance ran its first parallel test of policy administration on a Sunday. Production stayed live for members while the recovery site processed a copy of Friday's 41,000 transactions on restored data. The recovery site completed the run in seven hours against production's five, raised no errors, and the team recorded the test as passed. Nobody compared the two sets of output. The continuity manager is now preparing the report for the audit committee. Which step should be completed BEFORE the test is recorded as passed?

options.A: Reconcile the recovery site's output against production's for the same 41,000 transactions
options.B: Repeat the run until the recovery site matches production's five-hour completion time
options.C: Have the audit committee approve the test scope and the data set used
options.D: Confirm the restored data matched Friday's production database at the restore point

questionsV2.explanation:
The parallel test exists to answer one question: does the recovery environment produce the same results as production from the same inputs? Running the transactions is the procedure. Comparing the two outputs is the test (A). Until 41,000 results are reconciled, the exercise has shown only that the site starts and runs, which a walkthrough could have suggested. Seven hours against production's five is a real finding to carry to the recovery time objective, but it is a separate one.
Without the comparison, a test has no result.
questionsV2.recallLine: A parallel recovery test processed 41,000 transactions at the recovery site and nobody compared the outputs. Which step should be completed BEFORE recording a pass?

optionsShort.A: Reconcile the two sets of output
optionsShort.B: Repeat until completion times match production
optionsShort.C: Get audit committee approval of scope
optionsShort.D: Confirm the restored data matched production

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Measures throughput. A correct result delivered slowly is still a correct result.

C.label: wrong phase
C.wouldAnswer: Belongs before the Sunday. Scope approved after the fact approves whatever happened.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Validates the input side. That is a backup integrity question, and it would be the priority if the outputs disagreed.

questionsV2.question: Kirkbride Foods has passed tabletop, walkthrough, simulation and parallel tests of its warehouse management recovery, and the board has now approved a full interruption test: production will be shut down and the recovery site will carry live picking for four hours on a Saturday. Order volumes are lowest then, executive sponsorship is in place and the test window has been published. The continuity manager wants the test to be genuinely informative without putting Monday's deliveries at risk. Which addition to the test plan MOST reduces that risk?

options.A: An observer from internal audit recording each step against the documented procedure
options.B: A communications plan naming stakeholders and the start and stop calls made
options.C: Written abort criteria, a rehearsed fallback to production, and a named decision-maker
options.D: A rollback of the warehouse database to Friday's snapshot after the test

questionsV2.explanation:
This is the one exercise in a continuity program that can genuinely hurt the business. What makes it acceptable is a bounded downside (C). Criteria written before the day say which conditions end the test. A fallback to production the team has actually practiced. One named person with authority to call it. Everything else in the plan improves what is learned. Only this limits what is risked.
Decide how to stop before deciding to start.
questionsV2.recallLine: A board has approved a four-hour full interruption test of warehouse recovery on a Saturday. Which addition to the test plan MOST reduces the risk?

optionsShort.A: An internal audit observer recording each step
optionsShort.B: A communications plan with start and stop calls
optionsShort.C: Abort criteria, rehearsed fallback, named decision-maker
optionsShort.D: A database rollback to Friday's snapshot afterwards

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: Produces a better record of how the documented procedure held up, captured after the fact.

B.label: right control, wrong problem
B.wouldAnswer: Keeps a live-looking exercise from being mistaken for a real incident. It does nothing for Monday's deliveries.

D.label: true of a different thing
D.wouldAnswer: Describes a parallel test, where the output is discarded. Here the picking done at the recovery site is real work.

questionsV2.question: Nettlefold Engineering designs turbine blades and holds export-controlled drawings. A senior engineer returns from a five-day conference abroad where border officials took her corporate laptop and phone out of sight for forty minutes, and where she used the hotel business center's printer for a presentation. She reports both facts to the security team on her first morning back. The laptop has full-disk encryption and endpoint detection, and nothing has alerted. She is due to plug into the design network at ten o'clock. Which action should the security team take FIRST?

options.A: Add both devices to a watch list and monitor their traffic monthly
options.B: Run a full endpoint scan and review the laptop's logs for the trip
options.C: Report the border inspection to the export control officer and outside counsel
options.D: Rebuild the laptop and phone from trusted media and reset her credentials

questionsV2.explanation:
Any device that left its owner's control at a border crossing is untrusted from then on. The interesting attacks in that setting are the ones endpoint tooling never sees: firmware, the bootloader, an implant on the mainboard, a cloned credential store. Rebuilding from trusted media and rotating everything the device held costs a morning and closes all of them at once (D). It is why organizations holding export-controlled material issue clean devices for such trips.
Absence of an alert is not evidence of integrity.
questionsV2.recallLine: An engineer's laptop and phone were out of her sight for forty minutes at a foreign border. Which action should the security team take FIRST?

optionsShort.A: Watch-list the devices and monitor traffic
optionsShort.B: Scan the laptop and review its logs
optionsShort.C: Report the inspection to export control
optionsShort.D: Rebuild both devices and reset her credentials

A.label: detective when preventive is asked
A.wouldAnswer: Lets the device back onto the design network and waits for a callback competent tooling will delay.

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Tests for known malware in the operating system. It reaches no firmware, and its silence is already on offer.

C.label: correct but not first
C.wouldAnswer: A genuine obligation, and counsel will want the timeline. It does not decide the ten o'clock reconnection.

questionsV2.question: Bramber Bullion operates six vault branches. Each teller has a duress code that opens the safe normally while sending a silent alarm to the contracted monitoring center. Under the current runbook the center's operator responds to a duress alarm by telephoning the branch and asking a manager whether everything is in order. In a robbery last month a teller entered the code, the operator telephoned, the robber told the manager what to say, and police were not called for nineteen minutes. Which change to the arrangement MOST restores the control's value?

options.A: Dispatch police on the duress alarm without any call back to the branch
options.B: Give each teller a distinct duress code so the center identifies the sender
options.C: Replace the telephone check with a coded challenge phrase the manager answers
options.D: Retrain tellers on when to enter the duress code and log drills

questionsV2.explanation:
A duress signal is defined by what it does not require: the person who sent it never has to confirm it. Telephoning the branch puts that confirmation back in the room with the robber, so the runbook turned a silent alarm into a hostage negotiation, and the nineteen minutes follow from the design. Dispatching on the signal alone (A) accepts a small rate of false calls as the price of a control that works while someone is under a gun.
Never verify a duress alarm with the people under duress.
questionsV2.recallLine: A monitoring center answers every silent duress alarm by telephoning the branch to ask whether all is well. Which change MOST restores the control's value?

optionsShort.A: Dispatch police without calling the branch
optionsShort.B: Give each teller a distinct duress code
optionsShort.C: Use a coded challenge phrase instead
optionsShort.D: Retrain tellers on the duress code

B.label: wrong scope
B.wouldAnswer: Tells the center which position sent the signal, useful for the police briefing. The call back still happens.

C.label: symptom not cause
C.wouldAnswer: A technique for verifying a caller's identity. A phrase spoken beside an armed robber is still spoken under coercion.

D.label: right control, wrong problem
D.wouldAnswer: Would matter if the teller had frozen. She used the code correctly, and the failure sat downstream of her.

domains.title: Software Development Security
domains.caseStudy:
Domain 8 covers security in the software lifecycle: development methodologies, secure coding, code repositories and build pipelines, application testing, and the risks in software you buy or integrate instead of write.

Case Study: The "GitHub" API Key Leak

### Context

Global Bank built a "Cardless Cash" feature: the mobile app authenticates to a backend API and the ATM dispenses without a card. The right design used OAuth and short-lived tokens. During a hackathon, to save time, the developers hardcoded a master API key into the source. One developer pushed the code to a public GitHub repository to keep working from home.

### What went wrong

Bots that scan GitHub for strings like API_KEY found it within seconds. With the key, attackers authenticated to the backend as an administrator, skipping user authentication entirely. The API did not check whether the caller owned the records it asked for, so any account was readable; one endpoint was vulnerable to injection; and the same access could initiate transfers.

Cardless transactions are, in the white paper's terms, one of the strongest answers to skimming, shimming and card trapping, because there is no card at the fascia to attack. What that trade does is move the trust from the card reader to the mobile app and the API behind it. The paper's section on software vulnerabilities lists the failure modes that then matter: application flaws, insecure configuration, default credentials. It also observes that attack tooling is a commodity now, sold on darknet forums with manuals; scraping bots are the same economics applied to leaked secrets.

### What a practitioner does differently

Secrets never live in code. They live in a vault, are issued to services as short-lived tokens through OAuth 2.0 client credentials, and rotate on a schedule and instantly on suspicion. Secret scanning runs as a pre-commit hook and as a pre-receive hook on the server, so a key cannot reach a repository, public or private.

Authorization is checked per object: every API call verifies the caller owns the record. Queries are parameterized. Both are OWASP Top 10 items (broken access control, injection), and both are found by static analysis and code review before a hackathon branch is anywhere near production. Which is the larger point: hackathon code is a prototype. It enters the normal lifecycle, with threat modelling at design and testing before release, or it does not ship.

Repository policy closes the door the developer walked through: no public repositories for bank code, branch protection, and mandatory review before merge. Monitoring on the API catches an administrator identity doing what no administrator does at 2 AM.

### Outcome

The key was rotated as soon as the leak was found and the public repository taken down. The bank's postmortem added secret scanning to every pipeline, per-object authorization to the API, and a rule that prototype code re-enters the lifecycle at the requirements stage.

### What the exam tests

Expect questions on where security sits in each SDLC phase, on secure coding and the OWASP Top 10 categories this scenario touches (broken access control, injection, identification and authentication failures, cryptographic failures), on secrets management and repository security, on the difference between authentication and authorization, and on why a prototype needs the same gates as production code before it is deployed.

### Related reading

The bank in this scenario is a composite. The trade-off and the controls are documented in:

- [Technical Risks and Attack Vectors Targeting ATMs](https://portfolio.atmavailability.com/atm-technical-risks-white-paper.pdf), the sections on contactless and cardless transactions, on software, OS and firmware vulnerabilities, and on secure development practices for ATM applications.
- [ATM Security Capability Maturity Worksheet](https://portfolio.atmavailability.com/atm-capability-maturity-worksheet.pdf), Domain 2, logical and cybersecurity controls.

questions.question: During a hackathon, Global Bank's mobile developers hardcoded the backend Master_API_Key into source code, and the code was later pushed to a public repository. The bank now wants to keep credentials from ever residing in application code again. Which approach best achieves this goal?

options.A: Store credentials in a configuration file that is excluded from version control by .gitignore
options.B: Encrypt the hardcoded key within the source so it is unreadable in the repository
options.C: Restrict every company repository to private visibility so outsiders can no longer browse code
options.D: Retrieve credentials at runtime from a managed secrets vault with access control and rotation

questions.explanation: Code is for logic; secrets belong in a dedicated store. A vault (D) means the credential never enters the codebase at all: the application fetches it at runtime, access is authenticated and audited, and the key can be rotated centrally after any suspected exposure. Option A is wrong because it merely relocates the secret: a .gitignore entry is advisory, the file still sits unprotected on disks and in backups, and one wrong command commits it anyway; it is the right answer to keeping local developer settings out of a repo, not to protecting production secrets. Option B is wrong because the application must ship the decryption key too, so the secret remains recoverable from the artifact. That is obfuscation, not protection. Option C is wrong because it reduces external exposure while leaving the credential in code, visible to every employee, clone, and backup; private repositories leak regularly.

questions.question: A defense contractor is building flight-control software under a contract that fixes all requirements up front, mandates formal documentation with approval gates at every stage, and prohibits scope changes without a contract modification. Which development model is most appropriate for this project?

options.A: Waterfall, because its sequential phases and stage-gate approvals match fixed, documented requirements
options.B: Scrum, because short sprints let the team reprioritize the requirements as work proceeds
options.C: Rapid Application Development, because time-boxed prototyping delivers a working system fastest
options.D: Prototyping, because iterating on partial versions helps stakeholders discover what they need

questions.explanation: The environment described, with stable contractual requirements, formal documentation, and mandatory approval gates, is exactly what Waterfall's sequential, sign-off-driven structure was designed for, and its classic weakness (going back to an earlier phase is expensive) is neutralized when change is contractually prohibited anyway. Option B is wrong for this project because Scrum's core advantage is absorbing evolving requirements, which the contract forbids; it would be the right choice where needs shift between iterations. Option C is wrong because RAD deliberately trades documentation and rigor for speed, the opposite of what the mandate demands; it fits when time-to-market dominates. Option D is wrong because prototyping exists to help stakeholders who cannot yet articulate requirements; here the requirements are already fixed and signed. Choose the lifecycle from the stability of requirements and the rigor demanded, not from fashion.

questions.question: A startup is launching a product in a market where customer needs are poorly understood and expected to shift every few weeks. Leadership wants working software delivered early and refined continuously from real user feedback. Which development approach best fits these conditions?

options.A: Waterfall, since completing the full design before coding avoids expensive rework later
options.B: Cleanroom, since formally verified increments give the highest confidence in each release
options.C: Agile, since short iterations and continuous customer feedback absorb changing requirements
options.D: The V-model, since pairing every build phase with a matching test phase catches defects early

questions.explanation: Rapidly shifting requirements plus a demand for early, continuously refined releases are the exact conditions iterative Agile methods were created for: each short cycle delivers working software and folds user feedback into the next. Option A is wrong because Waterfall assumes requirements can be fixed before design begins — here they cannot, so the finished design would describe the wrong product; it is the right answer when requirements are stable and change is prohibited. Option B is wrong because Cleanroom's formal specification and verification are slow and assume a precise spec exists; it suits safety-critical software, not a moving target. Option D is wrong because the V-model is still a sequential, plan-driven shape; its paired test phases verify a fixed specification and cannot absorb change.

questions.question: An online retailer deploys code to production twenty times a day through an automated pipeline. Security reviews are performed manually by a separate team in the week before each quarterly compliance audit, and findings routinely reach developers months after the code shipped. What is the most effective way to close this gap?

options.A: Slow the release cadence so the security team can manually review every change before deployment
options.B: Integrate automated security testing into the pipeline so every build is checked before release
options.C: Increase the frequency of the compliance audits from quarterly to monthly reporting cycles
options.D: Have developers self-certify each release against a secure-coding checklist at deployment time

questions.explanation: The mismatch here is speed: delivery is automated and continuous while security is manual and periodic. DevSecOps closes it by making security run at the pipeline's own speed: automated static analysis plus dependency and secret scanning on every build, so findings reach the developer in minutes, while the change is still fresh. Option A is wrong because it sacrifices the delivery capability the business built and still scales linearly with reviewer headcount; reserving manual review for the highest-risk changes is sensible, but as the only control it fails. Option C is wrong because audits are detective and after the fact regardless of frequency; monthly audits still find problems months of deployments too late. Option D is wrong because self-certification adds no independent verification; checklists guide developers but do not test the code.

questions.question: A security analyst reviewing web logs finds that a request submitting the login value admin' OR '1'='1 caused the application to return every row of the customer table. The application is fully patched and its server configuration follows the vendor hardening guide. Which type of flaw most likely explains this behavior?

options.A: An injection flaw, because untrusted input was interpreted as part of a database command
options.B: A broken access control flaw, because the user viewed rows belonging to other customers
options.C: A security misconfiguration, because the database account held more privileges than needed
options.D: A cross-site scripting flaw, because attacker-supplied text was reflected in the response

questions.explanation: The tell is the quote and OR '1'='1: the input escaped its role as data and changed the logic of the SQL statement, turning a login check into a query that matches every row. That mechanism, input interpreted as code, defines injection (A). Option B is wrong because broken access control describes an application that correctly parses a legitimate request but fails to check authorization for it; here the request was malformed on purpose and subverted the query itself. B would be right if a well-formed request for another customer's ID had simply been honored. Option C is wrong because the stem states the configuration follows the hardening guide; over-privileged accounts amplify the damage of injection but do not create the flaw. Option D is wrong because XSS executes script in other users' browsers; the victim is the client, not the database. Classify a flaw by its mechanism, not by what data it exposed.

questions.question: A development team must remediate a confirmed SQL injection flaw in a banking application's search feature, and wants the fix that addresses the root cause and not one that filters attack traffic. Which control should the team implement first?

options.A: Deploy a web application firewall with rules that detect and drop known injection patterns
options.B: Sanitize request input by stripping quotes, comments, and SQL keywords before processing
options.C: Rewrite the data-access code to use parameterized queries that bind input as data values
options.D: Encrypt the customer database so records extracted through the flaw stay unreadable

questions.explanation: Injection exists because input and query text are concatenated into one string the database must reinterpret. Parameterized queries (C) remove that root cause: the statement's structure is compiled first and input is bound strictly as data, so no input value can change what the query does. Option A is wrong as a primary fix because a WAF is a compensating control, pattern-based and bypassable through encoding tricks, and it leaves the vulnerable code in place. It serves well as an interim shield while the code fix is developed, or for a product you cannot modify.
